      liver and/or bone marrow in children younger than 18 months. This is the
      Task Force's consensus definition, given in the results section of the
      structured abstract.
- name: INRGSS Stage MS
  description: >-
    Metastatic disease in a child younger than 18 months (547 days) with
    metastases confined to skin, liver and/or bone marrow, bone marrow
    involvement below 10% of nucleated cells, and meta-iodobenzylguanidine
    (MIBG) scintigraphy negative in bone and bone marrow; the primary tumor may
    be L1 or L2, with no restriction on crossing or infiltrating the midline.
    INSS stage 4S is the narrower INSS counterpart, limited to infants younger
    than 12 months with an INSS stage 1 or 2 primary tumor and dissemination to
    liver, skin and/or bone marrow (under 10% involvement); the INRGSS extended
    the age limit to 18 months and admitted primaries infiltrating the midline
    (INSS stage 3). In an Italian series of 30 infants with stage IV-S disease
    treated in 1970-1981, the liver was the most frequent site of spread (87%),
    and subcutaneous nodules were recorded. In infants with stage IV-S or 4S
    disease the pattern is associated with spontaneous regression and good
    survival. In two infant cohorts, one limited to symptomatic or biologically
    unfavorable cases, most deaths occurred in infants younger than 2 months at
    diagnosis, most often from complications of hepatomegaly or extensive
    abdominal involvement. In the selected cohort, enrolled on the COG trial
    ANBL0531, no further deaths from hepatomegaly occurred after the protocol
    was amended to require immediate chemotherapy for infants younger than 2
    months with evolving hepatomegaly. In a Children's Oncology Group cohort
    staged by the INRGSS, stage MS outcome was excellent except for
    MYCN-amplified tumors, which have a poor outcome. Whether toddlers aged 12
    to 18 months with a 4S pattern of metastasis share the favorable outcome of
    infants is contested. In the INRG database, toddlers grouped by metastatic
    sites alone, without the marrow limit of stage MS, had worse event-free
    survival than infants with the 4S pattern and outcomes similar to stage 4
    disease at the same age, and the authors concluded that tumor biology
    matters more than age or metastatic pattern. Registry data from two Japanese
    pediatric societies showed an excellent prognosis for stage 4s disease at 12
    to 17 months.
  notes: >-
    INSS stage 4S is recorded within this stage, not as a has_subtypes row,
    because the cancer granularity ladder (design decisions §3a) records stage
    under stages. The 4S category descends from the IV-S category of the 1971
    Evans staging system, recognizing patients with metastatic disease limited
    to skin, liver and bone marrow who have superior outcomes, and the 1993
    revision of the INSS added restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement
    for stage 4S. When the INRG Task Force extended the age limit to 18 months,
    it described the group aged 12 to 18 months as small, with an unclear
    outcome.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Stage MS is metastatic disease in patients younger than 18 months (547 days) with metastases confined to skin, liver, and/or bone marrow. Bone marrow involvement should be limited to less than 10% of total nucleated cells on smears or biopsy. MIBG scintigraphy must be negative in bone and bone marrow. Provided there is MIBG uptake in the primary tumor, bone scans are not required. The primary tumor can be L1 or L2 and there is no restriction regarding crossing or infiltration of the midline."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report that defines the INRGSS states each criterion
      of stage MS: age under 18 months (547 days); metastases confined to skin,
      liver and/or bone marrow; bone marrow involvement under 10% of nucleated
      cells; MIBG scintigraphy negative in bone and bone marrow; and an L1 or L2
      primary tumor with no restriction on crossing or infiltrating the midline.
      It is an expert-consensus definition; the report's own survival analysis
      covered only locoregional tumors.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Fourth, whereas INSS stage 4S has an upper age limit of 12 months, the Task Force decided to extend the age group for stage MS to patients younger than 18 months. ... Unlike INSS stage 4S, stage MS includes patients with primary tumors infiltrating the midline (INSS stage 3)."
    explanation: >-
      The same report names two differences between stage MS and INSS stage 4S:
      INSS 4S has an upper age limit of 12 months while the Task Force extended
      MS to children younger than 18 months, and unlike 4S, MS includes children
      whose primary tumor infiltrates the midline (INSS stage 3). These are
      consensus decisions, not outcome data.
  - reference: PMID:30754710
    reference_title: "The Evolution of Risk Classification for Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "4S | Localized primary tumor as defined by stage 1 or 2 in patient under 12 months with dissemination limited to the liver, skin, and/or bone marrow (<10% involvement)"
    explanation: >-
      Table 1 of this review, which sets out the International Neuroblastoma
      Staging System, defines stage 4S as a localized stage 1 or 2 primary tumor
      in a patient under 12 months with dissemination limited to the liver, skin
      and/or bone marrow (under 10% involvement). The row reproduces the
      consensus INSS definition and reports no patient data; the comparison with
      stage MS rests on the Task Force sentences above.
  - reference: PMID:8336186
    reference_title: "Revisions of the international criteria for neuroblastoma diagnosis, staging, and response to treatment."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Substantial changes included a redefinition of the midline, restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement for stage 4S, and the recommendation that meta-iodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scanning be implemented for evaluating the extent of disease."
    explanation: >-
      This is the 1993 consensus report that revised the INSS. Its abstract
      lists restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement for stage 4S among
      the substantial changes the revision made. The abstract does not give the
      numeric limits.
  - reference: PMID:30754710
    reference_title: "The Evolution of Risk Classification for Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In 1971, Evans et al. ... published the Evans Staging System based on extent of disease including a IV-S category, recognizing that there is a cohort of patients with metastatic disease limited to the skin, liver, and bone marrow, who have superior outcomes."
    explanation: >-
      This review states that the 1971 Evans staging system included a IV-S
      category, recognizing a group of patients with metastatic disease limited
      to the skin, liver and bone marrow who have superior outcomes. The
      sentence does not name INRGSS stage MS; that MS descends from this
      category, through INSS stage 4S, is an inference from the review's account
      of the staging systems. The ellipsis stands for an inline citation marker.
  - reference: PMID:10653863
    reference_title: "Favorable biology and outcome of stage IV-S neuroblastoma with supportive care or minimal therapy: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Stage IV-S neuroblastoma is a metastatic disease associated with spontaneous regression and good survival, but 10% to 20% of infants die from early complications."
    explanation: >-
      The opening sentence of the purpose section of this prospective Children's
      Cancer Group study of 80 infants states that stage IV-S neuroblastoma is
      associated with spontaneous regression and good survival, but that 10% to
      20% of infants die from early complications. The authors give this as
      background from earlier series; their own cohort had 6 deaths among 80
      infants. The quote concerns infants with IV-S disease.
  - reference: PMID:6727772
    reference_title: "IV-S neuroblastoma: a cooperative study of 30 children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The most frequent site of widespread disease was the liver (87%). Neither the size of the \"primary\" tumor, nor the number or size of subcutaneous nodules was of prognostic significance."
    explanation: >-
      In 30 Italian children with stage IV-S neuroblastoma (birth to 11 months,
      11 institutions, 1970-1981), the liver was the most frequent site of
      widespread disease (87%), and subcutaneous nodules were recorded, although
      their number and size did not predict outcome. The abstract does not call
      the nodules skin metastases or say how many children had them, so reading
      them as a presentation of skin metastasis is an inference. A small series
      from before the INSS, covering only children younger than 12 months.
  - reference: PMID:10653863
    reference_title: "Favorable biology and outcome of stage IV-S neuroblastoma with supportive care or minimal therapy: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Five of six deaths were in infants younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis and were due to complications of extensive abdominal involvement with respiratory compromise or disseminated intravascular coagulation."
    explanation: >-
      In this prospective Children's Cancer Group study of 80 infants with stage
      IV-S neuroblastoma, managed with supportive care alone or, when
      symptomatic, low-dose therapy, five of the six deaths were in infants
      younger than 2 months at diagnosis and were due to complications of
      extensive abdominal involvement with respiratory compromise or
      disseminated intravascular coagulation. The cohort had biologically
      favorable disease (MYCN was not amplified in any of the 58 tumors tested),
      so this pattern says nothing about MYCN-amplified disease, and it rests on
      six deaths.
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Eight of nine deaths were in patients younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis ... five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly and associated toxicities; two were a result of late relapse in patients with unfavorable biology; and two were a result of treatment complications. No deaths occurred after protocol-mandated pre-emptive treatment of infants younger than 2 months with hepatomegaly, regardless of symptoms."
    explanation: >-
      COG ANBL0531 enrolled a selected higher-risk subset of 49 infants with
      INSS stage 4S neuroblastoma: MYCN-non-amplified tumors with symptoms or
      impending organ dysfunction, or with unfavorable histology and/or a
      diploid DNA index. Eight of the nine deaths were in infants younger than 2
      months at diagnosis. Five were acute deaths from hepatomegaly and
      associated toxicities, two followed late relapse in infants with
      unfavorable tumor biology, and two followed treatment complications. The
      last sentence concerns infants enrolled after a protocol amendment; the
      next item gives the full-text figures. These results describe this
      selected cohort, not 4S as a whole, and the ellipsis stands for a
      bracketed age range.
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the protocol was amended to mandate immediate chemotherapy for patients with 4S disease younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis with evolving hepatomegaly. No deaths related to complications of hepatomegaly occurred in the subsequent 31 4S infants enrolled, including 18 who were younger than 2 months of age"
    explanation: >-
      After five deaths from hepatomegaly in the first 21 months of accrual,
      ANBL0531 was amended to require immediate chemotherapy for infants with 4S
      disease younger than 2 months at diagnosis with evolving hepatomegaly. No
      deaths from complications of hepatomegaly occurred among the 31 infants
      enrolled afterwards, 18 of them younger than 2 months. The full text
      limits the abstract's "no deaths" to deaths from hepatomegaly. This is a
      before-and-after comparison within one nonrandomized trial, with small
      numbers.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The outcome was excellent for our INRG MS cohort (EFS and OS: 85.8% +/- 2.5% and 92.1% +/- 1.9%) with the exception of those with MYCN-A tumors (EFS and OS: 59.9% +/- 17.0% and 64.3% +/- 15.7%), the only subgroup previously classified as HR"
    explanation: >-
      In the COG ANBL00B1 cohort (patients enrolled 2007-2017 and staged by
      INRGSS), the stage MS group as a whole had 5-year event-free and overall
      survival of 85.8% and 92.1%, which the authors call excellent. The
      exception was MS with MYCN-amplified tumors, at 59.9% and 64.3%, the only
      MS subgroup classified high risk under the earlier COG classifier. The
      MYCN-amplified estimates carry wide standard errors, so the subgroup is
      small.
  - reference: PMID:32932540
    reference_title: "Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: What Are the Outcomes? A Systematic Review of Published Studies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Twelve studies (544 patients) recorded MYCN status. Mortality in MYCN amplified tumors was 56%."
    explanation: >-
      Systematic review of 37 published stage 4S series (1,105 patients). In the
      12 studies (544 patients) that recorded MYCN status, mortality among
      patients with MYCN-amplified tumors was 56%. The abstract does not give
      the number of MYCN-amplified patients or say which staging definition each
      series used, and the pooled patients were managed in different ways.
  - reference: PMID:21969516
    reference_title: "Prognostic value of the stage 4S metastatic pattern and tumor biology in patients with metastatic neuroblastoma diagnosed between birth and 18 months of age."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "EFS was significantly better for infants younger than 12 months with 4S pattern than with stage 4 disease (P < .01) but similar for toddlers age 12 to 18 months with stage 4 versus 4S pattern. Among 717 patients with stage 4S pattern, patients age 12 to 18 months had worse EFS than those age younger than 12 months (P < .01). ... Tumor biology is more critical than age or metastatic pattern for prognosis of patients age younger than 18 months with metastatic neuroblastoma and should be considered for risk stratification. ... We divided the patients with stage 4 disease age 12 to 18 months into two groups--those with (n = 61) and without (n = 304) 4S pattern of metastasis--independent of size of primary tumor or extent of bone marrow involvement."
    explanation: >-
      Analysis of the INRG database (cooperative-group trials, 1990-2002) of 656
      INSS stage 4S infants younger than 12 months and 1,019 stage 4 patients
      younger than 18 months. Among the 717 patients with a 4S metastatic
      pattern, those aged 12 to 18 months had worse event-free survival than
      those younger than 12 months, and toddlers fared similarly whether their
      metastases followed the 4S or the stage 4 pattern. The authors conclude
      that tumor biology is more critical than age or metastatic pattern. The
      methods sentence shows that toddlers were grouped by metastatic pattern
      regardless of primary tumor size or the extent of bone marrow involvement,
      so the toddler group was not held to the marrow limit of stage MS. The
      first ellipsis skips the sentences naming individual prognostic factors.
  - reference: PMID:22305511
    reference_title: "Is the prognosis of stage 4s neuroblastoma in patients 12 months of age and older really excellent?"
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the children 12 months of age and older, stage 4s cases are markedly different from stage 4 cases in regard to the clinical features and prognosis. The prognosis of stage 4s cases from >= 12 to <= 17months of age is excellent. The concept of stage MS appears to be appropriate."
    explanation: >-
      Conclusion of a retrospective review of 3,834 patients registered with two
      Japanese pediatric oncology and surgery societies between 1980 and 1998:
      in children 12 months and older, stage 4s cases differed markedly from
      stage 4 cases, prognosis at 12 to 17 months was excellent, and the authors
      judge the stage MS concept appropriate. The abstract does not say how many
      4s patients aged 12 to 17 months the conclusion rests on, and the cases
      were not staged with the INRGSS.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The number of patients with \"stage 4S disease aged 12 to 18 months\" is small, but because the outcome in this patient cohort remains unclear, it is anticipated that the individual cooperative groups will give these patients special attention in prospective studies where careful stopping rules are included."
    explanation: >-
      In the discussion where the INRG Task Force extends the age limit of stage
      MS beyond the 12 months of INSS stage 4S, it states that the number of
      patients aged 12 to 18 months with otherwise classical 4S disease is small
      and that their outcome remains unclear, and it asks the cooperative groups
      to study them prospectively. This is the Task Force's judgement of
      evidence it did not itself produce, not a cohort result.
pathophysiology:
- name: LIN28B Overexpression
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    LIN28B, an RNA-binding protein normally restricted to fetal tissue, is
    overexpressed in high-risk neuroblastoma. It binds the terminal loop of
    primary and precursor let-7 transcripts and blocks their maturation, so
    less mature let-7 is produced. This is one of three routes into let-7
    depletion rather than the only one: in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell
    lines LIN28B can be removed without loss of MYCN protein or cell growth
    even though let-7 is de-repressed, which the same study reads as LIN28B
    serving a redundant let-7-suppressive role where the MYCN transcript is
    abundant.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LIN28B
    term:
      id: hgnc:32207
      label: LIN28B
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: primary miRNA binding
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0070878
      label: primary miRNA binding
  - preferred_term: pre-miRNA binding
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0070883
      label: pre-miRNA binding
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: negative regulation of miRNA processing
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:1903799
      label: negative regulation of miRNA processing
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest derived neuroblast
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23042116
    reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
      suppression.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "LIN28B showed genomic aberrations and extensive overexpression in high-risk neuroblastoma compared to several other tumor entities and normal tissues"
    explanation: >-
      The abstract reports, as the study's own finding, that LIN28B is
      extensively overexpressed in high-risk neuroblastoma compared with
      several other tumour entities and with normal tissues, which states the
      claim directly. The abstract does not name the comparator tumour types,
      the normal tissues or the cohort sizes, and several other tumor entities
      is a limited panel rather than tumours in general, so the comparison
      should not be read as against all cancers. The genomic aberrations
      reported in the same clause are a separate finding and are not curated
      on this node.
  - reference: PMID:40779030
    reference_title: Regulation and dysregulation of microRNA - transcription factor
      axes in differentiation and neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "LIN28B binds to the terminal loop of pri- and pre-let-7 and blocks let-7 maturation"
    explanation: >-
      The review states the claim directly: LIN28B binds the terminal loop of
      primary and precursor let-7 transcripts and blocks let-7 maturation.
      This sentence is the review's summary of let-7 biogenesis biochemistry
      rather than its own experiment, and it sits in the full text rather than
      the abstract, so it is graded IN_VITRO for the kind of work it describes
      and REVIEW_SYNTHESIS for where it sits. The terminal-loop and pre-let-7
      detail comes from work on the paralog LIN28A, so stating it of LIN28B is
      the review's own extension. It grounds the two molecular-function
      bindings on this node. The item below reports the LIN28B-pri-let-7
      association itself, so GO:0070878 does not rest on the extension alone;
      the pre-let-7 half of GO:0070883 still does.
  - reference: PMID:37991019
    reference_title: "N6-methyladenosine-mediated overexpression of long noncoding RNA ADAMTS9-AS2 triggers neuroblastoma differentiation via regulating LIN28B/let-7/MYCN signaling."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Additional mechanistic studies illustrated that the interactions between ADAMTS9-AS2 and LIN28B inhibited the association between LIN28B and primary let-7 (pri-let-7) miRNA, then released pri-let-7 into cytoplasm to form mature let-7, resulting in the inhibition of oncogene MYCN activity that subsequently affected cancer stemness and differentiation."
    explanation: >-
      A LIN28B-specific observation of the binding this node's primary miRNA
      binding term records, made in neuroblastoma cell lines: the sentence
      names an association between LIN28B and pri-let-7 that a competing
      interaction inhibits, which releases pri-let-7 for maturation. Graded
      INDIRECT because the association is reported through its disruption
      rather than measured directly, and because the quoted readout runs on to
      MYCN activity and differentiation. It says nothing about pre-let-7, so it
      grounds GO:0070878 and not GO:0070883.
  - reference: PMID:27383785
    reference_title: Multiple mechanisms disrupt the let-7 microRNA family in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "LIN28B is dispensable in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell lines, despite de-repression of let-7"
    explanation: >-
      The paper's summary of its own siRNA and Cas9 experiments in
      MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma lines: removing LIN28B does lift the brake
      on let-7, yet MYCN protein levels and cell proliferation are unaffected.
      Graded INDIRECT because the sentence carries the dispensability
      observation, while the conclusion that LIN28B is therefore one route
      among several rests on the MYCN-sponging result this sentence does not
      state. The finding is confined to cultured MYCN-amplified lines, and the
      same paper reports LIN28B suppressing let-7 and conferring a growth
      advantage in non-amplified cells; the study's shRNA arm gave the opposite
      result, which the authors attribute to hairpin toxicity. The item
      constrains when the LIN28B route is operative rather than establishing
      the node.
  downstream:
  - target: let-7 Depletion
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      LIN28B blockade of let-7 maturation is the route by which this node
      lowers mature let-7. The measurement behind the edge is in neuroblastoma
      cells rather than in patient tumours.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:23042116
      reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
        suppression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "LIN28B signaled through repression of the let-7 miRNAs and consequently resulted in elevated MYCN protein expression in neuroblastoma cells"
      explanation: >-
        States the claim itself: in neuroblastoma cells LIN28B acted through
        repression of the let-7 miRNAs. This is the paper's own cell-based arm,
        in which LIN28B was manipulated in neuroblastoma cell lines, rather
        than its human-cohort or mouse arms, so the evidence is graded in
        vitro. Only the first clause is relied on here; the elevated MYCN
        protein the same sentence reports is the downstream step and is cited
        on the edge from let-7 Depletion to MYCN-Driven Proliferation.
  notes: >-
    LIN28B also has a reported let-7-independent transcriptional function in
    neuroblastoma. It is named here and deliberately not modelled, because its
    downstream targets belong to the cell-state axis curated elsewhere in this
    entry. No lesion is recorded on this node: LIN28B contributes by
    overexpression rather than by a variant, so genetic_context has nothing to
    describe, and marking one would make this the node from which the entry's
    cell of origin is derived.
- name: let-7 Depletion
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    The mature let-7 microRNA family is depleted in neuroblastoma by three
    routes that substitute for one another rather than acting in series:
    LIN28B blockade of let-7 maturation; sponging of let-7 by the MYCN
    transcript, which in MYCN-amplified disease reaches levels high enough to
    titrate the family; and genetic loss of let-7 loci, which is common in
    neuroblastoma, inversely associated with MYCN amplification and
    independently associated with poor outcomes. let-7 represses MYCN
    post-transcriptionally, so depleting it de-represses MYCN and lifts the
    let-7 restraint on neuroblast differentiation. The routes converge on this
    node, which is why an entry whose flagship subtype is MYCN-amplified
    disease cannot model the LIN28B route alone.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: let-7 microRNA-mediated gene silencing
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0035195
      label: miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional gene silencing
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27383785
    reference_title: Multiple mechanisms disrupt the let-7 microRNA family in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "We propose that let-7 disruption by LIN28B, MYCN sponging, or genetic loss is a unifying mechanism of neuroblastoma development"
    explanation: >-
      The paper's closing proposition, quoted with the authors' hedge intact:
      the three routes to let-7 loss are put forward as one unifying mechanism
      of neuroblastoma development rather than as three separate chains, which
      is why this node is curated as the point where several routes converge.
      Graded OTHER because the sentence synthesises the paper's cell-line arm,
      its MYCN-sponging arm and its tumour copy-number and survival arm, so no
      single study-type value is true of it; the component results carry their
      own grades on the items that cite them.
  - reference: PMID:27383785
    reference_title: Multiple mechanisms disrupt the let-7 microRNA family in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We found that genetic loss of let-7 is common in neuroblastoma, inversely associated with MYCN amplification, and independently associated with poor outcomes"
    explanation: >-
      The authors' summary of their copy-number analysis of all eight let-7
      loci across 202 neuroblastomas, stating the three parts of the claim:
      genetic loss of let-7 is common, it is much rarer in MYCN-amplified
      tumours, and it carries outcome information. Independently here means
      independent of MYCN amplification status, since the survival comparison
      is made within MYCN strata; no multivariable model adjusting for stage,
      age or other genomic markers is reported. This is the one of the three
      routes into this node whose evidence is a patient tumour series.
  downstream:
  - target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Mature let-7 represses MYCN post-transcriptionally, so depleting let-7
      de-represses MYCN protein and feeds the proliferative programme the
      receiving node describes. This route is post-transcriptional, so it
      reaches that node without MYCN amplification. The measurement behind the
      edge is in neuroblastoma cells rather than in patient tumours.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:23042116
      reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
        suppression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "LIN28B signaled through repression of the let-7 miRNAs and consequently resulted in elevated MYCN protein expression in neuroblastoma cells"
      explanation: >-
        The paper's own result states that repression of the let-7 miRNAs
        consequently raises MYCN protein, which is the step this edge draws.
        Graded INDIRECT because the quote establishes the MYCN protein rise
        only: it measures no proliferation, so reaching the proliferative
        programme the receiving node describes takes one inference step. The
        measurement is in neuroblastoma cell lines; the same paper's mouse and
        human-tumour findings are separate sentences carried by separate
        evidence items.
  - target: Neural Crest Developmental Arrest
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    description: >-
      Loss of the let-7 restraint blocks differentiation of normal neuroblasts
      and of neuroblastoma cells, reaching from the microRNA axis the same
      arrest the receiving node describes. The differentiation block is
      reported for the whole LIN28B-let-7-MYCN axis rather than for the let-7
      step alone, and releasing mature let-7 in neuroblastoma cells inhibits
      MYCN activity and shifts the cells toward differentiation, which is the
      same link read in the restoring direction.
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "De-repression of MYCN protein following loss of post-transcriptional let-7 repression"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:23042116
      reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
        suppression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "LIN28B-let-7-MYCN signaling blocked differentiation of normal neuroblasts and neuroblastoma cells"
      explanation: >-
        States the differentiation block in the two cell populations the edge
        is about, normal neuroblasts and neuroblastoma cells. It attributes the
        block to the whole LIN28B-let-7-MYCN axis rather than to the let-7 step
        alone, so this edge carries the let-7 leg of that axis and should not
        be read as an observation independent of the MYCN step named as its
        intermediate. Graded IN_VITRO because the sentence names cell
        populations with no in vivo marker; the paper's mouse arm is reported
        separately as tumour development with low let-7 and high MYCN protein,
        not as a differentiation measurement.
    - reference: PMID:37991019
      reference_title: "N6-methyladenosine-mediated overexpression of long noncoding RNA ADAMTS9-AS2 triggers neuroblastoma differentiation via regulating LIN28B/let-7/MYCN signaling."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Additional mechanistic studies illustrated that the interactions between ADAMTS9-AS2 and LIN28B inhibited the association between LIN28B and primary let-7 (pri-let-7) miRNA, then released pri-let-7 into cytoplasm to form mature let-7, resulting in the inhibition of oncogene MYCN activity that subsequently affected cancer stemness and differentiation."
      explanation: >-
        Runs the same chain in the restoring direction: freeing pri-let-7 from
        LIN28B so that mature let-7 forms inhibits MYCN activity and moves the
        cells toward differentiation. The curated edge is let-7 depletion, so
        the support arrives by inversion, and the quoted readout is cancer
        stemness and differentiation rather than neural crest arrest
        specifically, which is why the item is graded INDIRECT. The sentence is
        the paper's account of its own mechanistic arm in neuroblastoma cell
        lines; the study's patient-sample sequencing and its xenograft arm are
        reported in separate sentences. ADAMTS9-AS2 is the tool used to release
        let-7 and is not a mechanism this entry models.
  notes: >-
    The genetic-loss route is named in this node's description and its loci are
    deliberately not bound: the arm-level copy-number evidence for let-7 locus
    loss belongs with the Segmental Chromosomal Aberrations genetic record and
    is left to the curation that owns it. No cell_types are bound here either,
    because the three routes are not all demonstrated in one compartment and
    the node is a molecular state rather than a cellular one.

    This node sits in a cycle with MYCN-Driven Proliferation, which both
    depletes let-7 by sponging and is de-repressed by that depletion. The cycle
    is the biology rather than a modelling artefact, and the pathograph has no
    acyclicity assumption.
- name: Neural Crest Developmental Arrest
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma arises from neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor
    cells that fail to complete differentiation. The tumor cells retain
    characteristics of immature neuroblasts with variable capacity for
    sympathetic neuronal differentiation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastoma (NB) is a pediatric solid tumor originating from neural
      crest cells (NCCs), which are precursors of the sympathetic nervous system."
    explanation: >-
      States that neuroblastoma originates from neural crest cells, the
      precursors of the sympathetic nervous system, supporting the
      developmental origin this node describes. It is the opening background
      sentence of an iPSC-derived neural crest model study and describes the
      human disease, not an observation from that model.
  - reference: PMID:32296467
    reference_title: "Nervous system: Embryonal tumors: Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Neuroblastoma is a clinically heterogenous pediatric cancer of the
      sympathetic nervous system that originates from neural crest cells.
    explanation: Supports neural crest origin and clinical heterogeneity of
      neuroblastoma.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest derived neuroblast
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: cell differentiation
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0030154
      label: cell differentiation
  locations:
  - preferred_term: adrenal gland
    term:
      id: UBERON:0002369
      label: adrenal gland
  downstream:
  - target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
    description: MYCN amplification drives aggressive proliferation
  - target: Adrenergic and Mesenchymal Cell-State Plasticity
    description: >-
      The arrested neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor is the
      lineage within which the two tumour cell identities are defined. The
      noradrenergic pole carries the committed sympathetic core regulatory
      circuitry, while the mesenchymal (NCC-like) pole sits close to the
      undifferentiated neural crest cell, so the two states map onto
      different points of the same blocked differentiation programme. The
      evidence cited here locates the two identities in that lineage; it
      does not show that the arrest itself drives switching between them.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37142597
      reference_title: "Reversible transitions between noradrenergic and mesenchymal tumor identities define cell plasticity in neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "The master transcriptional regulators controlling the gene expression program of neuroblastoma have been highlighted through the characterization of the super-enhancer landscape of neuroblastoma cell lines, revealing two distinct cell identities: a sympathetic noradrenergic identity defined by a core regulatory circuitry (CRC) module including the PHOX2A/B, HAND1/2 and GATA2/3 transcription factors and a NCC-like/mesenchymal identity, close to that of human neural crest cells (hNCCs), driven by factors of the AP1 family among others"
      explanation: >-
        Restating earlier super-enhancer profiling of neuroblastoma cell
        lines, this introduction defines the noradrenergic identity as
        sympathetic, with a core regulatory circuitry that includes
        PHOX2A/B, HAND1/2 and GATA2/3, and places the NCC-like/mesenchymal
        identity close to that of human neural crest cells. The source's
        list is explicitly open: the next sentence adds ISL1, TBX2 and
        ASCL1 to the noradrenergic circuitry, so this supports circuitry
        membership and not a complete roster. Graded IN_VITRO with
        quote_role BACKGROUND because the quoted sentence describes
        cell-line super-enhancer work performed in earlier studies rather
        than a result of the citing paper. It maps the two identities onto
        the neural crest and sympathetic ends of the lineage; it does not
        itself show that arrested differentiation causes switching between
        them.
  - target: Norepinephrine Transporter (NET/SLC6A2) Expression
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Arrest at an immature noradrenergic sympathoadrenal stage leaves the
      lineage's norepinephrine-uptake machinery in place. The edge is
      retention, not induction: the transporter is inherited from the
      sympathetic neuronal precursor rather than switched on by the arrest,
      and the cited sources state lineage-linked expression rather than any
      inducing step. It is recorded as an edge because the arrested lineage
      state is what accounts for the transporter still being there, which is
      the fact the therapy depends on.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:20424613
      reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "Metaiodobenzylguanidine (mIBG) is a guanethidine derivative and an analogue of norepinephrine and is therefore specifically taken up and stored in tumours derived from tissues of sympathetic nervous system origin, which express the norepinephrine transporter"
      explanation: >-
        Ties transporter expression to the tissue of origin rather than to any
        acquired event, which is what this edge asserts. Graded OTHER with
        quote_role REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the sentence is an INRG Task Force
        statement of established uptake biology and reports no measurement of
        its own. Full-text introduction sentence, quoted up to the
        parenthetical citation list.
- name: Norepinephrine Transporter (NET/SLC6A2) Expression
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma arises from sympathoadrenal and sympathetic neuronal
    precursors, and the tumor retains those precursors' norepinephrine
    transporter (NET, encoded by SLC6A2), a transmembrane protein that carries
    norepinephrine into the cell. That retained transporter is the route by
    which both the 123I-MIBG diagnostic tracer and therapeutic 131I-MIBG enter
    the tumor cell, with vesicular retention through VMAT once inside. The node
    claims only that the transporter is expressed and is what MIBG uses; the
    uptake and expression measurements themselves are curated on the
    MIBG-Avid Disease row of imaging_findings, and are not restated here.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SLC6A2
    term:
      id: hgnc:11048
      label: SLC6A2
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: norepinephrine:sodium symporter activity
    term:
      id: GO:0005334
      label: norepinephrine:sodium symporter activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: norepinephrine uptake
    term:
      id: GO:0051620
      label: norepinephrine uptake
  notes: >-
    No modifier is set on either descriptor. NET expression here is a lineage
    trait the tumor retains from its sympathoadrenal precursor, not a process
    running above its normal level or outside normal regulatory constraint, and
    the repository's INCREASED versus GAIN_OF_FUNCTION rule requires a
    quantitative or qualitative claim the cited sources do not make; one series
    reported an MIBG-avid tumor with no NET-expressing cells at all. There is
    no GO term for MIBG transport itself: OLS GO searches on 2026-10-22 for
    "metaiodobenzylguanidine", "iobenguane" and "MIBG" each returned nothing,
    so the bindings are to the physiological activity (GO:0005334) and process
    (GO:0051620). GO:0015874 must not be bound here: it is obsolete, and its
    label is literally "obsolete norepinephrine transport", so a cache grep
    alone looks like a hit.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25175627
    reference_title: "Nothing but NET: a review of norepinephrine transporter expression and efficacy of 131I-mIBG therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastoma is unique amongst common pediatric cancers for its expression of the norepinephrine transporter (NET), enabling tumor-selective imaging and therapy with radioactive analogues of norepinephrine."
    explanation: >-
      The node's whole claim in one sentence: neuroblastoma expresses NET, and
      that expression is what makes tumor-selective imaging and therapy with
      radiolabelled norepinephrine analogues possible. The authors' synthesis
      of earlier patient-level work rather than a new measurement, hence
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS. Note that expression makes therapy possible without
      predicting response: the same abstract records that most tumors are
      MIBG-avid while only about 30% respond. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:25175627
    reference_title: "Nothing but NET: a review of norepinephrine transporter expression and efficacy of 131I-mIBG therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Neuroblastoma and other cancers of sympathetic neuronal precursors express the norepinephrine transporter (NET), a transmembrane protein which functions to shuttle norepinephrine across the cell membrane."
    explanation: >-
      Names the molecular function bound on this node: a transmembrane protein
      that shuttles norepinephrine across the cell membrane. Graded OTHER
      rather than HUMAN_CLINICAL because the clause relied on is an uncited
      definitional statement in a narrative review's introduction and reports
      no patient data; the sodium coupling in the GO term's label comes from
      the term definition, not from this sentence. Full-text introduction
      sentence.
- name: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
  description: >-
    MYCN amplification results in massive overexpression of the MYCN
    transcription factor, a key contributor to aggressive neuroblastoma biology
    and poor prognosis. MYCN-amplified tumors have a distinct aggressive
    phenotype with rapid growth and early metastasis.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0003700
      label: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: cell population proliferation
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0008283
      label: cell population proliferation
  downstream:
  - target: T-Cell-Poor Tumor Microenvironment
    description: >-
      Amplified MYCN tracks a T-cell-poor microenvironment. In primary
      tumours from patients with metastatic disease a T-cell-poor
      microenvironment was associated with genomic MYCN amplification,
      and in a separate patient series high-risk MYCN-not-amplified
      tumours carried significantly higher cytotoxic
      tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte signatures than MYCN-amplified
      tumours. The route recorded here runs through suppressed
      interferon and pro-inflammatory signalling and the chemokine
      output that recruits T cells: in human and murine neuroblastoma
      cell lines N-Myc suppresses interferon and pro-inflammatory
      pathways, and N-Myc depletion amplified the interferon response to
      a cGAS-STING agonist, which in turn raised chemokine expression
      including Cxcl10 and drew T cells in a microfluidics migration
      assay. The limits sit on both halves. The patient half is an
      association in cross-sectional cohorts and does not establish
      direction, and the second series contrasts MYCN-not-amplified
      against MYCN-amplified tumours, so the direction is read off that
      contrast rather than measured within tumours over time. The
      intermediates are cell-line and microfluidics results; the
      cGAS-STING agonist used is specific for mouse and not human STING,
      so that arm was run in murine lines, and nothing in the model half
      was measured in patient tumours.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "N-Myc suppression of interferon and pro-inflammatory pathway activity"
    - "Reduced chemokine expression, including CXCL10, and reduced cytotoxic T-cell recruitment"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:28680756
      reference_title: Amplification of N-Myc is associated with a T-cell-poor microenvironment
        in metastatic neuroblastoma restraining interferon pathway activity and chemokine
        expression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Here, we report that a T-cell-poor microenvironment in primary metastatic neuroblastomas is associated with genomic amplification of the MYCN (N-Myc) proto-oncogene."
      explanation: >-
        Result from this study's patient tumour cohort: using an
        integrative transcriptomic approach on primary neuroblastomas, a
        T-cell-poor microenvironment in primary metastatic tumours was
        associated with genomic MYCN amplification. T-cell content was
        estimated from the averaged expression of a T-cell gene
        signature in bulk tumour RNA rather than counted in tissue
        sections, and the comparison was made in the INSS stage 4
        subgroup (65 MYCN-amplified against 116 non-amplified tumours,
        from a 498-tumour cohort whose stage 4 subgroup numbered 181);
        these are primary tumours of metastatic-stage disease rather
        than metastatic deposits. Support for the edge is indirect: the
        sentence reports that the two features occur together in
        tumours, and reading the edge's direction, from amplified MYCN
        to T-cell exclusion, into that co-occurrence is an inference the
        sentence does not make. The evidence for that direction comes
        from the same study's cell-line experiments, cited separately on
        this edge. The same paper also notes a contrasting
        immunohistochemical study of 84 neuroblastomas that found no
        significant association between T-cell infiltration and MYCN
        amplification status, so the association is to some degree
        method-dependent.
    - reference: PMID:29784674
      reference_title: Clinically Relevant Cytotoxic Immune Cell Signatures and Clonal
        Expansion of T-Cell Receptors in High-Risk MYCN-Not-Amplified Human Neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "We found that MYCN-not-amplified (MYCN-NA) tumors had significantly higher cytotoxic TIL signatures compared with MYCN-amplified (MYCN-A) tumors."
      explanation: >-
        Result from a second patient study, stated in its abstract. Deep
        RNA sequencing was run on pretreatment diagnostic tumours from
        129 high-risk and 21 low- or intermediate-risk patients
        consented at Children's Oncology Group institutions, with
        validation against expression profiles of 190 additional
        pretreatment diagnostic neuroblastomas, CD8 immunohistochemistry
        on an 80-tumour tissue microarray and T-cell-receptor
        sequencing. The comparison behind this sentence was made within
        high-risk disease: high-risk MYCN-not-amplified tumours had
        significantly higher activated natural killer cell, CD8-positive
        T cell and cytolytic scores than MYCN-amplified tumours, and
        stage 4S tumours, which are also MYCN-not-amplified, scored low
        as well, so the result does not extend to MYCN-not-amplified
        tumours as a whole. Neither cohort is new to this question: the
        authors note that others had already analysed these TARGET data,
        and the 190 validation tumours were downloaded from the Gene
        Expression Omnibus entry GSE49711, which is the series analysed
        by Layer and colleagues (PMID:28680756) and cited on this same
        edge. The signatures are inferred from bulk tumour RNA, and the
        sentence is stated from the non-amplified side, so the lower
        cytotoxic infiltrate in MYCN-amplified tumours is read off the
        contrast. Graded INDIRECT because this is an association with
        amplification status and does not show that MYCN causes the low
        cytotoxic infiltrate.
    - reference: PMID:28680756
      reference_title: Amplification of N-Myc is associated with a T-cell-poor microenvironment
        in metastatic neuroblastoma restraining interferon pathway activity and chemokine
        expression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Importantly, we identified a global role for N-Myc in the suppression of interferon and pro-inflammatory pathways in human and murine neuroblastoma cell lines."
      explanation: >-
        The study's own finding rather than borrowed framing, and the
        first named intermediate of this edge. Two independent MYCN
        siRNAs induced the interferon-response gene OAS1 in the
        MYCN-amplified human lines SKNBE and NMB with no cytokine added,
        and gene set enrichment analysis over the knockdown
        transcriptome of the murine mNB-A1 line placed
        interferon-response hallmark sets among those upregulated on
        N-Myc loss, which is what stands behind the word global. The
        same depletion then enhanced the CXCL9 and CXCL10 transcription
        induced by interferon gamma and TNF-alpha, so the
        interferon-response effect is seen in unstimulated cells while
        most of the pro-inflammatory chemokine effect is an enhanced
        response to stimulation. Every experiment behind the sentence is
        in cultured human or mouse cells, which this repository
        classifies as IN_VITRO rather than MODEL_ORGANISM, and none of
        it shows the step operating in patient tumours. Graded INDIRECT
        because the sentence asserts the intermediate, N-Myc holding
        interferon and pro-inflammatory signalling down, with the edge's
        endpoint following only by inference; that the intermediate is
        named and demonstrated is what the INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
        typing on this edge records.
    - reference: PMID:28680756
      reference_title: Amplification of N-Myc is associated with a T-cell-poor microenvironment
        in metastatic neuroblastoma restraining interferon pathway activity and chemokine
        expression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "N-Myc depletion potently enhanced targeted interferon pathway activation by a small molecule agonist of the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway. This promoted chemokine expression including Cxcl10 and T-cell recruitment in microfluidics migration assays."
      explanation: >-
        Grounds the second named intermediate of this edge, chemokine
        expression and T-cell recruitment; the two abstract sentences
        are quoted contiguously so the pronoun opening the second keeps
        its antecedent. Four limits bound what they establish. The
        interferon pathway activation was produced by a small-molecule
        cGAS-STING agonist applied on top of N-Myc depletion, so the
        readout belongs to that combination and not to N-Myc depletion
        alone. The agonist, DMXAA, is described by the authors as
        specific for mouse but not human STING, so this arm was run in
        murine neuroblastoma cell lines and the chemokine accordingly
        carries the murine capitalisation of the source. Recruitment was
        measured as directed migration of mouse OT-I T cells in a
        microfluidics gradient chamber rather than as infiltration of a
        tumour. And the second sentence places raised chemokine
        expression and raised recruitment side by side as consequences
        of the enhanced interferon response, so that Cxcl10 itself
        mediated the migration is the authors' reading of the
        conditioned-supernatant experiment rather than something this
        quote demonstrates. Graded IN_VITRO because every measurement is
        in cultured cells or an ex vivo migration device, and INDIRECT
        because the claim about human MYCN-amplified tumours follows
        only through an inference step from a loss-of-function
        experiment in mouse cells.
  - target: Telomerase Activation
    description: >-
      Amplified MYCN raises TERT transcription, which makes MYCN amplification a
      route to telomerase activation rather than a separate telomere maintenance
      mechanism. TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours, and in a
      MYCN-amplified cell line TERT was the gene most strongly downregulated
      when MYCN was knocked down. Not every MYCN-amplified tumour takes this
      route: some express TERT as low as ALT tumours do, and forced MYCN
      overexpression did not induce TERT where the promoter was repressed.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Increased TERT transcription driven by amplified MYCN"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "In addition, TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours than in the remaining samples (P = 0.021, Fig. 2d)."
      explanation: >-
        Result from this study's series of patient tumours: TERT expression was
        higher in MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas than in tumours carrying neither
        MYCN amplification nor a TERT rearrangement (P = 0.021). Support for
        MYCN driving telomerase activation is indirect. The sentence reports
        that MYCN amplification and higher TERT RNA levels occur together in
        tumours, so it shows neither that MYCN causes the rise nor that
        telomerase enzyme activity increases; the paper measured that activity
        only in cell lines.
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Thus, genomic rearrangements at 5p15.33 abrogate silencing of gene expression in this chromosomal region, whereas amplified MYCN selectively upregulates TERT by transcriptional activation."
      explanation: >-
        The authors' conclusion from their tumour expression data:
        MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas upregulated TERT and one neighbouring
        AceView-annotated gene (bleyplaby) but not SLC6A18 or SLC6A19, which
        TERT-rearranged tumours also upregulated, and TERT was among the most
        highly upregulated genes in 92 MYCN-amplified versus 238 low-risk
        tumours. So amplified MYCN raises TERT selectively, whereas
        rearrangements lift silencing more broadly across the region.
        Limitation: the paper does not measure MYCN binding at TERT, so
        'transcriptional activation' is inferred from expression data and
        earlier work it cites, and the sentence concerns TERT expression, not
        telomerase activity.
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "TERT was the most strongly downregulated gene upon short-interfering-RNA-mediated MYCN knockdown in a MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell line"
      explanation: >-
        Transcriptome sequencing of a cultured MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma line
        (IMR-5/75) before and after MYCN knockdown made TERT the most strongly
        downregulated gene of all, so TERT expression in an amplified background
        depends on MYCN rather than the reverse. That direction is what the
        tumour expression comparisons reported elsewhere in the same study
        cannot establish on their own. The limitation is scope: a single
        cultured cell line, with TERT transcript level as the readout rather
        than enzymatic telomerase activity.
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Surprisingly, some MYCN-Amp tumors had TERT expression as low as seen in ALT tumors"
      explanation: >-
        Bears against this edge holding in every MYCN-amplified tumour. In this
        high-risk cohort some MYCN-amplified tumours expressed TERT as low as
        ALT tumours do, so the edge's intermediate, increased TERT transcription
        in an amplified background, is not reached in every MYCN-amplified
        tumour. It qualifies the edge's universality rather than the route's
        existence: most MYCN-amplified tumours in the same comparison had high
        TERT expression.
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "MYCN overexpression by itself is not sufficient to overcome the TERT repression in TERT non-expressing cells"
      explanation: >-
        Forced MYCN overexpression in neuroblastoma cell lines without MYCN
        amplification raised TERT expression only where the TERT promoter was
        intact and not repressed, so the authors conclude that MYCN cannot by
        itself overcome TERT repression. This bears against the edge holding in
        every tumour. Indirect for this edge: overexpression in non-amplified
        cell lines is not the amplified state the edge describes, and the
        readout is TERT expression rather than telomerase activity.
  - target: Compensatory Polyamine Uptake from the Microenvironment
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      MYCN regulates SLC3A2, the transporter that carries polyamine uptake in
      neuroblastoma, alongside other components of the polyamine pathway, so
      amplified MYCN raises the import route as well as the synthesis route.
      As with the synthesis edge below, no return edge is drawn from the uptake
      node into this one, to avoid a two-node cycle in the pathograph.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30700572
      reference_title: "Inhibition of polyamine synthesis and uptake reduces tumor progression and prolongs survival in mouse models of neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "In addition, MYCN directly increased polyamine synthesis and promoted neuroblastoma cell proliferation by regulating SLC3A2 and other regulatory components of the polyamine pathway."
      explanation: >-
        The paper's own result placing SLC3A2 under MYCN control, which is what
        puts the uptake node downstream of this one rather than beside it.
        Cell-line evidence: the sentence reports regulation in neuroblastoma
        cells and does not quantify how much of the transporter's expression
        MYCN accounts for in patient tumours.
  - target: Polyamine Biosynthesis Dependence
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      ODC1, the rate-limiting enzyme of polyamine synthesis, is a direct
      transcriptional target of MYCN, so amplified MYCN raises flux through the
      pathway. The dependence runs the other way as well, which is what makes
      the pathway a target rather than only a consequence, but that return
      relation is recorded in the downstream node's description rather than as
      a second edge, because an edge back into this node would make a
      two-node cycle in the pathograph.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33918978
      reference_title: A G316A Polymorphism in the Ornithine Decarboxylase Gene Promoter Modulates MYCN-Driven Childhood Neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "MYCN was a stronger transcriptional regulator of the ODC1 promoter containing the G allele, and preferentially bound the G allele over the A."
      explanation: >-
        Direct evidence that MYCN acts on the ODC1 promoter, from reporter and
        binding assays on the two alleles of a promoter polymorphism. The
        allele-specific framing is incidental here: what this edge takes from
        it is that MYCN transactivates ODC1 at all.
  - target: let-7 Depletion
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      In MYCN-amplified tumours the MYCN transcript is itself abundant enough
      to act as a competing endogenous RNA for let-7, which is why deleting
      LIN28B from amplified cell lines leaves MYCN protein and growth intact.
      This is the least established of the three routes into let-7 depletion:
      the authors raise the stoichiometric question themselves, whether a rise
      of more than 100-fold in MYCN mRNA, which lifts the total pool of let-7
      target sites by only about a quarter, suffices for a competing-endogenous-RNA
      effect, and answer it with their own 3-prime-UTR-loss reporter and
      let-7-target mRNA sequencing. The quantification is in MYCN-amplified
      neuroblastoma cell lines.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:27383785
      reference_title: Multiple mechanisms disrupt the let-7 microRNA family in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "We further demonstrate that MYCN messenger RNA levels in amplified disease are exceptionally high and sufficient to sponge let-7, which reconciles the dispensability of LIN28B"
      explanation: >-
        The paper's own statement of the sponging route and of what it
        explains: MYCN messenger RNA in amplified disease is high enough to
        sponge let-7, which is why LIN28B is dispensable in those lines. The
        measurements behind it are in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell lines
        rather than in patient tumours, and sufficient to sponge is the
        authors' reading of their reporter and mRNA-sequencing data rather than
        a direct measurement of titration in a tumour.
  - target: LIN28B Overexpression
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Amplified MYCN also raises LIN28B itself, closing a loop with the let-7
      node: MYCN binds the LIN28B promoter directly in a neuroblastoma line
      carrying inducible MYCN, and acts in parallel through miR-26a-5p. This
      edge records the transcriptional arm only and makes no claim about which
      arm dominates in a given tumour.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26123663
      reference_title: MYCN-driven regulatory mechanisms controlling LIN28B in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "we provide evidence that MYCN regulates LIN28B expression via interaction with the LIN28B promoter, establishing a direct MYCN-LIN28B regulatory axis"
      explanation: >-
        The paper's own statement of the direct route: MYCN acts on LIN28B
        through the LIN28B promoter. The sentence says regulates rather than
        increases, so the direction of effect is taken from the edge
        description rather than from this quote. The promoter evidence behind
        it is MYCN chromatin immunoprecipitation in a neuroblastoma line
        carrying doxycycline-inducible MYCN, so the binding claim rests on one
        engineered cell line rather than on primary tumours, and the paper
        presents this as one of two parallel routes alongside indirect
        regulation through miR-26a-5p.
  - target: Replication-Stress Checkpoint Dependence
    description: >-
      N-Myc is what puts the replication checkpoint under load, so the
      dependence on CHK1 and WEE1 follows the oncogene rather than sitting
      beside it. Two results in one study carry the link: CHK1 inhibitor
      sensitivity tracked total MYC(N) protein, and inducing MYCN in
      untransformed retinal pigment epithelial cells was by itself enough to
      phosphorylate CHK1. The second is the causal half, and it is
      deliberately run outside neuroblastoma, because isolating what MYCN
      alone does requires a cell that does not already carry the
      amplification. That is also what keeps it a model rather than a
      measurement in the disease, which is why the edge is graded indirect.
      What this edge leaves out is the replication stress itself, the step
      between the oncogene and the checkpoint it activates.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Replication stress generated by MYCN-driven proliferation, which is not measured in this experiment"
    - "Phosphorylation of CHK1, reported at Ser345 and Ser296 in high-risk primary tumours on the target node"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:21289283
      reference_title: "RNAi screen of the protein kinome identifies checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "CHK1 inhibitor sensitivity correlated with total MYC(N) protein levels, and inducing MYCN in retinal pigmented epithelial cells resulted in CHK1 phosphorylation, which caused growth inhibition when inhibited."
      explanation: >-
        The correlation gives the association in neuroblastoma cells, and the
        induction experiment gives the direction: forcing MYCN in a cell that
        is not a neuroblastoma cell switches the checkpoint on, which is the
        step from co-occurrence to cause. Indirect for this edge because that
        causal half is in retinal pigment epithelial cells, so the direction
        is established in a model system and the edge asserts it of the
        disease. The same sentence is cited on the target node for the same
        reason, and carries the same IN_VITRO grade there.

Loss of MYCN leads to a global reduction in transcription, which is most pronounced at MYCN target genes with the greatest enhancer occupancy."
    explanation: >-
      Supports the molecular function bound on this node. ChIP-seq in

      at promoters and enhancers, and switching MYCN off in an engineered
      tet-off neuroblastoma line lowers transcription, most at the target genes

  - reference: PMID:31365300

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A positive correlation between MYCN gene amplification and protein expression by IHC was seen in 22 (91.66%) of the 24 MYCN-amplified NB cases ... Two cases had weak protein expression but no gene amplification (MED: n = 1; 5.0%; NAD: n = 1; 2.9%). ... An excellent overall correlation between MYCN gene status by FISH and MYCN protein expression by IHC was confirmed."
    explanation: >-
      In a pilot cohort of 78 patient neuroblastomas, nuclear MYCN protein was
      detected by immunohistochemistry in 22 of the 24 MYCN-amplified tumors,
      and only two non-amplified tumors stained, weakly. MYCN protein therefore

- name: Aurora A-Mediated N-Myc Protein Stabilization
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  mechanism_confidence: ESTABLISHED
  description: >-
    N-Myc protein is short-lived: degradation requires sequential
    phosphorylation by cyclin B/Cdk1 and GSK3, after which the SCF(Fbxw7)
    ubiquitin ligase ubiquitinates it for proteasomal destruction. Aurora A
    binds both N-Myc and that ligase and counteracts the degradation, which
    uncouples N-Myc abundance from the growth-factor signalling that would
    otherwise set it. The stabilising action does not need Aurora A's kinase
    activity: it is a protein-protein interaction, and inhibitors that merely
    block the catalytic site lower N-Myc only modestly, whereas compounds that
    distort the kinase's native conformation drive N-Myc degradation. An shRNA
    screen found AURKA required for the growth of MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma
    cells and largely dispensable without amplification, which is what makes
    the interaction a dependency rather than an incidental one. What does not
    follow is the therapeutic corollary: in the clinic, alisertib has done
    worse in MYCN-amplified disease than in non-amplified disease, the opposite
    of what this mechanism predicts. That tension is recorded as a
    human-model mismatch discussion rather than smoothed over here.

    modifier: INCREASED
    term:

      label: AURKA
  - preferred_term: FBXW7
    term:

      label: FBXW7

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Aurora A interacts with both N-Myc and the SCF(Fbxw7) ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitinates N-Myc and counteracts degradation of N-Myc, thereby uncoupling N-Myc stability from growth factor-dependent signals."
    explanation: >-
      The node's whole claim in one sentence, and the source of both its
      molecular-function binding (Aurora A interacting with the SCF ligase
      complex) and its two process bindings (stabilization up, proteasomal
      degradation down). Cell-line work; the sentence states the interaction
      and its consequence, not how much of the N-Myc pool it governs in a

    reference_title: "Stabilization of N-Myc is a critical function of Aurora A in human neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT

    evidence_source: IN_VITRO

      The route Aurora A counteracts, which is what makes the stabilization a

    supports: SUPPORT

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "In a shRNA screen of genes that are highly expressed in MYCN-amplified tumors, we have identified AURKA as a gene that is required for the growth of MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cells but largely dispensable for cells lacking amplified MYCN."
    explanation: >-
      Why the interaction is a dependency: knocking AURKA down stops growth in

    reference_title: "Drugging MYCN through an allosteric transition in Aurora kinase A."
    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:25175806

    explanation: >-

  downstream:

    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      By holding N-Myc protein above what growth-factor signalling would

      running. The dependency runs the other way as well, since amplified
      tumours are the ones that need AURKA, but no return edge is drawn, to

      explanation: >-

        than in one cell line. Cell and xenograft work.
- name: Extrachromosomal MYCN Amplicon Architecture
  description: >-
    In MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma the supernumerary MYCN copies are commonly
    carried on extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA), which can be highly
    rearranged. The extrachromosomal form is the common state and not the only
    one: the same paper reports a MYCN amplicon carried as a linear
    intrachromosomal array, a homogeneously staining region. Amplicon
    composition is not random. Across a copy-number meta-dataset of 240
    MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, a 290 kb region downstream of MYCN was
    co-amplified in more than 90% of tumours, and the distal MYCN-specific
    enhancer e4, driven by the noradrenergic core regulatory circuit (CRC),
    lay inside the consensus amplicon in 90% of cases. Two amplicon classes
    follow. The first always co-amplifies a proximal CRC-driven enhancer; the
    second is structurally complex, lacks the key local enhancers and instead
    carries distal chromosomal fragments harbouring CRC-driven enhancers,
    which the authors read as ectopic enhancer hijacking replacing the missing
    local elements. That classification was made on primary-tumour copy-number
    profiles, which cannot separate extrachromosomal from intrachromosomal
    amplicons, so it applies to both forms. The two classes were
    prognostically indistinguishable in the same series, so amplicon class
    sets the regulatory route to MYCN overexpression rather than clinical
    behaviour. Separately, rearrangements derived from extrachromosomal
    circles can give rise to cancer-causing lesions and are associated with
    adverse clinical outcome; that association belongs to the circle-derived
    rearrangements and not to amplicon class.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  cellular_components:
  - preferred_term: extrachromosomal circular DNA
    term:
      id: GO:0005727
      label: extrachromosomal circular DNA
  downstream:

    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
