    description: >-
      The two amplicon classes are what account for the regulatory
      requirements of MYCN overexpression, so the amplicon's architecture sits
      upstream of MYCN protein dosage and thereby of MYCN-driven
      proliferation. The architecture sets the regulatory route rather than
      gating the outcome: class II amplicons lacking the key local enhancers
      nevertheless expressed relatively high MYCN per gene copy, which is what
      the authors mean by ectopic enhancer hijacking compensating for the loss
      of local elements. Neither cited sentence reaches proliferation, so MYCN
      overexpression is named as the intermediate.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33199677
      reference_title: "Enhancer hijacking determines extrachromosomal circular MYCN amplicon architecture in neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "This reveals two distinct classes of amplicons which explain the regulatory requirements for MYCN overexpression."
      explanation: >-
        The authors' own summary of their result: resolving the MYCN amplicon
        into two structural classes is what accounts for how MYCN
        overexpression is regulated, which places the amplicon's architecture
        upstream of MYCN dosage. Class I retains the local CRC-driven enhancer
        e4; class II lacks it and instead carries hijacked distal CRC-driven
        enhancers. Graded IN_VITRO because the regulatory half of this
        sentence, that the co-amplified enhancers are active and contact the
        MYCN promoter, rests on ATAC-seq, H3K4me1 and H3K27ac ChIP-seq, 4C and
        nanopore de novo assembly in neuroblastoma cell lines (Kelly, NGP,
        IMR-5/75, CHP-212); the two-class boundary definition itself comes
        from primary-tumour copy-number profiles and is cited separately on
        this edge as human tumour evidence. An important qualification the
        source supplies: class II amplicons lacking the key local enhancers
        nevertheless expressed relatively high levels of MYCN per gene copy,
        so architecture sets the regulatory route by which MYCN overexpression
        is reached rather than gating whether it is reached. Graded INDIRECT
        because the sentence stops at the regulatory requirement for MYCN
        overexpression and the paper measures no proliferation endpoint, so

      reference_title: "Enhancer hijacking determines extrachromosomal circular MYCN amplicon architecture in neuroblastoma."

      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Co-amplification frequency quickly dropped downstream of e4, suggesting that MYCN-specific, CRC-driven enhancers are a determinant of MYCN amplicon structure and may be required for MYCN expression, even in the context of high-level amplification."
      explanation: >-
        The tumour-level half of this edge, one layer closer to the data.

        sentence's leading direction runs the other way, from enhancers to
        amplicon structure, with the MYCN-expression requirement as the
        subordinate clause, and the authors state that clause as a suggestion.
        Graded INDIRECT because the inference stops at MYCN expression rather
        than proliferation.
  - target: ecDNA Oncogene Dosage Heterogeneity
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-
      Because ecDNA segregates asymmetrically at mitosis, carrying the
      amplicon extrachromosomally rather than in a chromosomal array is what
      produces variation in oncogene dosage between cells of the same tumour.
      The cited sentence is the general statement of that property of ecDNA
      rather than a measurement in neuroblastoma; the measurements sit on the
      downstream node.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40773595
      reference_title: "Extrachromosomal DNA-Driven Oncogene Dosage Heterogeneity Promotes Rapid Adaptation to Therapy in MYCN-Amplified Cancers."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) amplification enhances intercellular oncogene dosage variability and accelerates tumor evolution by violating foundational principles of genetic inheritance through its asymmetric mitotic segregation."
      explanation: >-
        States the step this edge asserts directly: extrachromosomal
        amplification raises cell-to-cell variability in oncogene dosage,
        through asymmetric segregation of ecDNA at mitosis. Graded BACKGROUND
        because it is the paper's opening framing of a general property of
        ecDNA that it attributes to earlier work, rather than a measurement
        reported here, and IN_VITRO because the segregation and
        dosage-variability biology the sentence describes is observed in
        dividing cultured cancer cells. The sentence is about ecDNA in
        general; this paper's own measurements centre on MYCN ecDNA in
        neuroblastoma, with further work in MYC-amplified colon cancer,
        mesothelioma and gastric lines.

    snippet: "The supernumerary gene copies are commonly found on highly rearranged, extrachromosomal circular DNA (ecDNA)."
    explanation: >-
      The abstract states that the supernumerary gene copies are commonly
      found on highly rearranged, extrachromosomal circular DNA. The copies
      meant are the amplified MYCN copies named in the preceding sentence. The
      source's word is 'commonly', not 'always', so it does not support a
      statement that every MYCN amplicon is extrachromosomal: the paper's

      study's starting point rather than reporting its own measurement, and

    explanation: >-
      Carries the first amplicon class. 'Always' is the source's own word and
      is definitional for this class rather than a measured rate: class I is
      defined by co-amplification of the local MYCN-specific CRC-driven
      enhancer e4, which fell inside the consensus amplicon region in 90% of
      cases in a published copy-number meta-dataset of 240 MYCN-amplified
      neuroblastomas re-analysed here (class I N = 216, class II N = 24), with
      e4 co-amplification enriched above randomised amplicon boundaries
      (empirical P = 0.0003). It therefore does not carry over to MYCN
      amplicons generally, around a tenth of which do not retain e4. The
      co-amplification is the primary-tumour observation; that the enhancer is
      driven by the noradrenergic core regulatory circuit was established
      separately in this paper by H3K27ac and PHOX2B/HAND2/GATA3 ChIP-seq in
      neuroblastoma cell lines. The sentence says nothing about whether the
      amplicon is extrachromosomal, and the array-based copy-number data
      behind the classification cannot separate extrachromosomal from
      intrachromosomal amplicons.
  - reference: PMID:33199677
    reference_title: "Enhancer hijacking determines extrachromosomal circular MYCN amplicon architecture in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The second class of MYCN amplicons is characterized by high structural complexity, lacks key local enhancers, and instead contains distal chromosomal fragments harboring CRC-driven enhancers."
    explanation: >-
      Carries the second amplicon class in the source's own terms. In the same
      240-tumour copy-number meta-dataset, primary neuroblastomas with class
      II amplicons more often harboured more than one amplified fragment
      (66.7% versus 35.7%, Fisher's exact test P = 0.003; class II 36.0%
      versus class I 11.6% after restricting to fragments whose copy number
      closely matched MYCN), and all but one of the 24 class II amplicons
      co-amplified at least one CRC-driven enhancer element distal of MYCN.
      The cohort evidence is co-amplification rather than demonstrated
      physical fusion, which the authors note the largely array-based data
      cannot establish; the chimeric structure itself was reconstructed in two
      cell lines by long-read de novo assembly and Hi-C, one of them a linear
      homogeneously staining region rather than circular DNA. So this
      two-class split is a property of MYCN amplicons generally, not of
      extrachromosomal ones specifically.
  - reference: PMID:33199677
    reference_title: "Enhancer hijacking determines extrachromosomal circular MYCN amplicon architecture in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In contrast, differences in the MYCN amplicon enhancer structure, i.e. class I vs. class II amplification, did not confer prognostic differences"
    explanation: >-
      The tested null, and the reason the two amplicon classes carry no
      prognostic reading on this node. In a Kaplan-Meier comparison of 236 of
      the 240 MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, class I and class II amplicons
      did not differ significantly in survival, hazard ratio 1.3 (0.78 to
      2.1), two-sided log-rank P = 0.34, and the authors conclude that
      enhancer hijacking in class II amplicons does not change clinical
      behaviour, fully phenocopying class I. Recorded here so that the
      adverse-outcome association also cited on this node, which belongs to
      circle-derived rearrangements, is not read as a claim about amplicon
      class. Two limits: with 24 class II amplicons in the series this is an
      absence of a detected difference rather than demonstrated equivalence,
      and the cached figure legend names the analysis only as Kaplan-Meier
      survival analysis without stating whether the endpoint is overall or
      event-free survival.
  - reference: PMID:31844324
    reference_title: "Extrachromosomal circular DNA drives oncogenic genome remodeling in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Cancer-causing lesions can emerge out of circle-derived rearrangements and are associated with adverse clinical outcome."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract conclusion of a study combining whole-genome sequencing of 93
      neuroblastomas paired with normal blood specimens, circular-DNA
      sequencing and RNA sequencing with clinical follow-up: lesions arising
      from rearrangement of extrachromosomal circular DNA can be
      cancer-causing, and they are associated with adverse clinical outcome.
      Two limits on how far it reaches. The sentence attaches the outcome
      association to the lesions rather than to the rearrangements themselves,
      although the paper's results report the association for the presence of
      circle-derived rearrangements as well. And the rearrangements concerned
      arise from extrachromosomal circles across the genome rather than from
      the MYCN amplicon alone, so the claim it supports here is the general
      one.
  - reference: PMID:31844324
    reference_title: "Extrachromosomal circular DNA drives oncogenic genome remodeling in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In line with our hypothesis, patients with MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas and circle-derived rearrangement clusters involving MYCN had significantly worse overall survival compared to patients with MYCN-amplified tumors lacking such rearrangements"
    explanation: >-
      The MYCN-specific form of the outcome association, and the one that
      bears on this node: among patients whose tumours were MYCN-amplified,
      those also carrying circle-derived rearrangement clusters involving MYCN
      had significantly worse overall survival than those without them.
      Because both arms are MYCN-amplified, the association is not a
      restatement of MYCN amplification status, and the paper reports
      separately that the number of rearrangements in MYCN-amplified tumours
      did not correlate with survival, so the signal tracks the circle-derived
      pattern rather than rearrangement burden. Graded INDIRECT because it
      supports the general claim by generalisation from this subgroup rather
      than asserting it, and because it bears on outcome only, not on whether
      the lesions are cancer-causing. The comparison is a univariable survival
      analysis within one cohort.
- name: ecDNA Oncogene Dosage Heterogeneity
  description: >-
    MYCN copy number on ecDNA varies greatly from cell to cell, whereas copy
    number in cells carrying a linear homogeneously staining region appeared
    more evenly distributed, and in near-isogenic cell lines higher ecDNA copy
    number tracks greater colony-forming output. The second arm of the same
    biology runs the other way. ecDNA that is damaged and mis-segregated into
    a micronucleus is a constraint rather than a driver: the daughter cell
    inheriting an ecDNA-positive micronucleus divides later and dies more
    often, and a higher frequency of ecDNA-positive micronuclei in the
    diagnostic biopsy is associated with longer survival in MYCN-amplified
    neuroblastoma. The node is provisional because the measurements are
    recent, the clinical association rests on a single cohort with no
    independent replication, and the two arms point in opposite directions, so
    what the net effect of dosage heterogeneity on tumour behaviour is remains
    open.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40773595
    reference_title: "Extrachromosomal DNA-Driven Oncogene Dosage Heterogeneity Promotes Rapid Adaptation to Therapy in MYCN-Amplified Cancers."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Quantification of MYCN copy numbers by either the Find Maxima function in Fiji (ImageJ) or the corrected total cell fluorescence (CTCF) intensity score indicated that ecDNA copy number varied greatly from cell to cell, whereas copy numbers from cells with linear HSR amplifications appeared more evenly distributed"
    explanation: >-
      The study's own per-cell fluorescence in situ hybridization
      quantification of MYCN copy number, by two independent scoring methods,
      and it states the claim itself: copy number varied greatly between
      individual cells where MYCN sat on ecDNA, whereas cells carrying a
      linear homogeneously staining region appeared more evenly distributed.
      The source hedges the HSR half as 'appeared', which the claim keeps.
      Copy number was analysed within the MYCN-amplified samples (95 of 191)
      of a panel spanning primary and relapsed neuroblastomas, patient-derived
      xenografts and cell lines. Because one sentence pools all three sample
      types it cannot be split by source; HUMAN_CLINICAL is assigned because
      primary patient tumours are part of the quantified set, and the
      xenograft and cell-line components are recorded here rather than being
      graded separately.
  - reference: PMID:40773595
    reference_title: "Extrachromosomal DNA-Driven Oncogene Dosage Heterogeneity Promotes Rapid Adaptation to Therapy in MYCN-Amplified Cancers."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Indeed, ecDNA copy numbers were significantly higher in large (>=15 and 10-15) colony-forming cells than in smaller colony-forming cells (2-5, 6-9) or single cells"
    explanation: >-
      The paper's clonogenic experiment, and the measurement that makes the
      copy-number spread phenotypically consequential rather than merely
      genetic: cells were seeded at low density, grown for four days, and the
      oncogene copy number of colony-forming cells scored by fluorescence in
      situ hybridization, with ecDNA copy number significantly higher in the
      cells that formed large colonies (10-15 and 15 or more cells) than in
      those forming small colonies (2-5, 6-9 cells) or remaining single. The
      sentence establishes a difference between the large and the small size
      bins rather than a monotonic trend across every bin, and the size
      categories are small absolute cell numbers from a four-day assay, so the
      claim concerns clonogenic output and not tumour growth. The panel pooled
      near-isogenic neuroblastoma and colon cancer lines carrying either MYC
      or MYCN on ecDNA or on an HSR, so the result is a general property of
      extrachromosomal oncogene amplification rather than a
      neuroblastoma-exclusive one.
  - reference: PMID:42864499
    reference_title: "Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Cells inheriting ecDNA+ MNs display impaired proliferative capacity and are more likely to undergo cell death."
    explanation: >-
      Gives the cell-level arm of the claim: a daughter cell that inherits an
      ecDNA-bearing micronucleus reaches its next division later and dies more
      often than the sister cell that inherited none, so mis-segregation of
      the amplicon is a fitness penalty rather than only a dosage fluctuation.
      The underlying measurement is narrower than the sentence: micronuclei
      were enriched by hydroxyurea exposure before live-cell imaging, so the
      penalty is measured under induced replication stress; the comparison is
      between daughter and sister cells; and the delay and excess death were
      quantified for large ecDNA-containing micronuclei over 2 micrometres in
      diameter, being strongest where micronuclear ecDNA content was high
      while independent of copy number in the primary nucleus. Graded IN_VITRO
      because the readout is live-cell imaging of cultured cells, and INDIRECT
      for this entry because that imaging used a MYC-ecDNA colon cancer line
      rather than a MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma line, although the paper does
      use MYCN-ecDNA neuroblastoma lines for its micronucleus-formation and
      mis-segregation measurements. The route the authors propose is loss of
      oncogenic transcription after micronucleation, and they state that the
      exact mechanism by which micronuclei affect cancer cell fate remains to
      be determined.
  - reference: PMID:42864499
    reference_title: "Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In patients with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma, higher frequencies of ecDNA+ MNs at diagnosis are associated with improved overall survival."
    explanation: >-
      States the clinical arm of the claim: the more ecDNA-positive
      micronuclei a pre-treatment diagnostic biopsy carries, the longer
      overall survival. The analysis is the paper's own, over 86 children with
      MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma in whom ecDNA was identified by
      fluorescence in situ hybridization before treatment, selected from 387
      diagnostic biopsies screened and registered across three German national
      neuroblastoma trials and a registry, with median follow-up of 6.8 years.
      Read it with its effect size, which is real but modest: modelled as a
      continuous variable the frequency carried an overall-survival hazard
      ratio of 0.951 (95% CI 0.914 to 0.990, P = 0.015), stated by the authors
      as a 4.9% reduction in risk of death per 1% increase. The measure is
      specific rather than generic, because neither total ecDNA copy number in
      the primary nucleus nor overall micronucleus frequency correlated with
      survival in the same cohort. The paper reports only that a Cox
      regression was run on the ecDNA-positive micronucleus percentage and
      names no covariate set, so no adjustment for established risk factors is
      documented, and there is no independent replication cohort.
- name: c-MYC Activation by Enhancer Hijacking or Enhancer Amplification
  description: >-
    In a distinct subset of high-risk neuroblastoma, about 10% of cases when
    the subset is defined by high MYC expression, the MYC paralogue rather
    than MYCN is the driver. Activating mechanisms identified in some of these
    tumours are focal amplification of distal enhancers lying downstream of
    the MYC coding sequence, and translocation that brings a highly active
    enhancer from another locus into a topologically associating domain
    containing MYC. The subset is defined by expression rather than by lesion:
    MYC and MYCN expression are reciprocal across the cohort, some high-MYC
    tumours carry no detectable enhancer lesion, and of the primary tumours
    that do carry one only part rank in the high-expression group. Patients
    with high MYC expression had unfavourable outcomes that did not differ
    significantly from those of patients with MYCN-amplified tumours, which
    the authors describe as virtually identical.

  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MYC
    term:
      id: hgnc:7553
      label: MYC
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0003700
      label: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: MYC gene expression
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0010467
      label: gene expression
  notes: >-
    No regulatory_category is set. The cited sources report upregulation of
    MYC in tumour cells that already express the gene, which is not sufficient
    to record a gain-of-expression category for the regulatory lesion. What
    was measured is messenger RNA abundance, recorded here as INCREASED gene
    expression; the INCREASED modifier on DNA-binding transcription factor
    activity is inferred from that same expression evidence rather than from
    an activity measurement, and is kept because it is what grounds MYC as a
    transcription factor on this node. No biological-process term is bound for
    the amplification event itself: a GO search for 'gene amplification'
    returns GO:0006277 DNA amplification, defined as the process in which the
    number of copies of a gene is increased in certain cells as extra copies
    of DNA are made in response to certain signals of cell development or of
    stress from the environment, which is programmed developmental or
    stress-responsive amplification rather than somatic oncogene amplicon
    formation, and GO:0007307 eggshell chorion gene amplification, a
    developmental process in another lineage. This node carries no downstream
    edge, and that is deliberate rather than unfinished. The cited work
    connects MYC activation to clinical outcome and to a MYCN-non-amplified
    line's requirement for c-MYC, but not to any mechanism node this entry
    already holds; routing it into 'MYCN-Driven Proliferation' would assert a
    MYCN-driven mechanism, and the reciprocal-expression evidence on this node
    shows the MYC-high subset to be MYCN-non-amplified with low MYCN
    expression. No proliferation node is curated for this subset either,
    because no proliferation measurement for it has been published. The only
    index reported in these tumours is the mitosis-karyorrhexis index, and the
    cited series separates its two components, attributing the lower index in
    MYC-protein-positive tumours to karyorrhexis rather than to mitosis and
    reading that as a difference in apoptotic rather than proliferative
    pathways; neither Ki-67 nor MIB-1 appears anywhere in that paper. The
    proliferative advantage attributed to c-MYC is a zebrafish result, and the
    cell-line work measures a requirement for c-MYC rather than a rate of
    division. That gap is recorded as the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion
    nb_myc_high_subset_proliferation_model_mismatch rather than as a mechanism
    node.

  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."

    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we demonstrate that MYC is also activated as a potent oncogene in a distinct subset of neuroblastoma cases through either focal amplification of distal enhancers or enhancer hijacking mediated by chromosomal translocation."
    explanation: >-
      The paper's own summary of its main finding, and the mechanistic half of
      this claim: in a distinct subset of neuroblastoma, MYC is activated
      either by focal amplification of distal enhancers or by enhancer
      hijacking through chromosomal translocation. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL
      because the lesions were identified in patient tumours: among 74
      whole-genome-sequenced primary tumours of the TARGET cohort, two carried
      translocations with breakpoints downstream of MYC and two carried focal

      the evaluable samples. Two limits. That the translocated super-enhancers

      MYC-high tumours carrying no detectable enhancer lesion, so these two
      mechanisms account for part of the MYC-driven subset rather than all of
      it. The sentence's 'potent oncogene' wording also rests in part on the
      paper's transgenic zebrafish arm, which is cited separately on this
      node.
  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we show that the family member MYC is a potent transforming gene in a separate subset of high-risk neuroblastoma cases (~10%)"
    explanation: >-
      Gives the size of the MYC-driven subset as around 10% of high-risk
      neuroblastoma, from whole-transcriptome sequencing of 123 disseminated
      primary tumours in the TARGET cohort, hence HUMAN_CLINICAL. The figure
      is the paper's own subgroup definition rather than a separate
      measurement: its 12 'c-MYC high' cases were chosen on the basis of c-MYC
      expression levels in the highest 10%, a cut-off taken from an earlier
      immunohistochemistry study of c-MYC protein expression, cited separately
      on this node, which found 38 of 357 undifferentiated or poorly
      differentiated neuroblastomas MYC-positive, 11%. This paper's
      introduction restates that 11% for neuroblastomas without the histology
      restriction, and the two figures do not independently corroborate each
      other. Read it as the proportion in this series rather than a population
      frequency, and note that it describes the high-expression subgroup
      rather than the proportion carrying a detected enhancer lesion, which
      the paper puts at five percent of its genome-sequenced tumours. Of the
      123 tumours, 112 had whole-genome or whole-exome data. The quote stops
      before the sentence's stated grounds, the second of which is the
      transgenic zebrafish result cited separately on this node.
  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Whereas MYCN-amplified tumors expressed high levels of this gene but low levels of MYC, a subset of stage 4 tumors with non-amplified MYCN genes exhibited the opposite pattern (Fig. 1A)."
    explanation: >-
      Grounds the elevated level behind the INCREASED modifier bound on this
      node. In whole-transcriptome sequencing of 123 disseminated TARGET
      neuroblastomas, MYCN and MYC expression were reciprocal: MYCN-amplified
      tumours expressed MYCN highly and MYC at low levels, while a subset of
      MYCN-non-amplified stage 4 tumours showed the opposite, with high MYC.
      So the subset this node describes is defined by raised MYC in patient
      tumours rather than by amplification of MYC itself. The measurement is
      messenger RNA, so a matching rise in DNA-binding transcription factor
      activity is an inference from expression rather than a direct activity
      measurement, and the comparison is within-cohort rather than against
      non-malignant tissue.
  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

    snippet: "The clinical outcome for patients with high levels of MYC expression is virtually identical to that of patients with amplification of the MYCN gene, a known high-risk feature of this disease."
    explanation: >-
      The authors' summary of their own survival comparison in the TARGET
      cohort of disseminated neuroblastomas. The c-MYC-high group was the 12
      patients whose MYCN-non-amplified tumours came from the top 10% of c-MYC
      expression; one further top-10% tumour was MYCN-amplified and was
      counted with the amplified group. Outcomes in the two groups did not
      differ significantly by log-rank test, with no adjustment for other risk

      non-significant difference in a small group rather than a demonstrated
      equivalence, and it covers disseminated disease only. The group was
      defined by expression level rather than by mechanism: the paper reports
      that some c-MYC-high tumours had no detectable enhancer hijacking or
      focal enhancer amplification, and of the four primary tumours carrying
      such a lesion only two ranked in the top 10% of c-MYC expression. The
      item therefore concerns the prognosis of high MYC expression, not of
      enhancer-activated cases in particular.

      The MYC dependence this node's notes refer to, now cited rather than only

  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "Although our results in Figure 2 establish that c-MYC can induce highly penetrant neuroblastoma in the zebrafish"
    explanation: >-
      Carries the transforming half of the claim, which the human items on
      this node do not: expressing c-MYC in the developing peripheral
      sympathetic nervous system of transgenic zebrafish, under a
      dopamine-beta-hydroxylase promoter, induced neuroblastoma with high
      penetrance. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM because the result is in fish, and
      INDIRECT because transformation by a transgene in zebrafish supports the
      oncogenic potency of MYC in human neuroblastoma by inference rather than
      asserting it of the human tumours. The authors state that they used the
      zebrafish because transgenic mouse models testing whether c-MYC can
      initiate neuroblastoma had not yet been described. The quoted clause is
      the concessive opening of a sentence whose point is the opposite
      direction of travel: the human c-MYC locus is generally not amplified in
      neuroblastoma, which is what led them to look for enhancer lesions
      instead.
- name: Polyamine Biosynthesis Dependence
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma cells raise flux through polyamine biosynthesis, with ODC1 as
    the rate-limiting enzyme and a direct transcriptional target of MYCN.
    Transcriptome analysis of MYCN-amplified tumors shows the whole pathway
    deregulated rather than ODC1 alone, and high-risk tumors without MYCN
    amplification overexpress ODC1 as well, so the dependence is not confined
    to the amplified subset. Elevated ODC1 tracks reduced survival
    independently of MYCN status in two patient cohorts. The node is marked
    PROVISIONAL because the step from this pathway to the clinical effect of
    the approved drug is not established: at the approved low dose, polyamine
    depletion has not been shown to be the operative mechanism, and sensitivity
    to the inhibitor does not track MYCN or ODC1 copy number. See the
    Eflornithine treatment record for that evidence.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ODC1

  - reference: PMID:19047152

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:19047152

- name: Compensatory Polyamine Uptake from the Microenvironment
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma cells import polyamines from the surrounding microenvironment,
    which is the reason blocking synthesis does not deplete them. Treating
    neuroblastoma cells with the ODC1 inhibitor eflornithine (DFMO) is only
    partially effective against cell growth, because compensatory mechanisms
    raise polyamine uptake; in culture, polyamines taken from the medium rescue
    the deficit the drug creates. SLC3A2 was identified as the key transporter
    carrying that uptake in neuroblastoma, knocking it down lowered uptake of
    radiolabelled spermidine, and DFMO treatment itself raised SLC3A2 protein,
    so the drug induces the route around its own target. Blocking uptake with
    AMXT 1501 alongside DFMO prevented or delayed tumour development in
    neuroblastoma-prone mice and extended survival in rodent models of
    established tumours, and in a second laboratory the same combination
    deepened the inhibition of protein synthesis even in cell lines resistant
    to high-dose DFMO alone. Marked PROVISIONAL because every result here is
    from cell lines or rodent models: nothing establishes that uptake limits
    the approved drug's effect in patients. The synthesis arm is the Polyamine
    Biosynthesis Dependence node, and what the approval does and does not
    settle is in the Eflornithine treatment record.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: SLC3A2
    term:
      id: hgnc:11026
      label: SLC3A2
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: polyamine transmembrane transporter activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0015203
      label: polyamine transmembrane transporter activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: polyamine import from the extracellular microenvironment
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0140202
      label: polyamine import across plasma membrane
  notes: >-
    The molecular function is bound from the cited neuroblastoma work, not from
    SLC3A2's own GO annotations: on 2026-10-23 a QuickGO annotation search for
    UniProtKB:P08195 returned 11 molecular-function terms, amino-acid
    transmembrane transporter activities and protein-binding terms, and no
    polyamine or spermidine term in any aspect. The binding therefore records
    the activity this node asserts is running, on the strength of SLC3A2 being
    identified as the transporter that carries polyamine uptake in these cells,
    and should not be read as a curated GO annotation of the gene.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30700572
    reference_title: "Inhibition of polyamine synthesis and uptake reduces tumor progression and prolongs survival in mouse models of neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Treatment of neuroblastoma cells with the ODC1 inhibitor difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), although a promising therapeutic strategy, is only partially effective at impeding neuroblastoma cell growth due to activation of compensatory mechanisms resulting in increased polyamine uptake from the surrounding microenvironment."
    explanation: >-
      The escape itself, and the reason this node exists: inhibiting the
      rate-limiting synthetic enzyme only partly impedes growth, because
      compensatory mechanisms raise uptake from the microenvironment. Graded
      BACKGROUND because the sentence sets up the study rather than reporting
      its result, and IN_VITRO because the growth it describes is
      neuroblastoma cells in culture.
  - reference: PMID:30700572
    reference_title: "Inhibition of polyamine synthesis and uptake reduces tumor progression and prolongs survival in mouse models of neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "In this study, we identified solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2) as the key transporter involved in polyamine uptake in neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The source for naming SLC3A2 on this node. It is the paper's own
      identification in neuroblastoma, and it is what the molecular-function
      binding rests on rather than a GO annotation of the gene, as the note
      above records.
  - reference: PMID:30700572
    reference_title: "Inhibition of polyamine synthesis and uptake reduces tumor progression and prolongs survival in mouse models of neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Knockdown of SLC3A2 in neuroblastoma cells reduced the uptake of the radiolabeled polyamine spermidine, and DFMO treatment increased SLC3A2 protein."
    explanation: >-
      Two results in one sentence, and between them the node's whole claim:
      removing SLC3A2 lowers polyamine uptake, so the transporter carries it;
      and the ODC1 inhibitor raises SLC3A2 protein, so the drug induces the
      route that bypasses it. The uptake readout is radiolabelled spermidine, a
      single polyamine, and the induction is measured as protein level rather
      than as transport rate.
  - reference: PMID:30700572
    reference_title: "Inhibition of polyamine synthesis and uptake reduces tumor progression and prolongs survival in mouse models of neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "Inhibiting polyamine uptake with the small-molecule drug AMXT 1501, in combination with DFMO, prevented or delayed tumor development in neuroblastoma-prone mice and extended survival in rodent models of established tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The in vivo counter-move: blocking uptake alongside the synthesis
      inhibitor delayed or prevented tumours in predisposed mice and extended
      survival once tumours were established. Indirect for this node, because
      it is a therapeutic result cited as validation of the mechanism it
      targets rather than a measurement of uptake, and because benefit from
      the combination does not by itself fix how much of it came from closing
      the uptake route.
  - reference: PMID:40774224
    reference_title: "High-dose DFMO alters protein translation in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
