    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "DFMO inhibits ODC to block polyamine synthesis but compensatory polyamine uptake from the culture media can rescue this deficit"
    explanation: >-
      Independent corroboration from a different laboratory, reading its own
      translation experiments across five neuroblastoma cell lines: uptake
      from the medium rescues what the drug blocks. The rescue is inferred
      from the drug-combination comparison in those figures rather than from a
      direct uptake measurement in this study.
  - reference: PMID:40774224
    reference_title: "High-dose DFMO alters protein translation in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Co-exposure of cells to DFMO and AMXT-1501 led to enhanced inhibition of protein synthesis even in cell lines that were resistant to high-dose DFMO monotherapy (CHLA20, COG-N-278)."
    explanation: >-
      Closing the uptake route deepened polyamine depletion even where
      high-dose DFMO alone did nothing, which is what makes resistance to the
      synthesis inhibitor an uptake problem rather than only a dosing problem.
      Indirect: protein synthesis stands in for polyamine supply here, and the
      comparison is across cell lines rather than a measured change in uptake.
- name: ALK Signaling Activation
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  conforms_to: "sustaining_proliferative_signaling#Oncogenic Growth-Signal Lesion"
  description: >-
    ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) is activated by point mutations in
    approximately 8-10% of neuroblastomas at diagnosis, and by amplification in
    additional cases. In neuroblastoma cells, high expression of the wild-type
    receptor can also lead to its constitutive activation. Intragenic
    rearrangement of the ALK locus is a third and rare route, found in four of
    332 primary tumours screened, where the receptor is phosphorylated although
    no fusion protein is predicted. ALK mutations are
    enriched in familial neuroblastoma and represent a therapeutic target for
    ALK inhibitors.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ALK
    term:
      id: hgnc:427
      label: ALK
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0004714
      label: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: cell surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0007169
      label: cell surface receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway
  notes: >-
    The node conforms to sustaining_proliferative_signaling#Oncogenic
    Growth-Signal Lesion through ALK's activating point mutations and
    amplification: the module node names activating mutation or
    amplification of a receptor tyrosine kinase as one route to
    growth-signal autonomy and lists ALK among its examples. The module
    node's downstream edge is matched by this node's edge to RAS-MAPK
    Pathway Hyperactivation, which conforms to the module's Constitutive
    Mitogenic Pathway Activation and binds the pathway's process terms
    (GO:0007265 Ras protein signal transduction, GO:0070371 ERK1 and ERK2
    cascade), so this node binds no MAPK cascade term of its own.
    GO:0007169 is the process term the module node binds; an OLS search of
    GO for "anaplastic lymphoma kinase" on 2026-10-27 returned no term, and
    none of the 75 descendants OLS lists for GO:0007169 is specific to ALK.
    The patient-tissue evidence here is of two kinds, and they are not
    interchangeable. Phosphorylated ALK measured by immunohistochemistry in
    the primary tumours carrying an intragenic rearrangement is a measurement
    of the activated receptor, but only in that rare subset. ALK staining
    across a series not selected by ALK status reports receptor level rather
    than phosphorylation, and bears on activation only through the cell-line
    finding cited here that the wild-type receptor needs a high expression
    threshold before it is constitutively phosphorylated. That staining series
    concludes that ALK positivity by immunohistochemistry is an independent
    poor prognostic factor in neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma, and its
    own background notes that earlier evidence on that question had been
    inconclusive. Prognosis is not modelled on this mechanism node, so no
    prognostic claim is made here in either direction.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations, including mutations and amplification, activate oncogenic signaling pathways that, together with MYCN amplification, further enhance tumor malignancy."
    explanation: >-
      States that ALK alterations (mutations and amplification) activate
      oncogenic signaling that co-operates with MYCN amplification in
      neuroblastoma malignancy. Like the two sentences before it in this
      abstract, it is background describing the human disease, summarizing
      earlier work rather than reporting a result of the study's iPSC-derived
      model.
  - reference: PMID:18724359
    reference_title: "Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Mutations resulted in constitutive phosphorylation, and targeted knockdown of ALK messenger RNA resulted in profound inhibition of growth in all cell lines harbouring mutant or amplified ALK"
    explanation: >-
      Demonstrates that ALK mutations cause constitutive receptor
      phosphorylation and that ALK-altered neuroblastoma cells are dependent
      on ALK for growth, supporting the causal edge into proliferation.
  - reference: PMID:25517749
    reference_title: "ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We describe comprehensive genomic, biochemical, and computational analyses of ALK mutations across 1,596 diagnostic neuroblastoma samples. ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations occurred in 8% of samples--at three hot spots and 13 minor sites--and correlated significantly with poorer survival in high- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations in 8% of 1,596 diagnostic
      neuroblastoma samples, the lower end of the approximately 8-10% figure.
      The count is of tumors carrying a mutation, so on its own it does not
      separate somatic from germline events. The same abstract distinguishes
      oncogenic (constitutively activating) from nononcogenic mutations, so for
      activation the 8% is an upper bound.
  - reference: PMID:26059187
    reference_title: "Deep Sequencing Reveals Occurrence of Subclonal ALK Mutations in Neuroblastoma at Diagnosis."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In this series, deep sequencing allows the detection of F1174 and R1275 ALK mutational events at diagnosis in 10% of cases, with subclonal events in more than half of these, which would have gone undetected by Sanger sequencing."
    explanation: >-
      The upper end of the approximately 8-10% figure: targeted deep
      sequencing of the F1174 and R1275 hotspots found ALK mutations in 10% of
      cases at diagnosis. More than half were subclonal and would have been
      missed by Sanger sequencing, so part of the gap above the 8% estimate
      reflects detection sensitivity.
  - reference: PMID:19723661
    reference_title: "Mutation-independent anaplastic lymphoma kinase overexpression in poor prognosis neuroblastoma patients."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a receptor tyrosine kinase predominantly expressed in the developing nervous system."
    explanation: >-
      The opening background sentence of a primary neuroblastoma study states
      that ALK is a receptor tyrosine kinase, the molecular identity behind
      binding transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity on this
      node. It restates established knowledge rather than reporting the study's
      own results, and it does not by itself show that the activity is raised in
      neuroblastoma.
  - reference: PMID:18923524
    reference_title: "Oncogenic mutations of ALK kinase in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "The mutated kinases were autophosphorylated and displayed increased kinase activity compared with the wild-type kinase."
    explanation: >-
      The ALK kinase-domain mutants identified in neuroblastoma were
      autophosphorylated and had higher kinase activity than wild-type ALK,
      which gives both the direction and the wild-type comparator behind the
      INCREASED modifier. It is a laboratory measurement on mutant versus
      wild-type kinase, graded IN_VITRO although the same abstract also reports
      sequencing of primary tumors, and it describes the activating mutations
      this study tested.
  - reference: PMID:19723661
    reference_title: "Mutation-independent anaplastic lymphoma kinase overexpression in poor prognosis neuroblastoma patients."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "ALK constitutive phosphorylation/activation was observed in high-ALK expressing cells, harboring either a mutated or a wild-type receptor. No activation was found in cell lines with low expression of wild-type ALK."
    explanation: >-
      In neuroblastoma-derived cell lines, ALK was constitutively phosphorylated
      in cells expressing the receptor at a high level, whether mutated or
      wild-type, and not in lines expressing wild-type ALK at a low level.
      Receptor activation is therefore not confined to mutation; for the
      wild-type receptor it depends on its level of expression. This item
      supports the description's sentence on the highly expressed wild-type
      receptor, not activation by amplification. Cell-line measurement.
  - reference: PMID:18990089
    reference_title: "High incidence of DNA mutations and gene amplifications of the ALK gene in advanced sporadic neuroblastoma tumours."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ALK amplification or in-gene re-arrangements were found in 5% of NB tumours"
    explanation: >-
      In sporadic primary neuroblastomas, ALK amplification or in-gene
      rearrangement was found in 5% of tumors, which supports the description's
      statement that amplification activates ALK in additional cases. The 5%
      covers amplification and rearrangement together, and the abstract does not
      say whether these tumors also carried a point mutation. Indirect: the
      study shows that these alterations occur, not that the amplified receptor
      is phosphorylated, so activation is an inference from it.
  - reference: PMID:25251827
    reference_title: "Intragenic anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements: translocations as a novel mechanism of ALK activation in neuroblastoma tumors."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "None of the translocations characterized in primary NB tumors are likely to result in a chimeric protein. However, immunohistochemical analysis reveals high levels of phosphorylated ALK in these samples despite lack of initial exons, possibly due to alternative transcription initiation sites."
    explanation: >-
      Immunohistochemistry for phosphorylated ALK in primary neuroblastoma
      tumours, which measures the activated receptor in patient tissue rather
      than counting tumours that carry a lesion. Scope: 332 primary tumours
      were screened and breakpoints at the ALK locus were found in four, so
      the measurement is on that small subset, and the study calls the
      mechanism novel but rare. The first sentence is kept inside the quote
      because it is the finding's own control: no chimeric fusion protein is
      predicted from these translocations, so the phosphorylation is not
      explained by an ALK fusion of the kind seen in lymphoma and lung cancer.
      What the quote does not separate is rearrangement from amplification:
      the same abstract reports that samples carrying both ALK and MYCN
      amplification showed complex rearrangements with multiple breakpoints
      inside the amplicon, so in those tumours raised phosphorylated ALK is
      not attributable to the rearrangement alone.
  - reference: PMID:25251827
    reference_title: "Intragenic anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements: translocations as a novel mechanism of ALK activation in neuroblastoma tumors."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Both ALK proteins predicted to arise from such alterations and from the abnormal ALK exon 4-11 deletion observed in the CLB-BAR cell line show strong activation of downstream targets STAT3 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) when expressed in PC12 cells."
    explanation: >-
      The receptors predicted to arise from these rearrangements activate
      STAT3 and ERK, which shows the altered protein is signalling-competent
      and not merely phosphorylated. ERK activation is the output this node's
      edge to RAS-MAPK Pathway Hyperactivation asserts. Indirect here: the
      test expressed the receptor from a construct in PC12 cells, a
      heterologous line, so it does not measure signalling in the patient
      tumours of the item above.
  - reference: PMID:22203052
    reference_title: "High anaplastic lymphoma kinase immunohistochemical staining in neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma is an independent predictor of poor outcome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "half of all NBL samples showed ALK positivity in most (>50%) of tumor cells, whereas half of the GNBL showed staining in <20% of the tumor cells"
    explanation: >-
      Immunohistochemistry across a patient series not selected by ALK status,
      so unlike the rearrangement subset above this reports how common high
      receptor levels are in neuroblastoma generally. The abstract does not
      say how the samples were assembled, so no claim is made that the series
      is consecutive or population-based. Indirect for activation: staining
      reports how much receptor is present, not whether it is phosphorylated,
      and it bears on this node only through the cell-line finding already
      cited here that the wild-type receptor needs a high expression
      threshold before it is constitutively phosphorylated. The series is
      described as 71 neuroblastomas in the sentence stating what was
      investigated, while the mutation count later in the same abstract says
      2 of 72, an inconsistency internal to the source. Only those 2 carried
      an ALK mutation, which is why the study treats high ALK levels as
      mutation-independent.
  downstream:
  - target: RAS-MAPK Pathway Hyperactivation
    description: >-
      Activating ALK kinase-domain mutations found in neuroblastoma signal
      into the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, which is why relapse series count
      ALK among the RAS-MAPK-activating lesions while this entry models the
      receptor on this node rather than listing ALK among the pathway node's
      genes. The edge says that RAS-MAPK signalling is one output of the
      activated receptor, not its only one.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - >-
      Receptor-proximal adaptor recruitment and GTP loading of RAS
      downstream of the activated kinase, omitted from this edge.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26121087
      reference_title: "Relapsed neuroblastomas show frequent RAS-MAPK pathway mutations."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "To validate that ALK and RAS mutations directly activate the RAS/MAPK pathway in neuroblastoma cells, we inducibly expressed an ALK F1174L and an NRAS v61Q mutation in two cell lines that did not harbor RAS-MAPK mutations. Expression of both mutated proteins causes activation of this pathway"
      explanation: >-
        In an experiment this study ran to validate that ALK and RAS
        mutations directly activate RAS-MAPK signalling in neuroblastoma
        cells, inducible expression of ALK F1174L and of a mutant NRAS in
        two cell lines carrying no RAS-MAPK mutation of their own activated
        the pathway. This supports drawing the activated receptor as an
        input to the RAS-MAPK node. One ALK allele was tested, F1174L at a
        recurrent hotspot, so the step from this result to the frequent ALK
        mutations as a class is an inference the quote does not make, which
        is why it is graded indirect. The sentence reports the two
        constructs together, the main text says only that both were
        expressed in two cell lines, and the readout appears in a
        supplementary figure, so neither the measurement nor which line
        received which construct can be read from the quoted text.
  - target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
    description: >-
      Constitutive ALK kinase signalling converges on the same proliferative
      output as MYCN amplification and co-operates with it; ALK-mutant and
      MYCN-amplified disease frequently co-occur and jointly enhance
      malignancy.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41560679
      reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations, including mutations and amplification, activate oncogenic signaling pathways that, together with MYCN amplification, further enhance tumor malignancy."
      explanation: >-
        Supports co-operation between ALK signalling and MYCN amplification in
        driving malignancy. Indirect for this edge: the sentence, background in
        the citing study's abstract, says that ALK signalling and MYCN
        amplification together enhance tumor malignancy; that ALK signalling
        feeds the MYCN-driven proliferative program is an inference from it.
- name: GD2 Surface Antigen Expression
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    The disialoganglioside GD2 is expressed on the surface of nearly all
    neuroblastoma cells and only sparsely on normal tissue, which is what makes
    it the target of antibody therapy. Expression is not uniform, and it can be
    absent: in a series of 474 patients with unequivocal bone marrow
    infiltration, tumor cells showed complete or partial negative GD2 staining
    in 12.0% across diagnosis, treatment and recurrence, and 21 cases converted
    from positive to negative. That series found no event-free or overall
    survival difference between negative and positive staining, so loss of the
    antigen is recorded here as a property of the tumor rather than as a
    prognostic marker.
  chemical_entities:
  - preferred_term: ganglioside GD2
    term:
      id: CHEBI:28648
      label: beta-D-GalNAc-(1->4)-[alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->8)-alpha-Neu5Ac-(2->3)]-beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-beta-D-Glc-(1<->1')-Cer
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35435953
    reference_title: "Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma: Facts and Hopes."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The identification of strong expression of the disialoganglioside GD2 on the surface of nearly all neuroblastoma cells provided a target for immune recognition by anti-GD2 mAbs that recruit Fc receptor-expressing innate immune cells that mediate cytotoxicity or phagocytosis"
    explanation: >-
      The basis for the node: GD2 is on the surface of nearly all
      neuroblastoma cells, which is the property the antibody exploits. Graded
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER because the citing document is a review
      synthesising work it did not perform, so the quoted sentence is not
      itself a measurement in any cohort or system.
  - reference: PMID:27654028
    reference_title: "Lack of immunocytological GD2 expression on neuroblastoma cells in bone marrow at diagnosis, during treatment, and at recurrence."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Thirty-seven patients had tumor cells with complete or partial negative GD2 staining at initial diagnosis, nine during chemotherapy, and 11 at recurrence (altogether 12.0%)."
    explanation: >-
      The heterogeneity figure in the description, from 474 patients with
      unequivocal bone marrow infiltration assessed by immunocytology. It is
      the reason the node does not simply assert uniform expression. Abstract
      results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:27654028
    reference_title: "Lack of immunocytological GD2 expression on neuroblastoma cells in bone marrow at diagnosis, during treatment, and at recurrence."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Twenty-one cases changed from positive to negative"
    explanation: >-
      That the antigen can be lost within a patient over the course of
      treatment, rather than only differing between patients at diagnosis.
      Abstract results clause from the same 474-patient series.
  - reference: PMID:27654028
    reference_title: "Lack of immunocytological GD2 expression on neuroblastoma cells in bone marrow at diagnosis, during treatment, and at recurrence."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Event-free survival and overall survival comparing negative versus positive staining did not show any differences"
    explanation: >-
      A tested null, and the reason this node is not written as a prognostic
      marker: in the same series, GD2 staining status did not separate
      outcomes. It bears on whether loss predicts outcome, not on whether
      loss would matter for antibody binding, which the series did not test.
      Abstract results sentence.
  downstream:
  - target: Anti-GD2 Antibody-Mediated Tumor Cell Killing
    description: >-
      Surface GD2 is the antigen the therapeutic antibodies bind, so it is the
      precondition for antibody-mediated killing. This edge is
      intervention-conditioned: it carries flux only while an anti-GD2
      antibody is being given, and the downstream node describes what the
      drug then does rather than anything the untreated tumor does.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:34884452
      reference_title: "Mechanisms, Characteristics, and Treatment of Neuropathic Pain and Peripheral Neuropathy Associated with Dinutuximab in Neuroblastoma Patients."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "Dinutuximab targets the disialoganglioside GD2, which is highly expressed on neuroblastoma cells and minimally present on the surface of normal human neurons, peripheral pain fibers, and skin melanocytes."
      explanation: >-
        States the antigen-to-drug link this edge asserts, and the narrow
        normal-tissue distribution that makes the target usable. The same
        sparse expression on peripheral pain fibers is why the on-target
        toxicity is neuropathic pain. Graded REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER
        because the citing document is a review restating established
        pharmacology.
- name: Anti-GD2 Antibody-Mediated Tumor Cell Killing
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    An anti-GD2 antibody bound to surface GD2 recruits the host's innate
    effector arms: Fc-receptor-bearing innate immune cells kill the opsonized
    cell by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, and bound antibody also
    triggers complement-dependent cytotoxicity. This node exists only under
    treatment, and it is the node the antibody treatments point at.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity against neuroblastoma cells
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0001788
      label: antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity
  - preferred_term: complement-dependent cytotoxicity against neuroblastoma cells
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0006958
      label: complement activation, classical pathway
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34884452
    reference_title: "Mechanisms, Characteristics, and Treatment of Neuropathic Pain and Peripheral Neuropathy Associated with Dinutuximab in Neuroblastoma Patients."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Anti GD2 antibodies bind to surface GD2 and determine the lysis of neuroblastoma cells induced by immune response via the antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and the complement-dependent cytotoxicity"
    explanation: >-
      Names both effector routes this node binds as GO processes. Graded
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER because the citing document is a review
      restating established pharmacology rather than reporting an experiment.
  - reference: PMID:35435953
    reference_title: "Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma: Facts and Hopes."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The identification of strong expression of the disialoganglioside GD2 on the surface of nearly all neuroblastoma cells provided a target for immune recognition by anti-GD2 mAbs that recruit Fc receptor-expressing innate immune cells that mediate cytotoxicity or phagocytosis"
    explanation: >-
      Independent statement of the effector mechanism, and the reason no
      cell_types are bound on this node: the source commits only to
      Fc-receptor-expressing innate immune cells and does not say which
      population predominates in patients. Graded as above.
- name: Low Tumor Mutation Burden
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  description: >-
    High-risk neuroblastoma carries few somatic coding mutations.
    Across the coding regions of 240 high-risk tumours the median
    exonic mutation frequency was 0.60 per Mb (0.48 nonsilent), with
    few recurrently mutated genes, a rate the authors place alongside
    medulloblastoma and haematopoietic malignancies and well below
    adult solid tumours. It is low on average rather than uniformly
    low: per-tumour counts ranged from 0 to 218, and two tumours
    carrying DNA-repair gene alterations reached 7.27 and 4.29
    mutations per Mb. Two reviews of neuroblastoma immunotherapy name
    that burden as a hurdle to checkpoint blockade, one of them
    alongside the reduced tumour-cell MHC class I carried by the Low
    Tumor-Cell MHC Class I Expression node. Nothing cited here measures
    neoantigen load, antigen presentation or immune infiltration, so
    the step from few mutations to few mutation-derived neoantigens is
    an inference those reviews state rather than a result any of these
    sources tests.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23334666
    reference_title: The genetic landscape of high-risk neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "To determine the spectrum of somatic mutation in high-risk neuroblastoma, we studied 240 affected individuals (cases) using a combination of whole-exome, genome and transcriptome sequencing as part of the Therapeutically Applicable Research to Generate Effective Treatments (TARGET) initiative. Here we report a low median exonic mutation frequency of 0.60 per Mb (0.48 nonsilent) and notably few recurrently mutated genes in these tumors."
    explanation: >-
      In the TARGET initiative, 240 matched tumour and normal (blood
      leukocyte) pairs from patients older than 18 months at diagnosis
      with metastatic stage 4 disease were sequenced: 221 cases by whole
      exome, 18 by whole genome and one by both, with RNA sequencing on
      ten of the genome cases. Across their coding regions the median
      somatic mutation frequency was 0.60 per Mb (0.48 nonsilent) and
      few genes were recurrently mutated, a rate the authors call
      consistent with unselected neuroblastomas and significantly lower
      than adult solid tumours, so low here means low relative to adult
      solid tumours. The figure describes high-risk stage 4 tumours at
      diagnosis rather than neuroblastoma as a whole, and it is a
      median: per-tumour counts ranged from 0 to 218, and two tumours
      with DNA-repair gene alterations reached 7.27 and 4.29 mutations
      per Mb. Graded DIRECT because the quoted sentence reports the
      mutation frequency this node is named for. What it does not
      establish is any immune consequence: the study measures neither
      neoantigen load, antigen presentation nor immune infiltration, so
      the inference from few mutations to few mutation-derived
      neoantigens for T cells to recognise is carried by the two reviews
      cited below and not by this series.
  - reference: PMID:35435953
    reference_title: "Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma: Facts and Hopes."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Most children with cancer, including high-risk neuroblastoma, do not benefit from treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) that have revolutionized the treatment of many highly immunogenic adult solid tumors. This likely reflects the low tumor mutation burden as well as the downregulated MHC-I that characterizes most high-risk neuroblastomas."
    explanation: >-
      Review synthesis from the abstract of an expert review: most
      children with cancer, including those with high-risk
      neuroblastoma, do not benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors,
      and the authors attribute that to the low tumour mutation burden
      together with the downregulated MHC class I that characterises
      most high-risk neuroblastomas. Both sentences are quoted because
      the second opens with a pronoun whose antecedent is the first. The
      clause cited for this node is the low tumour mutation burden; the
      MHC class I clause of the same sentence is cited on Low
      Tumor-Cell MHC Class I Expression. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because
      the passage summarises clinical experience with checkpoint
      inhibitors in children and properties of patients' tumours, and
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the review ran no study of its own, so it
      is not independent evidence for the burden; the TARGET series
      cited above carries that. The authors hedge the attribution as
      what the non-response likely reflects, so this supports their
      reading and not a demonstrated mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:32167865
    reference_title: Targets and Antibody Formats for Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Although low tumor mutational burden is a major hurdle for immune checkpoint inhibitors, an immature or impaired immune system and inhibitory tumor microenvironment can further complicate the prospects for successful immunotherapy."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract sentence of a review of antibody immunotherapy for
      high-risk metastatic neuroblastoma, making a general point about
      immunotherapy: low tumour mutational burden is a major hurdle for
      immune checkpoint inhibitors, and an immature or impaired immune
      system and an inhibitory tumour microenvironment can further
      complicate the prospects for successful immunotherapy. Graded
      INDIRECT because the sentence names no tumour and the sentence
      before it concerns paediatric cancers in general, so applying it
      to neuroblastoma is an inference from the review's subject and
      from its next sentence, which calls neuroblastoma poorly
      immunogenic. Of the factors it names only the mutational burden
      belongs to this node: the review's own restatement gives
      chemotherapy as an example cause of the impaired immune system,
      which is a property of the treated host rather than of the tumour,
      and the inhibitory tumour microenvironment is left general enough
      that it maps onto no one node here. The review also scopes the
      cold phenotype to high-risk metastatic disease and describes
      low-risk neuroblastoma as having the characteristics of a hot
      tumour, so the claim does not extend across the disease, and the
      authors' hedge that these factors can further complicate
      immunotherapy is kept.
  notes: >-
    This node carries no ontology binding. The descriptor slots a
    pathophysiology node offers bind biological processes, molecular
    functions, chemical entities, genes and cell types; the claim here
    is a count of somatic coding mutations per megabase of tumour
    genome, which none of them describes.

    The burden figure is not stratified by MYCN status, so this node
    takes no incoming edge from MYCN-Driven Proliferation. The MYCN
    association cited in this entry is a T-cell observation and is
    recorded on T-Cell-Poor Tumor Microenvironment.
- name: Low Tumor-Cell MHC Class I Expression
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    MHC class I on neuroblastoma tumour cells is low rather than
    absent. Immunohistochemistry with a panel of antibodies to the
    HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C loci, beta-2-microglobulin and HLA-DR found
    none of 17 evaluable diagnostic specimens immunopositive for MHC
    class I or class II, and an earlier series of ten tumours detected
    no HLA class I or beta-2-microglobulin reactivity on more than 94%
    of the small round cells in each tumour while a population under 6%
    did stain. Yet HLA class I tumour-cell density was quantified
    across tumours by in situ immunohistochemistry in 77 specimens and,
    combined with PD-L1, carried outcome information, being prognostic
    for overall survival, which is why this node says low and not
    absent. Two caveats bound the node. The two series that detected
    none are small, 17 and ten tumours, and date from 2005 and 1985.
    And nothing cited here measures T-cell infiltration or stratifies
    class I by MYCN status: the 2005 series states that its own result
    does not support a direct correlation between MYCN amplification
    and loss of MHC class I, so this node takes no incoming edge from
    MYCN-Driven Proliferation.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: antigen processing and presentation of endogenous peptide antigen
      via MHC class I on tumour cells
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0019885
      label: antigen processing and presentation of endogenous peptide antigen via
        MHC class I
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:15449039
    reference_title: "Expression of MHC class I, MHC class II, and cancer germline antigens in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "None of the 17 tumors was immunopositive with any of our antibodies to MHC class I or MHC class II molecules"
    explanation: >-
      Immunohistochemistry on patient tumour tissue obtained at surgery
      to confirm the initial diagnosis, with the denominator stated
      inside the sentence. Snap-frozen specimens matched to the paraffin
      blocks were stained with antibodies to the HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C
      loci, beta-2-microglobulin and HLA-DR, and the surrounding stromal
      cells served as the internal positive control, so the negative
      tumour cells are unlikely to reflect a failed stain. Of 68 tumours
      screened by RT-PCR, 19 had paraffin blocks available and 17 of
      those could be evaluated for MHC, two being too necrotic; that
      19-tumour immunohistochemistry series included a
      ganglioneuroblastoma, and cases were chosen by availability of
      material rather than to represent the distribution of
      neuroblastoma by stage, so this is not a prevalence estimate. The
      authors note that absence of MHC class I by immunohistochemistry
      does not exclude class I molecules present below the detection
      level of the method, and that earlier work found expression
      inducible by interferon gamma, so the finding is undetectable by
      immunohistochemistry in untreated tissue rather than proven
      absence. Read beside the HLA class I tumour-cell density measured
      across 77 specimens by Melaiu et al. 2017 (PMID:28270499), cited
      on this node, that is why the node says low rather than absent.
      Only 2 of the 17 were MYCN-amplified, and the authors state that
      this does not support a direct correlation between MYCN
      amplification and loss of MHC class I, which is why no edge runs
      from MYCN-Driven Proliferation to this node.
  - reference: PMID:3902214
    reference_title: HLA class I and beta 2-microglobulin expression in frozen and formaldehyde-fixed
      paraffin sections of neuroblastoma tumors.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Ten solid neuroblastoma tumors were examined for beta 2-microglobulin (beta 2-m) and HLA-class I expression in an immunocytochemical assay. Blood vessel endothelium and a small population of cells (less than 6% of small round cells) were consistently stained in frozen sections of each tumor. No beta 2-m or HLA-class I reactivity was detected in the remainder (greater than 94%) of the small round cells in each tumor."
    explanation: >-
      Immunocytochemistry for beta-2-microglobulin and HLA class I on
      ten solid neuroblastoma tumours from patients. In frozen sections
      of every tumour, blood vessel endothelium and a small population
      of cells, under 6% of the small round cells, stained, while no
      reactivity for either molecule was detected on the remaining more
      than 94%. The endothelial staining acts as an internal positive
      control in each section, so the negative small round cells are
      unlikely to reflect a failed stain. The authors report that the
      localisation of most positive cells near stromal tissue and blood
      vessels suggests most of them may be of non-tumour origin, so the
      stained minority is not shown to be tumour cells presenting class
      I. Patients differed in degree of disease involvement, yet no
      differences in beta-2-microglobulin or HLA class I expression were
      found among the tumours, and the paper describes a method for
      formaldehyde-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue alongside the
      frozen-section result. The authors present the finding as
      extending earlier reports of weak beta-2-microglobulin and HLA
      class I levels in cells of neuronal origin, so not detected means
      below what this 1985 immunocytochemical assay could detect rather
      than proven absence. The denominator is ten tumours, the readout
      is a stain scored on morphologically defined small round cells,
      and nothing here measures T-cell infiltration.
  - reference: PMID:28270499
    reference_title: "PD-L1 Is a Therapeutic Target of the Bromodomain Inhibitor JQ1 and, Combined with HLA Class I, a Promising Prognostic Biomarker in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that the combination of PD-L1 and HLA class I tumor cell density is a prognostic biomarker for predicting overall survival in neuroblastoma patients (P = 0.0448)."
    explanation: >-
      The paper's own multivariate Cox regression on 77 neuroblastoma
      specimens found that HLA class I tumour-cell density, in
      combination with PD-L1, predicted overall survival (P = 0.0448).
      What it establishes for this node is that class I density on
      tumour cells was quantified across a patient series and carried
      outcome information. The result is for the combination of the two
      markers rather than for HLA class I density alone, it rests on a
      single cohort with a borderline p value and no independent
      validation cohort, and the abstract does not name the covariates,
      so it should not be read as class I density being independently
      prognostic. Graded INDIRECT because the sentence asserts the
      prognostic value of the two markers combined; that class I is
      measurable on tumour cells across a series, and so low rather
      than absent, follows from it by inference.
  - reference: PMID:35435953
    reference_title: "Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma: Facts and Hopes."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Most children with cancer, including high-risk neuroblastoma, do not benefit from treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) that have revolutionized the treatment of many highly immunogenic adult solid tumors. This likely reflects the low tumor mutation burden as well as the downregulated MHC-I that characterizes most high-risk neuroblastomas."
    explanation: >-
      Review synthesis from the abstract of an expert review: most
      children with cancer, including those with high-risk
      neuroblastoma, do not benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors,
      and the authors attribute that to the low tumour mutation burden
      together with the downregulated MHC class I that characterises
      most high-risk neuroblastomas. Both sentences are quoted because
      the second opens with a pronoun whose antecedent is the first. The
      clause cited for this node is the downregulated MHC class I; the
      mutation-burden clause of the same sentence is cited on Low Tumor
      Mutation Burden. The authors scope that downregulation to most
      rather than all high-risk tumours, which is the same
      low-rather-than-absent reading the three primary series above
      support. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because the passage summarises
      clinical experience with checkpoint inhibitors in children and
      properties of patients' tumours, and REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the
      review ran no study of its own, so it is not independent evidence
      for the tumour property; the primary series cited above carry it.
  notes: >-
    Low rather than absent is a reading of three series together, not a
    quotation from any of them. The two series that detected no class I
    on tumour cells rest on immunohistochemical detection limits in
    untreated tissue. The 2005 authors state that an absence of class I
    by immunohistochemistry does not exclude class I molecules below the
    detection level of the method, and that neuroblastoma cell lines
    have been lysed by specific T cells without the prior interferon
    gamma treatment that up-regulates class I; the 1985 report makes
    neither statement, and in it a stained minority, under 6% of the
    small round cells, was present in every tumour and attributed mostly
    to non-tumour origin. The later study quantified HLA class I
    tumour-cell density across 77 specimens, which is a measured
    quantity rather than a negative. Note what that later result does
    not license: it is prognostic for the combination of PD-L1 and class
    I density, so the between-patient variation it demonstrates cannot
    be attributed to class I density alone.

    The GO:0019885 binding, antigen processing and presentation of
    endogenous peptide antigen via MHC class I marked DECREASED, is read
    off that reduced class I surface protein. No cited item assays
    antigen processing or presentation itself; the step from low or
    undetectable surface class I to reduced presentation rests on class
    I molecules being required for it.
- name: T-Cell-Poor Tumor Microenvironment
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    Tumours are T-cell-poor, and that poverty tracks MYCN
    amplification: in primary tumours from patients with metastatic
    disease the T-cell-poor tumours showed lower interferon-response and
    chemokine signature expression, in line with reduced immune cell
    infiltration. The contrast with MYCN-not-amplified tumours in a
    second patient series, and the interferon and chemokine route
    proposed for the MYCN link, are recorded on the incoming edge from
    MYCN-Driven Proliferation rather than on this node. The clinical
    corollary is cited here as patient evidence and not as a treatment
    claim: in the ADVL1412 phase 1-2 trial of single-agent nivolumab in
    children and young adults with relapsed or refractory non-CNS solid
    tumours or lymphoma, objective responses were confined to the
    lymphoma cohorts and were not observed in any other tumour type,
    neuroblastoma being one of the part-B expansion cohorts. Two caveats
    bound the node. The patient evidence is association and
    signature-based description rather than a demonstrated mechanism,
    with the T-cell content inferred from bulk-RNA signatures rather
    than counted in tissue. And the trial result is a non-response to
    one checkpoint antibody in heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory
    disease, with no per-cohort response rate reported for
    neuroblastoma, so it corroborates the T-cell-poor phenotype rather
    than measuring it.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: tumour-infiltrating T cell
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: CL:0000084
      label: T cell
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28680756
    reference_title: Amplification of N-Myc is associated with a T-cell-poor microenvironment
      in metastatic neuroblastoma restraining interferon pathway activity and chemokine
      expression.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we report that a T-cell-poor microenvironment in primary metastatic neuroblastomas is associated with genomic amplification of the MYCN (N-Myc) proto-oncogene. These tumors exhibited lower interferon pathway activity and chemokine expression in line with reduced immune cell infiltration."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract statement of the authors' integrative transcriptomic
      analysis of human primary neuroblastomas. Both sentences are
      quoted because the second opens with a pronoun whose antecedent is
      the first, the primary metastatic neuroblastomas with a
      T-cell-poor microenvironment that the authors associate with MYCN
      amplification. The measured contrast behind both readouts is
      MYCN-amplified against non-amplified INSS
      stage 4 tumours (65 against 116) within a 498-tumour RNA
      sequencing cohort whose stage 4 subgroup numbered 181. The
      specimens are primary tumours from patients with metastatic-stage
      disease rather than metastatic deposits, and the authors re-ran the
      analysis on abdomen, pelvis and adrenal primaries to rule out
      lymphoid tissue from metastatic sites as a confounder. Both
      readouts are bulk-RNA-sequencing gene-signature scores, so
      interferon pathway activity here is a signature score rather than
      a measured pathway flux, and the reduced immune cell infiltration
      is itself inferred from immune-cell signatures rather than counted
      in tissue, which is why the source's in line with hedge is kept.
      The paper reports no chemokine-signature against
      T-cell-signature comparison, so the T-cell-poor framing of the
      chemokine half rests on the MYCN association stated in the first
      quoted sentence; the cell-line route proposed for that association
      is recorded on the incoming edge from MYCN-Driven Proliferation.
  - reference: PMID:32192573
    reference_title: "Nivolumab in children and young adults with relapsed or refractory solid tumours or lymphoma (ADVL1412): a multicentre, open-label, single-arm, phase 1-2 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Objective responses were not observed in other tumour types."
    explanation: >-
      ADVL1412 gave single-agent nivolumab, a PD-1-blocking antibody, to
      children and young adults with relapsed or refractory non-CNS
      solid tumours or lymphoma. The sentence closes the abstract's
      findings and follows the report of responses in the lymphoma
      cohorts, one of ten patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma among them
      and every responder expressing PD-L1, so other tumour types means
      every tumour type outside Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
      Neuroblastoma was one of the seven part-B expansion cohorts the
      abstract lists; the full text enrolled 22 patients with
      neuroblastoma, four in part A and 18 in part B, the latter
      combining a measurable-disease and an MIBG-only cohort, and
      reports stable disease as the best response in a minority of the
      neuroblastoma cohort, so the result is an absence of objective
      response rather than of disease stabilisation. Those are enrolment
      rather than response-evaluable counts, and no per-cohort response
      rate is reported. The result is cited on this node rather than on
      Low Tumor Mutation Burden or Low Tumor-Cell MHC Class I Expression
      because PD-1 blockade acts on T cells, so a non-response bears on
      whether a tumour-reactive T-cell population is present to be
      released, and the trial measured neither mutation burden nor class
      I. Graded INDIRECT because a therapeutic non-response is cited as
      corroboration of the T-cell-poor phenotype rather than as a
      measurement of it, in a heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory
      population.
  notes: >-
    This node declares no conformance to the immune_checkpoint_blockade
    module, and neither do its two sibling nodes. That module's chain
    runs from Neoantigen Generation through Anti-Tumor T Cell Response
    and Adaptive Immune Resistance to T Cell Exhaustion and Immune
    Escape, which describes tumours whose neoantigens do provoke a
    T-cell response that is then resisted. A T-cell-poor tumour is the
    absence of that chain, so conformance would assert steps this entry
    does not carry.

    The checkpoint-inhibitor non-response is filed here rather than on
    the mutation-burden or class I nodes because PD-1 blockade acts on T
    cells. The review cited on those two nodes (PMID:35435953) reads the
    lack of consistent responses the same way in its body text, as
    consistent with histopathologic evidence of a general lack of
    tumour-reactive infiltrating T cells in a majority of cases.

    The complementary cell-state result, that the immune-enriched tumour
    subset is predominantly characterised by mesenchymal lineage
    signatures while adrenergic tumours are less immunogenic, is carried
    by the Mesenchymal-State Immune Activation node and is not restated
    here.

    The route from amplified MYCN to T-cell exclusion is cell-line
    derived and is recorded on the incoming edge from MYCN-Driven
    Proliferation rather than on this node, which describes the tissue
    state.

    mechanism_confidence is deliberately left unset, which the schema
    reads as established. That is meant for the tissue state only, which
    rests on two independent patient series, and not for any mechanism
    producing it: the MYCN route is cell-line derived and carries its
    own caveats on the incoming edge.
- name: Tumor-Associated Macrophage Infiltration
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Tumour-associated macrophages are more abundant in metastatic than
    in locoregional neuroblastoma, and macrophage-associated gene
    expression carries prognostic weight in one stratum of the disease.
    In 71 localised and metastatic tumours assessed by
    immunohistochemistry, significantly greater numbers of infiltrating
    macrophages were seen only with CD163 staining, which identifies the
    alternatively activated (M2) phenotype, and only in stage 4 against
    locoregional tumours (t test P = .003); the excess did not reach
    significance with the other macrophage marker used, AIF1, and stage
    4S tumours, which undergo spontaneous regression, did not differ
    from locoregional ones. Among metastatic MYCN-non-amplified tumours,
    those diagnosed at 18 months or older carried higher expression of
    inflammation-related genes than those diagnosed earlier, and in 133
    such tumours the expression of five genes representing
    tumour-associated macrophages contributed 25% of the accuracy of a
    novel 14-gene tumour classification score. Among children diagnosed
    at 18 months or older, that score's low- against high-risk groups
    separated 5-year progression-free survival in the 94-patient
    subgroup of the CCG training cohort (47% against 12%, by
    leave-one-out cross-validation) and in two independent validation
    cohorts (57% against 8% in 39 patients treated on GPOH protocols,
    50% against 20% in 52 treated on COG protocols). The 39 CCG
    patients diagnosed before 18 months are part of the 133-tumour
    training set behind the 25% figure but not of those
    survival comparisons. That score is a prognostic tumour score with a
    macrophage-associated part rather than a macrophage signature: in
    the authors' permutation analysis the tumour cell-related genes
    explained 63% of its accuracy and age at diagnosis a further 12%.
    The stratum here is metastatic MYCN-non-amplified disease, a
    different stratum from the MYCN-amplified association recorded on
    T-Cell-Poor Tumor Microenvironment, and the source's own conclusion
    is hedged: interactions between tumour and inflammatory cells may
    contribute to the clinical metastatic neuroblastoma phenotype.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: tumour-associated macrophage
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: CL:0000235
      label: macrophage
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22927533
    reference_title: Clinical significance of tumor-associated inflammatory cells in
      metastatic neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Metastatic neuroblastomas had higher infiltration of TAMs than locoregional tumors, and metastatic tumors diagnosed in patients at age >= 18 months had higher expression of inflammation-related genes than those in patients diagnosed at age < 18 months."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract results sentence covering two separate analyses of
      patient tumours. The macrophage comparison is immunohistochemistry
      on 71 localised and metastatic neuroblastomas, and the full text
      narrows the abstract's wording: the excess was significant only
      with the M2 marker CD163 and not with AIF1, and only for stage 4
      against locoregional tumours (t test P = .003), while stage 4S
      tumours were comparable to locoregional ones. The age comparison
      is a separate gene-expression contrast, run on a TaqMan
      low-density array in 133 metastatic MYCN-non-amplified tumours and
      shown as a heat map with no test statistic in the main text; the
      inflammation-related genes expressed more highly in the older
      group were those associated with monocytes and macrophages,
      myeloid cells and B cells. That half measures transcript levels in
      whole tumour samples rather than macrophage counts, and because
      every tumour in it was MYCN-non-amplified it says nothing about
      MYCN-amplified tumours.
  - reference: PMID:22927533
    reference_title: Clinical significance of tumor-associated inflammatory cells in
      metastatic neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Expression of genes representing TAMs (CD33/CD16/IL6R/IL10/FCGR3) contributed to 25% of the accuracy of a novel 14-gene tumor classification score."
    explanation: >-
      In metastatic MYCN-non-amplified neuroblastoma the authors
      selected a 14-gene score from 44 candidate genes, 31
      tumour-related and 13 inflammation-related, quantified in 133
      tumours of the CCG training cohort, and validated it in 91 further
      tumours from patients treated on GPOH (39) and COG (52) protocols.
      Nine of its 14 genes are tumour cell-related and five are the
      inflammation-related genes the abstract calls TAM-representing;
      the full text names those five as CD14, CD33, FCGR3 (CD16), IL6R
      and IL10 and states that they are mainly expressed by macrophages
      and myeloid cells, so the abstract's list, which gives FCGR3 twice
      (once as CD16) and omits CD14, shows four distinct genes for a
      claim about five. In a permutation analysis the
      inflammation-related genes explained on average 25% of the model's
      accuracy in predicting progression-free survival, against 63% for
      the tumour cell-related genes and 12% for age at diagnosis, so the
      14-gene score is a prognostic tumour score with a
      macrophage-associated part and not a macrophage signature. The
      gene levels are measured in tumour samples rather than as
      macrophage counts, and the result shows that
      macrophage-associated expression adds prognostic information
      alongside tumour genes, not that macrophage content alone predicts
      outcome.
  notes: >-
    This node carries no causal edge in either direction, and the
    absence is deliberate rather than an oversight. The cited series
    shows differential macrophage infiltration between stages and
    prognostic weight for macrophage-associated gene expression; it does
    not show that macrophage infiltration produces the states described
    on T-Cell-Poor Tumor Microenvironment and Low Tumor-Cell MHC Class I
    Expression, and an edge in the other direction is equally
    unsupported. Those nodes also describe a different stratum: this one
    rests on metastatic MYCN-non-amplified disease.

    The natural future conformance target is
    tumor_promoting_inflammation#Pro-Tumorigenic Inflammatory
    Microenvironment, which binds the same CL:0000235 under the
    preferred term Tumor-Associated Macrophage. Conformance is
    deliberately not declared: that module node sits in a chain running
    from a chronic inflammatory stimulus to a hallmark-promoting
    inflammatory output, which this entry does not carry and which the
    hedged conclusion of the one cited series does not establish.
- name: Telomerase Activation
  description: >-
    Telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance, one of the two telomere
    maintenance mechanisms in neuroblastoma. TERT rearrangements at 5p15.33
    juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, with
    chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region, and
    despite their structural diversity they all induced massive transcriptional
    upregulation of TERT. MYCN amplification raises TERT transcription, and some
    tumours have high TERT expression with neither alteration. In 457
    pretreatment neuroblastomas, TERT rearrangement was found in 46 and MYCN
    amplification in 93, and high TERT expression without either in 10 of 223
    tumours with expression data. TERT promoter mutations are rare: none was
    found in 131 primary tumours representing the whole spectrum of the disease,
    and a single-centre series found them in 17 of 603 tumours. Activated
    telomerase, defined by these routes, was associated with the poorest overall
    survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses.
    Enzymatic telomerase activity has been shown in neuroblastoma cell lines
    that carry a TERT rearrangement or MYCN amplification.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  conforms_to: "enabling_replicative_immortality#Telomere Maintenance Reactivation"

  - preferred_term: TERT
    term:
      id: hgnc:11730
      label: TERT
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: telomerase activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0003720
      label: telomerase activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: telomere maintenance via telomerase
    modifier: INCREASED

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Despite a large structural diversity of these rearrangements, they all induced massive transcriptional upregulation of TERT."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract result in patient tumours (whole-genome sequencing of 56, an
      extended series of 217, plus expression profiling): the TERT
      rearrangements were structurally diverse, yet all came with massive
      transcriptional upregulation of TERT. 'All' can only cover rearranged
      tumours with expression data, such as the 10 in the transcriptome
      comparison; 28 rearrangements were detected. 'Induced' is the authors'
      causal reading, backed by enhancer juxtaposition and TERT mRNA not
      tracking copy number, not by engineering a rearrangement. The quote
      concerns TERT mRNA; telomerase enzyme activity was measured only in cell
      lines.
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 5p15.33 rearrangements juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, resulting in massive chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region."
    explanation: >-
      This abstract sentence summarises the paper's own results, mainly from
      patient tumour tissue: 5p15.33 rearrangements place TERT next to strong
      enhancer elements, with chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the
      affected region. The enhancer mapping rested on ChIP-seq of only three
      TERT-rearranged tumours, and part of the histone-mark survey used cell
      lines. The rise in CpG methylation across the TERT locus, measured in 39
      primary tumours (six rearranged), was also seen in MYCN-amplified tumours,
      so it is not specific to rearrangement.
  - reference: PMID:35100718
    reference_title: "Telomerase Is a Prognostic Marker of Poor Outcome and a Therapeutic Target in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We detected TERT rearrangements in 46 of 457 cases (10.1%), MYCN amplification in 93 of 457 cases (20.4%), and elevated TERT expression in tumors lacking TERT or MYCN alterations in 10 of 223 cases (4.5%)."
    explanation: >-
      In a series of 457 pretreatment neuroblastomas, the study found TERT
      rearrangement in 46 and MYCN amplification in 93 by fluorescence in situ
      hybridization, and elevated TERT expression without either alteration in
      10 of 223 tumours profiled by microarray, a subset of the 273 also
      examined for ALT. The denominators differ, so the three percentages cannot
      be added together. The sentence itself does not mention telomerase: the
      authors class these alterations as activated telomerase in a later
      sentence, and the abstract reports no telomerase-activity assay on the
      tumours.
  - reference: PMID:35100718
    reference_title: "Telomerase Is a Prognostic Marker of Poor Outcome and a Therapeutic Target in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The presence of activated telomerase (ie, TERT rearrangements, MYCN amplification, or high TERT expression without these alterations) was associated with poorest overall survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses."
    explanation: >-
      In an outcome analysis of pretreatment neuroblastomas, activated
      telomerase (TERT rearrangement, MYCN amplification, or high TERT
      expression without either) was associated with the poorest overall
      survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable
      analyses. Activation is defined by genomic and expression markers, not
      enzyme activity, and the abstract names neither the covariates nor the
      number of tumours analysed (FISH for TERT and MYCN covered 457 tumours;
      microarray TERT expression covered 223). As MYCN amplification is a
      defining route, this does not show prognostic value beyond MYCN
      amplification.
  - reference: PMID:40638875
    reference_title: "Clinical Significance of TERT Promoter Mutations in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "TERT-PM and TERT-RA were detected in 17 of 603 (2.8%) and 31of 168 (18.4%) tumors from individual patients, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective single-centre (MSK) review of sequenced neuroblastomas,
      TERT promoter mutations were found in 17 of 603 tumours profiled on the
      MSK-IMPACT targeted panel (2.8%) and TERT rearrangements in 31 of 168
      whole-genome-sequenced tumours (18.4%), so promoter mutations occur, but
      less often than rearrangements. The two rates come from different tumour
      sets and assays, because rearrangements were scored only by whole-genome
      sequencing. The sentence shows frequency, not telomerase activation:
      promoter-mutant tumours showed no statistically significant TERT mRNA
      difference from TERT-wild-type tumours, only a trend towards higher
      expression.
  - reference: PMID:26171145
    reference_title: "Absence of telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter mutations in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In 131 neuroblastoma primary tumors representing the whole spectrum of neuroblastoma, no TERT promoter mutations were detected."
    explanation: >-
      Sanger sequencing of a 474-bp TERT promoter region covering the C228T and
      C250T hotspots found no mutation in any of 131 pretreatment primary
      neuroblastomas from a German tumour bank, a cohort the authors describe as
      representing the whole spectrum of the disease; this is the description's
      131-tumour observation. Main limitation: zero of 131 cannot rule out a low
      frequency, and a later series of 603 tumours (PMID:40638875) found
      promoter mutations in 2.8%, mostly in high-risk disease, so the mutation
      is rare rather than absent.
  - reference: PMID:26171145
    reference_title: "Absence of telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter mutations in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In conclusion, the TERT promoter mutations are not a frequent mechanism of TERT overexpression in neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      Drawing chiefly on the 131 primary tumours, none with a promoter mutation,
      the authors conclude that promoter mutation is not a frequent mechanism of
      TERT overexpression in neuroblastoma, which supports the description's
      statement that TERT promoter mutations are rare. Their cell-line finding
      (C228T in 3 of 19 lines, all SK-N-SH and two of its subclones, with no
      correlation to TERT expression) is separate in-vitro evidence. Limitation:
      only a 474-bp region around the TERT start codon was sequenced; the
      authors name epigenetic changes and mutations in more distant, unanalysed
      regulatory elements as possible alternative mechanisms.
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Supporting a functional role of TERT, neuroblastoma cell lines bearing rearrangements or amplified MYCN exhibited both upregulated TERT expression and enzymatic telomerase activity."
    explanation: >-
      In this primary research paper, neuroblastoma cell lines with a TERT
      rearrangement or MYCN amplification showed both raised TERT expression and
      enzymatic telomerase activity; the Methods state that activity in cell
      lines was measured with a PCR-based telomeric repeat amplification
      protocol (TRAP) ELISA. The node's telomerase activity (GO:0003720) binding
      therefore rests on a measured enzyme activity, not on TERT expression
      alone. Limitation: activity was assayed only in cultured cell lines; the
      paper's tumour data report TERT expression and telomere content, not
      enzyme activity.
  downstream:
  - target: Unlimited Replicative Potential
    description: >-
      Telomerase keeps telomeres from eroding, so tumour cells can go on
      dividing. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither telomerase
      activity nor ALT showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost
      viability in culture.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that were non-ALT, low TERT expressing, and lacked telomerase activity showed continuous shortening of telomeres with growth in vitro and 2 of 3 TERT-L/non-ALT cell lines spontaneously lost viability after multiple passages in culture"
      explanation: >-
        Three patient-derived high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that lacked ALT
        and were negative for telomerase activity, not merely low in TERT mRNA,
        shortened their telomeres continuously with passage in culture, and 2 of
        3 spontaneously lost viability. Losing both telomere maintenance
        mechanisms therefore costs replicative capacity, which supports this
        edge by its converse. Viability held up in the third line, which had
        very high telomere content, so the finding establishes that a
        maintenance mechanism is required, not that telomerase alone suffices.
- name: RAS-MAPK Pathway Hyperactivation
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  conforms_to: "sustaining_proliferative_signaling#Constitutive Mitogenic Pathway Activation"
  description: >-
    Ligand-independent flux through the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, driven by
    activating lesions in NRAS, KRAS, HRAS, BRAF, PTPN11 or FGFR1, or by
    inactivation of the RAS GTPase-activating protein NF1. These lesions are
    enriched in relapse tumours rather than specific to them. Whole-genome
    sequencing of 23 matched diagnostic and relapse neuroblastomas found
    mutations predicted to activate the pathway in 18 of the 23 relapse
    tumours (78%), a figure that counts ALK, which this entry models on its
    own ALK Signaling Activation node and which accounted for 10 of the 18;
    the other 8 were NF1 inactivation in two tumours and NRAS, KRAS, HRAS,
    BRAF, PTPN11 and FGFR1 alterations in one each, one lesion per tumour
    because no tumour carried more than one. Seven of the 18 events were not
    detected in the matched diagnostic tumour by whole-genome sequencing,
    and deeper testing of those primaries recovered two, so 13 of the 18
    were detectable at diagnosis. At diagnosis the same mutations are
    uncommon and mostly subclonal: an ultra-deep panel covering NRAS, KRAS,
    HRAS, BRAF and PTPN11 found them in 7.9% of 242 pretherapy high-risk
    tumours, 15 of the 19 below that study's 20% variant-allele-frequency
    cut-off for clonality. A pan-paediatric paired series adds NF1 as a
    lesion selected at relapse; that cohort's finding that lesions outside
    these two classes are also selected at relapse is recorded on the
    Relapsed or Refractory Disease progression phase rather than here.
