      not examine the cerebellum or brainstem; its two-percent figure and its
      clause on cancer outcomes are not used here.
  downstream:
  - target: Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome
    description: >-
      In children with neuroblastoma, OMAS is described as a paraneoplastic
      disease characterized by autoimmunity directed at the cerebellum and
      brainstem, and that autoimmunity is taken to produce the syndrome's
      eye-movement, motor and behavioral signs; there is good evidence that OMAS
      is immune-mediated. The cited sources do not identify which immune
      effector acts on which neurons.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37537844
      reference_title: "Polyclonal lymphoid expansion drives paraneoplastic autoimmunity in neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Two percent of children with neuroblastoma develop opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia syndrome (OMAS), a paraneoplastic disease characterized by cerebellar and brainstem-directed autoimmunity but typically with outstanding cancer-related outcomes."
      explanation: >-
        The opening of the abstract of a study of OMAS-associated neuroblastomas
        describes OMAS in children with neuroblastoma as a paraneoplastic
        disease characterized by cerebellar and brainstem-directed autoimmunity,
        which names the autoimmunity in this edge's source node and its two
        targets. It characterizes the syndrome by that autoimmunity rather than
        stating that the autoimmunity produces the neurological signs, so
        reading the autoimmunity as the cause, as this edge does, takes one
        inference step. The sentence is the abstract's framing rather than a
        result of the study, which compared tumor transcriptomes and lymphocyte
        repertoires and did not examine the cerebellum or brainstem. Its
        two-percent figure and its clause on cancer outcomes are not used here.
    - reference: PMID:35260471
      reference_title: "Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "There is good evidence that OMAS is an immune-mediated condition that may be paraneoplastic in the context of neuroblastoma."
      explanation: >-
        This international expert review of pediatric OMAS states that there is
        good evidence that OMAS is an immune-mediated condition, which supports
        this edge's claim that an immune process produces the syndrome. The
        sentence is weaker than the edge in two respects: it says only that OMAS
        may be paraneoplastic in the context of neuroblastoma, and it names
        neither autoimmunity nor the structures the immune response targets. The
        review reports no patient data of its own.
- name: Replication-Stress Checkpoint Dependence
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma cells carry enough replication stress that they depend on the
    S and G2 checkpoint to survive it. CDK1 is held in check by CHK1 and WEE1,
    which buy time for repair before mitosis and let the cell tolerate stressed
    replication; removing either kinase collapses replication forks or forces
    an unprepared mitosis. A loss-of-function screen across the protein kinome
    found CHK1 the most potent of thirty cytotoxic hits in neuroblastoma, and
    the checkpoint is demonstrably running in patient material rather than only
    in culture: CHK1 was constitutively phosphorylated at Ser345 and Ser296 in
    six of eight high-risk primary tumours and in only one of eight low-risk
    ones. The dependence tracks N-Myc, since inhibitor sensitivity followed
    total MYC(N) protein and inducing MYCN in untransformed cells was by itself
    enough to phosphorylate CHK1. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the
    disease-specific dependency rests largely on one screen and its follow-up
    assays, and because the clinical test of it has so far produced few
    responses in heavily pre-treated children.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CHEK1
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: hgnc:1925
      label: CHEK1
  - preferred_term: WEE1
    term:
      id: hgnc:12761
      label: WEE1
  - preferred_term: CDK1
    term:
      id: hgnc:1722
      label: CDK1
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: checkpoint kinase activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0004672
      label: protein kinase activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: DNA replication checkpoint signaling
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0000076
      label: DNA replication checkpoint signaling
  notes: >-
    The incoming edge from MYCN-Driven Proliferation is now drawn, on the two
    results that tie the dependence to the oncogene: inhibitor sensitivity
    tracks MYC(N) protein, and inducing MYCN phosphorylates CHK1. Its causal
    half was run in retinal pigment epithelial cells rather than in
    neuroblastoma, so the edge is graded indirect.
    No outgoing edge is drawn, and that is a decision rather than a gap. This
    node is a dependence, a vulnerability the cell carries, not a step that
    produces a further lesion. What follows from it is what happens when it is
    removed, which is cell death, and an edge to a survival or proliferation
    node would invert the relationship: the checkpoint permits survival under
    replication stress, it does not cause it. The consequence that can be
    stated is therapeutic, and it is already carried the other way by the
    adavosertib record, whose target_mechanisms link points into this node
    with treatment_effect INHIBITS.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21289283
    reference_title: "RNAi screen of the protein kinome identifies checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Thirty kinases showed significant cellular cytotoxicity when depleted, with loss of the cell cycle checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1/CHEK1) being the most potent."
    explanation: >-
      The dependency claim, from an unbiased loss-of-function screen across the
      kinome rather than a candidate test, which is what makes CHK1 the leading
      vulnerability rather than one of many. Cell lines.
  - reference: PMID:21289283
    reference_title: "RNAi screen of the protein kinome identifies checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This pattern was also seen in six of eight high-risk primary tumors but not in control nonneuroblastoma cell lines or in seven of eight low-risk primary tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The checkpoint is active in patient tumours, not only in culture, and it
      separates high-risk from low-risk disease. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because
      the measurement here is on primary tumours. Small numbers, eight against
      eight, and the readout is phosphorylation rather than outcome.
  - reference: PMID:21289283
    reference_title: "RNAi screen of the protein kinome identifies checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "cell cycle analysis revealed that CHK1 inhibition in neuroblastoma cells caused apoptosis during S-phase, consistent with its role in replication fork progression"
    explanation: >-
      Where the cells die when the checkpoint is removed, which is what ties
      the dependency to replication rather than to mitotic entry alone and is
      the basis for binding DNA replication checkpoint signaling.
  - reference: PMID:21289283
    reference_title: "RNAi screen of the protein kinome identifies checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "CHK1 inhibitor sensitivity correlated with total MYC(N) protein levels, and inducing MYCN in retinal pigmented epithelial cells resulted in CHK1 phosphorylation, which caused growth inhibition when inhibited."
    explanation: >-
      Why the dependency is tied to N-Myc: sensitivity tracks the protein, and
      forcing MYCN in untransformed retinal pigment epithelial cells is enough
      to switch the checkpoint on. Indirect for this node because the causal
      half is in a non-neuroblastoma cell system, which is what the experiment
      needs in order to isolate MYCN but also what keeps it a model for the
      tumour rather than a measurement in one.
  - reference: PMID:37081608
    reference_title: "Pediatric phase 2 trial of a WEE1 inhibitor, adavosertib (AZD1775), and irinotecan for relapsed neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "CDK1 activity is restrained by the checkpoint kinases CHK1 and WEE1. These checkpoints allow for repair of DNA before mitosis and tolerance of replication stress, thereby maintaining tumor cell viability."
    explanation: >-
      The general cell-biology the node assembles, and the source for naming
      both kinases and CDK1 on it. Graded BACKGROUND and OTHER because the
      sentence is textbook pathway description in a trial report's
      introduction, not evidence this or any cited study produced.
  - reference: PMID:37081608
    reference_title: "Pediatric phase 2 trial of a WEE1 inhibitor, adavosertib (AZD1775), and irinotecan for relapsed neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "WEE1 is a tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates and inhibits CDK1, affecting proper coordination of DNA replication as well as entry into mitosis."
    explanation: >-
      WEE1's half of the checkpoint, which the CHK1 screen does not cover. Same
      grading and for the same reason as the item above.
- name: Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres
  description: >-
    Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT), the recombination-based telomere
    maintenance mechanism that works without telomerase. Its measured frequency
    depends on cohort and assay: C-circle screening classified 9.2% of a
    720-tumour screening cohort as ALT-positive, ALT-associated PML nuclear
    bodies marked 49 of 273 pretreatment neuroblastomas, and the C-circle assay
    marked 25 of 107 high-risk tumours from patients older than 18 months. In a
    registry cohort of 40 relapsed tumours, 47.5% were ALT-positive. ATRX
    alterations are found in only about half to 60% of ALT tumours. In primary
    tumours, ALT and the routes to telomerase activation occur almost mutually
    exclusively, and ATRX mutation and MYCN amplification co-occurred in only 1
    of 819 tumours. ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate slowly, with a
    protracted clinical course, yet children with these tumours have a dismal
    outcome. About a third of ALT-positive tumours present with localized
    disease classified as low or intermediate risk, and in one cohort survival
    did not differ between ALT-positive tumours classified high risk and those
    classified low or intermediate risk.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: telomere maintenance via recombination
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0000722
      label: telomere maintenance via recombination
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32291317
    reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ALT was identified in 23.4% of high-risk neuroblastoma tumors and genomic alterations in ATRX were detected in 60% of ALT tumors; 40% of ALT tumors lacked genomic alterations in known ALT-associated genes."
    explanation: >-
      In a Children's Oncology Group cohort of patient primary tumours taken at
      diagnosis, this abstract sentence states the paper's own result:
      C-circle-defined ALT in 23.4% of high-risk tumours, with ATRX alterations
      in 60% of ALT tumours. The other 40% were ATRX wild-type by Sanger
      sequencing, and no DAXX, H3F3A or SMARCAL1 alteration was detected in
      them. The 60% (15 of 25) includes two cases called only from RNA-seq
      overexpression of in-frame-fusion ATRX transcripts; DNA sequencing alone
      found ATRX alterations in 13 of 23 sequenced ALT tumours (57%).
  - reference: PMID:32291317
    reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of the 107 high-risk tumors (age > 18 months), 25 (23.4%; 95% CI: 15.3-31.4%) were positive for the ALT biomarker C-circles"
    explanation: >-
      This Results sentence gives the count behind the 23.4%: among 134 primary
      tumours taken at diagnosis and assayed, 25 of the 107 high-risk tumours
      from patients older than 18 months were positive for C-circles, a highly
      specific DNA marker of ALT measured by qPCR. It supports the frequency,
      assay and population, not the share of ALT tumours with ATRX alterations.
      The figure is specific to this assay: three APB-positive tumours fell
      below the C-circle cutoff, and counting either marker gives 28 of 107 ALT
      tumours.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "9.2% of the neuroblastomas in a screening cohort of 720 tumors were classified as ALT-positive"
    explanation: >-
      C-circle screening of a cohort of 720 neuroblastomas from German and
      Austrian trials and registries classified 9.2% as ALT-positive. Because
      the cohort was not restricted to high-risk disease, this is the
      broadest-spectrum frequency among the cohorts cited here. It is a trial
      and registry series rather than a population-based sample, and C-circle
      frequencies are not directly comparable with those from ALT-associated PML
      nuclear bodies.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Importantly, 47.5% of the INFORM tumors were ALT-activated, indicating a strong enrichment of this molecular subgroup in relapsed cases"
    explanation: >-
      The same C-circle assay applied to 40 relapsed neuroblastomas from the
      INFORM registry found 47.5% ALT-positive, which the authors read as strong
      enrichment of ALT among relapsed cases. The cohort is small and not a
      random sample of relapses: the authors note that registry entry requires
      sufficient general condition and a life expectancy of at least three
      months, which may underrepresent the most aggressive, mostly
      MYCN-amplified or TERT-rearranged tumours.
  - reference: PMID:39635126
    reference_title: "Copy-number dosage regulates telomere maintenance and disease-associated pathways in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Alterations at the ATRX locus are key drivers of ALT but only present in ~50% of ALT tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The abstract of this whole-genome and transcriptome study of 115 primary
      neuroblastomas states that alterations at the ATRX locus are key drivers
      of ALT yet are present in only about half of ALT tumours. The sentence
      frames the study and restates earlier work rather than reporting the
      paper's own measurement; the introduction credits the frequency (ATRX
      mutations in 50-60% of ALT-positive neuroblastomas) to earlier studies.
      The figure counts genomic alterations only; the discussion cites earlier
      work finding reduced ATRX protein in ATRX-wild-type ALT-positive
      neuroblastomas.
  - reference: PMID:39635126
    reference_title: "Copy-number dosage regulates telomere maintenance and disease-associated pathways in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among ALT tumors 9/20 (45%) harbored ATRX alterations and a single tumor (NBL49) a H3F3A missense mutation (p.A48E)."
    explanation: >-
      In the paper's own cohort of 115 primary neuroblastomas, profiled by
      tumour and matched-normal whole-genome sequencing plus tumour RNA-seq, 9
      of the 20 tumours classified as ALT (45%) carried ATRX alterations. This
      supports only the frequency, not that ATRX alterations drive ALT. The ALT
      group is small, and ALT status was inferred from telomere content in the
      sequencing data, checked against ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies and
      C-circles in subsets of 52 and 36 tumours.
  - reference: PMID:35100718
    reference_title: "Telomerase Is a Prognostic Marker of Poor Outcome and a Therapeutic Target in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ALT activation was found in 49 of 273 cases (17.9%). All these alterations occurred almost mutually exclusively and were associated with unfavorable prognostic variables and adverse outcome."
    explanation: >-
      This patient series covered 457 pretreatment neuroblastomas, 273 of them
      assessed for ALT by detecting ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies. The
      authors report that ALT and the three events they count as activated
      telomerase (TERT rearrangement, MYCN amplification, or high TERT
      expression without either) occurred almost mutually exclusively and were
      associated with unfavourable prognostic variables and adverse outcome.
      'Almost' means some overlap the abstract does not count, comparisons
      involving ALT cover only the 273 assessed tumours, and only activated
      telomerase was reported as an independent prognostic marker in
      multivariable analyses.
  - reference: PMID:32060267
    reference_title: "MYCN amplification and ATRX mutations are incompatible in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here we show that ATRX mutations and MYCN amplification are mutually exclusive across all ages and stages in neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The authors' abstract summary of their own analysis of patient tumours,
      made by merging the COG, TARGET and PCGP data (819 tumours), states the
      exclusivity directly and extends it across all ages and stages. The
      exclusivity is statistical rather than absolute: one of the 819 tumours
      carried both lesions. For infants the result is uninformative, because
      none of the 213 COG patients diagnosed before 18 months had an ATRX
      mutation.
  - reference: PMID:32060267
    reference_title: "MYCN amplification and ATRX mutations are incompatible in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the cohort of 819 tumors, ATRX mutations (n = 64) and MYCN amplification (n = 140) showed statistically significant mutual exclusivity (p = 0.0037, Cochrane-Mantel-Haenszel test) (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Note 1). Only 1 of 819 (0.1%) tumors had both lesions."
    explanation: >-
      The authors' pooled analysis of patient tumours (COG, TARGET and PCGP data
      merged) found significant mutual exclusivity of ATRX mutation and MYCN
      amplification among 819 tumours, with only one tumour carrying both, which
      supports near-complete rather than absolute exclusivity. That tumour was
      MYCN-amplified by FISH at the COG neuroblastoma reference lab but not by
      sequencing read depth, and repeat FISH found regional heterogeneity of
      MYCN amplification. In the COG cohort alone, ATRX mutation frequency did
      not differ significantly by MYCN status, so the significance comes from
      the merged data.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ALT-positive neuroblastomas proliferate slowly, which is reflected by a protracted clinical course of disease."
    explanation: >-
      This abstract sentence, from a study screening 760 primary and relapsed
      neuroblastomas for ALT, states both slow proliferation and a protracted
      clinical course. Slow proliferation rests on proteomics of 34 tumours,
      where proliferation-associated protein pathways were lower than in
      telomerase-activated tumours, and on fewer cycling cells than in
      MYCN-amplified tumours. Survival curves (60 ALT-positive vs 34
      MYCN-amplified tumours) showed significantly longer overall survival time
      but similarly poor event-free survival. Both findings are relative to
      telomerase-activated tumours, and the link between them is the authors'
      interpretation rather than a tested relationship.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Nevertheless, children with an ALT-positive neuroblastoma have dismal outcome."
    explanation: >-
      Closing abstract sentence of a retrospective neuroblastoma study, resting
      on the authors' own Kaplan-Meier analysis (60 ALT-positive vs 34
      MYCN-amplified tumours). It states that despite the slow proliferation and
      protracted course reported before it, children with ALT-positive
      neuroblastoma have a dismal outcome. In that analysis event-free survival
      was similarly poor to that with MYCN amplification, but overall survival
      was significantly longer, so 'dismal' means long-term outcome. Limitation:
      the cohort was deliberately enriched for ALT tumours, with survival data
      from German GPOH-trial patients (1991-2018), so it gives no
      population-based estimate.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "about one third of the ALT-positive neuroblastomas had localized disease and were stratified at diagnosis as low or intermediate risk using a standard risk classification system"
    explanation: >-
      Although ALT was associated with stage 4, high-risk disease and older age
      at diagnosis, about a third of the ALT-positive tumours in this study had
      localized disease and were classified as low or intermediate risk at
      diagnosis, so ALT is not confined to high-risk disease at presentation.
      None of the 83 stage 4S tumours screened was ALT-positive. The sentence
      reports the authors' own cohort and says nothing about outcome.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "No difference in event-free or overall survival was observed between patients with ALT-positive tumors stratified into high-risk and those predicted as low/intermediate risk"
    explanation: >-
      In the sequenced, ALT-enriched cohort, event-free and overall survival did
      not differ between patients with ALT-positive tumours classified high risk
      and those classified low or intermediate risk, which the authors read as
      current risk stratification underestimating the poor prognosis of
      ALT-positive tumours. The comparison is retrospective with small groups,
      so the absence of a difference is weak evidence of equivalent outcome, and
      the cohort was deliberately enriched for ALT.
  downstream:
  - target: Unlimited Replicative Potential
    description: >-
      ALT maintains telomere length without telomerase, giving the tumour cells
      that use it an unlimited replicative capacity. High-risk neuroblastoma
      cell lines with neither ALT nor telomerase activity showed continuous
      telomere shortening, and most lost viability in culture.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40638875
      reference_title: "Clinical Significance of TERT Promoter Mutations in Neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Advances in molecular techniques have highlighted the critical role of telomere maintenance mechanisms that stabilize telomeres for unlimited replicative capacity and immortality in the pathogenesis of high-risk neuroblastoma ... Telomere maintenance is mediated by telomerase-dependent (classical) and independent (alternate) pathways."
      explanation: >-
        The introduction of this neuroblastoma clinical cohort study states that
        telomere maintenance mechanisms, which stabilise telomeres for unlimited
        replicative capacity and immortality, have a critical role in high-risk
        neuroblastoma, and that telomere maintenance is mediated by
        telomerase-dependent and telomerase-independent ('alternate') pathways;
        later in the paragraph the authors name this route the alternate
        lengthening of telomeres (ALT) pathway. Support for ALT is indirect
        because the first quoted sentence covers telomere maintenance mechanisms
        as a class. It is cited background about high-risk disease, not this
        study's finding.
    - reference: PMID:24792489
      reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in neuroblastoma cell lines is associated with a lack of MYCN genomic amplification and with p53 pathway aberrations."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a telomerase-independent telomere length maintenance mechanism that enables the unlimited proliferation of a subset of cancer cells."
      explanation: >-
        The opening sentence of this study of 40 neuroblastoma cell lines
        describes alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) as a
        telomerase-independent telomere length maintenance mechanism that
        enables the unlimited proliferation of a subset of cancer cells. It
        names ALT and unlimited proliferation together, but as general
        background about cancer cells rather than a neuroblastoma result, so
        support for neuroblastoma is indirect. The abstract's next sentence says
        only that some neuroblastoma tumours appear to maintain telomere length
        by activating ALT.
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that were non-ALT, low TERT expressing, and lacked telomerase activity showed continuous shortening of telomeres with growth in vitro and 2 of 3 TERT-L/non-ALT cell lines spontaneously lost viability after multiple passages in culture"
      explanation: >-
        Three patient-derived high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that lacked ALT
        as well as telomerase activity shortened their telomeres continuously in
        culture, and 2 of 3 spontaneously lost viability, so losing both
        telomere maintenance mechanisms costs replicative capacity, which
        supports this edge by its converse. Viability held up in the third line,
        which had very high telomere content, so the result shows that a
        maintenance mechanism is required for sustained growth, not that ALT
        alone suffices.
- name: Spontaneous Tumor Regression
  description: >-
    Involution of a neuroblastoma, or its maturation toward
    ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma, without cytotoxic treatment. It is
    seen mainly in infants whose tumours lack MYCN amplification, with
    localized disease or the 4S/MS pattern of metastasis: in the prospective
    NB95-S and NB97 trials, 44 of the 93 infants observed with gross residual
    localized tumour regressed spontaneously, with first signs 1 to 18 months
    after diagnosis and, in 15 of the 44, after the first year of life.
    Regression in this entry covers maturation as well as shrinkage, because
    among mass-screened localized adrenal tumours left in place, the six
    resected after one to four years of observation had all matured toward
    ganglioneuroblastoma, which the authors call a common phenomenon; 16 of 45
    resected in infancy showed the same change. It is not universal
    in the 4S pattern: of 268 evaluable Italian infants with stage 4S disease,
    29 progressed at 4S sites and 28 progressed to stage 4. Mass screening
    gives a figure for how much disease screening finds that never needed
    finding rather than a count of regressions: screening at about one year of
    age produced an estimated 7 overdiagnosed cases per 100,000 children, while
    stage 4 incidence and neuroblastoma mortality stayed similar to the
    unscreened control states. That estimate mixes tumours that would have
    regressed with tumours that would have stayed silent, and it cannot see
    tumours that regressed before the screening age or after clinical
    diagnosis, so it neither measures nor cleanly bounds regression. This node is the
    phenomenon rather than a mechanism; which mechanism produces it is
    unsettled, and the competing candidates are recorded as the entry's
    mechanistic hypothesis groups, two of which carry an edge into this node.
  role: outcome
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest derived neuroblast
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  notes: >-
    This node binds a cell type and no process term. An OLS search of GO for "tumor
    regression" returns nothing, and one for "regression" returns
    developmental classes only; the most general of them, GO:0060033
    anatomical structure regression, is defined as the destruction of an
    anatomical structure as part of its normal progression and has GO:0032502
    developmental process as its parent, so binding it would call tumour
    regression a normal developmental process. An OLS search of HPO for
    "spontaneous regression" returns only HP:0005534 Transient
    myeloproliferative syndrome and one for "tumor regression" returns
    nothing; a pathophysiology node takes no phenotype binding in any case.
    NCIT:C53298 Spontaneous Regression resolves, defined as remission without
    treatment, but it names a clinical course rather than a process, chemical
    entity, gene product or cell type, which are what this node's bindable
    slots take.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:18349403
    reference_title: "Localized infant neuroblastomas often show spontaneous regression: results of the prospective trials NB95-S and NB97."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "For infants with localized neuroblastoma without MYCN amplification, chemotherapy was scheduled only in cases with threatening symptoms; otherwise, the tumor was either resected or observed by ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). ... Of 340 eligible participants, 190 underwent resection, 57 were treated with chemotherapy, and 93 were observed with gross residual tumor. Of those 93 patients with unresected tumors, spontaneous regression was seen in 44, local progression in 28, progression to stage 4S in seven, and progression to stage 4 in four. Time to regression was quite variable, with first signs of regression noted 1 to 18 months after diagnosis and in 15 of 44 patients even after the first year of life."
    explanation: >-
      In the prospective trials NB95-S and NB97, infants with localized
      neuroblastoma without MYCN amplification were given chemotherapy only for
      threatening symptoms; otherwise the tumour was resected or watched by
      ultrasound and MRI. Of 340 eligible participants, 190 underwent
      resection, 57 were given chemotherapy and 93 were observed with gross
      residual tumour. Of these 93, 44 showed spontaneous regression, with
      first signs 1 to 18 months after diagnosis and, in 15 of the 44, after
      the first year of life. This is direct human evidence that localized
      neuroblastoma can regress without resection or chemotherapy, and that
      regression can begin after the first year of life. The 44 of 93 figure
      describes this observed subgroup only and is not a population-wide
      regression rate; the abstract does not say whether the 39 infants whose
      tumours progressed were treated later. The ellipsis skips only the
      RESULTS section label.
  - reference: PMID:29305654
    reference_title: Spontaneous regression of neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastomas are characterized by heterogeneous clinical behavior, from spontaneous regression or differentiation into a benign ganglioneuroma, to relentless progression despite aggressive, multimodality therapy. Indeed, neuroblastoma is unique among human cancers in terms of its propensity to undergo spontaneous regression. The strongest evidence for this comes from the mass screening studies conducted in Japan, North America and Europe and it is most evident in infants with stage 4S disease."
    explanation: >-
      The opening of this single-author review's abstract states four things:
      neuroblastomas range in clinical behaviour from spontaneous regression or
      differentiation into a benign ganglioneuroma to relentless progression
      despite aggressive multimodality therapy; neuroblastoma is unique among
      human cancers in its propensity to undergo spontaneous regression; the
      strongest evidence for this comes from the mass screening studies
      conducted in Japan, North America and Europe; and it is most evident in
      infants with stage 4S disease. These statements are the review's
      synthesis of earlier screening programmes and stage 4S series, not data
      it generated. The quote presents differentiation into a benign
      ganglioneuroma as an alternative outcome to spontaneous regression rather
      than as a form of it. The body of the review qualifies two points.
      Spontaneous regression has also been observed in renal cell carcinoma,
      malignant melanoma, choriocarcinoma and lymphoid malignancies, so
      "unique" refers to how prevalent regression is in neuroblastoma. And
      regression is not restricted to stage 4S, because it can be seen in
      infants with virtually any stage of disease when the tumour is
      biologically favourable.
  - reference: PMID:11685689
    reference_title: Maturation of mass-screened localized adrenal neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Fifty-one mass-screened adrenal neuroblastomas were divided into 2 groups. In infants less than 1 year of age (Group A), 45 neuroblastomas were resected, whereas 6 neuroblastomas were resected after observation in 1- to 4-year-old children (group B). ... Maturation toward ganglioneuroblastoma was observed in 16 neuroblastomas of group A (36%) and 6 neuroblastomas of group B (100%). ... If left untreated, maturation of mass-screened, localized adrenal neuroblastomas is a common phenomenon."
    explanation: >-
      Iwanaka et al. compared the histology of 51 mass-screened localized
      adrenal neuroblastomas: 45 resected in infancy (group A) and 6 resected
      after a period of observation, in children aged 1 to 4 years (group B).
      Maturation toward ganglioneuroblastoma was present in 16 of the 45 infant
      resections (36%) and in all six tumours resected after observation, so
      the 100% is 6 of 6. From this the authors conclude that, left untreated,
      maturation of mass-screened localized adrenal neuroblastoma is common.
      The finding is histological maturation rather than shrinkage or
      disappearance of the tumour, which is why this node counts maturation as
      one course of spontaneous regression. The study compares two different
      groups of tumours rather than repeated samples of the same tumour, and
      the abstract gives neither the length of observation nor how the six
      observed children came to resection, so group B may not represent every
      tumour that was observed. The ellipses skip the comparison and statistics
      sentences, the International Neuroblastoma Pathological Classification
      counts and the mitosis karyorrhexis index result.
  - reference: PMID:11932471
    reference_title: Neuroblastoma screening at one year of age.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The screened group and children in the control area had a similar incidence of stage 4 neuroblastoma ... and a similar rate of death among children with neuroblastoma ... Comparison of the screened group and the children in the control area revealed substantial overdiagnosis in the former group (an estimated rate of 7 cases per 100,000 children ...); the overdiagnosis rate represents children who had neuroblastoma that was diagnosed by screening but who would not benefit from earlier diagnosis and treatment."
    explanation: >-
      German population-based controlled study: urine screening for
      neuroblastoma was offered at about one year of age in 6 of the 16 German
      states from 1995 to 2000, and eligible children in the remaining states
      served as controls, so the comparison is geographic rather than
      randomised. Screened and control children had a similar incidence of
      stage 4 neuroblastoma and a similar neuroblastoma death rate. Comparing
      the two areas also gave an estimated overdiagnosis rate of 7 per 100,000
      children, which the abstract defines as children whose neuroblastoma was
      diagnosed by screening but who would not benefit from earlier diagnosis
      and treatment. The abstract never mentions regression and does not say
      what became of those tumours: reading them as tumours that would have
      regressed or stayed clinically silent is an inference, and the estimate
      cannot separate the two. It therefore neither measures regression nor
      bounds it: a tumour that would have stayed clinically silent counts
      toward the overdiagnosis estimate exactly as one that would have
      regressed, and the estimate is blind to tumours that regressed before
      the screening age or after clinical diagnosis. The ellipses skip the
      bracketed confidence intervals and the point estimates they qualify.
  - reference: PMID:33459514
    reference_title: Metastatic progression in infants diagnosed with stage 4S neuroblastoma. A study of the Italian Neuroblastoma Registry.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of 280 Italian infants diagnosed with stage 4S neuroblastoma between 1979 and 2013 and registered in the Italian Neuroblastoma Registry, 268 were evaluable for this study, of whom 57 developed metastatic progression. ... Progression to stage 4S sites occurred in 29/268 infants (10.8%) (Group A) and to stage 4 in 28/268 (10.4%) (Group B)."
    explanation: >-
      Study of the Italian Neuroblastoma Registry: of 280 infants diagnosed
      with stage 4S neuroblastoma between 1979 and 2013, 268 were evaluable and
      57 of them developed metastatic progression, 29 (10.8%) at stage 4S sites
      and 28 (10.4%) to stage 4. The abstract counts progression rather than
      regression, so the claim that regression is not universal in this pattern
      follows by one inference step: in about one evaluable infant in five, the
      metastatic disease progressed after diagnosis instead of following a
      purely regressing course. The abstract does not say whether any infant
      who progressed at 4S sites later regressed, or how many of the remaining
      211 infants regressed without treatment. The cohort is reported as stage
      4S rather than INRGSS stage MS, and the abstract does not state which 4S
      definition was applied in the earlier years, so the figures bear on stage
      MS only where the two definitions overlap. The ellipsis skips the RESULTS
      section label.
- name: NGF-TRKA Trophic Signaling Withdrawal
  description: >-
    Loss of NGF-dependent TrkA signalling in the neuroblasts of a
    TRKA-expressing tumour, the cellular state on which the
    neurotrophin-deprivation account of spontaneous regression rests. Many more
    sympathetic neuronal precursors are produced during normal development than
    are needed, and those that fail to reach a target undergo developmentally
    programmed cell death, a process set primarily by the TrkA neurotrophin
    receptor and the limiting availability of its ligand NGF at the target
    site. Tumours from infants, especially with low-stage or 4S disease,
    generally express high levels of TrkA, and in patient tumours high TRK
    expression goes with favourable stage, age under one year and normal MYCN
    copy number. Cells cultured from TRK-expressing tumours survive and
    differentiate when NGF is supplied and die when it is withheld. Why
    TrkA-expressing favourable tumours survive at all despite a lack of
    available NGF is unresolved: a developmentally programmed switch from the
    ligand-independent TrkAIII isoform to TrkAI has been proposed as the step
    that makes such a tumour NGF-dependent. The node commits to no mode of
    death; that step is carried by the downstream edge, whose intermediate
    mechanisms state what has been measured and where.
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NTRK1
    term:
      id: hgnc:8031
      label: NTRK1
  - preferred_term: NGF
    term:
      id: hgnc:7808
      label: NGF
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest derived neuroblast
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: neurotrophin TRK receptor signaling pathway
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0048011
      label: neurotrophin TRK receptor signaling pathway
  notes: >-
    No apoptosis term is bound here and no separate cell-death node is added,
    because the mode of death in regressing neuroblastoma is disputed: in
    screening-detected tumours the degenerating cells were fragmented without
    nuclear condensation, essentially lacked caspase-3 activation and apoptotic
    DNA fragmentation, and had ultrastructural features of autophagic
    degeneration, with increased Ras expression in those areas (Kitanaka et
    al., PMID:11880474). That Ras-associated, caspase-independent route is a
    further candidate explanation of regression and is deliberately not
    recorded as a hypothesis group in this entry. GO:0048011 is bound rather
    than GO:0038180 nerve growth factor signaling pathway, which resolves and
    is not obsolete but whose definition covers the p75 low-affinity NGF
    receptor as well as TrkA. GO:0048011 is not TrkA-specific either, since its
    own label names the TRK receptors as a family and so spans TrkA, TrkB and
    TrkC, and GO has no TrkA-only pathway term; it is bound here as the closest
    available term for signalling through a TRK receptor, with the receptor
    identity carried by the NTRK1 gene descriptor on this node. It is the same
    binding, with the same DECREASED modifier, that
    Congenital_Insensitivity_to_Pain carries on its NGF-TRKA trophic signalling
    node.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29305654
    reference_title: Spontaneous regression of neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Those that make a proper connection to a target organ or tissue will survive and those that do not are destined to undergo developmentally programmed cell death"
    explanation: >-
      The developmental premise this node rests on, stated in a review of
      spontaneous regression: of the sympathetic neuronal precursors produced
      during normal development, those that reach a target survive and those
      that do not die by a developmentally programmed route. Graded
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the review is restating developmental
      neurobiology it did not produce, and OTHER rather than HUMAN_CLINICAL
      because the sentence describes normal sympathetic development and not a
      human clinical observation; the underlying developmental work the review
      cites is largely from animal systems, which is why this item grounds the
      premise rather than the regression claim.
  - reference: PMID:29305654
    reference_title: Spontaneous regression of neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This process is regulated primarily by the TrkA neurotrophin receptor and the limiting availability of its cognate ligand, nerve growth factor (NGF) at their target site."
    explanation: >-
      Names the two things this node is about: the developmental cell-death
      programme in the sentence above is set primarily by the TrkA receptor and
      by how much NGF is available at the target. The review states it as
      established neurobiology rather than as its own measurement, which is
      what the quote role records, and the sentence describes developmental
      neurobiology rather than a human clinical observation, which is why it is
      graded OTHER.
  - reference: PMID:29305654
    reference_title: Spontaneous regression of neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Thus, the conversion from a TrkA-expressing, NGF-independent neuroblastoma to a NGF-dependent tumor could result simply from a developmentally programmed isoform switch from TrkAIII to TrkAI."
    explanation: >-
      The review's own proposal for why a TrkA-expressing favourable tumour
      survives at all before becoming NGF-dependent: a developmentally
      programmed switch from the ligand-independent TrkAIII isoform to TrkAI.
      Quoted from the 2018 review rather than the same author's 2014 one, which
      states the direction of the switch the other way round; the node's
      description follows the 2018 direction. Graded indirect because the
      sentence is explicitly a could, a mechanism the review proposes rather
      than one it or anyone cited here has shown in a regressing tumour, and
      OTHER because a proposed mechanism drawn from isoform work in cells is
      not a human clinical observation.
  - reference: PMID:8441429
    reference_title: Association between high levels of expression of the TRK gene and favorable outcome in human neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "TRK expression strongly correlated with favorable tumor stage (I, II, and IVS vs. III and IV), younger age (< 1 year vs. > or = 1 year), normal N-myc copy number, and low level of N-myc expression."
    explanation: >-
      This results sentence reports that TRK expression strongly correlated
      with favourable tumour stage (I, II and IVS versus III and IV), age under
      one year, normal N-myc copy number and low N-myc expression. The
      abstract's methods say TRK messenger RNA was measured in frozen tumour
      samples from 77 patients; the quoted sentence itself does not name the
      cohort. The abstract uses the 1993 names: it describes TRK as the
      proto-oncogene encoding the primary component of the nerve growth factor
      receptor in neuroblastoma, and HGNC lists TRK and TRKA as aliases of
      NTRK1 (hgnc:8031), while N-myc is MYCN. HGNC gives the approved name
      nerve growth factor receptor to a different gene, NGFR, so the receptor
      measured here is TrkA. The sentence correlates TRK expression with stage,
      age and N-myc status rather than with outcome, and it observes neither
      NGF withdrawal nor regression, so it bears on this node only by
      inference: the favourable group includes stage IVS, the stage associated
      with spontaneous regression, but also localized stages I and II, whose
      capacity to regress this study did not assess.
  - reference: PMID:8441429
    reference_title: Association between high levels of expression of the TRK gene and favorable outcome in human neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "In primary cultures of neuroblastoma cells expressing TRK, exposure to nerve growth factor induced early gene expression and neurite outgrowth, but deprivation of nerve growth factor led to neuronal cell death."
    explanation: >-
      Nakagawara et al. tested two primary neuroblastomas that expressed TRK,
      the gene encoding the NGF receptor TrkA, in primary culture. Exposure to
      nerve growth factor induced early gene expression and neurite outgrowth,
      and deprivation of nerve growth factor led to neuronal cell death. This
      is an in-vitro demonstration, in cells cultured from patients' tumours,
      that such cells can depend on NGF for survival, which is the cellular
      premise of the trophic-withdrawal account of regression. The abstract
      names the outcome only as neuronal cell death, without specifying the
      death pathway, and the culture result rests on two tumours. Graded
      IN_VITRO because the quoted result comes from primary cultures of tumour
      cells, although the same paper's cohort analysis is a human clinical
      study.
  downstream:
  - target: Spontaneous Tumor Regression
    description: >-
      The neurotrophin-deprivation account of spontaneous regression: a tumour
      whose cells have become dependent on NGF through TrkA regresses when NGF
      is not available in its microenvironment. The edge is indirect because no
      study has observed NGF becoming limiting in a regressing patient tumour;
      what the cited work measured is stated in the intermediate mechanisms
      below.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - regression_trka_ngf_deprivation
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Programmed death of TRKA-expressing tumour cells deprived of NGF, shown in cells cultured from TRK-expressing primary tumours rather than in a regressing tumour"
    - "Induction of the dependence receptor UNC5D with E2F1 and p53 on NGF withdrawal, shown in cultured cells from two primary favourable-biology tumours rather than in a regressing tumour"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:8441429
      reference_title: Association between high levels of expression of the TRK gene and favorable outcome in human neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "A tumor with a functional nerve growth factor receptor may be dependent on the neurotrophin nerve growth factor for survival and may regress in its absence, allowing a new approach to the treatment of certain patients with neuroblastoma."
      explanation: >-
        The authors' concluding hypothesis, not an observed mechanism: a
        neuroblastoma with a functional NGF receptor (TRK, that is TrkA) may
        depend on NGF for survival and may regress without it. It rests on two
        results in the same abstract, a correlation in tumours from 77 patients
        (high TRK expression went with favourable stage including IVS, age
        under one year, and five-year cumulative survival of 86% against 14%)
        and the death of cultured cells from TRK-expressing primary tumours
        deprived of NGF. Support for this edge is indirect because the sentence
        never mentions spontaneous regression and its closing clause presents
        the absence of NGF as a route to treatment, so applying it to
        spontaneous regression takes the further step that NGF becomes limiting
        in an untreated tumour. The abstract reports no measurement of NGF in
        patients and no regression outcome.
    - reference: PMID:23778138
      reference_title: Dependence receptor UNC5D mediates nerve growth factor depletion-induced neuroblastoma regression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "NGF withdrawal strongly upregulated UNC5D, E2F1, and p53 in human primary favorable NBs."
      explanation: >-
        In ex vivo cultures of cells from two human favourable-biology
        neuroblastomas (9 months, stage 1; 18 months, stage 3; both
        single-copy MYCN with high TRKA expression), withdrawal of NGF by
        adding an anti-NGF antibody strongly upregulated the dependence
        receptor UNC5D together with E2F1 and p53. The paper notes that p53 and
        E2F1 induction after NGF depletion was already known, so UNC5D is the
        new element; the value of the result here is that the
        trophic-withdrawal response is measured in human neuroblastoma cells
        rather than only in a surrogate system. The quoted sentence reports the
        induction alone: the death programme it initiates (caspase 2/3 cleavage
        of UNC5D, nuclear translocation of the released fragment and its
        interaction with E2F1, and inhibition of both cleavage and apoptosis by
        netrin-1) is reported in other parts of the same paper. The route is
        not specific to neuroblastoma, since the same paper reports UNC5D
        induction and caspase cleavage across several cell lines and apoptotic
        stimuli and calls UNC5D a common proapoptotic molecule. Indirect for
        this edge because induction in culture is not regression; the authors
        also report no significant increase in UNC5D mRNA in the 6 stage 4s
        tumours among the 108 primary cases they tested, which they attribute
        to the small number and to such cells having already died.
    - reference: PMID:23778138
      reference_title: Dependence receptor UNC5D mediates nerve growth factor depletion-induced neuroblastoma regression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "It should be noted that induction and nuclear localization of UNC5D were observed in regressing NB tissue obtained from a patient in stage 1, who had been found by mass screening at the age of 6 months"
      explanation: >-
        The other side of the same paper's tumour-tissue evidence, cited here
        so the item above is not read as a uniformly negative result in
        patients: in regressing tissue from a mass-screened stage 1 tumour,
        UNC5D was induced and localized to the nucleus, and the authors read
        that as evidence that UNC5D is involved in regression. The same figure
        reports netrin-1 as almost negative in regressing tumours, which is the
        ligand-withdrawal condition the dependence-receptor account needs.
        Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because the observation is immunostaining of
        patient tumour tissue, and indirect because it rests on one patient's
        tumour and on staining pattern rather than on a measured rate of cell
        death.
- name: Absence of a Telomere Maintenance Mechanism
  description: >-
    Neuroblastomas in which neither route to telomere maintenance is present:
    no TERT rearrangement, no MYCN amplification, no elevated TERT expression
    in the absence of those alterations, and no ALT-associated PML nuclear
    bodies. Of 208 pretreatment neuroblastomas assessed for both telomerase
    activation and ALT, 99 met none of these criteria; they came mainly from
    young patients (mean age at diagnosis 378 days), and 96 of the 99 were from
    patients classified clinical low or intermediate risk, the other three from
    young stage 4 patients. This node is the mirror image of the entry's
    Telomerase Activation and Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres nodes, and
    carries the same two process terms with the modifier ABSENT. Whether the
    absence produces regression is unsettled, and the downstream edge records
    it as a hypothesis group of its own.
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: telomere maintenance via telomerase
    modifier: ABSENT
    term:
      id: GO:0007004
      label: telomere maintenance via telomerase
  - preferred_term: telomere maintenance via recombination
    modifier: ABSENT
    term:
      id: GO:0000722
      label: telomere maintenance via recombination
  notes: >-
    Two bindings with the modifier ABSENT, rather than one on the parent
    GO:0000723 telomere maintenance: OLS lists GO:0016233 telomere capping and
    GO:0032201 telomere maintenance via semi-conservative replication among
    that parent's children, and both continue in tumours that do not lengthen
    their telomeres, so ABSENT on the parent would overstate what is missing.
    What is absent is telomere lengthening by either route. The node carries no
    genes on purpose: TERT and ATRX each have their own record in the genetic
    section of this entry, and naming either here would auto-link that record
    into a node describing the absence of a mechanism. No conforms_to is
    declared either; the nearest module node,
    enabling_replicative_immortality#Progressive Telomere Attrition, binds
    GO:0010833 and carries a downstream crisis edge that this entry does not
    model.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30523111
    reference_title: A mechanistic classification of clinical phenotypes in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "we considered tumors telomere maintenance positive if they harbored TERT rearrangements or MYCN amplification, elevated TERT expression in the absence of these alterations, or were positive for APBs as a marker of ALT ... Neuroblastomas lacking telomere maintenance were mainly derived from young patients (mean age at diagnosis, 378 days; fig. S17A) classified as clinical low or intermediate risk(96 of 99 cases; P < 0.001)"
    explanation: >-
      In this patient cohort, 208 of 416 sequenced pretreatment neuroblastomas
      were assessed for telomere maintenance. A tumour counted as telomere
      maintenance positive if it carried a TERT rearrangement or MYCN
      amplification, had elevated TERT expression in the absence of those
      alterations, or was positive for ALT-associated PML nuclear bodies as a
      marker of ALT. The 99 tumours meeting none of these criteria came mainly
      from young patients (mean age at diagnosis 378 days), and 96 of the 99
      were from patients classified clinical low or intermediate risk; the
      remaining three came from young stage 4 patients. The quote defines the
      state this node names and gives its clinical profile at diagnosis; it
      reports no regression, which is the downstream edge's claim. The authors
      caution that classifying tumours by a TERT expression threshold carries
      some risk of misclassification from tumour cell content or RNA integrity.
      The second quoted sentence restates the denominator of 99, so the
      ellipsis bridges prose the claim does not rely on. The source's own
      missing space in "risk(96" is kept verbatim.
  downstream:
  - target: Spontaneous Tumor Regression
    description: >-
      The telomere-shortening account of spontaneous regression: a tumour that
      maintains its telomeres by neither route cannot sustain indefinite
      proliferation, so its telomere reserve is drawn down. The absence is
      proposed as a precondition for the tumour to involute or differentiate
      rather than as a sufficient cause: this entry's own Unlimited Replicative
      Potential node records high-risk tumours without significant telomere
      lengthening activity whose cells kept proliferating. The edge is indirect because the steps
      between the missing mechanism and the regression have not been observed
      in a regressing tumour, and because the source states the absence as a
      prerequisite, a necessary condition, rather than as a cause.
    hypothesis_groups:
    - regression_absent_telomere_maintenance
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Progressive telomere attrition ending in senescence, crisis or cell death, inferred from the absence of a maintenance mechanism rather than observed in a regressing tumour"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:30523111
      reference_title: A mechanistic classification of clinical phenotypes in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Indeed, we observed that the outcome of patients whose tumors lacked telomere maintenance (n = 99) was excellent, irrespective of the presence of RAS or p53 pathway mutations (Fig. 4A). Fifty-seven of these patients had never received cytotoxic treatment, including 18 cases with documented spontaneous regression (Fig. 2A and table S10)."
      explanation: >-
        In the same cohort, the 99 patients whose tumours lacked a telomere
        maintenance mechanism had an excellent outcome whatever their RAS or
        p53 pathway mutation status; 57 of them had never received cytotoxic
        treatment, and 18 of those 57 had documented spontaneous regression.
        This is co-occurrence of an absent mechanism with regression in an
        observational cohort rather than a demonstration that the absence
        causes regression, and the quoted passage gives no comparator: how
        often tumours that did have a maintenance mechanism regressed is not
        stated. Spontaneous regression can only be documented in patients
        managed without cytotoxic treatment, and 96 of these 99 tumours came
        from patients classified low or intermediate risk, a group the paper
        says receives limited or no cytotoxic treatment, so the counts partly
        reflect risk-adapted management.
- name: Unlimited Replicative Potential
  description: >-
    The ability of tumour cells to keep dividing indefinitely, which a telomere
    maintenance mechanism (telomerase activation or ALT) provides. Its binding,
    increased cell population proliferation, follows the module node it conforms
    to and means expansion continuing past the limit that telomere shortening
    sets on normal cells, not a faster division rate: ALT-positive
    neuroblastomas proliferate more slowly than telomerase-activated ones.
    Aggressive neuroblastomas show a prolonged evolution during which they
    acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms, whereas tumours with a favourable
    prognosis expand clonally after a short evolution. In pretreatment
    neuroblastomas, patients whose tumours lacked a telomere maintenance
    mechanism had an excellent prognosis and those whose tumours had one did
    substantially worse. Within high-risk disease the picture is less clear: in
    one cohort the telomere maintenance groups differed in overall but not in
    event-free survival, and a subset of high-risk tumours lacks significant
    telomere lengthening activity, with cells derived from them proliferating
    for more than 200 population doublings while their telomeres shortened.

  - preferred_term: cell population proliferation
    modifier: INCREASED

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30523111
    reference_title: "A mechanistic classification of clinical phenotypes in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We found that patients whose tumors lacked telomere maintenance mechanisms had an excellent prognosis, whereas the prognosis of patients whose tumors harbored telomere maintenance mechanisms was substantially worse."
    explanation: >-
      In a patient cohort, 208 of 416 sequenced pretreatment neuroblastomas were
      assessed for both telomerase activation (MYCN amplification, TERT
      rearrangement or high TERT expression) and ALT (ALT-associated PML nuclear
      bodies). Patients whose tumours lacked a telomere maintenance mechanism
      had an excellent prognosis, while those whose tumours had one did
      substantially worse. Indirect for this node: an outcome association does
      not measure replicative capacity, and the link rests on telomere
      maintenance being essential for immortal proliferation, a premise the
      paper takes from earlier work.
  - reference: PMID:32291317
    reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Event-free survival was similar among TERT-high, ALT+, or TERT-low/non-ALT patients. However, overall survival (OS) for TERT-low/non-ALT patients was significantly higher relative to TERT-high or ALT patients (log-rank test; P < 0.01) independent of current clinical and molecular prognostic markers."
    explanation: >-
      In 107 stage 4 high-risk patients diagnosed after 18 months of age,
      grouped by C-circle (ALT) status and TERT mRNA above or below the median,
      event-free survival did not differ significantly across the three groups
      (P = 0.137), while overall survival was significantly higher for
      TERT-low/non-ALT patients. The authors attribute this to more successful
      salvage therapy after an event, and hypothesise that tumours lacking a
      telomere maintenance mechanism keep eroding their telomeres, which
      eventually lets salvage therapy eradicate them. Indirect for this node:
      survival does not measure replicative capacity, and the link rests on that
      telomere-erosion hypothesis. Limitations are a single cohort not uniformly
      treated on current protocols and a median TERT cutoff that may not be
      optimal.
  - reference: PMID:28636942
    reference_title: "Extensive Proliferation of Human Cancer Cells with Ever-Shorter Telomeres."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we show that a subset of high-risk neuroblastomas (with ~50% 5-year mortality) lacked significant TLM activity."
    explanation: >-
      Bears against this node as a universal feature of high-risk neuroblastoma,
      though not against it in tumours that maintain their telomeres. In patient
      tumours the authors identify a subset of high-risk neuroblastomas that
      lacked significant telomere lengthening mechanism (TLM) activity, TLM
      being their term for telomerase or alternative lengthening of telomeres.
      Indirect from this sentence alone, because the abstract also raises an
      unrecognised lengthening mechanism or a false-negative assay; the
      continued telomere shortening in cells derived from these tumours argues
      against both. The ~50% 5-year mortality describes the high-risk category
      the subset was drawn from, and the abstract gives neither the subset's
      size nor the assay.
  - reference: PMID:28636942
    reference_title: "Extensive Proliferation of Human Cancer Cells with Ever-Shorter Telomeres."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Cancer cells derived from these highly aggressive tumors initially had long telomeres and proliferated for >200 population doublings with ever-shorter telomeres."
    explanation: >-
      Cell lines derived from the high-risk neuroblastomas that lacked
      significant TLM activity grew for more than 200 population doublings while
      their telomeres kept shortening, so their extensive proliferation drew
      down a finite telomere reserve rather than reflecting unlimited
      replicative potential. Continued shortening over that many doublings
      argues against a false-negative assay or an unrecognised maintenance
      mechanism. Indirect because the inference to tumour behaviour is from cell
      culture.
  - reference: PMID:36973454
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma arises in early fetal development and its evolutionary duration predicts outcome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastomas with favorable prognosis expand clonally after short evolution, whereas aggressive neuroblastomas show prolonged evolution during which they acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms."
    explanation: >-
      The quoted conclusion comes from deep whole-genome sequencing and
      molecular-clock analysis of patient neuroblastomas covering the clinical
      spectrum: aggressive tumours evolve over a prolonged period and acquire
      telomere maintenance mechanisms during it, whereas favourable-prognosis
      tumours expand clonally after a short evolution. An independent cohort (n
      = 86) was assembled to test the outcome prediction from the duration of
      evolution; the telomere maintenance enrichment behind this conclusion was
      computed on both cohorts pooled. Indirect for this node: the sentence is
      about when telomere maintenance is acquired, and the link to replicative
      capacity rests on telomere maintenance being what confers it. The order of
      events is reconstructed from single tumour samples, and the rearrangements
      conferring telomere maintenance cannot themselves be timed from mutation
      densities.
  - reference: PMID:36973454
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma arises in early fetal development and its evolutionary duration predicts outcome."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "12% of early-MRCA tumors but 81% of late-MRCA tumors gained telomere maintenance - via MYCN amplification, ALT or TERT rearrangement - in the combined discovery and validation cohorts"
    explanation: >-
      Across the pooled discovery and validation cohorts, telomere maintenance
      - by MYCN amplification, ALT or TERT rearrangement - had been gained in
      81% of patient tumours whose most recent common ancestor emerged late,
      after a long evolution, against 12% of those with an early common
      ancestor. This quantifies the enrichment behind the timing conclusion. It
      is prevalence by evolutionary class rather than a timing measurement, and
      the authors state that these small rearrangements cannot be timed from
      mutation densities, so acquisition during the prolonged evolution follows
      by inference.
- name: Primary Tumor Growth and Local Mass Effect
  description: >-
    Growth of the primary tumor at its site of origin along the sympathetic
    nervous system, and the pressure it exerts on, or its growth into,
    neighboring structures. About three-quarters of primary tumors arise in the
    abdomen or pelvis, half of these in the adrenal medulla, about a fifth in
    the posterior mediastinum and about a twentieth in the neck, and the local
    signs follow from the site. An abdominal primary can present as a palpable
    abdominal mass, abdominal distension or abdominal pain. A paravertebral
    tumor can grow through the neural foramina into the spinal canal and
    compress the spinal cord or nerve roots. Horner syndrome is seen mostly with
    localized disease, often with cervical or thoracic tumors, and is attributed
    to mass effect of the tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye.
    Compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma is the usual explanation
    offered for hypertension at diagnosis, but a registry survey of hypertensive
    children could not demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and
    compression of the renal vascular pedicle. Cells leaving the primary tumor
    give rise to metastases at distant sites.
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neuroblastoma tumor cell
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  locations:
  - preferred_term: adrenal medulla
    term:
      id: UBERON:0001236
      label: adrenal medulla
  - preferred_term: paraspinal sympathetic ganglia
    term:
      id: UBERON:0001807
      label: paravertebral ganglion
  notes: >-
    The node has no upstream edge from Unlimited Replicative Potential:
    neuroblastomas with a favorable prognosis expand clonally after a short
    evolution, whereas aggressive ones acquire telomere maintenance mechanisms
    during a prolonged evolution (PMID:36973454), so a primary tumor can grow
    without one.

    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastoma is a malignant tumor of neural crest origin that may arise anywhere along the sympathetic ganglia or within the adrenal medulla. ... Seventy-five percent of neuroblastomas originate within the abdomen or pelvis, and half of these occur within the adrenal medulla, whereas 20% originate within the posterior mediastinum and 5% within the neck."
    explanation: >-
      Review abstract: neuroblastoma may arise anywhere along the sympathetic
      ganglia or within the adrenal medulla, and 75% of primary tumors originate
      in the abdomen or pelvis (half of these in the adrenal medulla), 20% in the
      posterior mediastinum and 5% in the neck. This supports the node's account
      of where primary tumors grow, which decides the local signs each can
      produce. It is a review summary rather than a cohort reported by the paper,
      and it does not itself describe mass effect.

  - target: Horner Syndrome
    description: >-
      Horner syndrome arises mostly with localized disease, often with cervical
      or thoracic tumors, and can be the presenting sign. It is attributed to
      mass effect of the tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye; the
      cited series show its association with tumor site and localized disease
      rather than the nerve involvement itself. Horner syndrome can also follow
      surgical resection of the tumor, a complication of treatment that this
      edge does not cover.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Tumor involvement of the cervical or upper thoracic sympathetic pathway to the eye"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:6493702
      reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Unilateral Horner's syndrome occurred in 14 children, as the presenting sign in 9, related to localized disease in 11 and in a favorable location (cervical or thoracic neuroblastoma) in 8."
      explanation: >-
        In a retrospective series of 405 children with neuroblastoma seen at the
        Hospital for Sick Children, unilateral Horner syndrome occurred in 14,
        as the presenting sign in 9; it was related to localized disease in 11
        and to a cervical or thoracic tumor in 8. That ties the sign to the
        primary tumor rather than to metastases. Indirect for this edge: the
        abstract reports tumor site and extent, not involvement of the
        sympathetic pathway, and does not say whether the cases that were not
        presenting signs followed surgery.

      snippet: "Horner syndrome and opsoclonus are infrequent manifestations of neuroblastic tumor mass effect on the sympathetic innervation of the eye."
      explanation: >-
        In the discussion of a population-based study of neuroblastoma in
        Olmsted County, Minnesota, the authors, citing earlier reports,
        describe Horner syndrome as an infrequent manifestation of mass effect
        of a neuroblastic tumor on the sympathetic innervation of the eye, which
        is the mechanism this edge records. It is a statement drawn from the
        literature, not a finding of this cohort, in which no child had Horner
        syndrome. The sentence also groups opsoclonus with Horner syndrome; that
        clause is not used here, because this entry records
        opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome as immune-mediated rather than as

    - reference: PMID:33174155

      explanation: >-
        In a retrospective single-center series of 119 children with
        neuroblastic tumors (108 neuroblastomas, 9 ganglioneuroblastomas and 2

        support the edge; that mass effect of the tumor caused them is an

        post-surgical cases are a complication of treatment that this edge
        does not explain, so counts of Horner syndrome in neuroblastoma can
        include cases from surgery. A small series.
  - target: Spinal Cord Compression
    description: >-
      A paravertebral tumor can extend through the neural foramina into the

      radicular pain, motor deficit up to paraplegia, and sphincter
      dysfunction. Extension into the spinal canal does not always cause
      symptoms: in a prospective cohort selected for it, a third of the
      children were asymptomatic at enrollment.
