  - target: Hypertension
    description: >-
      Compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma by the tumor, with a
      renin-mediated rise in blood pressure, is the usual explanation offered
      for hypertension at diagnosis, and such hypertension frequently resolves
      after resection. The cited sources state this explanation rather than
      demonstrate it, and the link is contested. A registry survey of
      hypertensive children could not demonstrate a correlation between
      hypertension and compression of the renal vascular pedicle, although it
      found involvement of the renal pedicle to be the only risk factor
      consistently associated with hypertension persisting after surgery. In a
      single-center series of children with at least stage II hypertension,
      four had radiologic evidence of renal compression, but renin was normal
      in all four children in whom it was measured.

    - "Renin-mediated rise in blood pressure after compression of the renal artery or renal parenchyma"

      explanation: >-

  - target: Metastatic Dissemination
    description: >-
      Tumor cells spread from the primary tumor through the lymphatic and
      hematogenous systems and establish metastases at distant sites. Tumors
      with unfavorable clinical behavior combine locally invasive growth with
      widespread metastatic dissemination, and orbital metastases mostly arise
      from an abdominal primary.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:

      explanation: >-
        The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group Biology Committee's
        consensus report states that neuroblastomas with unfavorable clinical
        behavior have a high propensity for locally invasive growth and for
        widespread metastatic dissemination through the lymphatic and
        hematogenous systems. This supports the edge and names the routes
        recorded as its intermediates. It is a synthesis of earlier work rather
        than data from the report, and it describes tumors with unfavorable
        behavior, not the limited metastatic pattern of stage MS.
    - reference: PMID:6493702
      reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "In 53 of 60 cases with orbital metastases the neuroblastoma originated in the abdomen."
      explanation: >-
        In the Hospital for Sick Children series, the neuroblastoma had
        originated in the abdomen in 53 of the 60 children with orbital
        metastases, so these metastases had spread from a primary tumor at a
        distant site. Indirect: the sentence gives where the primary tumors
        lay, not how tumor cells left them, and it covers orbital metastases
        only.
- name: Metastatic Dissemination
  description: >-
    Spread of neuroblastoma cells from the primary tumor to distant sites,
    where they establish metastases. In 648 children with stage IV or IVS
    disease on two Children's Cancer Group protocols, metastases at diagnosis
    were in bone marrow (70.5%), bone (55.7%), lymph nodes (30.9%), liver
    (29.6%), and intracranial and orbital sites (18.2%), and rarely in lung or
    the central nervous system. Skeletal and marrow metastases account for bone
    pain, and orbital metastases for proptosis. Marrow infiltration has been
    associated with anemia and thrombocytopenia, but not in every series, and
    two series found anemia common with or without infiltration. In the
    metastatic pattern of INRGSS stage MS, in children younger than 18 months,
    metastases are confined to skin, liver and/or bone marrow; the liver is the
    main site and can enlarge enough to compress vital structures, and skin
    metastases present as subcutaneous nodules.
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  conforms_to: "invasion_and_metastasis#Metastatic Colonization"
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: disseminated neuroblastoma cell
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  biological_processes:

    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0008283
      label: cell population proliferation
  locations:

  - preferred_term: bone

  notes: >-
    The binding to GO:0008283 cell population proliferation, modifier
    INCREASED, follows the module node this node conforms to, in which
    disseminated tumor cells resume proliferation at the distant site.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:10363850
    reference_title: "Metastatic sites in stage IV and IVS neuroblastoma correlate with age, tumor biology, and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The incidence of metastatic sites at diagnosis was 70.5% in bone marrow, 55.7% in bone, 30.9% in lymph nodes, 29.6% in liver, 18.2% in intracranial and orbital sites, 3.3% in lung, and 0.6% in CNS."
    explanation: >-
      Among the 648 patients with stage IV or IVS neuroblastoma registered on
      Children's Cancer Group protocols 3881 and 3891, metastases at diagnosis
      were in bone marrow in 70.5%, bone in 55.7%, lymph nodes in 30.9%, liver
      in 29.6%, intracranial and orbital sites in 18.2%, lung in 3.3% and the
      central nervous system in 0.6%, with site data supplied by the treating
      institutions. This supports the node's metastatic sites and their order of
      frequency. The figures pool stage IV and IVS, and the abstract gives no
      frequency for skin metastases.
  downstream:
  - target: Bone Pain
    description: >-
      Skeletal and bone marrow metastases cause bone pain, which can be diffuse
      and intense enough to stop a child moving freely.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:29995142
      reference_title: "CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROBLASTOMA: 21 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AT THE INSTITUTO DE ONCOLOGIA PEDIÁTRICA, IN SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Not infrequently, patients seek out a doctor with complaints due to the metastases: diffuse bone pain, anemia, pancytopenia, irritability, ocular proptosis, periorbitary bruising, nodules in the skull, etc. The bone pain can be intense and prevent the child from moving freely."
      explanation: >-
        In the discussion of the São Paulo series, directly after reporting that
        46% of its patients had distant metastases at diagnosis, mainly in bone
        marrow and the skeleton, the authors state that patients often come to a
        doctor with complaints due to the metastases, first among them diffuse
        bone pain, and that the bone pain can be intense and prevent the child
        from moving freely. This supports the edge directly. The sentences are
        the authors' general clinical statement rather than a measured result
        of the series.
  - target: Proptosis
    description: >-
      Orbital metastases infiltrating the periorbital bones cause proptosis
      and periorbital ecchymosis, often on both sides.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:6493702
      reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Proptosis or periorbital ecchymosis due to orbital metastases was present in 60 of 80 children (bilaterally in 33)."
      explanation: >-
        In the Hospital for Sick Children series, proptosis or periorbital
        ecchymosis due to orbital metastases was present in 60 of the 80
        children with ophthalmic involvement, bilaterally in 33. The authors
        attribute the sign to orbital metastases, which is the edge's claim. The
        count combines proptosis with periorbital ecchymosis, so it does not
        give how many of the 60 had proptosis.
    - reference: PMID:29995142
      reference_title: "CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROBLASTOMA: 21 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AT THE INSTITUTO DE ONCOLOGIA PEDIÁTRICA, IN SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Proptosis and periorbital bruising are frequent and result from the way the tumor infiltrates the periorbital bones."
      explanation: >-
        In the introduction of the São Paulo series, citing earlier work, the
        authors state that proptosis and periorbital bruising are frequent
        and result from the way the tumor infiltrates the periorbital bones.
        This supports the edge's mechanism. It is background, not a finding of
        the series.
  - target: Anemia
    description: >-
      Infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells has been associated with
      anemia at diagnosis, in one series with infiltration by more than 10%
      malignant cells. The link is contested: two other series found anemia
      common in children with and without marrow infiltration and attributed it
      to iron or nutritional deficiency. The cited series report associations
      and do not measure how infiltration would lower red cell production.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:28801367
      reference_title: "Comparison of Hematological Aspects between Neuroblastoma Patients with and without Bone Marrow Infiltration."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Erythrocytopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia were significantly (p<0.05) associated with marrow infiltration of >10% malignant cells."
      explanation: >-
        In a retrospective series of 111 patients, 62 with marrow infiltration,
        anemia was significantly associated with infiltration by more than 10%
        malignant cells. This supports the edge. Indirect: it is an association
        in one series, not a demonstration that infiltration causes the anemia,
        and the abstract gives no anemia definition.
    - reference: PMID:37323595
      reference_title: "Study of Hemato-morphological Features in Neuroblastoma Infiltrating Marrow."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "No significant correlation was noted for anemia in patients of neuroblastoma with and without infiltration, presumably due to the frequency of iron insufficiency in India rather than related to the illness itself."
      explanation: >-
        In a retrospective series of 79 newly diagnosed patients referred for
        staging marrow examination at one North Indian center, anemia was not
        significantly correlated with marrow infiltration, and the authors
        attribute it to iron insufficiency rather than to the disease. The
        paper's table gives anemia in 36 of 44 patients with infiltration
        (81.82%) and 26 of 35 without (74.29%; p = 0.594). This bears against the
        edge in this setting. Indirect: a null association in a population with
        common iron deficiency does not exclude infiltration contributing to
        anemia elsewhere.
    - reference: PMID:25548446
      reference_title: "Bone Marrow Involvement in Neuroblastoma: A Study of Hemato-morphological Features."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Anemia, though was common in both group of patients with and without infiltration, it is thought to be due to nutritional deficiency rather than due to tumor infiltration in marrow."
      explanation: >-
        In 44 newly diagnosed children aged 6 months to 11 years who were
        referred for staging marrow examination at the Postgraduate Institute
        of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, from 2009 to 2012, 24
        had marrow infiltration. Anemia was present in 87.5% of the children
        with infiltration and 75% of those without, and the authors attribute
        it to nutritional deficiency rather than to infiltration. This bears
        against the edge. Indirect: the attribution is the authors'
        interpretation, the series is small, and it does not exclude
        infiltration contributing to anemia in some children.
  - target: Thrombocytopenia
    description: >-
      Infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells has been associated with
      thrombocytopenia at diagnosis in two series, in one of them with
      infiltration by more than 10% malignant cells, although a third series
      found it no more frequent with marrow involvement than without. The
      cited series report associations and do not measure how infiltration
      lowers the platelet count.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES

      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT

      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Erythrocytopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia were significantly (p<0.05) associated with marrow infiltration of >10% malignant cells."
      explanation: >-
        In a retrospective series of 111 patients, 62 with marrow infiltration,
        thrombocytopenia was significantly associated with infiltration by more
        than 10% malignant cells. This supports the edge. Indirect: it is an
        association in one series, not a demonstration that infiltration causes
        the thrombocytopenia, and the abstract gives no platelet cut-off.
    - reference: PMID:37323595
      reference_title: "Study of Hemato-morphological Features in Neuroblastoma Infiltrating Marrow."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The bone marrow infiltration was significantly linked to thrombocytopenia (p = 0.043) and nucleated red blood cells (p = 0.003) in peripheral blood."
      explanation: >-
        In the same North Indian series, 44 of 79 patients had marrow
        infiltration at staging, and infiltration was significantly linked to
        thrombocytopenia (p = 0.043); the paper's table gives thrombocytopenia
        in 13 of 44 patients with infiltration (29.55%) and 3 of 35 without
        (8.57%). This supports the edge. Indirect: an association close to the
        significance threshold in one referral series, with no platelet
        cut-off stated.
    - reference: PMID:25548446
      reference_title: "Bone Marrow Involvement in Neuroblastoma: A Study of Hemato-morphological Features."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Of these, 24 cases (54.5 %) showed marrow infiltration. Leucopenia and bicytopenia were significantly (p < 0.05) associated with marrow infiltration. ... Complete blood counts in involved cases showed that ... platelet count below 150 ... (thrombocytopenia) was seen in 8.3 % cases ... In the uninvolved cases anemia was seen in 75 %, leucopenia in none and thrombocytopenia in 10 % cases."
      explanation: >-
        In 44 newly diagnosed children referred for staging marrow examination
        at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research,
        Chandigarh, 24 had marrow infiltration. Thrombocytopenia, a platelet
        count below 150 x 10^9/L, was seen in 8.3% of the children with
        infiltration and 10% of those without, and the authors report
        leucopenia and bicytopenia as the cytopenias significantly associated
        with infiltration. This bears against the edge in this series. Indirect: the series is
        small, and the comparison does not exclude infiltration lowering the
        platelet count in some children.
  - target: Hepatomegaly
    description: >-
      In the INRGSS stage MS pattern the liver is the main metastatic site, and
      extensive liver involvement enlarges the liver, which in young infants
      can compress vital structures, with signs of pulmonary, renal or hepatic
      compromise.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:6727772
      reference_title: "IV-S neuroblastoma: a cooperative study of 30 children."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The most frequent site of widespread disease was the liver (87%). ... Unfavorable features were age less than 2 months and clinical signs of pulmonary, renal, or hepatic embarrassment. These data confirm the need for prompt intervention in the infant who is suffering from compression of these vital structures by the enlarged liver."
      explanation: >-
        In 30 Italian infants with stage IV-S neuroblastoma (1970-1981), the
        liver was the most frequent site of widespread disease (87%).
        Unfavorable features were age under 2 months and clinical signs of
        pulmonary, renal or hepatic compromise, and the authors conclude that
        infants suffering from compression of these vital structures by the
        enlarged liver need prompt intervention. Indirect: the abstract names
        liver spread and an enlarged liver but does not state that the
        enlargement is caused by the metastases. A small series from before the
        INSS, limited to infants younger than 12 months.
  - target: Subcutaneous Nodules
    description: >-
      Skin metastases can present as noncompressible, blue-purple subcutaneous
      nodules, part of the INRGSS stage MS pattern in young children.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39640139
      reference_title: "Metastatic Neuroblastoma Mimicking Multiple Infantile Hemangiomas Diagnosed With Ultrasound."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Here, we present a case of a nine-month-old male infant who presented with multiple noncompressible blue-purple subcutaneous nodules, initially suggestive of atypical deep hemangiomas. ... A subcutaneous mass biopsy showed stroma-poor neuroblastoma infiltrating the fibroadipose and fibroconnective tissues, confirming a diagnosis of neuroblastoma metastatic to the skin."
      explanation: >-
        Case report of a nine-month-old infant with multiple blue-purple
        subcutaneous nodules, first taken for deep hemangiomas, in whom imaging
        found an adrenal mass and liver lesions and biopsy of a subcutaneous
        mass showed neuroblastoma metastatic to the skin. This shows directly
        that the nodules were skin metastases. A single case; the infant also
        had masses in fat and muscle, so the case is not a strict stage MS
        pattern.
- name: Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide Hypersecretion
  description: >-
    Secretion of vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) by tumor cells, the cause
    of a rare watery-diarrhea syndrome. In a French series of 22 patients with
    neuroblastic tumors and watery diarrhea, VIP secretion was confirmed by
    serum assay and/or immunohistochemistry. In 91 children with resected
    neuroblastic tumors, of which about a third were ganglioneuroblastomas, VIP
    was detected in the tumor by immunohistochemistry in 27.5%, and its
    staining intensity was higher in children with diarrhea and in those with
    hypokalemia and was associated with histopathological classification.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: vasoactive intestinal peptide secretion
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0030072
      label: peptide hormone secretion
  chemical_entities:
  - preferred_term: vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: CHEBI:80331
      label: Vasoactive intestinal peptide
  notes: >-
    The node has no upstream edge: VIP-secreting neuroblastic tumors are
    usually associated with differentiation (PMID:19143025), whereas the
    entry's Neural Crest Developmental Arrest node models arrested
    differentiation, and no node models maturation of tumor cells. On
    2026-10-23, OLS4 searches of GO for "vasoactive intestinal peptide
    secretion", "vasoactive intestinal peptide", "vasoactive intestinal
    polypeptide" and "VIP secretion" returned no VIP secretion process: only
    VIP receptor binding and receptor activity terms (GO:0031890, GO:0031891,
    GO:0031892, GO:0004999), glucagon family peptide binding (GO:0120022), and
    cell-type and anatomy terms from other ontologies. None of the direct
    children of GO:0030072 peptide hormone secretion is VIP secretion, so the
    process is bound to GO:0030072 as the closest broader term. The peptide is
    bound to CHEBI:80331 because the NCIT term NCIT:C21442 Vasoactive
    Intestinal Peptide sits under Peptide Hormone and VIP Gene Product, outside
    the Pharmacologic Substance root that the chemical-entity binding admits
    for NCIT.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40082825
    reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "However, recent studies have updated the typical watery-diarrhea syndrome caused by VIP secretion in NB; this is now considered one of the rare digestive tract-related PNS, accounting for less than 3% of all patients with NB"
    explanation: >-
      The discussion of this single-center study, summarizing the literature,
      describes the typical watery-diarrhea syndrome caused by VIP secretion in
      neuroblastoma as a rare paraneoplastic syndrome affecting less than 3% of
      all patients. This supports the node as tumor VIP secretion that causes
      a rare syndrome. It is the authors' summary of earlier studies, not a
      proportion measured in their own series.
  - reference: PMID:19143025
    reference_title: "VIP hypersecretion as primary or secondary syndrome in neuroblastoma: A retrospective study by the Société Française des Cancers de l'Enfant (SFCE)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We conducted a retrospective analysis of the French experience of NTs associated with watery diarrhea due to VIP-secretion. VIP secretion was confirmed by seric dosage and/or immunohistochemistry. ... Twenty-two patients met the diagnostic criteria between 1988 and 2007."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective review by the French pediatric cancer society (SFCE)
      of neuroblastic tumors with watery diarrhea due to VIP secretion, VIP
      secretion was confirmed by serum assay and/or immunohistochemistry, and
      22 patients met the criteria between 1988 and 2007. This supports tumor
      VIP secretion. The abstract does not say how many patients had raised
      serum VIP rather than tumor staining alone, and it covers neuroblastic
      tumors as a group without a breakdown by histological subtype.
  - reference: PMID:40082825
    reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "VIP expression was detected in 25/91 patients with NB (27.5%). VIP expression intensity was significantly increased in children with diarrhea and hypokalemia (P < 0.001, and P < 0.001, respectively)"
    explanation: >-
      In 91 children whose neuroblastic tumors were resected at Shengjing
      Hospital of China Medical University (2015-2021), VIP was detected by
      immunohistochemistry in 25 tumors (27.5%), and staining intensity was
      significantly higher in children with diarrhea and in those with
      hypokalemia. This supports tumor VIP production linked to the syndrome.
      Indirect for secretion: VIP was measured in tumor tissue rather than in
      plasma, so that the tumor released it is an inference. Other limits: the
      series counts ganglioneuroblastoma (31 of the 91) as neuroblastoma, and
      it was selected by resection and mostly low-stage.
  downstream:
  - target: Diarrhea
    description: >-
      VIP released by the tumor binds VPAC1 receptors on intestinal epithelial
      cells and causes secretory, watery diarrhea with ion disturbance;
      resection of the tumor relieves it.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "VIP binding to VPAC1 receptors on intestinal epithelial cells, driving intestinal fluid and electrolyte secretion"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40082825
      reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "VIP is one of the main causes of refractory diarrhea in patients with NB"
      explanation: >-
        The authors' conclusion from their series of 91 resected neuroblastic
        tumors: VIP is one of the main causes of refractory diarrhea in
        patients with neuroblastoma. It rests on tumor VIP staining being
        stronger in children with diarrhea and on the diarrhea of all six
        affected children resolving immediately after resection, not on
        measured plasma VIP. The series counts ganglioneuroblastoma as
        neuroblastoma.
    - reference: PMID:40082825
      reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "In the digestive tract, VIP binds to VPAC1 on intestinal epithelial cells, causing secretory diarrhea and ion disturbance"
      explanation: >-
        Background sentence in the introduction: in the digestive tract,
        vasoactive intestinal peptide binds to VPAC1 receptors on intestinal
        epithelial cells and causes secretory diarrhea and ion disturbance.
        This supports the edge's intermediate step. It is a statement of
        general physiology cited from earlier work, not a finding of this
        study.
    - reference: PMID:40082825
      reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Refractory watery diarrhea was observed in six patients (6.6%), all of whom were immediately relieved after NB surgical resection."
      explanation: >-
        In the same series of 91 children whose tumors were resected,
        refractory watery diarrhea occurred in six, and all six were relieved
        immediately after resection. This supports the edge's statement that
        resection relieves the diarrhea. Indirect: relief after removing the
        tumor shows that the tumor caused the diarrhea; that VIP was the
        mediator rests on the tumor staining, not on plasma VIP measured before
        and after surgery.
    - reference: PMID:19143025
      reference_title: "VIP hypersecretion as primary or secondary syndrome in neuroblastoma: A retrospective study by the Société Française des Cancers de l'Enfant (SFCE)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "In all cases, only surgical excision of the tumor was able to control the digestive symptoms."
      explanation: >-
        In the French SFCE series of 22 patients whose neuroblastic tumors
        secreted VIP, surgical excision of the tumor was the only treatment
        that controlled the digestive symptoms, in every case. This supports
        the edge's statement that resection relieves the diarrhea, in a series
        selected for VIP secretion. Indirect: control by excision shows that
        the tumor drove the symptoms but is not itself a measurement of VIP,
        and the series covers neuroblastic tumors as a group.
- name: Adrenergic and Mesenchymal Cell-State Plasticity
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma tumour cells occupy two transcriptionally divergent
    identity states, and the field names them twice over. van Groningen
    and colleagues name them adrenergic and mesenchymal, defined by a
    super-enhancer contrast between isogenic cell-line pairs. Boeva and
    colleagues, profiling the super-enhancer landscape of neuroblastoma
    cell lines, name a sympathetic noradrenergic identity whose core
    regulatory circuitry module includes PHOX2B, HAND2 and GATA3, an
    NCC-like identity driven by a circuitry module containing AP-1
    transcription factors, and a mixed type. Mesenchymal and NCC-like are
    close but not identical concepts: the first is defined by an
    isogenic-pair super-enhancer contrast, the second by membership of a
    core regulatory circuitry.

    In cell lines and xenografts the switch between the two identities
    arises spontaneously, runs in both directions and is accompanied by
    epigenetic reprogramming. The noradrenergic-to-mesenchymal shift
    occurs in culture; the reverse shift was documented after engraftment
    in mice. Enforced expression of a NOTCH3 intracellular domain drives
    the adrenergic-to-mesenchymal direction with genome-wide remodelling
    of the H3K27ac landscape, and a NOTCH feed-forward loop then
    maintains the induced state. SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling ATPases
    are required to establish the mesenchymal gene-permissive chromatin
    state that facilitates this plasticity.

    In patient tumours the dominant identity is noradrenergic.
    Gene-expression signatures derived from established cell lines fail
    to identify mesenchymal tumour cells in patient tumours, whereas
    signatures developed from early-passage orthotopic patient-derived
    xenografts enable their identification. A minority subpopulation of
    noradrenergic tumour cells co-expresses mesenchymal features, found
    in a subset of tumours rather than in all of them, and the
    mesenchymal-like programme detectable in some pre-treated high-risk
    patient tumours is weakly expressed, sits inside cancer cells that
    remain otherwise adrenergic, and appears distinct from the
    presumptive drug-resistance mesenchymal programmes of cell lines.
    Whether patient tumours also carry a discrete, purely mesenchymal
    tumour-cell population of the kind cultured cells show is unsettled;
    the evidence collected here establishes neither its presence nor its
    exclusion.

    Microenvironmental influence is not one-directional, and the two
    documented cues were measured in different systems. In mouse
    xenografts, cells of either starting identity gave rise to tumours
    with a noradrenergic phenotype, which the authors read as
    microenvironmental pressure towards that state. In cultured cell
    panels, hypoxia shifted adrenergic cells towards mesenchymal gene
    expression.

    The mesenchymal state is not the less malignant of the two: in vivo
    reprogramming of adrenergic cells found mesenchymal and adrenergic
    cells equally oncogenic.
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest cell-like (mesenchymal) tumour cell state
    term:
      id: CL:0011012
      label: neural crest cell
  - preferred_term: adrenergic (noradrenergic) tumour cell state
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: reversible switching between two tumour cell identities
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0090677
      label: reversible differentiation
  - preferred_term: chromatin remodelling accompanying the identity switch
    modifier: DYSREGULATED
    term:
      id: GO:0006338
      label: chromatin remodeling
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28650485

  - reference: PMID:28740262
    reference_title: "Heterogeneity of neuroblastoma cell identity defined by transcriptional circuitries."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "We discovered three types of identity in neuroblastoma cell lines: a sympathetic noradrenergic identity, defined by a CRC module including the PHOX2B, HAND2 and GATA3 transcription factors (TFs); an NCC-like identity, driven by a CRC module containing AP-1 TFs; and a mixed type, further deconvoluted at the single-cell level."
    explanation: >-

      a circuitry module containing AP-1 transcription factors, and a
      mixed type resolved at the single-cell level. The word "including"
      is the source's, so the transcription factors named are circuitry
      members rather than a complete set. Graded IN_VITRO because the
      quoted sentence is explicitly about cell lines, and INDIRECT because
      this abstract never equates its noradrenergic and NCC-like
      identities with the adrenergic and mesenchymal states, so reading it
      onto the two poles of this node takes one inference step.
  - reference: PMID:28740262
    reference_title: "Heterogeneity of neuroblastoma cell identity defined by transcriptional circuitries."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Most neuroblastoma primary tumors express TFs from the noradrenergic and NCC-like modules"
    explanation: >-
      The authors' expression analysis of primary tumours found that most
      tumours express transcription factors from both the noradrenergic
      and the NCC-like modules, so the two identities first defined in
      cell lines are represented in patient material rather than being a

  - reference: PMID:37142597
    reference_title: "Reversible transitions between noradrenergic and mesenchymal tumor identities define cell plasticity in neuroblastoma."

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:37142597

    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

  - reference: PMID:37142597
    reference_title: "Reversible transitions between noradrenergic and mesenchymal tumor identities define cell plasticity in neuroblastoma."

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Accordingly, such a noradrenergic cell identity is systematically observed in single-cell RNA-seq of 18 tumor biopsies and 15 PDX models. Yet, a subpopulation of these noradrenergic tumor cells presents with mesenchymal features that are shared with plasticity models, indicating that the plasticity described in these models has relevance in neuroblastoma patients."

  - reference: PMID:37142597
    reference_title: "Reversible transitions between noradrenergic and mesenchymal tumor identities define cell plasticity in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In our patient tumor dataset, we identified a cluster of noradrenergic tumor cells forming a bridge towards a cluster of normal Schwann and mesenchymal cells and composed of cells of three tumors at diagnosis and one case at relapse. These cells are unambiguously tumor cells exhibiting copy number alterations that co-express markers of a noradrenergic identity and markers of mesenchymal features."

  - reference: PMID:42849441
    reference_title: "Spatial omics resolves adrenergic and mesenchymal cell states in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We show that tumor cells occupy distinct cellular neighborhoods separated from nonmalignant immune and stromal cells, yet established cell line-derived gene expression signatures fail to identify MES neuroblastoma cells"
    explanation: >-
      In a profiling study of 54 neuroblastoma tumours using single-cell

      to identify mesenchymal neuroblastoma cells. The word "established"
      is load-bearing: the signatures tested are published ones, not every
      signature a cell line could yield. The cached record is
      abstract-only, so neither the cohort composition nor the size of any
      mesenchymal cell population is readable, and none is asserted here.
  - reference: PMID:42849441
    reference_title: "Spatial omics resolves adrenergic and mesenchymal cell states in neuroblastoma."

    explanation: >-
      Signatures developed from early-passage orthotopic patient-derived

      because the only experimental system the sentence names is
      xenograft material, which is patient tumour carried in an animal

  - reference: PMID:38898465
    reference_title: "An integrated single-cell RNA-seq map of human neuroblastoma tumors and preclinical models uncovers divergent mesenchymal-like gene expression programs."

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We confirm a weakly expressed, mesenchymal-like program in otherwise adrenergic cancer cells in some pre-treated high-risk patient tumors, but this appears distinct from the presumptive drug-resistance mesenchymal programs evident in cell lines."
    explanation: >-
      An integrated single-cell analysis of published patient tumour
      cohorts alongside the authors' own cell line, xenograft and mouse

      cells that remain otherwise adrenergic, in some pre-treated
      high-risk patient tumours, and reports it as apparently distinct
      from the presumptive drug-resistance mesenchymal programmes of cell
      lines. Both hedges are the source's. The human basis is narrow: one
      pre-treated high-risk tumour from a published cohort plus a
      pre-treated high-risk tumour in the authors' xenograft series, while
      their decomposition of a third dataset found no clear evidence of
      mesenchymal-like cancer cells. The comparator half of the sentence
