- category: Neurologic
  name: Horner Syndrome
  frequency: VERY_RARE
  description: >-
    Unilateral Horner syndrome is a rare sign, seen mostly with localized
    disease and often with cervical or thoracic tumors; it can be the presenting
    sign.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Horner syndrome
    term:
      id: HP:0002277
      label: Horner syndrome
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6493702
    reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "On retrospective review of children seen at the Hospital for Sick Children, ophthalmic involvement was seen in 80 of 405 (20%). ... Unilateral Horner's syndrome occurred in 14 children, as the presenting sign in 9, related to localized disease in 11 and in a favorable location (cervical or thoracic neuroblastoma) in 8."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective single-center series of children seen at the Hospital for
      Sick Children, from a study of ocular involvement in neuroblastoma. Of the
      405 children, 80 had ophthalmic involvement and 14 had unilateral Horner
      syndrome (14/405 = 3.5%), which places Horner syndrome in the VERY_RARE
      band. The series was not limited to one stage or tumor site, so it is used
      for the overall frequency band. Horner syndrome was the presenting sign in
      9 and was related to localized disease in 11, and in 8 the neuroblastoma
      was cervical or thoracic, a location the authors call favorable. The first
      quoted sentence supplies the 405 denominator. The abstract does not say
      whether the cases in which Horner syndrome was not the presenting sign
      were caused by the tumor or followed surgery.
  - reference: PMID:32006485
    reference_title: "Incidence and Prognostic Role of the Ocular Manifestations of Neuroblastoma in Children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There were 523 patients with neuroblastoma in the study cohort. ... A total of 86 patients (16.4%) had ocular manifestations of neuroblastoma, 58 at presentation and 29 during the disease course. The most common findings were ... Horner syndrome in 24 (27.9%). In 16 patients (3.1%), there were only ocular findings at presentation, including ... 7 (1.3%) with Horner syndrome"
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective cohort study of 523 patients with neuroblastoma diagnosed at
      a tertiary care pediatric hospital. Horner syndrome was recorded in 24 of
      the 523 (24/523 = 4.6%), which is within the VERY_RARE band but close to
      its upper limit. The 27.9% in the quote is a share of the 86 patients with
      ocular manifestations, not of the whole cohort, and those 86 include
      manifestations first seen during the disease course, so the count of 24
      covers Horner syndrome at presentation or later. Of the 16 patients whose
      only findings at presentation were ocular, 7 (1.3% of the cohort) had
      Horner syndrome, so it can be the presenting sign on its own. The abstract
      does not give laterality, stage or tumor site for these patients, or say
      whether any case followed surgery.
- category: Neurologic
  name: Spinal Cord Compression
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Tumors next to the spine can grow through the intervertebral foramina into
    the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord, causing motor deficit, pain,
    sphincter dysfunction or sensory loss; the adjacent nerve roots can be
    compressed as well.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: spinal cord compression from intraspinal tumor extension
    term:
      id: HP:0002176
      label: Spinal cord compression
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11134211
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma with symptomatic spinal cord compression at diagnosis: treatment and results with 76 cases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of 1,462 children with neuroblastoma registered between 1979 and 1998, 76 (5.2%) presented with signs/symptoms of SCC, including motor deficit in 75 patients ... pain in 47, sphincteric deficit in 30, and sensory loss in 11."
    explanation: >-
      Of 1,462 children with neuroblastoma registered between 1979 and 1998 in
      this registry series (De Bernardi et al.), 76 (5.2%) presented with signs
      or symptoms of spinal cord compression; the abstract's purpose statement
      defines SCC as spinal cord compression. The denominator is every
      registered child with neuroblastoma rather than a selected subgroup, and
      5.2% falls in the OCCASIONAL band. The deficit counts are within the 76
      children with compression, not the whole series: 75 had a motor deficit,
      47 pain, 30 a sphincteric deficit and 11 sensory loss. Limitations: this
      is a single registry series; it counts only compression with signs or
      symptoms at diagnosis, not intraspinal tumor extension without symptoms;
      and 5.2% is only just above the lower edge of the OCCASIONAL band, next to
      VERY_RARE.
  - reference: PMID:36299690
    reference_title: "Presenting features of neuroblastoma with spinal canal invasion. A prospective study of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology Europe - Neuroblastoma (SIOPEN)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "As NB grows close to the spine, it may infiltrate the intervertebral foramina, invade the spinal canal (SCI) and compress the spinal cord and/or nerve roots"
    explanation: >-
      The introduction of this SIOPEN prospective study of neuroblastoma with
      spinal canal invasion (NB-SCI) states how the phenotype can arise:
      neuroblastoma growing close to the spine may infiltrate the intervertebral
      foramina, invade the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord and/or
      nerve roots. The sentence is background that the authors cite to an
      earlier publication, not a finding of this study, and it is in the
      introduction of the full text rather than in the abstract.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Children with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion in the SIOPEN prospective multinational NB-SCI study (196 evaluable patients)"
    notes: >-
      A cohort selected for spinal canal invasion, which the study defines as
      tumor growth through the neural foramina into the spinal canal, so the
      proportions below are conditional on intraspinal extension, not rates for
      neuroblastoma as a whole. Of the 208 patients registered, 196 were
      evaluable; 67% were symptomatic and 33% asymptomatic at enrollment.
      Symptomatic means any symptom attributed to the spinal canal invasion and
      recorded with standardized measures (motor deficit, pain, sensory deficit,
      bladder or bowel dysfunction, spine deformity or dyspnea), which is
      somewhat broader than signs of cord compression alone, so the symptomatic
      proportion is not recorded as a frequency of spinal cord compression. The
      cohort also includes tumors the authors class as histologically benign
      (ganglioneuroma, intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma) and a few patients
      enrolled at relapse. The asymptomatic share shows that tumor in the spinal
      canal does not always cause clinical compression; such asymptomatic
      extension is not counted in the registry rate given in the phenotype's
      main evidence.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36299690
      reference_title: "Presenting features of neuroblastoma with spinal canal invasion. A prospective study of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology Europe - Neuroblastoma (SIOPEN)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Of the 208 NB-SCI patients registered, 196 were evaluable for this analysis of whom 67% were symptomatic and 33% asymptomatic."
      explanation: >-
        In the SIOPEN prospective NB-SCI cohort, 196 of the 208 registered
        patients with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion were evaluable,
        and 67% of them were symptomatic while 33% were asymptomatic. The quote
        counts patients with any symptom of spinal canal invasion and does not
        itself name cord compression; reading it as symptomatic compression
        relies on the abstract's background statement that the majority of
        children with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion have symptoms of
        epidural compression of the spinal cord and/or spinal nerves, which is
        why it is graded indirect. The cohort was selected for spinal canal
        invasion, so the proportion is not a frequency for neuroblastoma in
        general.
- category: Neurologic
  name: Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome
  frequency: VERY_RARE
  description: >-
    Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (OMAS), also called
    opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (OMS), classically combines a characteristic
    eye-movement disorder (opsoclonus) and myoclonus with ataxia, irritability
    and sleep disturbance. There is good evidence that it is immune-mediated,
    and with neuroblastoma it may be paraneoplastic. It develops in a small
    minority of children with neuroblastoma: 9 of 405 children in a Hospital for
    Sick Children series and 21 of 675 children in a Children's Cancer Group
    questionnaire study of patients whose sera were banked at diagnosis, while
    15 of 1,187 children with previously untreated neuroblastic tumors in an
    Italian registry had it at presentation. More recent figures are 2.7% of
    neuroblastoma presentations in a meta-analysis of mainly abdominal
    neuroblastoma series published from 2005 to 2023, 4.7% of 776 children with
    peripheral neuroblastic tumors across 14 Polish centers, and 12 of 189
    children with neuroblastoma (6.3%) at one tertiary care center in India. It
    can be the presenting sign of an occult, localized tumor. In the cited
    series the associated tumors were mostly non-metastatic, mostly of favorable
    histology and mostly without MYCN amplification, and ganglioneuroblastoma
    was common among them. Survival in these series was excellent, but many
    children were left with developmental or neurological sequelae. Read the
    other way, a neuroblastic tumor, most often neuroblastoma, is found in
    roughly 40-50% of children with OMAS in recent series; that proportion has a
    different denominator and does not set the frequency band.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015247
      label: opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome
  notes: >-
    Bound to MONDO:0015247 opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome because HPO has no term
    for the syndrome: on 2026-10-22, OLS4 searches of HP for "opsoclonus
    myoclonus syndrome", "opsoclonus-myoclonus" and "dancing eye" returned
    nothing, and "opsoclonus" returned only HP:0010543 Opsoclonus, which names
    one sign of it. MONDO files MONDO:0015247 under movement disorder
    (MONDO:0005395) and paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome (MONDO:0018215), the
    disease term of the Paraneoplastic_Neurological_Syndromes entry. The
    VERY_RARE band (<5%) rests on the figures given for neuroblastoma: the two
    older series (9 of 405, 2.2%, and 21 of 675, 3.1%) and the meta-analysis's
    pooled 2.7%, which counts OMAS only as a sign before diagnosis. The band is
    kept because these estimates are under 5%, although one single-center
    series ran higher: a tertiary care center in India reported 12 of 189
    (6.3%). Several cited series count ganglioneuroblastoma, which has its own
    entry, together with neuroblastoma (the Italian registry's 1.3% and the
    Polish centers' 4.7%), and their figures are not used for the band.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6493702
    reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "On retrospective review of children seen at the Hospital for Sick Children, ophthalmic involvement was seen in 80 of 405 (20%). The three major eye signs of neuroblastoma, proptosis, Horner's syndrome and opsoclonus, are closely related to the site, stage of tumor, and outcome of the patient. ... Opsoclonus-myoclonus was the presenting sign of occult, localized neuroblastoma in all 9 children in whom it occurred. The 3-year survival rate was 100%."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective single-center review of children with neuroblastoma seen at
      the Hospital for Sick Children, published in 1984. The first quoted
      sentence supplies the denominator, 405 children reviewed, 80 of whom had
      ophthalmic involvement; the second names opsoclonus as one of the three
      major eye signs the study examined, with proptosis and Horner syndrome;
      and the third says opsoclonus-myoclonus occurred in 9 children and in all
      9 was the presenting sign of an occult, localized tumor. The abstract
      gives the 9 and the 405 in separate sentences and states no percentage.
      Read as 9 of the 405 reviewed, which is how a later population-based study
      citing this series reports it (PMID:20149339), the frequency is
      9/405 = 2.2%, inside the VERY_RARE band (<5%). Each eye sign's 3-year
      survival rate follows that sign's counts in the abstract, so the 100%
      figure refers to these 9 children. The abstract calls the syndrome
      opsoclonus-myoclonus and does not mention ataxia, and it reports survival
      only, not neurological outcome. The series was not limited to one stage or
      tumor site, the abstract gives no study period, and 2.2% is the frequency
      in this one cohort.
  - reference: PMID:20149339
    reference_title: "Incidence, ocular manifestations, and survival in children with neuroblastoma: a population-based study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Musarella et al7 observed opsoclonus in only 9 (2.2%) of 405 cases."
    explanation: >-
      In its discussion, a population-based study of neuroblastoma in Olmsted
      County, Minnesota, restates the Hospital for Sick Children series as
      opsoclonus in 9 (2.2%) of 405 cases; the 7 after 'et al' is the paper's
      citation marker. This gives as a proportion of the whole series the figure
      that the series' own abstract gives only as separate counts. It is a
      citation of that series rather than new data, so it confirms the 9/405
      reading without adding a second cohort; opsoclonus-myoclonus was not
      observed among the 14 children of the population-based cohort itself.
  - reference: PMID:11344492
    reference_title: "Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in neuroblastoma: clinical outcome and antineuronal antibodies-a report from the Children's Cancer Group Study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of the 675 responses received, 21 patients had OMA. Ninety percent of OMA patients presented with non-metastatic disease, vs. 35% of non-OMA patients. Estimated 3-year survival for the OMA patients with nonmetastatic disease (stage I, II, III) greater than 1 year of age was 100% vs. 77% for similar non-OMA patients (P = 0.0222). At follow-up, 14/19 evaluable OMA patients displayed some form of developmental or neurologic abnormality. ... Patients with OMA and neuroblastoma have excellent survival but a high risk of neurologic sequelae."
    explanation: >-
      Children's Cancer Group questionnaire study of neuroblastoma patients: of
      the 675 responses received, 21 patients had OMA. The study reports counts
      rather than a percentage for its cohort; 21/675 = 3.1%, inside the
      VERY_RARE band (<5%). The denominator is the questionnaire responses about
      patients who submitted sera at diagnosis to the CCG serum bank from 1980
      to 1994, not every child with neuroblastoma, so 3.1% is a proportion
      within a selected cohort, not a population-based frequency. The quote also
      gives the stage contrast at presentation (90% of OMA patients
      non-metastatic, against 35% of non-OMA patients); estimated 3-year
      survival of 100% for OMA patients older than 1 year with non-metastatic
      (stage I, II or III) disease, against 77% for similar non-OMA patients
      (P = 0.0222); and some form of developmental or neurologic abnormality at
      follow-up in 14 of 19 evaluable OMA patients. Its last part is the
      authors' conclusion that patients with OMA and neuroblastoma have
      excellent survival but a high risk of neurologic sequelae; the abstract
      gives no survival figure for OMA patients younger than 1 year or with
      metastatic disease.
  - reference: PMID:11344493
    reference_title: "Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in neuroblastoma: histopathologic features-a report from the Children's Cancer Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All tumors were classified into either the favorable (FH) or unfavorable histology (UH) group according to the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (the Shimada system). ... Twelve of 13 cases with opsoclonus-myoclonus were in the FH group."
    explanation: >-
      In a blinded Children's Cancer Group pathology review of 13 tumors
      associated with opsoclonus-myoclonus and 41 age- and stage-matched
      controls, every tumor was assigned to the favorable (FH) or unfavorable
      histology (UH) group of the International Neuroblastoma Pathology
      Classification (Shimada system), and 12 of the 13 tumors associated with
      opsoclonus-myoclonus were FH. The controls were also mostly FH (27 FH, 14
      UH) and the abstract reports no test comparing cases with controls, so the
      result shows that most of these tumors were FH, not that FH is more
      frequent with OMAS than in tumors of the same age and stage. This 12 of 13
      is the histology-group count; the abstract's separate 12 of 13 for
      diffuse, extensive lymphocytic infiltration with lymphoid follicles is a
      different finding, and the abstract does not say whether the same 12
      tumors are meant. The abstract gives no breakdown by INPC category, so it
      does not say whether ganglioneuroblastomas, which have their own entry,
      are among the 13.
  - reference: PMID:12709798
    reference_title: "Neuroblastic tumors associated with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome: histological, immunohistochemical and molecular features of 15 Italian cases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of 1187 children (age 0-15 years) with previously untreated NTs registered between 1979 and 1995, 15 (1.3%) had OMS at presentation. The majority of patients showed favorable biological characteristics, such as lack of amplification of the neuroblastoma-associated avian myelocytomatosis homolog MYCN oncogene and aneuploid nuclear DNA content. Tumor histology was reviewed according to the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification. Histology of the 15 cases of NTs with OMS was ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed, in 10 patients; ganglioneuroma, maturing, in 1; and neuroblastoma in 4."
    explanation: >-
      This Italian registry series (the title describes 15 Italian cases)
      reports that 15 of 1,187 children aged 0-15 years with previously
      untreated neuroblastic tumors registered between 1979 and 1995 (1.3%) had
      OMS, the paper's term for opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome, at presentation.
      After review under the International Neuroblastoma Pathology
      Classification, 10 of the 15 tumors were intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma,
      1 was maturing ganglioneuroma and 4 were neuroblastoma. Three limits apply
      when reading it for this entry. First, the 1.3% is a proportion of all
      neuroblastic tumors, including ganglioneuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma,
      which this entry treats as separate diseases (ganglioneuroblastoma has
      its own entry); the abstract does not say how many of the 1,187 were
      neuroblastoma, so no neuroblastoma-specific frequency can be derived and
      the figure does not set the band. Second, only OMS present at
      presentation was counted, so OMS that appeared after diagnosis is not in
      the 1.3%. Third, favorable biology, such as lack of MYCN amplification and
      aneuploid DNA content, is reported for the majority of the 15 OMS patients
      as a group, without counts; 11 of those 15 had ganglioneuroblastoma or
      ganglioneuroma, and the abstract gives no MYCN result for the 4
      neuroblastomas on their own.
  - reference: PMID:41047153
    reference_title: "Spotting childhood abdominal tumours: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the clinical presentation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Nineteen studies reported clinical presentation data specific to abdominal neuroblastoma ... The most frequently reported symptoms/signs reported among these 1026 cases included ... and/or opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (2.7% (0.0% to 8.3%)). ... the more specific presentation with opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome was reported in 28 of 1026 cases. ... Therefore, it is important not to overinterpret the absolute pooled proportions or their rank."
    explanation: >-
      A systematic review and meta-analysis of the symptoms and signs before
      diagnosis of childhood abdominal tumors, in studies published from 2005
      to 2023. Its neuroblastoma figures pool 19 studies with 1,026 cases that
      reported presentation data for abdominal neuroblastoma (the discussion
      notes that some included studies combined abdominal tumors with tumors at
      other sites), and OMAS was reported in 28 of the 1,026, a pooled
      proportion of 2.7% (95% confidence interval 0.0% to 8.3%), inside the
      VERY_RARE band (<5%). Three limits apply. It counts OMAS only as a sign
      before diagnosis, so OMAS that appears after diagnosis is not included.
      The confidence interval reaches above the band. And the authors, citing
      high heterogeneity between studies, caution against over-interpreting
      the absolute pooled proportions. Its search window starts after the
      1984, 2001 and 2003 series cited above, so those publications are not
      among its pooled studies.
  - reference: PMID:42497414
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma With Opsoclonus-Myoclonus Ataxia Syndrome: A 10-Year Experience From a Low- and Middle-Income Country Setting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Children aged younger than 14 years with NB-OMAS treated between January 1, 2013 and December 31, 2022, were retrospectively analyzed. Among 189 children with NB, 12 (6.3%) had OMAS."
    explanation: >-
      A retrospective series from a single tertiary care center in India: of
      189 children with neuroblastoma (NB) treated there from 2013 to 2022, 12
      (6.3%) had OMAS. This is the highest figure cited here for children with
      neuroblastoma and lies above the VERY_RARE band (<5%). It comes from one
      referral center, and the abstract does not say whether OMAS was counted
      only at presentation, so it is recorded beside the band rather than used
      to set it.
  - reference: PMID:41979173
    reference_title: "Ophthalmological manifestations of neuroblastoma - A retrospective multicenter study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We collected and analyzed retrospectively the data of 776 children with a clinical diagnosis of peripheral neuroblastic tumors reported between 2004 and 2022 from 14 Polish pediatric oncology centers. ... The reported manifestations comprised opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (OMS), Horner syndrome (HS), exophthalmos, periorbital hemorrhages, with the highest incidence of OMS (4.74% of all the patients)."
    explanation: >-
      A retrospective multicenter study of 776 children with peripheral
      neuroblastic tumors reported from 2004 to 2022 by 14 Polish pediatric
      oncology centers found OMS, the commonest of the ophthalmological
      manifestations recorded, in 4.74% of all patients. The denominator is all
      peripheral neuroblastic tumors, which include ganglioneuroblastoma and
      ganglioneuroma, so the figure is not specific to neuroblastoma and does
      not set the frequency band.
  - reference: PMID:35260471
    reference_title: "Diagnosis and Management of Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome in Children: An International Perspective."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This condition classically presents with a combination of characteristic eye movement disorder and myoclonus, in addition to ataxia, irritability, and sleep disturbance. In around 50% of children presenting with OMAS, there is an underlying neuroblastoma. There is good evidence that OMAS is an immune-mediated condition that may be paraneoplastic in the context of neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      An international expert review of childhood OMAS, written by a group drawn
      from the International OMS Study Group, gives the classic presentation: a
      characteristic eye-movement disorder and myoclonus, with ataxia,
      irritability and sleep disturbance. It states that there is good evidence
      that OMAS is immune-mediated and may be paraneoplastic in the context of
      neuroblastoma, and that around 50% of children presenting with OMAS have
      an underlying neuroblastoma. That 50% is the share of children with OMAS
      who have a tumor, the reverse of this phenotype's frequency among children
      with neuroblastoma, so it does not set the frequency band. Later in the
      same review the 50% is given for peripheral neuroblastic tumors as a
      group, of which neuroblastoma makes up 73% (ganglioneuroblastoma 22%,
      ganglioneuroma 4%), and the association with neuroblastoma itself is given
      as 26%-44%, so the share for neuroblastoma alone is below half. The
      review's tumor figures match the 389-child cohort it cites
      (PMID:28959231), so this item and that one rest on the same data for the
      50% figure.
  - reference: PMID:28959231
    reference_title: "Demographic, Clinical, and Immunologic Features of 389 Children with Opsoclonus-Myoclonus Syndrome: A Cross-sectional Study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the 50% of patients in whom a tumor was found (n = 194), the tumor was neuroblastic: neuroblastoma in 73%, particularly with younger OMS onset age (Table 5)."
    explanation: >-
      In a single-center cross-sectional study of 389 children with OMS at the
      National Pediatric Myoclonus Center, a specialty referral center, a tumor
      was found in 50% (194 children), and every tumor was neuroblastic.
      Neuroblastoma was the most common type, 73% of the tumors whose type was
      recorded (134 of 183 in Table 5), followed by ganglioneuroblastoma (41)
      and ganglioneuroma (8), so neuroblastoma itself was found in about a third
      of the cohort (134 of 389). The authors note that a tumor can be small
      enough to evade detection, so 50% is the share in which a tumor was
      detected. This is the share of children with OMS who have a
      tumor, the reverse of this phenotype's frequency among children with
      neuroblastoma, so it does not set the frequency band. The quoted sentence
      does not address the clinical features or the immune mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:41499722
    reference_title: "HLA and T-Cell Receptor Investigations in Idiopathic and Paraneoplastic Opsoclonus-Myoclonus in Children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among 25 patients with OMAS, 12 (48%) were paraneoplastic, all with neuroblastoma (6 female, 6 male), and 13 were idiopathic (4 female, 9 male)."
    explanation: >-
      In a Spanish nationwide prospective study of children with OMAS enrolled
      from 2013 to 2024, 12 of 25 children (48%) had paraneoplastic OMAS, all
      with neuroblastoma, and 13 had idiopathic OMAS. The cohort is small but
      independent of the US referral cohort behind the 50% figure
      (PMID:28959231). Like that figure, it is the share of children with OMAS
      who have a tumor, the reverse of this phenotype's frequency among
      children with neuroblastoma, so it does not set the frequency band.
  - reference: PMID:41499722
    reference_title: "HLA and T-Cell Receptor Investigations in Idiopathic and Paraneoplastic Opsoclonus-Myoclonus in Children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (OMAS) is a rare pediatric autoimmune neurologic disorder, with 40%-50% of cases occurring as a paraneoplastic syndrome in the setting of neuroblastoma or other neuroblastic tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The opening of the same study's abstract states as background that 40%
      to 50% of pediatric OMAS cases are paraneoplastic, occurring with
      neuroblastoma or another neuroblastic tumor. It restates earlier work
      rather than this cohort's own result, and like the other figures for
      this direction it is the share of children with OMAS who have a tumor,
      so it does not set the frequency band.
- category: Hematologic
  name: Anemia
  description: >-
    Anemia is one of the commonest general symptoms at presentation. In one
    retrospective series it was significantly associated with heavier
    infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells, although two smaller series
    that compared any marrow infiltration with none found it common in both
    groups.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Anemia
    term:
      id: HP:0001903
      label: Anemia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6670848
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma in 88 children. Clinical features, prognostic factors, results and late effects of therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A retrospective series of 88 patient under 15 with primary neuroblastoma from years 1951-1978 was analyzed. ... On the basis of histological differentiation, the series contained 67 (76.1%) neuroblastomas and 21 (23.9%) ganglioneuroblastomas. ... The commonest general symptoms were anemia (34.1% of all patients), vague pyrexia (25.0%), lack of appetite, weight loss (18.2%) and poor general condition (15.9%)."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective series of 88 patients under 15 years of age with
      primary neuroblastoma, admitted between 1951 and 1978, anemia was the
      commonest general symptom, recorded in 34.1% of all patients. On
      histological re-examination the series held 67 neuroblastomas and 21
      ganglioneuroblastomas, and the anemia figure is given for all patients,
      not for the neuroblastomas alone. Ganglioneuroblastoma is a separate
      neuroblastic tumor outside this entry, so no frequency band is set from
      this series; the figure would sit just above the lower edge of the
      Frequent band. All Evans stages, I to IV-S, were represented, but general
      symptoms as a group were commonest in stage III and IV patients, so the
      figure reflects this series' stage mix. Anemia is not defined in the

    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Erythrocytopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia were significantly (p<0.05) associated with marrow infiltration of >10% malignant cells."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective series comparing blood counts in neuroblastoma patients
      with and without bone marrow infiltration, anemia, together with
      erythrocytopenia and thrombocytopenia, was significantly associated
      (p<0.05) with marrow infiltration by more than 10% malignant cells. This

      infiltration and was not significantly correlated with infiltration (p =
      0.594). The authors attribute the anemia to the frequency of iron
      insufficiency in India rather than to the disease. No frequency is given

      infiltration.

All remaining hematological parameters such as anemia ( p = 0.594), leukopenia ( p = 0.189), and bicytopenia ( p = 0.369) were not significantly correlated with marrow infiltration in neuroblastoma cases. ... No significant correlation was noted for anemia in patients of neuroblastoma with and without infiltration, presumably due to the frequency of iron insufficiency in India rather than related to the illness itself."
      explanation: >-

        infiltration (p = 0.594); the authors suggest iron insufficiency, common

  - population: "Newly diagnosed children with neuroblastoma referred for staging bone marrow examination, Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, India (44 children, 24 with marrow involvement)"

Anemia, though was common in both group of patients with and without infiltration, it is thought to be due to nutritional deficiency rather than due to tumor infiltration in marrow."

- category: Hepatic
  name: Hepatomegaly
  description: >-
    In the metastatic pattern of INRGSS stage MS, in which metastases in a child
    younger than 18 months are confined to skin, liver and/or bone marrow, the
    liver is the main metastatic site. Hepatomegaly and its complications can be
    fatal in infants with this pattern. The cited series studied infants with
    stage 4S disease; INSS stage 4S is the narrower counterpart, limited to
    infants younger than 12 months with a localized primary tumor.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hepatomegaly
    term:
      id: HP:0002240
      label: Hepatomegaly
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly and associated toxicities"
    explanation: >-
      In the Children's Oncology Group trial ANBL0531, which enrolled infants
      with stage 4S neuroblastoma who had impaired or impending organ
      dysfunction or unfavorable tumor biology and excluded infants whose tumors
      had known MYCN amplification (infants too ill for biopsy could enroll with
      tumor biology unknown), five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly
      and associated toxicities. The trial counted deaths from late relapse and
      from treatment complications separately, so the authors attribute these
      deaths to hepatomegaly and its complications rather than to treatment.
      This shows that hepatomegaly can be fatal in stage 4S disease. The trial
      enrolled only a higher-risk subset of stage 4S infants (most infants with
      stage 4S disease do well with observation or minimal chemotherapy), so the
      quote speaks to severity, not to how often hepatomegaly occurs.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Infants with stage 4s neuroblastoma treated in French Society of Paediatric Oncology centers, 1990-2000 (94 infants)"
    notes: >-
      In this SFOP series, hepatic dissemination was present in 87 of 94 infants
      (92%). This counts liver metastasis rather than measured liver
      enlargement, so no hepatomegaly frequency is given. The series excluded
      infants whose liver involvement came from contiguous spread of a large
      abdominal primary tumor.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:12888814
      reference_title: "Treatment of stage 4s neuroblastoma--report of 10 years' experience of the French Society of Paediatric Oncology (SFOP)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Most tumours showed hepatic dissemination (87 out of 94, 92%), with bone marrow and skin metastasis occurring much less frequently."
      explanation: >-
        In this retrospective review by the French Society of Paediatric
        Oncology (SFOP) of infants with stage 4s neuroblastoma, 87 of 94 (92%)
        had hepatic dissemination, while bone marrow and skin metastases were
        much less frequent, so the liver was the main metastatic site. The paper
        counts liver metastasis, not liver size: it reports no hepatomegaly
        count, and in some infants liver metastases were found only at surgery,
        so liver involvement was not always clinically evident. Hepatomegaly
        follows from this metastatic burden only by inference, so the figure
        supports the phenotype indirectly and is not entered as a hepatomegaly
        frequency. The series did not apply the INSS limit on marrow involvement
        and included infants with bilateral adrenal tumors, which the authors
        note strict INSS staging does not take into account, so its stage 4s
        group is broader than strict INSS stage 4S.

biochemical:
- name: Catecholamine Metabolites
  notes: >-
    Elevated urinary catecholamine metabolites, classically vanillylmandelic
    acid (VMA) and homovanillic acid (HVA), are found in most neuroblastomas
    at diagnosis and support the diagnosis. Reviews cite high urinary
    catecholamine levels in more than 90% of cases (92% for VMA and HVA in
    clinically presenting neuroblastoma), and in a series of patients who
    later relapsed or progressed, urinary VMA and/or HVA had been abnormal at
    diagnosis in 92%. In two diagnostic series published in 2017 and 2020,
    however, the VMA and HVA pair had a diagnostic sensitivity of 82-84%,
    rising to 95% in the 2017 series when all eight urinary metabolites in
    its panel were combined. Relapse or progression cannot be detected
    reliably by monitoring tumor markers alone.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28061374
    reference_title: "Catecholamines profiles at diagnosis: Increased diagnostic sensitivity and correlation with biological and clinical features in neuroblastoma patients."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The combination of the classical markers VMA and HVA had a diagnostic sensitivity of 84%. NMN was the most sensitive single diagnostic metabolite with overall sensitivity of 89%. When all 8 metabolites were combined, a diagnostic sensitivity of 95% was achieved."
    explanation: >-
      In patients at diagnosis, VMA and HVA together had a diagnostic
      sensitivity of 84%, below the classical figure of more than 90%;
      combining all eight urinary metabolites measured raised it to 95%.
      Normetanephrine (NMN) alone reached 89%.
  - reference: PMID:31724812
    reference_title: "Biochemical testing for neuroblastoma using plasma free 3-O-methyldopa, 3-methoxytyramine, and normetanephrine."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall, 94 of the 96 patients with neuroblastoma had concentrations of 3-methoxytyramine or normetanephrine above age-specific upper limits of reference intervals, providing a diagnostic sensitivity of 97.9% that was higher (P < 0.0001) than that of 82.2% for HVA and VMA."
    explanation: >-
      A second diagnostic series: urinary HVA and VMA had a diagnostic
      sensitivity of 82.2%, lower than the 97.9% of plasma 3-methoxytyramine
      or normetanephrine. The abstract does not give the denominator for the
      urinary comparison.
  - reference: PMID:8790511
    reference_title: "Screening for neuroblastoma: a review of the evidence."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The screening test consists of measurements of the levels of vanillylmandelic acid and homovanillic acid in the urine; these metabolites of catecholamine are excreted in the urine of 92% of patients with clinically presenting neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The classical review figure for the VMA and HVA pair: 92% of patients
      with clinically presenting neuroblastoma, stated without a source cohort
      in the abstract.
  - reference: PMID:15235064
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma: a disease requiring a multitude of imaging studies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Origin from precursors of the sympathetic nervous system accounts for (a) primary sites in adrenal glands and in paraspinal locations from neck to pelvis and (b) high urinary levels of catecholamines in >90% of cases."
    explanation: >-
      A review statement of high urinary catecholamine levels in more than 90%
      of cases. It refers to urinary catecholamines in general rather than to
      VMA and HVA specifically.
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "At diagnosis, we found abnormal results in 75% for VMA and/or HVA (s), 92% for VMA and/or HVA (u), 90% for NSE, and 81% for LDH."
    explanation: >-
      In patients who later relapsed or progressed after first-line treatment,
      urinary (u) VMA and/or HVA had been abnormal in 92% at diagnosis (serum
      (s) 75%). The cohort is restricted to patients who relapsed or
      progressed, so it is not an unselected diagnostic series.
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Relapse or progression in neuroblastoma cannot be detected reliably by monitoring tumour markers alone."
    explanation: >-
      Qualifies the use of these markers in follow-up: in patients who
      relapsed or progressed after first-line treatment, the authors conclude
      that monitoring tumour markers, which in this study included urinary and
      serum VMA and HVA, does not reliably detect relapse or progression on
      its own.
- name: Neuron-Specific Enolase
  presence: INCREASED
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: neuron-specific enolase

      id: NCIT:C62216
      label: Gamma-Enolase
  notes: >-
    Serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is raised at diagnosis in most children
    with metastatic (stage IV) neuroblastoma: in a Children's Cancer Study Group
    series of 122 such children, 96% had levels more than three standard
    deviations above the mean for age-matched normal children. In a series of 61
    children with neuroblastoma of all stages, sampled at diagnosis, median
    serum NSE was 13, 23, 40 and 214 ng/ml in stages I, II, III and IV, whereas
    stage IV-S levels (median 40 ng/ml) were significantly lower than stage IV
    levels despite extensive tumor burden, so NSE does not simply track tumor
    burden. In stage III and IV disease in that series, a level above 100 ng/ml
    was associated with poor outcome, and the stage IV series, which shares its
    lead authors, suggested the same for stage IV disease. In a cohort
    restricted to 196 patients who had successfully completed first-line
    treatment and later relapsed or progressed, NSE had been abnormal at
    diagnosis in 90%, but that study's abstract does not say how many of them
    had NSE measured or in which specimen.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We analysed the data of neuroblastoma patients who had successfully completed first-line treatment and had laboratory results available from their initial diagnosis and from relapse/progression (n=196). ... At diagnosis, we found abnormal results in 75% for VMA and/or HVA (s), 92% for VMA and/or HVA (u), 90% for NSE, and 81% for LDH."
    explanation: >-
      In a cohort restricted to 196 patients who had successfully completed
      first-line treatment and had laboratory results from both initial
      diagnosis and relapse or progression, NSE results at diagnosis had been
      abnormal in 90%. Every patient in it went on to relapse or progress, so
      this is a cohort selected on outcome, not an unselected diagnostic series.
      The abstract does not say how many of the 196 had NSE measured, in which
      specimen, or against what cut-off, so 196 is the cohort size rather than
      the NSE denominator.
  - reference: PMID:3002599
    reference_title: "Serum neuron-specific enolase in children with neuroblastoma. Relationship to stage and disease course."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) was measured in 61 children at diagnosis with all stages of neuroblastoma. The median serum values for Stages I, II, III, IV, and IV-S were 13, 23, 40, 214, and 40 ng/ml, respectively. ... In patients with Stages III and IV disease, a raised serum NSE level was associated with poor outcome: only 1/19 (5%) survived with NSE levels greater than 100 ng/ml, whereas survival was 5/8 (63%) with values below 100 ng/ml. ... In patients with Stage IV-S disease serum NSE levels were significantly lower than those in Stage IV despite their extensive tumor burden."
    explanation: >-
      In a series of 61 children with neuroblastoma of all stages, sampled at
      diagnosis, median serum NSE was 13, 23, 40 and 214 ng/ml in stages I, II,
      III and IV, and 40 ng/ml in stage IV-S. The authors report stage IV-S
      levels as significantly lower than stage IV levels despite extensive tumor
      burden, so serum NSE does not simply track tumor burden. In stage III and
      IV disease, 1 of 19 patients (5%) with NSE above 100 ng/ml survived,
      against 5 of 8 (63%) with values below 100 ng/ml. Limitations: this
      comparison rests on 19 patients above and 8 below the cut-off, and the
      abstract gives no significance test for it and does not report it within
      stage III or stage IV separately, so from the abstract the effect of NSE
      cannot be separated from that of stage. Staging follows the Roman-numeral
      system then in use (stages I to IV and IV-S), and the 100 ng/ml cut-off
      was set with an assay of that era and may not transfer to current
      immunoassays.
  - reference: PMID:6135871
    reference_title: "Raised neuron-specific enolase in serum of children with metastatic neuroblastoma. A report from the Children's Cancer Study Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Serum levels of neuron-specific enolase (NSE) were measured by radioimmunoassay at diagnosis in 122 children with widespread metastatic neuroblastoma (clinical stage IV). 96% of these patients had NSE levels more than three standard deviations above the mean for age-matched normal children. ... Analysis of survival in relation to the level of NSE at diagnosis suggested that serum levels greater than 100 ng/ml were associated with a poor outcome. This relation was highly significant in the subgroup of infants less than 1 year old at diagnosis; all 7 with serum NSE below 100 ng/ml were alive up to 36 months after diagnosis, whereas 7 of 8 with serum NSE above 100 ng/ml died within 12 months of diagnosis."
    explanation: >-
      In a Children's Cancer Study Group series of 122 children with stage IV
      neuroblastoma sampled at diagnosis, 96% had serum NSE more than three
      standard deviations above the mean for age-matched normal children, and
      survival analysis suggested that levels above 100 ng/ml were associated
      with poor outcome. The abstract reports this relation as highly
      significant in the subgroup of infants under 1 year at diagnosis (all 7
      below 100 ng/ml alive up to 36 months; 7 of 8 above it dead within 12
      months) and gives no significance level for the stage IV group as a whole.
      It therefore supports raised NSE in stage IV disease only, not in
      neuroblastoma generally. Its stage IV finding is consistent with the 100
      ng/ml threshold that PMID:3002599 reported for stage III and IV disease
      combined, but the studies share their lead authors, so their patients may
      overlap and they are not independent replications.
genetic:
- name: MYCN Amplification
  association: Oncogene Amplification
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  notes: >-
    MYCN amplification occurs in approximately 20% of neuroblastomas overall;
    in a Children's Oncology Group cohort of 4,672 patients, 845 (18.1%) had
    amplification and a further 133 (2.8%) had MYCN gain, a smaller
    copy-number increase below the amplification threshold. MYCN
    amplification is among the most powerful adverse genomic prognostic
    markers, used alongside stage, age, histology, 11q status, and ploidy for
    risk stratification. The proportion depends strongly on stage: in the
    original 1984 series of untreated tumors, amplification was found in none
    of 15 patients with stage 1 or 2 disease but in 24 of 48 with stage 3 or
    4 disease.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047291
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Stage, age, histologic category, grade of tumor differentiation, the status of the MYCN oncogene, chromosome 11q status, and DNA ploidy were the most highly statistically significant and clinically relevant factors."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force analysis of 8,800 patients establishes MYCN status
      as one of the most statistically significant prognostic factors, and
      places it alongside (not above) stage, age, histology, 11q status, and
      ploidy in risk classification.
  - reference: PMID:6719137
    reference_title: "Amplification of N-myc in untreated human neuroblastomas correlates with advanced disease stage."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "N-myc amplification is highly correlated with advanced stages of disease"
    explanation: >-
      The original Brodeur series in untreated primary tumors established the
      association of MYCN amplification with advanced-stage disease.
  - reference: PMID:6719137
    reference_title: "Amplification of N-myc in untreated human neuroblastomas correlates with advanced disease stage."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Amplification was found in 0 of 15 patients with stage 1 or 2 disease, whereas 24 of 48 cases (50 percent) with stage 3 or 4 had evidence of N-myc amplification."
    explanation: >-
      The stage dependence given in the notes: in the original series,
      amplification was found in none of 15 stage 1-2 tumors and in 24 of 48
      (50%) stage 3-4 tumors, so cohorts weighted toward advanced stage report
      higher frequencies than the overall figure.
  - reference: PMID:28696504
    reference_title: "Association of MYCN copy number with clinical features, tumor biology, and outcomes in neuroblastoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among 4672 patients, 3694 (79.1%) had MYCN wild-type tumors, 133 (2.8%) had MYCN gain, and 845 (18.1%) had MNA."
    explanation: >-
      A primary cohort figure consistent with the rounded approximately 20%:
      of 4,672 Children's Oncology Group patients, 845 (18.1%) had MYCN
      amplification (MNA) and 133 (2.8%) had MYCN gain, which in this paper
      is a smaller increase below the amplification threshold.
  - reference: PMID:25345447
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma models for insights into tumorigenesis and new therapies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "MYCN amplification is found in about 20% of cases"
    explanation: >-
      A review statement of the rounded figure, about 20% of cases. The
      review's subject is mouse models; this sentence restates the human
      clinical figure.
- name: LIN28B
  association: Common-variant susceptibility locus at 6q16
  relationship_type: SUSCEPTIBILITY
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: LIN28B
    term:
      id: hgnc:32207
      label: LIN28B
  notes: >-
    rs17065417 within LIN28B is an independent association signal at 6q16,
    separate from the HACE1 signal at the same locus, in a genome-wide
    association study of 2,817 cases and 7,473 controls (odds ratio 1.38, 95%
    CI 1.23-1.54). The study's cohorts are a North American discovery cohort of
    European ancestry, an Italian replication cohort and an African American
    cohort; the replication quoted here is the Italian one. The same study
    reports that risk-allele homozygotes show higher LIN28B, lower let-7 and
    higher MYCN expression in neuroblastoma cell lines, which is a cell-line
    arm rather than a patient measurement. This entry does not extend the
    association to further populations: the Southern Chinese reports in the
    literature test other LIN28B variants rather than rs17065417.
  variants:
  - name: rs17065417
    description: >-
      The common intronic LIN28B risk allele at 6q16, reported with a combined
      odds ratio of 1.38 (95% CI 1.23-1.54) across a North American discovery
      cohort, an Italian replication cohort and an African American cohort.
      Carried here as a structured variant so the rsID and effect size are
      queryable rather than held in prose. No clinical_significance is set: the
      enum's values describe Mendelian variant classification, and a common
      risk allele of this effect size is none of them.
    variant_type: single nucleotide variant
    identifiers:
    - dbSNP:rs17065417
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:22941191
      reference_title: Common variation at 6q16 within HACE1 and LIN28B influences susceptibility
        to neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Here, we report a genome-wide association study of 2,817 neuroblastoma cases and 7,473 controls. We identified two new associations at 6q16 ... the second within LIN28B (rs17065417; combined P=1.2×10(-8); odds ratio 1.38, 95% CI 1.23-1.54)."
      explanation: >-
        Names the variant and its combined effect size in the authors' own
        genome-wide association study; the ellipsis omits the HACE1 result at
        the same locus.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22941191
    reference_title: Common variation at 6q16 within HACE1 and LIN28B influences susceptibility
      to neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we report a genome-wide association study of 2,817 neuroblastoma cases and 7,473 controls. We identified two new associations at 6q16 ... the second within LIN28B (rs17065417; combined P=1.2×10(-8); odds ratio 1.38, 95% CI 1.23-1.54)."
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own genome-wide association study, with the study size, the
      variant and the effect size in the quoted sentences; the ellipsis omits
      the HACE1 result at the same locus. The odds ratio of 1.38 is the
      risk-allele estimate from an inverse-variance meta-analysis of the three
      cohorts that make up the 2,817 cases and 7,473 controls, so it is a
      combined figure rather than one cohort's. The quoted text does not say
      what the signal is independent of; that the LIN28B signal is separate
      from the HACE1 signal at the same locus is stated elsewhere in the paper
      and is recorded in this record's notes.
  - reference: PMID:22941191
    reference_title: Common variation at 6q16 within HACE1 and LIN28B influences susceptibility
      to neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We next sought to replicate the rs4336470 and rs17065417 associations in an Italian cohort of 351 cases and 780 controls using PCR-based genotyping. Both SNPs showed evidence for association in the same direction seen in the discovery effort"
    explanation: >-
      The same study's replication step, quoted so the association is not left
      resting on one cohort: the LIN28B variant rs17065417 was genotyped again
      in an independent Italian cohort of 351 cases and 780 controls and
      associated in the same direction as in the discovery cohort. Both cohorts
      are of European ancestry, so this is independent replication rather than
      evidence of a cross-population association, and the sentence reports the
      direction of effect without a replication p value.
- name: LIN28B Tumour Expression
  association: Prognostic expression biomarker in primary tumours
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: LIN28B
    term:
      id: hgnc:32207
      label: LIN28B
  notes: >-
    High LIN28B expression in primary neuroblastoma is associated with worse
    outcome. The source calls it an independent risk factor for adverse outcome
    without naming the covariates in its abstract, and the paper has no
    open-access full text, so this entry does not state what the model was
    adjusted for. The 6q16 association study (PMID:22941191) reports the same
    direction of effect independently, in diagnostic primary neuroblastomas,
    and is cited below.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23042116
    reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
      suppression.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "High LIN28B expression was an independent risk factor for adverse outcome in neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The abstract reports, as the authors' own patient-outcome result, that
      high LIN28B expression was an independent risk factor for adverse outcome
      in neuroblastoma. The abstract names neither the covariates nor the
      survival endpoint behind independent, and the full text is
      subscription-only, so what the result was adjusted for rests on the

  - reference: PMID:22941191
    reference_title: Common variation at 6q16 within HACE1 and LIN28B influences susceptibility
      to neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Low HACE1 and high LIN28B expression in diagnostic primary neuroblastomas were associated with worse overall survival"
    explanation: >-
      A second, independent study reporting the same direction of effect in
      diagnostic primary neuroblastomas, which is what stops this biomarker
      record resting on one abstract sentence. The quoted span is the
      association alone; the paper gives P = 0.014 for the LIN28B arm, and the
      sentence states neither the cohort size nor whether the model was
      adjusted, so this is a univariate association and is not read as

- name: MYC Activation
  association: Oncogene Activation by Enhancer Hijacking
  relationship_type: SOMATIC_DRIVER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: MYC
    term:
      id: hgnc:7553
      label: MYC
  affected_regions:
  - name: Distal enhancer region downstream of MYC
    regulatory_element_type: ENHANCER
    chromosomal_region: 8q24
    description: >-
      Enhancer region lying downstream of the MYC coding sequence, reported in
      neuroblastoma either as a focal amplification of two known enhancer
      regions in primary tumours or as the acceptor side of an 8q
      translocation whose breakpoints fall downstream of MYC. Disease-level
      region, described by landmark rather than by coordinates: the band is
      the one the cited work gives for the MYC locus and for the translocation
      breakpoints that fall downstream of it, and no interval within the band
      is recorded.
  notes: >-
    MYC rather than MYCN drives a separate subset of high-risk neuroblastoma.
    Activation runs through the regulatory landscape rather than through
    amplification of the gene: either focal amplification of distal enhancers
    downstream of the coding sequence, or translocation bringing a highly
    active enhancer from another locus, for instance one that normally
    regulates HAND2 and FBXO8, into a topologically associating domain
    containing MYC. The subset's frequency and outcome are recorded on the
    pathophysiology node 'c-MYC Activation by Enhancer Hijacking or Enhancer
    Amplification'.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29284669
    reference_title: "MYC Drives a Subset of High-Risk Pediatric Neuroblastomas and Is Activated through Mechanisms Including Enhancer Hijacking and Focal Enhancer Amplification."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Here, we demonstrate that MYC is also activated as a potent oncogene in a distinct subset of neuroblastoma cases through either focal amplification of distal enhancers or enhancer hijacking mediated by chromosomal translocation."
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the gene-disease relationship this record asserts and the
      kind of lesion that carries it: MYC acts as a somatic driver in a subset
      of neuroblastoma through its regulatory landscape, by focal
      amplification of distal enhancers or by enhancer hijacking through
      translocation, which is why the affected region recorded here is an
      enhancer region downstream of MYC rather than the gene. Graded
      HUMAN_CLINICAL because the lesions were found in patients' tumours, four
      of the 74 whole-genome-sequenced primary tumours of the TARGET cohort.
      The cell-line chromatin work behind the hijacking mechanism, the
      zebrafish transformation arm, and the subset's frequency and outcome are
      cited on the pathophysiology node 'c-MYC Activation by Enhancer
      Hijacking or Enhancer Amplification'.
- name: ALK Mutations
  association: Oncogenic Driver Mutations
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ALK
    term:
      id: hgnc:427
      label: ALK
  notes: >-
    ALK point mutations occur in approximately 8-10% of neuroblastomas at
    diagnosis; in 1,596 diagnostic samples, three hotspot residues accounted
    for 85% of the mutations: R1275 (43%), F1174 (30%) and F1245 (12%).
    Germline activating ALK mutations are the major cause of hereditary
    (familial) neuroblastoma, making ALK the principal familial neuroblastoma
    predisposition gene, and R1275Q is the most frequent germline mutation.
    Published estimates of the share of familial cases carrying a germline
    ALK mutation range from about 50% to 80%: the group that mapped ALK as
    the major familial gene reported more than 50%, one review gives 50%, and
    two others give 75% and 80%. Together with PHOX2B, ALK accounts for most
    familial cases. ALK is a therapeutic target for crizotinib and, in
    the current Children's Oncology Group frontline phase 3 trial, lorlatinib.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32296467
    reference_title: "Nervous system: Embryonal tumors: Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The primary predisposition genes in familial neuroblastoma are ALK and PHOX2B."
    explanation: >-
      Identifies ALK as a primary predisposition gene in familial
      neuroblastoma, consistent with its role as an oncogenic driver.
  - reference: PMID:18724359
    reference_title: "Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Our results demonstrate that heritable mutations of ALK are the main cause of familial neuroblastoma, and that germline or acquired activation of this cell-surface kinase is a tractable therapeutic target for this lethal paediatric malignancy."
    explanation: >-
      The linkage-plus-resequencing study in neuroblastoma pedigrees that
      established heritable ALK mutation as the main cause of familial
      neuroblastoma and ALK as the principal familial predisposition gene.
  - reference: PMID:18724359
    reference_title: "Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Resequencing in 194 high-risk neuroblastoma samples showed somatically acquired mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain in 12.4% of samples."
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies somatic ALK tyrosine-kinase-domain mutation in a high-risk
      cohort at 12.4%; the 8-10% figure cited in the notes refers to
      unselected neuroblastoma, which is enriched for lower-risk disease.
  - reference: PMID:25517749
    reference_title: "ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We describe comprehensive genomic, biochemical, and computational analyses of ALK mutations across 1,596 diagnostic neuroblastoma samples. ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations occurred in 8% of samples--at three hot spots and 13 minor sites--and correlated significantly with poorer survival in high- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      ALK tyrosine kinase domain mutations in 8% of 1,596 diagnostic
      neuroblastoma samples, the lower end of the approximately 8-10% figure
      in the notes. The count is of tumors carrying a mutation, so on its own
      it does not separate somatic from germline events.
  - reference: PMID:26059187
    reference_title: "Deep Sequencing Reveals Occurrence of Subclonal ALK Mutations in Neuroblastoma at Diagnosis."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In this series, deep sequencing allows the detection of F1174 and R1275 ALK mutational events at diagnosis in 10% of cases, with subclonal events in more than half of these, which would have gone undetected by Sanger sequencing."
    explanation: >-
      The upper end of the approximately 8-10% figure: targeted deep
      sequencing of the F1174 and R1275 hotspots found ALK mutations in 10% of
      cases at diagnosis, more than half of them subclonal events that Sanger
      sequencing would have missed.
  - reference: PMID:29589100
    reference_title: "Genetic susceptibility to neuroblastoma: current knowledge and future directions."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "It is estimated that gain-of-function mutations in ALK account for 75% of familial neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      A review estimate of 75%: ALK gain-of-function mutations account for 75%
      of familial neuroblastoma. The sentence is in the review's full text,
      not its abstract.
  - reference: PMID:38791942
    reference_title: "The Neuroblastoma Microenvironment, Heterogeneity and Immunotherapeutic Approaches."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Germline mutations in the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene are found in 80% of familial cases"
    explanation: >-

      germline ALK mutations in 80% of familial cases. It is a passing

  - reference: PMID:21734404
    reference_title: "Genome-wide linkage analysis to identify genetic modifiers of ALK mutation penetrance in familial neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Following a genome-wide linkage analysis and sequencing of candidate genes in the critical region, we identified ALK as the major familial NB gene. Dominant mutations in ALK are found in more than 50% of familial NB cases."
    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:28674118

  - reference: PMID:25345447
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma models for insights into tumorigenesis and new therapies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) mutation is also found in 7% of sporadic neuroblastomas and 50% of familial neuroblastomas."
    explanation: >-
      A review figure at the low end of the published range: ALK mutation in

  - reference: PMID:25517749
    reference_title: "ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Three 'hotspot' residues accounted for 85% of mutations (Figure 1, Table 1): R1275 (43%), F1174 (30%), and F1245 (12%)"
    explanation: >-
      The distribution of ALK mutations by residue in the same 1,596-sample

  - reference: PMID:28674118
    reference_title: "Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Germline mutations in ALK encode for single-base substitutions in key regions of the kinase domain that result in constitutive activation of the kinase, with the R1275Q mutation most frequently observed (Table 2)."
    explanation: >-
      Supports R1275Q as the most frequent germline ALK mutation, and germline

- name: Segmental Chromosomal Aberrations
  association: Adverse prognostic genomic profile
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  notes: >-
    This record carries the genome-wide copy-number profile claim only: whether
    a tumor's changes are confined to whole chromosomes (numerical) or include
    any segmental, part-arm gain or loss. In an array-CGH series of 493 tumors,
    those presenting exclusively whole-chromosome changes had excellent
    survival with no disease-related death, while any segmental alteration
    marked a high risk of relapse, and tumors carrying both numerical and
    segmental changes shared the higher risk of the segmental-only group. In
    the INRG project's MYCN-non-amplified cohort it was the segmental profile,
    rather than the individual markers, that added prognostic information to
    age and stage; within the segmental group of the array-CGH series the
    individual markers were still independent predictors of overall survival,
    so the two analyses answer different questions. The recurrent individual
    segmental changes have their own records in this section: 1p36 deletion,
    11q deletion and 17q gain. No gene_term is bound because the record
    describes a genome-wide copy-number pattern rather than a gene.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19171713
    reference_title: Overall genomic pattern is a predictor of outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Tumors presenting exclusively whole-chromosome copy number variations were associated with excellent survival. No disease-related death was observed in this group. In contrast, tumors with any type of segmental chromosome alterations characterized patients with a high risk of relapse."
    explanation: >-
      The profile-level contrast this record is about, from array CGH of 493
      tumors in two consecutive series, unrestricted by stage or MYCN status.
      Three consecutive abstract sentences.
  - reference: PMID:19171713
    reference_title: Overall genomic pattern is a predictor of outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients with both numerical and segmental abnormalities clearly shared the higher risk of relapse of segmental-only patients."
    explanation: >-
      Establishes that the profile is read by the presence of any segmental
      change rather than by the absence of numerical ones, which is why a
      mixed profile is not an intermediate category. Abstract sentence from
      the same 493-tumor series.
  - reference: PMID:22976801
    reference_title: "Segmental chromosomal alterations have prognostic impact in neuroblastoma: a report from the INRG project."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A segmental genomic profile, rather than the single genetic markers, adds prognostic information to the clinical markers age and stage in neuroblastoma patients without MNA"
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own conclusion for 505 INRG-database patients without MYCN
      amplification, of whom 397 had a segmental and 108 a non-segmental
      profile. Supports giving the composite profile its own record: here the
      profile carried the prognostic information that the individual markers
      did not. Abstract conclusion.
  - reference: PMID:19171713
    reference_title: Overall genomic pattern is a predictor of outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Finally, within tumors showing segmental alterations, stage 4, age, MYCN amplification, 1p and 11q deletions, and 1q gain were independent predictors of decreased overall survival."
    explanation: >-
      The complement of the INRG result above, and the reason both are
      recorded: restricted to the tumors that already carry a segmental
      profile, the individual arm-level markers were independent predictors of
      overall survival. The two cohorts differ, as do the questions asked, so
      neither item refutes the other. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:35053166
    reference_title: "Retrospective Analysis of INRG Clinical and Genomic Factors for 605 Neuroblastomas in Japan: A Report from the Japan Children's Cancer Group Neuroblastoma Committee (JCCG-JNBSG)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "segmental chromosome aberrations, and the number of chromosome breakpoints (BP) correlated with lower survival rates, while the thorax as the primary tumor site and numerical chromosome aberrations correlated with a favorable prognosis"
    explanation: >-
      Independent replication of the profile-level contrast in 605 tumors
      diagnosed in Japan between 1990 and 2014, of which 524 could be
      classified (404 segmental, 120 numerical-only). Quoted from mid-sentence
      in the unstructured abstract; the omitted opening lists the clinical
      factors analysed alongside.
- name: Chromosome 1p36 Deletion
  association: Adverse prognostic segmental chromosomal aberration
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  affected_regions:
  - name: Distal 1p deleted region
    chromosomal_region: 1p36
    description: >-
      Loss of heterozygosity across distal chromosome 1p, assayed at band 1p36
      in the cited cohorts. Disease-level region; individual tumors differ in
      the extent of the deletion.
  notes: >-
    Loss of heterozygosity at distal 1p is one of the recurrent segmental
    aberrations used in neuroblastoma risk assessment. Reported frequencies are
    23% of 898 informative tumors in a Children's Oncology Group series and 35%
    of 238 tumors in an earlier Children's Cancer Group trial cohort. The
    lesion is strongly associated with MYCN amplification, which is the main
    reason its independent contribution is hard to establish. Its association
    with decreased event-free survival is reproducible across cohorts, but
    independence from the other prognostic factors is not settled: 1p loss was
    the most powerful factor in an 89-tumor Dutch series and independent within
    the low- and intermediate-risk subgroup of the COG series, while in a
    bone-marrow-metastatic cohort it was not independent regardless of MYCN
    status and 11q loss was. No gene_term is bound because the record describes
    a chromosomal segment rather than a single gene.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16306521
    reference_title: Chromosome 1p and 11q deletions and outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "LOH at 1p36 was identified in 209 of 898 tumors (23 percent) and LOH at 11q23 in 307 of 913 (34 percent)."
    explanation: >-
      The frequency figure in notes, from 915 primary tumor samples collected
      through the Children's Oncology Group across all stages and risk groups;
      898 were informative at 1p36. The denominator is tumors, not patients.
      Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:10784629
    reference_title: "Loss of heterozygosity at 1p36 independently predicts for disease progression but not decreased overall survival probability in neuroblastoma patients: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "LOH at 1p36 was detected in 83 (35%) of 238 neuroblastomas."
    explanation: >-
      The second frequency figure in notes, from 238 patients enrolled on
      Children's Cancer Group phase III trials, one tumor per patient. Higher
      than the COG series above, which is expected of a trial-enrolled
      population. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:16306521
    reference_title: Chromosome 1p and 11q deletions and outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "LOH at 1p36 was associated with amplification of the MYCN oncogene (P<0.001)"
    explanation: >-
      The co-segregation with MYCN amplification stated in notes, in the same
      915-sample COG series. Opening clause of a longer abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:10784629
    reference_title: "Loss of heterozygosity at 1p36 independently predicts for disease progression but not decreased overall survival probability in neuroblastoma patients: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "LOH at 1p36 was associated with decreased event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) probabilities (P<.0001)."
