    explanation: >-
      The univariate outcome association, in the 238-patient Children's Cancer
      Group trial cohort. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:16306521
    reference_title: Chromosome 1p and 11q deletions and outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In a multivariate model, unb11q LOH was independently associated with decreased event-free survival (P=0.009) in the entire cohort, and both 1p36 LOH and unb11q LOH were independently associated with decreased progression-free survival in the subgroup of patients with features of low-risk and intermediate-risk disease (P=0.002 and P=0.02, respectively)."
    explanation: >-
      Where 1p36 LOH was independent in this series, and the scope of that
      result: the low- and intermediate-risk-feature subgroup, not the whole
      cohort. For the whole COG cohort the sentence reports independence for
      unbalanced 11q only. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:8531999
    reference_title: Allelic loss of chromosome 1p as a predictor of unfavorable outcome in patients with neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In a multivariate analysis, loss of chromosome 1p was the most powerful prognostic factor."
    explanation: >-
      The strongest claim of independence for this lesion, from an 89-tumor
      Dutch series assayed by Southern blot. A single-centre series two orders
      of magnitude smaller than the INRG cohorts, which is why notes presents
      independence as unsettled rather than established. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:10784629
    reference_title: "Loss of heterozygosity at 1p36 independently predicts for disease progression but not decreased overall survival probability in neuroblastoma patients: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Furthermore, allelic status at 1p36 was the only prognostic variable that was significantly associated with decreased EFS in low-risk neuroblastoma patients (P = .0148)."
    explanation: >-
      Supports the clinical point of recording this lesion separately: in the
      low-risk subset of the 238-patient cohort it was the only variable that
      discriminated event-free survival. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:35137546
    reference_title: MYCN amplification plus 1p36 loss of heterozygosity predicts ultra high risk in bone marrow metastatic neuroblastoma.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "11q23 LOH was an independent prognostic factor for patients without MYCN amplification, whereas 1p36 LOH was not an independent marker regardless of MYCN amplification."
    explanation: >-
      Contradicts the independent-prognostic-factor reading of this record in
      154 children with bone-marrow-metastatic disease, about 95% of them
      high-risk, assayed by FISH on bone marrow cells. The cohort is narrower
      and more advanced than the series above, so the disagreement may be one
      of population rather than of fact; it is recorded as its own item rather
      than folded into the prose. Abstract results sentence.
- name: Chromosome 11q Deletion
  association: Adverse prognostic segmental chromosomal aberration; INRG classification factor
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  affected_regions:
  - name: 11q deleted region
    chromosomal_region: 11q
    description: >-
      Unbalanced deletion within the long arm of chromosome 11, assayed at 11q23
      or with a distal 11q probe in the cited cohorts. Disease-level region;
      breakpoints differ between tumors.
  notes: >-
    Chromosome 11q status is one of the factors formally incorporated into the
    INRG classification system. Unbalanced 11q loss of heterozygosity was
    present in 17% of a 915-sample Children's Oncology Group series, 151 of the
    307 tumors with 11q23 LOH, and 11q alterations in 26% of a 611-tumor German
    cohort. In the COG series three-year event-free and overall survival were
    50% and 66% with unbalanced 11q LOH against 74% and 83% without. The
    deletion is inversely related to MYCN amplification and the two are almost
    mutually exclusive, which is why 11q carries most of its information in
    MYCN-non-amplified disease; it is characteristically the marker of
    MYCN-non-amplified high-risk tumors. In the German cohort 11q status was
    prognostic for event-free survival in the whole cohort and in stage 1, 2, 3
    and 4S disease without MYCN amplification, but did not discriminate outcome
    within stage 4. Whether the deletion carries prognostic information
    independently of the wider segmental profile is contested: it was retained
    in the German cohort's multivariate model, while the INRG project's model
    retained a composite segmental genomic type instead of any individual
    marker. No gene_term is bound because the record describes a chromosomal
    segment rather than a single gene.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047291
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Stage, age, histologic category, grade of tumor differentiation, the status of the MYCN oncogene, chromosome 11q status, and DNA ploidy were the most highly statistically significant and clinically relevant factors."
    explanation: >-
      Establishes chromosome 11q status as a statistically significant,
      clinically relevant prognostic factor in the 8,800-patient INRG analytic
      cohort, and as a formal component of INRG risk classification. This is
      the item that makes 11q, alone of the three arm-level markers here, part
      of a risk classifier rather than a research finding.
  - reference: PMID:16306521
    reference_title: Chromosome 1p and 11q deletions and outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Unb11q LOH was found in 151 of 307 tumors with 11q23 LOH (17 percent of the total cohort)."
    explanation: >-
      The frequency figure in notes, and the distinction the cohort draws
      between any 11q23 LOH and the unbalanced subset that carries the
      prognostic signal. Abstract results sentence from the 915-sample COG
      series.
  - reference: PMID:16306521
    reference_title: Chromosome 1p and 11q deletions and outcome in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Cases with unb11q LOH were associated with three-year event-free and overall survival rates (+/-SE) of 50+/-5 percent and 66+/-5 percent, respectively, as compared with 74+/-2 percent and 83+/-2 percent among cases without unb11q LOH (P<0.001 for both comparisons)."
    explanation: >-
      The survival figures quoted in notes, comparing the 151 unbalanced-11q
      tumors with all other cases in the COG series. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:16740759
    reference_title: Loss in chromosome 11q identifies tumors with increased risk for metastatic relapses in localized and 4S neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Alterations in 11q were found in 159 of 611 tumors in the whole cohort (26%) and were associated with stage 4 disease (P < 0.001) and age at diagnosis of >2.5 years (P < 0.001)."
    explanation: >-
      Independent frequency estimate from a representative German cohort of
      611 tumors of all stages, assayed by interphase FISH for distal 11q
      deletion, plus the stage and age associations. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:16740759
    reference_title: Loss in chromosome 11q identifies tumors with increased risk for metastatic relapses in localized and 4S neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "By multivariate analysis, the 11q status proved prognostic for event-free survival in the whole cohort (P = 0.008; hazard ratio, 1.573) and in the subgroup of stages 1, 2, 3, and 4S without MNA (P < 0.001; hazard ratio, 3.534)."
    explanation: >-
      The independence claim, and the subgroup where it is strongest: the
      hazard ratio more than doubles in localized and 4S disease without MYCN
      amplification compared with the whole 611-tumor cohort. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:16740759
    reference_title: Loss in chromosome 11q identifies tumors with increased risk for metastatic relapses in localized and 4S neuroblastoma.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In stage 4, the 11q status did not discriminate outcome."
    explanation: >-
      The boundary of this record's prognostic claim, from the stage 4 subset
      of the same 611-tumor cohort: where almost every patient is already
      high-risk, 11q status adds nothing. Recorded as a REFUTE item against
      the record's general adverse-prognostic claim rather than folded into
      the prose, because it is a tested null and not a caveat. Abstract
      results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:10490829
    reference_title: Allelic deletion at 11q23 is common in MYCN single copy neuroblastomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Allelic loss at 11q23 was inversely related to MYCN amplification (P<0.001)."
    explanation: >-
      The inverse relationship with MYCN amplification stated in notes, from
      295 sporadic primary tumors typed at 24 microsatellite loci on 11q.
      Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20145112
    reference_title: "High-risk neuroblastoma tumors with 11q-deletion display a poor prognostic, chromosome instability phenotype with later onset."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "MNA and 11q deletion were almost mutually exclusive; only one case harbored both aberrations."
    explanation: >-
      How near-complete the mutual exclusivity is, in 165 Swedish tumors on
      high-density SNP arrays comprising MYCN-amplified (n=37) and
      11q-deleted (n=21) high-risk groups. Supports treating 11q as the marker
      of MYCN-non-amplified high-risk disease. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:19401703
    reference_title: "International consensus for neuroblastoma molecular diagnostics: report from the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Biology Committee."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "11q aberration was associated with 17q gain (P<0.0001) and inversely associated with MYCN amplification (P=0.0006), but 11q aberration was not associated with diploidy or 1p aberration."
    explanation: >-
      The marker's company in the INRG analytic cohort: it travels with 17q
      gain, runs against MYCN amplification, and is independent of 1p
      aberration and ploidy. The last clause matters for this section, because
      it means the 1p36 and 11q records describe lesions that are not simply
      two readouts of one event. Graded REVIEW_SYNTHESIS for the same reason
      as the frequency item on the 17q record: the citing document is an INRG
      Biology Committee consensus report synthesising the INRG database.
      Full-text sentence; 11q status was known for a subset of the cohort
      only.
  - reference: PMID:22976801
    reference_title: "Segmental chromosomal alterations have prognostic impact in neuroblastoma: a report from the INRG project."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In multivariate analysis modelling EFS, the parameters age, stage and a segmental genomic type were retained in the model, whereas the individual genetic markers were not"
    explanation: >-
      Cuts against an independent prognostic role for 11q deletion in the 505
      MYCN-non-amplified INRG patients, and it bears on 11q as much as on 17q:
      the individual markers entered in that model were 11q deletion and 17q
      gain, the two the same abstract names in its univariate result. Read it
      with the same caveat as on the 17q record, that the retained
      segmental-genomic-type variable is itself defined by the presence of 1p
      deletion, 11q deletion or 17q gain, so non-retention means 11q adds
      nothing beyond the composite profile rather than that it lacks
      prognostic value. It stands against the German cohort's multivariate
      result above, which did retain 11q status; the cohorts and the models
      differ. Abstract results sentence, quoted up to the parenthetical
      relative risks.
- name: Chromosome 17q Gain
  association: Adverse prognostic segmental chromosomal aberration
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  affected_regions:
  - name: 17q gained region
    chromosomal_region: 17q
    description: >-
      Unbalanced gain of a distal segment of the long arm of chromosome 17,
      reported as 17q21-qter in the European series. Disease-level region;
      breakpoints differ between tumors.
  notes: >-
    Unbalanced gain of distal 17q is the most frequent copy-number change in
    neuroblastoma: 53.7% of 313 tumors in a six-centre European series, and 48%
    of the patients with a known 17q result in the INRG analytic cohort.
    Whether it carries prognostic information beyond the aberrations it travels
    with is disputed, and this record keeps both sides. In the European series
    five-year overall survival was 30.6% with 17q gain against 86.0% without,
    and 17q gain was the most powerful factor in multivariate analysis; a
    605-patient Japanese cohort found it the strongest of the three segmental
    markers. A 193-patient German cohort using a distal-17q FISH probe found no
    outcome difference, and in the INRG project's multivariate model the
    individual markers, 17q gain among them, were not retained once a segmental
    genomic type was in the model. No gene_term is bound because the record
    describes a chromosomal segment rather than a single gene.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:10379019
    reference_title: Gain of chromosome arm 17q and adverse outcome in patients with neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Unbalanced gain of segment 17q21-qter was found in 53.7 percent of the tumors, whereas the chromosome was normal in 46.3 percent."
    explanation: >-
      The frequency figure in notes, from 313 patients with primary
      neuroblastoma at six European centres, one tumor per patient, with no
      stage or risk restriction stated. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:19401703
    reference_title: "International consensus for neuroblastoma molecular diagnostics: report from the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Biology Committee."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the INRG analytic cohort (n=8800; see Cohn et al (2009) for details), 29% were diploid, 16% were MYCN amplified, 21% had an 11q aberration, 23% had a 1p aberration, and 48% had a 17q gain."
    explanation: >-
      The second frequency figure in notes, and the one that puts 17q gain
      above the other two arm-level markers in the same cohort. Each
      percentage is among the patients with that marker known rather than
      among all 8,800, so the figures are not shares of one denominator.
      Graded REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the citing document is an international
      consensus report of the INRG Biology Committee, and the sentence itself
      credits the cohort to Cohn et al (2009), so the committee is restating
      the database rather than reporting a study of its own. Full-text
      sentence, not in the abstract.
  - reference: PMID:10379019
    reference_title: Gain of chromosome arm 17q and adverse outcome in patients with neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among the patients with this abnormality, overall survival at five years was 30.6 percent (95 percent confidence interval, 21 to 40 percent), as compared with 86.0 percent (95 percent confidence interval, 78 to 91 percent) among those with normal 17q status."
    explanation: >-
      The survival figures quoted in notes, from the same 313-patient European
      series. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:10379019
    reference_title: Gain of chromosome arm 17q and adverse outcome in patients with neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "in multivariate analysis, gain of 17q was the most powerful prognostic factor, followed by the presence of stage 4 disease and deletion of 1p (hazard ratios, 3.4, 2.3, and 1.9, respectively)."
    explanation: >-
      The strongest claim of independence for this lesion, ranking it above
      stage 4 disease and 1p deletion in the European series. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:35053166
    reference_title: "Retrospective Analysis of INRG Clinical and Genomic Factors for 605 Neuroblastomas in Japan: A Report from the Japan Children's Cancer Group Neuroblastoma Committee (JCCG-JNBSG)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "17q partial gain was the best poor survival marker for all and stage 4, MYCN non-amplified patients among the typical chromosome aberrations, including 1p loss and 11q loss"
    explanation: >-
      Independent replication of the ranking above in 605 tumors diagnosed in
      Japan between 1990 and 2014, assayed by array CGH at diagnosis, and the
      only cohort here that compares the three arm-level markers against each
      other directly. Full-text discussion sentence restating the paper's own
      result.
  - reference: PMID:22976801
    reference_title: "Segmental chromosomal alterations have prognostic impact in neuroblastoma: a report from the INRG project."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In univariate analysis, 11q deletion, 17q gain and a segmental genomic type were associated with a poorer event-free survival (EFS) (P<0.0001, P=0.0002 and P<0.0001, respectively)."
    explanation: >-
      The univariate association in 505 INRG-database patients without MYCN
      amplification; per the paper's Table 2, 17q status was known in 264 of
      them. Paired with the multivariate item below, which is where it drops
      out. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:22976801
    reference_title: "Segmental chromosomal alterations have prognostic impact in neuroblastoma: a report from the INRG project."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In multivariate analysis modelling EFS, the parameters age, stage and a segmental genomic type were retained in the model, whereas the individual genetic markers were not"
    explanation: >-
      Cuts against an independent prognostic role for 17q gain in the 505
      MYCN-non-amplified INRG patients. Read carefully: the retained
      segmental-genomic-type variable is itself defined by the presence of 1p
      deletion, 11q deletion or 17q gain, so non-retention means 17q gain adds
      nothing beyond the composite profile, not that it lacks prognostic
      value. Abstract results sentence, quoted up to the parenthetical
      relative risks.
  - reference: PMID:14581355
    reference_title: Gain of distal chromosome arm 17q is not associated with poor prognosis in neuroblastoma.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Outcome was not different between patients with 17q gain compared with those without, however."
    explanation: >-
      A direct tested null against this record's outcome claim, in 193 German
      patients of all stages. The assay differs from the European series: FISH
      with a distal-17q probe against the chromosome 17 centromere, scoring
      gain when excess 17q was present in at least half the tumor cells, so
      the two cohorts may not be counting the same lesion. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "we identified key features of NB, including loss of NF1 and gain of 17q chromosome, which are critical for the development of malignant tumor."
    explanation: >-
      Supports 17q gain as a feature the study's own expression profiling and
      exome sequencing identified in MYCN/ALK-induced clones of iPSC-derived
      cranial neural crest cells, cells that formed neuroblastoma-like tumors
      when transplanted into immunodeficient mice; it is not patient-derived
      prognostic data. Indirect for this record: the sentence calls 17q gain
      critical for malignant tumor development in a model system, and an
      association with worse prognosis in patients follows only by inference.
- name: Chromothripsis
  association: Adverse prognostic somatic structural event in high-stage tumors
  relationship_type: BIOMARKER
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  notes: >-
    Chromothripsis is a localized shredding of a chromosomal region with random
    reassembly of the fragments. Whole-genome sequencing of 87 primary
    neuroblastomas annotated 10 as chromothripsis-like, 18% of the high-stage
    tumors, and those tumors were associated with a poor prognosis. Two further
    series put the frequency at 19% of 105 high-risk tumors in the TARGET
    cohort, localized to a single chromosome in 15 of the 20 positive cases,
    and 4.3% of 233 tumors of all stages profiled by SNP array, again
    predominantly high-stage. The spread between those figures tracks the
    cohort's stage and risk composition and the detection method, so none of
    them is a frequency for neuroblastoma as a whole. Unlike the three
    arm-level records in this section, chromothripsis is a class of genome
    structural event rather than a recurrent gain or loss at a fixed location,
    which is why no affected_regions or gene_term is given.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22367537
    reference_title: Sequencing of neuroblastoma identifies chromothripsis and defects in neuritogenesis genes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "analysis of structural defects identified a local shredding of chromosomes, known as chromothripsis, in 18% of high-stage neuroblastoma"
    explanation: >-
      The headline frequency in notes, from whole-genome sequencing of 87
      untreated primary tumors of all stages with matched lymphocyte DNA. The
      18% denominator is the high-stage (INSS stage 3 and 4) tumors, not the
      whole series. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:22367537
    reference_title: Sequencing of neuroblastoma identifies chromothripsis and defects in neuritogenesis genes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "we annotated 10 out of the 87 patients as chromothripsis-like"
    explanation: >-
      The whole-cohort count behind the 18% high-stage figure, which is what
      makes the two numbers readable together. Full-text methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:22367537
    reference_title: Sequencing of neuroblastoma identifies chromothripsis and defects in neuritogenesis genes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The neuroblastoma with chromothripsis were associated with a poor prognosis"
    explanation: >-
      The outcome association in notes; the paper's comparison is of overall
      survival. The same paragraph reports that this prognostic impact was not
      independent of age and stage in multivariate analysis, which is expected
      of an event the paper found only in stage 3 and 4 tumors. Full-text
      sentence, quoted up to the start of the log-rank statistic, whose
      characters were garbled in extraction from the PDF.
  - reference: PMID:32796005
    reference_title: Somatic structural variation targets neurodevelopmental genes and identifies SHANK2 as a tumor suppressor in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "in the current study, 19% of high-risk tumors from the TARGET cohort showed chromothripsis (N = 20/105), involving a total of 27 chromosomal regions."
    explanation: >-
      Independent replication at a similar rate in a different cohort,
      high-risk primary diagnostic tumors sequenced as tumor-normal pairs in
      TARGET. Its denominator is high-risk tumors, where the item above uses
      high stage, so the two rates are close but not measuring the same
      subset. Full-text discussion sentence restating the paper's own result.
  - reference: PMID:32796005
    reference_title: Somatic structural variation targets neurodevelopmental genes and identifies SHANK2 as a tumor suppressor in neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Chromothripsis in most cases (15/20) was localized to a single chromosome."
    explanation: >-
      The localization figure in notes, across the 20 chromothripsis-positive
      TARGET tumors. Supports describing the event as confined rather than
      genome-wide, which is what separates it from a general
      chromosomal-instability phenotype. Full-text results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:25161957
    reference_title: Ultra-High Density SNParray in Neuroblastoma Molecular Diagnostics.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "So far, we have detected chromothripsis in 4.3% of neuroblastomas (10 out of 233 evaluable tumors, all stages). These patients with chromothripsis tumors had predominantly high stage tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The low end of the range in notes, and the reason for it: an all-stages
      denominator and an array rather than a sequencing assay. The
      predominantly-high-stage observation is consistent with the two
      whole-genome series above. Full-text passage, not in the abstract.
- name: TERT Rearrangement
  association: Telomere Maintenance Activation
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: TERT
    term:
      id: hgnc:11730
      label: TERT
  notes: >-
    Genomic rearrangements juxtaposing enhancers to the TERT locus drive massive
    TERT upregulation and telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance. TERT
    rearrangement occurs in high-risk disease and is largely mutually exclusive
    with MYCN amplification and ATRX mutation. Like MYCN amplification, it is a
    genomic route into telomerase activation, one of the two telomere
    maintenance mechanisms in neuroblastoma.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "These rearrangements occurred only in high-risk neuroblastomas (12/39, 31%) in a mutually exclusive fashion with MYCN amplifications and ATRX mutations, which are known genetic events in this tumour type."
    explanation: >-
      Establishes TERT rearrangement as a high-risk-restricted event in the
      whole-genome discovery series, where it was mutually exclusive with MYCN
      amplification and ATRX mutation.
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "TERT rearrangements defined a subgroup of high-risk tumours with particularly poor outcome."
    explanation: Links TERT rearrangement to adverse outcome in an extended case series.
- name: ATRX Mutation
  association: Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: ATRX
    term:
      id: hgnc:886
      label: ATRX
  notes: >-
    Somatic ATRX alterations, most often multi-exon deletions, are the commonest
    known lesion behind alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) in
    neuroblastoma, although many ALT tumours carry none. ATRX alteration is
    strongly age-dependent, rare in infancy and most frequent in adolescents and
    young adults, and it is almost mutually exclusive with MYCN amplification.
    The clinical course is often slow but progressive. Poor response to standard
    induction chemotherapy has been reported for large ATRX deletions and
    truncating mutations in one two-centre retrospective cohort, and
    chemo-resistance with late recurrence in a small series of ATRX- or
    DAXX-altered tumours.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22416102
    reference_title: "Association of age at diagnosis and genetic mutations in patients with neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ATRX mutations were associated with an absence of the ATRX protein in the nucleus and with long telomeres."
    explanation: >-
      Links ATRX mutation to loss of nuclear ATRX protein and to the long
      telomeres characteristic of alternative lengthening of telomeres.
  - reference: PMID:22416102
    reference_title: "Association of age at diagnosis and genetic mutations in patients with neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ATRX mutations were associated with age at diagnosis in children and young adults with stage 4 neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      This is the conclusion of a retrospective study of 104 patients with stage
      4 neuroblastoma. ATRX mutations were found by whole-genome sequencing in a
      40-patient discovery cohort and by PCR and Sanger sequencing in a
      64-patient validation cohort, in tumours from 14 of 32 adolescents and
      young adults, 9 of 54 children and none of 18 infants, which supports the
      age dependence of ATRX alteration. Patients were sampled to represent each
      age group, so these are per-age-group rates, not an overall frequency.
  - reference: PMID:42558321
    reference_title: "ATRX large deletions and truncating mutations are associated with primary induction chemotherapy resistance in high-risk neuroblastoma: a multicenter propensity-weighted cohort study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Compared with the WT group (71.0%), the LDT group exhibited a substantially lower ORR (36.0%; P < 0.001), with a primary induction-refractory rate of 64.0%."
    explanation: >-
      A retrospective cohort at two Chinese hospitals compared 33 high-risk
      neuroblastomas carrying large ATRX deletions or truncating mutations with
      92 ATRX wild-type tumours, scoring response to multi-agent,
      platinum-containing induction by blinded central review. The objective
      response rate was 36% against 71%, and the quoted 64% induction-refractory
      rate is the complement of that response rate rather than a separate
      measurement. The figures are propensity-weighted estimates from one
      unreplicated cohort of 33 such tumours, and missense ATRX variants did not
      differ from wild-type.
  - reference: PMID:25487495
    reference_title: "Clinical features of ATRX or DAXX mutated neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ATRX altered cases without MYCN amplification detected at greater than 18months showed poor prognosis, suggesting that ATRX or DAXX alterations are a particular NBL subtype. Since these tumors showed chemo-resistance and late recurrence, complete resection in a surgical approach should be performed to improve patient prognosis."
    explanation: >-
      Among 121 neuroblastomas, all 11 ALT tumours carried ATRX (10) or DAXX (1)
      alterations, and the authors conclude that this ATRX/DAXX-altered subtype
      showed chemo-resistance and late recurrence. Only that observation is
      cited, not the complete-resection recommendation that follows it. The
      abstract presents no chemotherapy-response or relapse data and reports
      poor prognosis only for the seven ALT cases detected after 18 months of
      age. Its purpose statement says the group had already reported ALT as a
      possible biomarker of chemotherapy response and late recurrence; the
      ATRX/DAXX genotype is the new element.
  - reference: PMID:22416102
    reference_title: "Association of age at diagnosis and genetic mutations in patients with neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Specifically, patients with ATRX mutations, ultrabright telomere FISH signal characteristic of ALT, loss of nuclear ATRX protein and absence of MYCN gain may be more likely to have a chronic but progressive clinical course with standard therapeutic approaches and may require a different treatment strategy."
    explanation: >-
      This retrospective genomic study of 104 patients with advanced-stage
      neuroblastoma hedges its own conclusion: patients whose tumors combine
      ATRX mutation, the ultrabright telomere FISH signal of ALT, nuclear ATRX
      loss and no MYCN gain 'may be more likely' to follow a chronic but
      progressive course with standard therapy and 'may require' a different
      treatment strategy. The study tests neither: its course data are
      descriptive (4 of 5 ATRX-mutant children in the discovery cohort lived at
      least twice as long as their time to first relapse), and it has no
      treatment-response analysis.
  - reference: PMID:35384159
    reference_title: "Mutational spectrum of ATRX aberrations in neuroblastoma and associated patient and tumor characteristics."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We subdivide the ATRX aberrations into nonsense, missense, and multiexon deletions (MEDs) and show that 68% of them are MEDs. Of these MEDs, 75% are predicted to be in-frame."
    explanation: >-
      This meta-analysis pooled 127 neuroblastoma patients and three cell lines
      with ATRX aberrations from 20 published papers and found that 68% of the
      aberrations were multi-exon deletions, the commonest class, and that 75%
      of these were predicted to be in-frame. All but two of the tumours were
      stage 4, and the pooled series are published cases rather than an
      unselected cohort.
  - reference: PMID:32291317
    reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "ALT was identified in 23.4% of high-risk neuroblastoma tumors and genomic alterations in ATRX were detected in 60% of ALT tumors; 40% of ALT tumors lacked genomic alterations in known ALT-associated genes."
    explanation: >-
      In a Children's Oncology Group cohort of high-risk primary tumours, ATRX
      alterations were found in 60% of the tumours with ALT, and the other 40%
      had no alteration in known ALT-associated genes. ATRX is therefore the
      commonest known altered gene behind ALT, while many ALT tumours carry no
      known lesion. The cohort is high-risk only.
  - reference: PMID:32060267
    reference_title: "MYCN amplification and ATRX mutations are incompatible in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the cohort of 819 tumors, ATRX mutations (n = 64) and MYCN amplification (n = 140) showed statistically significant mutual exclusivity (p = 0.0037, Cochrane-Mantel-Haenszel test) (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Note 1). Only 1 of 819 (0.1%) tumors had both lesions."
    explanation: >-
      In patient tumours pooled from three sequencing datasets (819 tumours),
      ATRX mutation and MYCN amplification were significantly mutually exclusive
      and only one tumour carried both, so the exclusivity is near-complete
      rather than absolute.
- name: PHOX2B
  association: Germline Predisposition
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: PHOX2B
    term:
      id: hgnc:9143
      label: PHOX2B
  notes: >-
    PHOX2B is a master regulator of autonomic nervous system development and,
    with ALK, one of the two primary familial neuroblastoma predisposition
    genes; it was the first neuroblastoma predisposition gene to be
    identified. Germline PHOX2B mutations cause neuroblastoma predisposition
    that may co-occur with other neurocristopathies — Hirschsprung disease
    and congenital central hypoventilation syndrome — reflecting a shared
    neural-crest developmental origin.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32296467
    reference_title: "Nervous system: Embryonal tumors: Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The primary predisposition genes in familial neuroblastoma are ALK and PHOX2B."
    explanation: >-
      Identifies PHOX2B alongside ALK as one of the two primary familial
      neuroblastoma predisposition genes.
  - reference: PMID:29589100
    reference_title: "Genetic susceptibility to neuroblastoma: current knowledge and future directions."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "These cases of neuroblastoma comorbid with other neural crest-implicated diseases facilitated the discovery of the first neuroblastoma predisposition gene, the paired-like homeobox 2B gene (PHOX2B) (Mosse et al. 2004; Trochet et al. 2004)."
    explanation: >-
      States that PHOX2B was the first neuroblastoma predisposition gene to be
      identified, through cases that co-occurred with other neural crest
      disorders. The sentence is in the review's full text.
- name: TP53
  association: Germline Predisposition (TP53 p.R337H)
  relationship_type: RISK_FACTOR
  variant_origin: GERMLINE
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: TP53
    term:
      id: hgnc:11998
      label: TP53
  notes: >-
    Germline TP53 variants cause Li-Fraumeni syndrome, in which neuroblastoma
    has been reported but is not a classic tumour, and the evidence for a
    raised neuroblastoma risk concerns mainly the p.R337H allele, which has
    an unusually high prevalence in southern Brazil. The 2017 AACR Childhood
    Cancer Predisposition Workshop review notes several reported cases of
    neuroblastoma in patients with Li-Fraumeni syndrome and germline TP53
    variants, especially p.R337H, recommends neuroblastoma surveillance for
    Li-Fraumeni syndrome with germline TP53 p.R337H, and states that it is
    unclear whether other TP53 variants raise the risk. Its source for
    p.R337H is a study from a single Brazilian institution, where 7 of 83
    children with neuroblastoma (8.4%) carried p.R337H, which the authors put
    at about 28 to 42 times the 0.2% to 0.3% frequency estimated for people
    from the region not selected by cancer diagnosis. That comparison is
    with published population estimates rather than a control group of the
    study's own, the 83 were the patients with samples available out of 178
    diagnosed at the institution, the study was prompted by carriers there
    who had both neuroblastoma and an adrenocortical tumour, two of the seven
    carriers had both tumours, and three of the seven were tested in tumour
    tissue only.

    Graded RISK_FACTOR rather than CAUSATIVE because a germline TP53 p.R337H
    variant raises the risk of neuroblastoma without being necessary or
    sufficient for it. A TP53 3' untranslated region polymorphism
    (rs78378222) associated with neuroblastoma susceptibility is a separate
    signal and is not recorded here. Li-Fraumeni syndrome is curated
    separately as Li-Fraumeni_Syndrome.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26452166
    reference_title: "Occurrence of Neuroblastoma among TP53 p.R337H Carriers."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Seven out of 83 patients tested (8.4%) were carriers of 337H allele. This frequency is about 28 to 42 times higher than the estimated 0.2 to 0.3% frequency for p.R337H in people not selected by cancer diagnosis from our region ... suggesting that carriers of the p.R337H are at increased risk of developing NB than the general population."
    explanation: >-
      A single-institution study from Campinas, Brazil, which screened 83 of
      the 178 children diagnosed with neuroblastoma there between 2000 and
      July 2014, chosen only by sample availability, for TP53 p.R337H. Seven
      (8.4%) carried it, which the authors compare with published estimates
      of 0.2% to 0.3% in people from the region not selected by cancer
      diagnosis and read as an increased neuroblastoma (NB) risk for
      carriers; the ellipsis skips the citations for those estimates. The
      study has no control group of its own and only seven carriers. It was
      prompted by carriers at the same institution with both neuroblastoma
      and an adrenocortical tumour, two of the seven had both, and three of
      the seven were tested in tumour tissue only, so their germline status
      rests on the tumour genotype. The result concerns a population in
      which the allele is unusually common and may not apply to other TP53
      variants. The sentences are in the paper's full text.
  - reference: PMID:28674118
    reference_title: "Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Several cases of NB have been reported in patients with LFS and germline mutations of TP53, especially the R337H mutation (refs. 100-102; Table 2), although NB is not generally considered a classic LFS tumor."
    explanation: >-
      The AACR Childhood Cancer Predisposition Workshop review notes reported
      cases of neuroblastoma (NB) in Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) with germline
      TP53 variants, especially p.R337H, while stating that neuroblastoma is
      not a classic Li-Fraumeni tumour. Reported cases give no risk estimate,
      so a raised risk follows from them only by inference. The review's
      source for p.R337H, its reference 102 and Table 2, is the Brazilian
      study cited above, so the two items are not independent. The review
      also states that it is unclear whether TP53 variants other than
      p.R337H raise the risk. The sentence is in the review's full text.
  - reference: PMID:28674118
    reference_title: "Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "In addition, we recommend NB surveillance for individuals with the following disorders: (i) LFS and germline TP53-R337H mutations"
    explanation: >-
      The same workshop review recommends neuroblastoma surveillance for
      Li-Fraumeni syndrome with germline TP53 p.R337H, first in a list that
      also includes Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome with germline CDKN1C
      mutations and Costello syndrome with HRAS mutations. The quote is the
      panel's recommendation and gives no risk figure. The sentence is in the
      review's full text.
diagnosis:
- name: 123I-MIBG Scintigraphy
  description: >-
    Whole-body scintigraphy with iodine-123-labelled metaiodobenzylguanidine
    (123I-MIBG), the functional imaging test for staging and response
    assessment. In its 2010 guideline on MIBG scans, the INRG Task Force called
    123I-MIBG the radiopharmaceutical of choice in children, and MIBG scans,
    particularly with a semi-quantitative score, the most sensitive and specific
    method of staging and response evaluation. The INRG staging system makes
    123I-MIBG scintigraphy mandatory, preferably before tumor excision. Under
    the 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria (INRC),
    response is assessed with anatomic imaging, 123I-MIBG or FDG-PET, and
    bilateral bone marrow aspirates and trephine biopsies; 123I-MIBG replaces
    technetium-99m bone scintigraphy at osteomedullary lesions, and skeletal
    uptake is scored relative to baseline with the same scoring method (for
    example Curie or SIOPEN) at each time point. In a prospective multicenter
    trial of patients with known or suspected neuroblastoma, 123I-MIBG
    scintigraphy had a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of 83%. A 2024
    systematic review of ten head-to-head studies found that PET/CT with
    catecholaminergic tracers (11C-HED, 18F-DOPA, 124I-MIBG or 18F-mFBG)
    detected significantly more lesions than MIBG scintigraphy in seven of them
    but was superior per patient in only two; the authors judged PET
    diagnostically superior but said its effect on clinical decisions was
    unknown, and noted that these tracers were rarely used in clinical practice
    and not included in new high-risk treatment protocols. Drugs can interfere
    with MIBG uptake: labetalol, which is usually effective for
    neuroblastoma-associated hypertension, must be stopped for several days
    before MIBG is given, and a tumor without MIBG uptake should raise the
    question of interfering medication, although complete blockade of uptake is
    rare.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: 123I-MIBG whole-body scintigraphy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C219704
      label: Whole Body Gamma Scan
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: 123I-MIBG whole-body tumor scan
    term:
      id: LOINC:82136-3
      label: NM Whole body Views for tumor W I-123 MIBG IV
  results: >-
    In the INRG staging system, one unequivocal MIBG-positive lesion at a
    distant site is sufficient to define metastatic disease, and a single
    equivocal lesion requires confirmation by another imaging modality (plain
    radiographs and, if they are negative, MRI) and/or biopsy. In high-risk
    stage 4, MIBG-avid neuroblastoma, a post-induction Curie score above 2 was
    associated with inferior outcome in two cooperative-group trials (COG A3973
    and SIOPEN/HR-NBL1), and an absolute SIOPEN skeletal score above 3 after
    induction marked very poor outcome in the SIOPEN/HR-NBL1 and COG-A3973
    cohorts. Both cut-offs apply to the score of the post-induction scan itself,
    not to the relative score (that score divided by the baseline score) that
    the INRC use for response assessment. Anti-GD2 immunotherapy, now standard
    of care, was given to only a minority of patients in those cohorts. Among 80
    tandem-transplant recipients on the later COG trial ANBL0532, 70% of whom
    then received dinutuximab, the optimal end-of-induction Curie cut point
    derived from the data was 0; in the trial's single-transplant arm it was
    again 2, but event-free survival did not differ significantly.
  notes: >-
    NCIT has no term for the MIBG scan itself, so the action is bound to Whole
    Body Gamma Scan (NCIT:C219704), which NCIT defines as whole-body
    scintigraphy that uses a gamma emitter for imaging and which is the only
    child of Whole-Body Scintigraphy (NCIT:C19565); the tracer is named in
    preferred_term. OLS NCIT searches on 2026-10-21: "MIBG scintigraphy"
    returned NCIT:C79553 Increased Uptake by 123-Iodine-Meta-Iodobenzylguanidine
    Scintigraphy (a finding), NCIT:C179784 SIOPEN Lewington Neuroblastoma 2017
    Oncology Response Criteria and NCIT:C198075 Stage MS Childhood Neuroblastoma
    by Toronto Guidelines v2; "I-123 MIBG" returned the tracers NCIT:C80094
    Iobenguane I-123 and NCIT:C74049 Iobenguane Sulfate I-123, NCIT:C79553,
    NCIT:C179784, NCIT:C179778 Ady Neuroblastoma 1995 Oncology Response
    Criteria, NCIT:C133462 Curie Scoring System and NCIT:C133468 Curie Intensity
    Score; "MIBG scan" returned NCIT:C222601 Stable Disease in Neuroblastoma,
    NCIT:C133462, NCIT:C198865 International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria,
    Brodeur 1993, NCIT:C9504 Stage 4S Neuroblastoma and NCIT:C179778;
    "iobenguane scintigraphy" and "metaiodobenzylguanidine scintigraphy"
    returned nothing. The two Curie terms sit under Clinical Intervention or
    Procedure (NCIT:C25218), but they name the semi-quantitative score read from
    the scan, not the scan, and this row also covers SIOPEN scoring, so neither
    is used as the diagnosis_term. A reference range names its measurement by a
    LOINC code, and LOINC has no code for the Curie or SIOPEN score: Monarch KG
    ClinicalMeasurement searches for "Curie score", "SIOPEN" and "MIBG score" on
    2026-10-21 returned no records, so the post-induction cut-offs are recorded
    in results rather than reference_ranges. LOINC:82136-3 is the only I-123
    MIBG code among the nine records the same search returns for "MIBG".
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20424613
    reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Metaiodobenzylguanidine labelled with 123I is the radiopharmaceutical of choice in children for high-quality functional imaging of neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      This consensus guideline from the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group
      (INRG) Task Force, developed by a subcommittee including expert nuclear
      medicine physicians and oncologists based on their experience and the
      medical literature, states directly that 123I-labelled MIBG is the
      radiopharmaceutical of choice in children for high-quality functional
      imaging of neuroblastoma. Its main limitation is that it is a 2010 expert
      recommendation rather than a comparative imaging study, and 'of choice'
      states a preference without ruling out other tracers.
  - reference: PMID:20424613
    reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Metaiodobenzylguanidine scans are the most sensitive and specific method of staging and response evaluation in neuroblastoma, particularly when used with a semi-quantitative scoring method."
    explanation: >-
      The 2010 INRG Task Force consensus guideline on 123I-MIBG scans concludes
      that MIBG scans, especially with a semi-quantitative score, are the most
      sensitive and specific method for staging and response evaluation in
      neuroblastoma. This is an expert judgement from the panel's experience and
      the literature, not new data. The guideline qualifies it: about 10% of
      neuroblastomas do not concentrate MIBG, very small marrow deposits are
      often missed, FDG-PET is often more sensitive for small soft-tissue
      tumours and nodal metastases, and no PET tracer other than FDG is
      considered.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Iodine-123 metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scintigraphy is mandatory, and it is recommended that the study is performed before tumor excision and according to the Standard Operating Procedure previously described."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report that introduced the INRG staging system states
      that iodine-123 MIBG scintigraphy is mandatory and recommends performing
      it before tumour excision. The sentence sits in the report's diagnostic
      and staging work-up, after the bone-marrow and CT/MRI requirements and
      before the INRGSS stage definitions, which is where its staging scope
      comes from. The scan is required, but the pre-excision timing is only
      recommended, and this is the Task Force's consensus rule, not a result of
      its 661-patient survival analysis.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "One unequivocal MIBG-positive lesion at a distant site is sufficient to define metastatic disease. A single equivocal lesion on MIBG requires confirmation by another imaging modality (plain radiographs, and if negative, MRI) and/or biopsy."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report that defines the INRG staging system states how
      a staging MIBG scan is read: one unequivocal MIBG-positive lesion at a
      distant site is enough to define metastatic disease, whereas a single
      equivocal lesion must be confirmed by another imaging modality (plain
      radiographs, then MRI if they are negative) and/or by biopsy. Metastatic
      disease is then staged M or MS by the system's other criteria. This is the
      Task Force's consensus rule, not a result of the report's 661-patient
      survival analysis.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Response assessment will include anatomic imaging for primary and metastatic soft tissue disease, nuclear medicine imaging using 123I-MIBG or FDG-PET for assessment of soft tissue and bone disease and bilateral bone marrow aspirates and trephine biopsies for assessment of marrow disease."
    explanation: >-
      This sentence comes from the 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma
      Response Criteria, a consensus developed by 52 investigators from 13
      countries through a National Cancer Institute-sponsored clinical trials
      planning meeting. It lists what response assessment will include: anatomic
      imaging of primary and metastatic soft-tissue disease, 123I-MIBG or
      FDG-PET imaging of soft-tissue and bone disease, and bilateral bone marrow
      aspirates and trephine biopsies. It is expert consensus, not patient data;
      elsewhere the paper specifies FDG-PET for tumours that do not concentrate
      MIBG and does not use anatomic imaging for osteomedullary lesions.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Because of its higher sensitivity and specificity, 123I-MIBG uptake will replace technetium-99m (99mTc) bone scintigraphy for evaluation of response at osteomedullary lesions."
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria, a
      consensus statement from a National Cancer Institute planning meeting,
      state that 123I-MIBG uptake will replace technetium-99m bone scintigraphy
      for evaluating response at osteomedullary lesions because of its higher
      sensitivity and specificity. The rule reflects investigators from 13
      countries reviewing published trial data, not an imaging comparison the
      panel ran, and the sentence gives no accuracy figures. The quote covers
      MIBG only; the next sentence assigns FDG-PET or PET/CT to detecting bone
      disease in tumours that do not concentrate MIBG.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The consensus recommendation is to use the MIBG relative score on bone sectors (the absolute score of bone lesions at time of response assessment divided by the absolute score of bone lesions at baseline before therapeutic interventions) for response assessment. The same scoring method (eg, Curie, SIOPEN) should be used at each time point of response assessment."
    explanation: >-
      This consensus statement from the NCI Clinical Trials Planning Meeting,
      which revised the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria,
      recommends scoring bone-sector MIBG uptake for response assessment as a
      relative score: the absolute bone-lesion score at the response assessment
      divided by the absolute score at baseline, before therapy. It adds that
      the same scoring method (for example Curie or SIOPEN) should be used at
      each response time point. This is an expert recommendation rather than new
      patient data, and Curie and SIOPEN are named only as examples.
  - reference: PMID:19185008
    reference_title: "(123)I-mIBG scintigraphy in patients with known or suspected neuroblastoma: Results from a prospective multicenter trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "(123)I-mIBG scintigraphy had a sensitivity of 88% (56/64) and specificity of 83% (25/30)."
    explanation: >-
      This prospective multicentre phase III trial enrolled 100 patients (not
      restricted to children), 86 of whom already had a neuroblastoma diagnosis
      and 13 had suspected disease; three blinded readers interpreted the scans.
      The quoted sentence states the trial's overall patient-level result: 88%
      sensitivity (56 of 64 patients with active disease detected) and 83%
      specificity (25 of 30 patients without disease read negative).
      Limitations: the cohort mixed newly diagnosed and previously treated
      patients, six indeterminate patients were excluded, and four
      false-negative readings were in patients with minimal residual disease.
  - reference: PMID:37962616
    reference_title: "The evidence-based role of catecholaminergic PET tracers in Neuroblastoma. A systematic review and a head-to-head comparison with mIBG scintigraphy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "For the PBA, the superiority of the PET method was reported in two out of ten studies ... For LBA, PET detected significantly more lesions than scintigraphy in seven out of ten studies. ... PET/CT using catecholaminergic tracers shows superior diagnostic performance than mIBG scintigraphy. However, it is still unknown if such superiority can influence clinical decision-making."
    explanation: >-
      This 2024 systematic review found ten studies (181 patients) comparing
      MIBG scintigraphy head to head with PET/CT using 11C-HED (two studies),
      18F-DOPA (four), 124I-MIBG (one) or 18F-mFBG (three). PET detected
      significantly more lesions in seven studies (lesion-based analysis, LBA)
      but was superior per patient (patient-based analysis, PBA) in only two.
      The authors state that it is unknown whether this changes clinical
      decisions. No meta-analysis was performed, and the included data allowed
      sensitivity but not specificity to be calculated, so the review qualifies
      the sensitivity half of the 2010 INRG statement and says nothing about its
      specificity half.
  - reference: PMID:37962616
    reference_title: "The evidence-based role of catecholaminergic PET tracers in Neuroblastoma. A systematic review and a head-to-head comparison with mIBG scintigraphy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "PET/CT with catecholaminergic tracers are rarely used in clinical practice and not included in new therapeutic protocols for HR-NB patients, despite their apparent superiority and the recognition of their relevant diagnostic role by recent international procedural guidelines"
    explanation: >-
      The introduction of this 2024 systematic review, which compares
      catecholaminergic PET tracers (11C-HED, 18F-DOPA, 124I-mIBG and 18F-mFBG)
      with mIBG scintigraphy, states that PET/CT with these tracers was rarely
      used in clinical practice and left out of new high-risk treatment
      protocols, despite apparent superiority and recognition in international
      procedural guidelines. This is the authors' framing at the time of writing
      (search closed May 2023), not a result of the review, and gives no usage
      figures.
  - reference: PMID:20424613
    reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "labetolol is a beta-adrenergic antagonist for blood pressure control. The latter is usually quite effective for treatment of neuroblastoma-associated hypertension, but must be discontinued for several days before mIBG administration. ... a tumour without mIBG uptake should always raise the question of possible interfering substances; however, it is rare that uptake is completely blocked."
    explanation: >-
      This 2010 INRG Task Force guideline on 123I-MIBG scans lists labetalol
      (spelled labetolol in the source) among the agents that most commonly
      interfere with MIBG uptake and retention in children. It says labetalol is
      usually effective for neuroblastoma-associated hypertension but must be
      stopped for several days before MIBG is given, and that a tumour without
      uptake should raise the question of interfering substances, although
      complete blockade is rare. This is expert guidance citing earlier
      pharmacological work, not patient data, and it gives no rate of
      drug-induced false-negative scans.
  - reference: PMID:28887399
    reference_title: "Validation of Postinduction Curie Scores in High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group and SIOPEN Group Report on SIOPEN/HR-NBL1."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The prognostic significance of postinduction CSs has now been validated in an independent cohort of patients (SIOPEN/HR-NBL1), with a postinduction CS of more than 2 being associated with an inferior outcome in 2 independent large, cooperative group trials."
    explanation: >-
      This retrospective review scored 123I-MIBG scans from patients
      prospectively enrolled in SIOPEN/HR-NBL1, all with MIBG-avid INSS stage 4
      neuroblastoma (330 post-induction scans), grading each of 10 anatomic
      regions 0-3 and summing them into a cumulative Curie score per scan. A
      post-induction Curie score above 2, previously linked to poor event-free
      survival (EFS) in COG A3973, was again associated with inferior outcome
      (5-year EFS 39.2% for scores of 2 or less vs 16.4% above 2, P < 0.0001),
      so the association holds in two independent cooperative-group trials. The
      HR-NBL1 cut point of 2 was chosen from that cohort's own data by the
      Youden method, not fixed in advance.
  - reference: PMID:28940046
    reference_title: "Validation of the mIBG skeletal SIOPEN scoring method in two independent high-risk neuroblastoma populations: the SIOPEN/HR-NBL1 and COG-A3973 trials."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In particular, patients with an absolute SIOPEN score > 3 after induction have very poor outcomes"
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective validation study in which planar mIBG scans (123I- or
      131I-labelled) from 341 SIOPEN/HR-NBL1 and 216 COG-A3973 patients with
      stage 4, mIBG-avid high-risk neuroblastoma were scored with the SIOPEN
      method, which rates skeletal uptake from 0 to 6 in each of 12 anatomical
      regions. The authors conclude that an absolute score above 3 after
      induction marks very poor outcome, measured as 5-year event-free survival.
      The post-induction analysis was limited to patients with skeletal uptake
      at diagnosis and no event before the post-induction scan. Anti-GD2
      immunotherapy reached only 20 SIOPEN/HR-NBL1 and 24 COG-A3973 patients in
      the analysis set, and 131I-MIBG therapy was part of neither protocol.
  - reference: PMID:37199022
    reference_title: "Impact of diagnostic and end-of-induction Curie scores with tandem high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplants for metastatic high-risk neuroblastoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "To date, the prognostic significance of Curie scoring has been reported within the context of patients who underwent induction followed by consolidation therapy with a single HDC, with either busulfan/melphalan or CEM ... although few patients received post-transplant anti-disialoganglioside (GD2) immunotherapy which is now considered standard of care."
    explanation: >-
      The introduction of this Children's Oncology Group analysis states that
      the prognostic value of Curie scoring had so far been reported only in
      patients consolidated with a single course of high-dose chemotherapy
      (busulfan/melphalan or CEM), few of whom received post-transplant anti-GD2
      immunotherapy, which the authors describe as now standard of care. This is
      the authors' summary of prior work, not a result of this study.
  - reference: PMID:37199022
    reference_title: "Impact of diagnostic and end-of-induction Curie scores with tandem high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplants for metastatic high-risk neuroblastoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Fifty-six tandem HDC recipients (70%) subsequently received immunotherapy with dinutuximab and cytokines, either on ANBL0032 (n=50) or ANBL0931 (n=6). ... The optimal CS cut point at EOI was 0 for recipients of tandem HDC."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective Children's Oncology Group analysis of 80 patients with
      MIBG-avid INSS stage 4 neuroblastoma who received tandem high-dose
      chemotherapy on ANBL0532, 56 (70%) of whom went on to dinutuximab and
      cytokines. The Youden-optimal end-of-induction Curie cut point was 0
      (3-year EFS 73% for a score of 0 versus 46% above 0), and it stayed
      prognostic among the 56 who received immunotherapy (81% versus 58%). The
      cut point was chosen from this cohort's own data; the authors note
      possible selection bias, because a more favourable group may have made up
      the patients who were randomized and completed consolidation, and say the
      cut point needs validation in later COG trials.
  - reference: PMID:37199022
    reference_title: "Impact of diagnostic and end-of-induction Curie scores with tandem high-dose chemotherapy and autologous transplants for metastatic high-risk neuroblastoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Our current study confirmed this optimal CS cut point (CS=2) in single HDC recipients, though the differences in EFS (CS≤2 vs CS>2) were not significant."
    explanation: >-
      In the 99 contemporaneous ANBL0532 patients randomized to a single
      transplant, the Youden-optimal end-of-induction Curie cut point was again
      2, but 3-year event-free survival did not differ significantly between
      scores of 2 or less and above 2 (46% vs 29%, p = 0.29), with only 18
      patients above the cut point.
- name: 18F-FDG PET/CT for MIBG-Nonavid Disease
  description: >-
    18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT, which the 2017 revised INRC use in
    place of 123I-MIBG when the tumor does not concentrate MIBG: FDG-PET or
    PET/CT for tumor detection in bone, and FDG-PET as an alternative modality
    for assessing primary or metastatic soft tissue and bony sites. FDG is less
    specific than MIBG, because inflammatory lesions and normal or
    cytokine-stimulated bone marrow also take it up, so the INRC add that a
    biopsy of at least one FDG-avid, MIBG-nonavid lesion may be required to
    confirm neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma. The earlier INRG documents
    named bone scintigraphy, not FDG-PET, for skeletal assessment in these
    patients: the 2009 INRG staging system requires technetium-99m bone
    scintigraphy, at any age, when MIBG positivity of the primary tumor cannot
    be confirmed because the primary has been removed or is not MIBG-avid, and
    the 2010 INRG Task Force MIBG guideline called the technetium-99m MDP bone
    scan the standard test for skeletal metastases in tumors negative for MIBG
    at diagnosis. That guideline considered investigating alternatives
    preferable, because the bone scan has low specificity and is hard to
    interpret in young children with growing bones, but judged the clinical
    value of FDG-PET not yet well defined and its routine use, especially as a
    substitute for 123I-MIBG scintigraphy, not justified. A 2015 Cochrane review
    advised an additional test, such as FDG-PET(-CT), for staging and response
    assessment in patients whose tumor does not accumulate 123I-MIBG, while
    noting that more evidence of its clinical value was needed. The 2018 EANM
    guideline covers PET/CT with 18F-FDG, 18F-DOPA and 68Ga-DOTA peptides and
    describes these studies as increasingly used in clinical practice.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: 18F-FDG PET/CT
    term:
      id: NCIT:C137817
      label: FDG-Positron Emission Tomography and Computed Tomography Scan
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "For patients whose tumors do not concentrate MIBG, FDG-PET or PET/CT scan will be used for tumor detection in bone."
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria (INRC), a
      consensus statement by an international panel of 52 investigators from 13
      countries, state that FDG-PET or PET/CT scanning is used for tumour
      detection in bone when the tumour does not concentrate MIBG. The sentence
      comes directly after the rule that 123I-MIBG replaces technetium-99m bone
      scintigraphy for evaluating response at osteomedullary lesions. It is a
      consensus criterion rather than a measured result, covers bone only, and
      belongs to response-assessment criteria rather than a staging system.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "In the minority of patients with MIBG-nonavid disease, FDG-PET provides an alternative modality to assess disease status at primary or metastatic soft tissue sites and bony sites."
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria consensus
      statement says that, in the minority of patients with MIBG-nonavid
      disease, FDG-PET provides an alternative modality to assess disease status
      at primary or metastatic soft-tissue sites and at bony sites. So the
      FDG-PET substitution is not limited to bone. The sentence names FDG-PET
      only, not PET/CT, and it concerns disease assessment within response
      criteria; it reports no diagnostic accuracy data.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In patients whose tumors do not concentrate MIBG, FDG-PET is an alternative modality for tumor detection, although FDG is less specific than MIBG because of uptake of FDG in inflammatory lesions, as well as normal and cytokine-stimulated bone marrow."
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria, a
      consensus statement on assessing treatment response in children with
      neuroblastoma, names FDG-PET as an alternative for detecting tumours that
      do not concentrate MIBG and states that FDG is less specific than MIBG,
      because inflammatory lesions and normal and cytokine-stimulated bone
      marrow also take up FDG. The sentence summarises earlier imaging
      literature it cites (references 15-17 and 49); it reports no new
      measurement and gives no specificity figures.
  - reference: PMID:28471719
    reference_title: "Revisions to the International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria: A Consensus Statement From the National Cancer Institute Clinical Trials Planning Meeting."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Because FDG is less specific for neuroblastoma, a tissue biopsy of at least one of the lesions may be required to confirm that FDG-avid, MIBG-nonavid lesions are histologically confirmed to be neuroblastoma and/or ganglioneuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The 2017 revised INRC consensus statement adds that, because FDG is less
      specific for neuroblastoma, a biopsy of at least one lesion may be needed
      to confirm that FDG-avid, MIBG-nonavid lesions are neuroblastoma or
      ganglioneuroblastoma. It directly follows the sentence naming FDG-PET as
      the alternative for tumours that do not concentrate MIBG. It is a
      consensus recommendation with no accuracy data, and "may be required"
      leaves the decision to biopsy to the treating team.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Technetium-99 bone scintigraphy is required only exceptionally, but in all age groups, if MIBG positivity of the primary tumor cannot be confirmed (ie, the primary tumor is removed or is not MIBG-avid)."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report that introduced the INRG staging system
      requires technetium bone scintigraphy (written "Technetium-99" in the
      report) only exceptionally, in all age groups, when MIBG positivity of the
      primary tumour cannot be confirmed because the primary was removed or is
      not MIBG-avid. It names bone scintigraphy, not FDG-PET, for that situation
      and covers skeletal disease only. It is the Task Force's consensus rule,
      not a result of its survival analysis, and it predates the 2017 response
      criteria that introduced FDG-PET for MIBG-nonavid disease.
  - reference: PMID:20424613
    reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "For those patients whose tumours are negative for mIBG uptake at diagnosis, the 99mTechnetium MDP bone scan is the standard test recommended to evaluate skeletal metastases ... However, the low specificity of this test and the difficulty interpreting uptake in young children with actively growing bones make investigation of alternative methods preferable."
    explanation: >-
      The 2010 INRG Task Force guideline on 123I-MIBG scans names the
      technetium-99m MDP bone scan as the standard test for skeletal metastases
      when the tumour does not take up MIBG at diagnosis, then says the bone
      scan's low specificity and the difficulty of reading uptake in young
      children's growing bones make investigating alternatives preferable. The
      ellipsis skips the first sentence's citation list. It is an expert
      recommendation covering skeletal disease only, and it predates the 2017
      response criteria, which use FDG-PET for bone in MIBG-nonavid disease.
  - reference: PMID:20424613
    reference_title: "Criteria for evaluation of disease extent by (123)I-metaiodobenzylguanidine scans in neuroblastoma: a report for the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) Task Force."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The clinical value of FDG-PET in neuroblastoma patients is at present not well defined and the routine use of FDG-PET, especially in case of intention to use this as a substitute for 123I-mIBG scintigraphy, is not justified."
    explanation: >-
      The 2010 INRG Task Force guideline on 123I-MIBG scans judged the clinical
      value of FDG-PET in neuroblastoma not yet well defined and its routine
      use, especially as a substitute for 123I-MIBG scintigraphy, not justified.
      The same paragraph reports studies suggesting that MIBG is more sensitive
      for bone lesions and FDG-PET for small soft-tissue tumours and nodal
      metastases. The judgement concerns routine use as of 2010, not FDG-PET in
      MIBG-nonavid disease specifically.
  - reference: PMID:26417712
    reference_title: "123I-MIBG scintigraphy and 18F-FDG-PET imaging for diagnosing neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
