  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22529259
    reference_title: "Outcome after surgery alone or with restricted use of chemotherapy for patients with low-risk neuroblastoma: results of Children's Oncology Group study P9641."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Chemotherapy was reserved for patients with, or at risk for, symptomatic disease, with less than 50% tumor resection at diagnosis, or with unresectable progressive disease after surgery alone."
    explanation: >-
      COG P9641's rule for who received chemotherapy. The abstract gives the
      protocol: patients underwent maximally safe resection of tumor, and
      chemotherapy was reserved for the three situations quoted. The full text
      defines them more narrowly. Immediate chemotherapy was offered for
      protocol-defined symptoms that compromised organ function or were life
      threatening and could not be relieved by surgery, for less than partial
      resection, and, at the investigator's discretion, for symptomatic spinal
      cord compression or the risk of it; at progression, surgery was repeated
      and patients with less than 90% resection were offered chemotherapy. The
      sentence states the design, not its outcome. The paper calls P9641 a phase
      III nonrandomized prospective study, so it does not compare observation
      with chemotherapy head to head. Abstract methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:22529259
    reference_title: "Outcome after surgery alone or with restricted use of chemotherapy for patients with low-risk neuroblastoma: results of Children's Oncology Group study P9641."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Immediate use of chemotherapy may be restricted to a minority of patients with low-risk NBL."
    explanation: >-
      The trialists' own conclusion from COG P9641, and the source for the
      statement that most low-risk patients may need no immediate chemotherapy.
      The full text gives the denominators behind 'minority': of the 915
      eligible patients, 115 received chemotherapy at diagnosis, and 800 were
      asymptomatic and observed after their initial operation, 89 of whom
      (11.1%) later had recurrence or progression. Five-year overall survival
      was 97% for the patients treated with surgery alone and 98% for those
      given immediate chemotherapy. The word 'immediate' matters, because
      chemotherapy could still be given at progression. Outcomes were not
      equally good in every subgroup. The abstract notes that stage 2b patients
      who are older or have diploid or unfavorable-histology tumors fare less
      well, and in the full text the 41 asymptomatic stage 4S patients treated
      with surgery alone had lower 5-year event-free survival than the 39 stage
      4S patients given surgery and chemotherapy (63% vs 92%, P = .0016),
      although overall survival did not differ significantly (84% vs 97%,
      P = .1302); the authors call that overall-survival difference surprising
      and say its reason is not yet evident. P9641 was nonrandomized, so this is
      a conclusion about withholding chemotherapy, not a head-to-head comparison
      with it. Abstract conclusion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:18349403
    reference_title: "Localized infant neuroblastomas often show spontaneous regression: results of the prospective trials NB95-S and NB97."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall survival (OS; 3-year OS, 0.99 +/- 0.01) and metastases-free survival (rate at 3 years, 0.94 +/- 0.03) for patients with unresected tumors was excellent and was not different from patients treated with surgery or chemotherapy."
    explanation: >-
      In the prospective multicenter trials NB95-S and NB97, the protocol for
      infants with localized neuroblastoma without MYCN amplification scheduled
      chemotherapy only for threatening symptoms; otherwise the tumor was either
      resected or observed by ultrasound and MRI. Of 340 eligible participants,
      190 underwent resection, 57 received chemotherapy and 93 were observed
      with gross residual tumor. For the 93 observed infants, 3-year overall
      survival was 0.99 and 3-year metastases-free survival 0.94, which the
      authors report as excellent and not different from the infants treated
      with surgery or chemotherapy. This supports observing these infants first
      instead of treating them. Observation was not uneventful: of the 93, 28
      had local progression, 7 progressed to stage 4S and 4 to stage 4, and the
      abstract neither says how they were then treated nor reports event-free
      survival, so the survival figures describe the observe-first strategy as a
      whole, not observation alone in every infant. Allocation among resection,
      chemotherapy and observation was not randomized: chemotherapy was reserved
      for threatening symptoms, and the abstract does not say how resection or
      observation was chosen for the others, so the three groups were selected
      differently. 'Not different' means no difference was detected, not that
      equivalence was shown, and the figures are 3-year only. The result is
      confined to infants and does not test observation in older children with
      low-risk disease. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20879880
    reference_title: "Outcome after reduced chemotherapy for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients who had disease with favorable histopathological features and hyperdiploidy were assigned to four cycles of chemotherapy, and those with an incomplete response or either unfavorable feature were assigned to eight cycles."
    explanation: >-
      The treatment-assignment rule of Children's Oncology Group trial A3961
      (NCT00003093), a prospective, nonrandomized phase 3 trial of reduced
      chemotherapy for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma without MYCN
      amplification: patients with favorable histology and hyperdiploidy were
      assigned four cycles, and those with an incomplete response or either
      unfavorable feature eight. Four cycles was a starting assignment rather
      than a fixed course: in the full text, 138 patients whose tumors had
      favorable biologic features and who did not have a complete or very good
      partial response after cycle 4 received four more. The full text names the
      trial A3961 (the abstract gives only the registry number) and states that
      the DNA index was used for risk stratification in infants only. Abstract
      methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20879880
    reference_title: "Outcome after reduced chemotherapy for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients who had tumors with favorable biologic features received four cycles and those who had tumors with unfavorable biologic features received eight cycles of chemotherapy with carboplatin, etoposide, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin, administered at 3-week intervals"
    explanation: >-
      Full-text methods sentence of COG A3961 naming the four agents of its
      intermediate-risk regimen: carboplatin, etoposide, cyclophosphamide and
      doxorubicin, given at 3-week intervals for four or eight cycles by tumor
      biology. It is the basis for binding carboplatin on this row; the other
      three agents are shared with the high-risk induction regimen. Full-text
      methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20879880
    reference_title: "Outcome after reduced chemotherapy for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 3-year estimate (±SE) of overall survival for the entire group was 96±1%, with an overall survival rate of 98±1% among patients who had tumors with favorable biologic features and 93±2% among patients who had tumors with unfavorable biologic features."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract results of COG A3961, giving 3-year overall survival by tumor
      biology. The full text defines favorable biologic features as favorable
      histology with a DNA index above 1, and unfavorable features as
      unfavorable histology, a DNA index of 1 or less, or both; of the 464
      patients whose features were fully known, 323 had favorable and 141
      unfavorable biology. In the full text the difference was significant for
      both event-free survival (90% vs 83%, P = 0.04) and overall survival (98%
      vs 93%, P = 0.02), and of the two stratification factors only ploidy was
      significantly associated with outcome. The very high survival on the
      reduced regimen was therefore not uniform across tumor biology. The two
      biology groups were assigned different numbers of cycles by design, so
      this describes outcome by biology under the trial's assignment, not the
      effect of shortening therapy within one group. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20879880
    reference_title: "Outcome after reduced chemotherapy for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A very high rate of survival among patients with intermediate-risk neuroblastoma was achieved with a biologically based treatment assignment involving a substantially reduced duration of chemotherapy and reduced doses of chemotherapeutic agents as compared with the regimens used in earlier trials."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract conclusion of COG A3961, a prospective, phase 3, nonrandomized
      trial in 479 eligible patients with intermediate-risk neuroblastoma
      without MYCN amplification. The very high survival is overall survival:
      the 3-year estimate for the entire group was 96 +/- 1% (abstract; the
      full-text Kaplan-Meier estimate uses the 476 patients with follow-up
      data). Event-free survival among the same 476 was lower, 88 +/- 2% at 3
      years; 42 of the 479 patients had disease progression as a first event and
      36 of them survived after salvage therapy, so the overall-survival figure
      includes patients rescued after progression. Severe adverse events without
      disease progression occurred in 10 of 479 patients (2.1%), including 3
      secondary leukemias, 3 deaths from infection and 4 deaths at surgery. The
      full text calls the design uncontrolled: survival was judged against a
      fixed 3-year overall-survival benchmark of 90% selected on the basis of
      the previous COG intermediate-risk study, so the comparison with earlier
      regimens is historical. Against CCG-3881 the authors report the duration
      of therapy reduced by 40% (eight cycles) and 70% (four cycles). Abstract
      conclusion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:31386611
    reference_title: "Maintaining Outstanding Outcomes Using Response- and Biology-Based Therapy for Intermediate-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Between 2007 and 2011, 404 evaluable patients were enrolled. Compared with legacy Children's Oncology Group studies, subsets of patients had a reduction in treatment. The 3-year event-free survival and OS rates were 83.2% (95% CI, 79.4% to 87.0%) and 94.9% (95% CI, 92.7% to 97.2%), respectively."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract results of COG ANBL0531, a prospective, single-arm phase III
      trial in intermediate-risk neuroblastoma. It used the same chemotherapy
      regimens as A3961 and assigned an initial two, four or eight cycles by
      age, stage and tumor biology, with response setting the final length of
      treatment. Compared with the legacy trials, the full text says the
      reduction for group 2 and 3 patients was prescribed as fewer chemotherapy
      cycles and/or a partial response of the primary tumor as the treatment end
      point instead of a very good partial response, and initial treatment was
      also reduced for 10 toddlers previously treated with high-risk regimens.
      In the results, 97 of 175 group 2 patients, 31 of 141 group 3 patients and
      16 of 88 group 4 patients received fewer chemotherapy cycles than in the
      legacy studies (144 of 404 by sum; the paper does not state the total).
      The reduction applied to subsets, not the whole cohort, and 94.9% is the
      overall survival of the whole cohort, not of the patients whose treatment
      was cut. The trial's benchmark was 3-year overall survival of 95% or more
      for the whole cohort, and 94.9% sits just below it. The planned comparison
      with a historical cohort could not be made, so the paper's primary
      analysis used a confidence-interval rule instead: an upper 95% confidence
      limit above the benchmark would mean survival was not significantly lower
      than it. The upper limit here is 97.2%, but the paper does not state that
      conclusion in its results, and the interval reaches down to 92.7%; the
      authors call the outcome excellent and do not say the objective was met.
      The 404 include the 49 stage 4S infants reported in PMID:30444686.
      Abstract results sentences.
  - reference: PMID:31386611
    reference_title: "Maintaining Outstanding Outcomes Using Response- and Biology-Based Therapy for Intermediate-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "More-effective treatment strategies still are needed for infants with unfavorable biology stage 4 disease."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract conclusion of COG ANBL0531, drawn from its stage 4 infant
      subgroup. In the abstract results, infants with stage 4 tumors with
      favorable biology (n = 61) had superior 3-year event-free survival
      compared with those with one or more unfavorable biologic features
      (n = 47), 86.9% versus 66.8% (P = .02), with only a trend toward better
      overall survival (95.0% versus 86.7%, P = .08). The whole-cohort figures
      therefore do not describe this subgroup. The comparison is between biology
      subgroups of a single-arm trial, so it shows that outcome differed by
      tumor biology; it does not test a different treatment. Abstract conclusion
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:31619207
    reference_title: "Clinical outcomes and prognostic factors to predict treatment response in high risk neuroblastoma patients receiving topotecan and cyclophosphamide containing induction regimen: a prospective multicenter study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All patients received 6 cycles of induction regimen consisting of 2 cycles topotecan (1.2 mg/m2/day) and cyclophosphamide (400 mg/m2/day) for 5 days followed by cisplatin (50 mg/m2/day) for 4 days combined with etoposide (200 mg/m2/day) for 3 days on the third and fifth cycles and cyclophosphamide (2100 mg/m2/day) for 2 days combined with doxorubicin (25 mg/m2/day) and vincristine (0.67 mg/m2/day) for 3 days on the fourth and sixth cycles."
    explanation: >-
      A prospective multicenter study of 107 children with newly diagnosed
      high-risk neuroblastoma, treated in 2016-2017 on the Thai Pediatric
      Oncology Group protocol ThaiPOG-NB-13HR, whose induction regimen the full
      text says follows that used in the Children's Oncology Group study
      ANBL0532. The abstract states that all patients received the same
      six-cycle induction: topotecan with cyclophosphamide in cycles 1 and 2,
      cisplatin with etoposide in cycles 3 and 5, and cyclophosphamide with
      doxorubicin and vincristine in cycles 4 and 6. The sentence names all six
      agents in the description, which is the basis for binding vincristine,
      doxorubicin and topotecan on this row alongside cisplatin, etoposide and
      cyclophosphamide. It is cited for what the regimen contains, not for how
      well it works. Directness is INDIRECT because one national protocol,
      adapted from the COG ANBL0532 induction, stands for high-risk induction in
      general. The abstract's 'we proposed' describes the authors'
      use of this induction in a nationwide trial; the full text notes that
      upfront topotecan with cyclophosphamide was first introduced more than a
      decade earlier. Abstract methods sentence.
- name: Surgical Resection
  description: >-
    Resection of the primary tumor has a role that differs by risk group. In
    low-risk disease surgery can be the only treatment: in the Children's
    Oncology Group trial P9641, asymptomatic patients with low-risk INSS stage
    2a or 2b disease who were observed after their initial operation, without
    upfront chemotherapy, had excellent survival. Most infants younger than six
    months with a small adrenal mass suspected to be neuroblastoma, and confined
    to the adrenal gland on imaging, can be spared surgery by expectant
    observation with serial ultrasound and urine catecholamine monitoring: in
    the Children's Oncology Group study ANBL00P2, 81% of the 83 infants managed
    by expectant observation were spared resection. On long-term follow-up,
    10-year event-free and overall survival for all 87 eligible infants,
    including the 4 who had immediate surgery, were 93.7% and 98.0%. In
    high-risk disease the primary tumor is resected after induction
    chemotherapy. More complete resection has been associated with better
    event-free survival and local control in two cooperative-group analyses,
    which disagree on overall survival. In the SIOPEN HR-NBL1 trial, complete
    macroscopic excision was associated with higher 5-year event-free and
    overall survival and a lower cumulative incidence of local progression than
    incomplete resection; severe operative complications occurred in 9.7% of
    patients and surgical mortality was 0.46%. In the Children's Oncology Group
    trial A3973, resection of 90% or more was associated with longer event-free
    survival and less local progression, but on multivariable analysis it had
    no significant effect on overall survival. Neither comparison was
    randomized, and the A3973 investigators described the role of primary
    tumor resection in high-risk disease as controversial.

  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22529259
    reference_title: "Outcome after surgery alone or with restricted use of chemotherapy for patients with low-risk neuroblastoma: results of Children's Oncology Group study P9641."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Excellent survival rates can be achieved in asymptomatic low-risk patients with stages 2a and 2b NBL after surgery alone."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract conclusion of COG P9641, stated for the trial's primary cohort,
      asymptomatic INSS stage 2a and 2b disease. In this phase III nonrandomized
      prospective study, patients underwent maximally safe resection, and
      asymptomatic low-risk patients with at least partial (more than 50%)
      resection were eligible for observation without chemotherapy. The 306
      asymptomatic stage 2a/2b patients observed after their initial operation
      had 5-year event-free survival of 87% +/- 2% and overall survival of
      96% +/- 1%, and the primary objective, 3-year overall survival of 95% in
      this cohort, was met (95% CI on 3-year overall survival, 96% to 100%).
      'Surgery alone' names the initial strategy, analyzed by intent to treat,
      not the whole course of treatment: event-free survival counted relapse and
      progression as events, per protocol recurrent or progressive disease was
      treated with surgery again, with chemotherapy offered when less than 90%
      could be resected, and 42 of the 89 observed patients (all stages) whose
      disease recurred or progressed received off-protocol therapy that is not
      recorded. Within stage 2b, event-free and overall survival were
      significantly lower for unfavorable-histology or diploid tumors, and
      overall survival was significantly lower for patients 18 months or older.
      There was no randomized chemotherapy comparator: overall survival was
      similar to earlier POG studies that gave these patients multiagent
      chemotherapy for up to 8 months. Abstract conclusion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:22964741
    reference_title: "A prospective study of expectant observation as primary therapy for neuroblastoma in young infants: a Children's Oncology Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Eighty-one percent of patients on the observation arm were spared resection."
    explanation: >-
      Primary result of COG ANBL00P2, a prospective multicenter study of infants
      younger than 6 months with a small adrenal mass confined to the gland on
      imaging. Parents chose the arm, so it was not randomized: of 87 eligible
      infants, 83 were managed by expectant observation with serial ultrasound
      and urine VMA/HVA monitoring, and 4 had immediate surgery. Sixteen of the
      83 observed infants eventually had surgery, so 67 of 83 (81%) were spared
      resection. Three-year overall survival across all 87 infants was 100%,
      with a median follow-up of 3.2 years among infants without an event.
      Eligibility did not require a tissue diagnosis, so this is a cohort of
      suspected neuroblastoma. Of the 16 observed infants who went to surgery,
      10 had neuroblastoma (8 INSS stage 1, one stage 2B, one stage 4S) and 6
      had other lesions (2 low-grade adrenocortical neoplasms, 2 adrenal
      hemorrhages, 2 extralobar pulmonary sequestrations). The 81% is a crude
      proportion: the 67 spared include the 12 infants lost to follow-up before
      any known resection. The paper also gives a 3-year resection-free survival
      estimate for the observation arm, with resection as the only event
      counted, of 79.8% (standard error 6.0%). Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:40452136
    reference_title: "Long-Term Outcome of Young Infants With Suspected Neuroblastoma following Observation as Primary Therapy: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among 87 eligible patients, the 10-year event-free survival (EFS) was 93.7%, and overall survival (OS) was 98.0%."
    explanation: >-
      Long-term follow-up of COG ANBL00P2, in which the parents of infants aged
      6 months or younger with small localized adrenal masses (suspected
      perinatal neuroblastoma, in the paper's own term) chose expectant
      observation or immediate surgery. These are whole-cohort figures: the 87
      include 4 infants who had immediate surgery (original ANBL00P2 report,
      PMID:22964741), and the full text gives 10-year event-free and overall
      survival of 93.3% and 97.9% for the 83 on the observation arm alone, an
      estimated 79.9% of whom were still resection-free. Event-free survival
      here counts any malignant event as well as a neuroblastoma event or death,
      so it is not the same measure as the 3-year neuroblastoma-event figure of
      the original report. The 10-year estimates rest on few patients: median
      follow-up for the 82 observed children still alive was 4.7 years, 13 of
      the 27 who stopped observation early were lost to follow-up, and the
      authors note that relatively few completed 10 years, although the survival
      curves were flat between 5 and 10 years. One observed infant was found to
      have INSS stage 4 disease after 4.5 years and was treated for high-risk
      disease; that child was censored at 5.7 years with vital status
      unavailable, so the overall-survival figure cannot include that outcome.
      One observed child died of causes unrelated to neuroblastoma. Abstract
      results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:32639845
    reference_title: "Influence of Surgical Excision on the Survival of Patients With Stage 4 High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the HR-NBL1/SIOPEN Study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Five-year event-free survival (EFS) ± SE (0.40 ± 0.01) and overall survival (OS; 0.45 ± 0.02) were significantly higher with CME compared with IME (5-year EFS, 0.33 ± 0.03; 5-year OS, 0.37 ± 0.03; P < .001 and P = .004). The cumulative incidence of local progression (CILP) was significantly lower after CME (0.17 ± 0.01) compared with IME (0.30 ± 0.02; P < .001)."
    explanation: >-
      HR-NBL1/SIOPEN analysis of 1,531 patients (stage 4 disease over 1 year of
      age, or stage 4/4S with MYCN amplification under 1 year) who completed
      induction chemotherapy without progression, met the response criteria for
      high-dose therapy and had no resection before induction. All 1,531 had a
      surgeon-assessed resection, either complete macroscopic excision (CME,
      1,172 patients, 77%) or incomplete macroscopic resection (IME, 359
      patients, 23%), so every resection analyzed took place after induction.
      CME was associated with significantly higher 5-year event-free and overall
      survival than IME, and with a lower cumulative incidence of local
      progression. Patients were not randomized to extent of resection, so tumor
      resectability may confound the association. Abstract results sentences.
  - reference: PMID:32639845

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT

    explanation: >-
      The harms of resection in the same HR-NBL1/SIOPEN cohort: 7 of 1,531
      patients died of surgery, 142 had severe operative complications and 124
      underwent nephrectomy. The complication and nephrectomy percentages imply
      denominators smaller than 1,531 (142 of 1,531 would be 9.3%), which the
      abstract does not state, and the abstract does not report complications
      separately for complete and incomplete resection. Abstract results

  - reference: PMID:27870572
    reference_title: "Impact of Extent of Resection on Local Control and Survival in Patients From the COG A3973 Study With High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "EFS was higher with ≥ 90% resection (45.9% ± 4.3%) than with < 90% resection (37.9% ± 7.2%; P = .04). Lower CILP (P = .01) was associated with ≥ 90% resection (8.5% ± 2.3%) compared with < 90% resection (19.8% ± 5.0%). On multivariable analysis, ≥ 90% resection was associated with longer EFS after adjustment for MYCN amplification or diploidy but had no significant effect on OS."
    explanation: >-
      Analysis of the 220 patients in the Children's Oncology Group high-risk
      trial A3973 who had both central surgery review and resection of the
      primary tumor site, comparing surgeon-assessed resection of 90% or more
      (154 patients, 70%) with less than 90% (66 patients, 30%). Resection of
      90% or more was associated with higher 5-year event-free survival and a
      lower cumulative incidence of local progression (CILP). Overall survival

      but not for overall survival, which is where this cohort parts from

- name: Autologous Stem Cell Transplant
  description: >-
    High-dose, myeloablative chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue, as
    consolidation after induction chemotherapy and surgery. Two randomized
    phase 3 trials set the current standard, and each changed a different part
    of it. The Children's Oncology Group's ANBL0532 compared tandem transplant,
    thiotepa and cyclophosphamide followed by dose-reduced carboplatin,
    etoposide and melphalan, with a single carboplatin-etoposide-melphalan
    transplant, and found three-year event-free survival from randomization of
    61.6% against 48.4%. SIOPEN's HR-NBL1 compared two single regimens,
    busulfan with melphalan against carboplatin, etoposide and melphalan, and
    found three-year event-free survival of 50% against 38%, with fewer severe
    adverse events on busulfan-melphalan but more veno-occlusive disease. That
    high-dose therapy with autologous rescue is worth giving at all comes from
    CCG-3891, where it beat non-myeloablative chemotherapy on five-year
    event-free survival, 30% against 19%. The two newer results are not
    additive, because ANBL0532's tandem arm is itself
    carboplatin-etoposide-melphalan-based: tandem transplant and
    busulfan-melphalan have not been compared with each other. That gap is
    recorded as a knowledge gap attached to this record.
  therapeutic_modality: CELL_THERAPY
  notes: >-
    ANBL0532 randomized 355 of 652 eligible patients, with 207 not randomized
    by physician or parent preference, and tested a one-sided superiority
    hypothesis; its authors state that the findings may not represent all
    patients with high-risk neuroblastoma. Read the absolute percentages from
    the two trials separately rather than against each other: they differ in
    induction regimen and era, and they randomize different populations, since
    HR-NBL1 randomized only patients who had already achieved an adequate
    response to induction.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15431
      label: Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation

- name: Radiation Therapy
  description: >-
    Radiation to the primary tumor site is used in high-risk disease after
    induction chemotherapy, surgical resection and consolidation with stem cell
    transplant. In the Children's Oncology Group phase III trial ANBL0532,
    patients were prescribed 21.6 Gy to the preoperative primary tumor volume,
    starting no sooner than 28 days after transplantation, with a boost to
    36 Gy for gross residual tumor after incomplete resection; the boost did
    not significantly improve the 5-year cumulative incidence of local
    progression compared with historical controls. Primary-site relapse still
    occurs after radiotherapy.

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients were prescribed 21.6 Gy in 1.8 Gy daily fractions to the preoperative primary tumor volume after induction chemotherapy. For patients with an incomplete resection of the primary tumor (defined as > 1 cm3 residual soft tissue density on end-induction scans), a boost of 14.4 Gy in 1.8 Gy daily fractions, for a total dose of 36 Gy, was delivered to gross residual tumor volume (Fig 1). Patients received radiotherapy no sooner than 28 days after transplantation."
    explanation: >-
      Radiotherapy protocol of the Children's Oncology Group phase III trial
      ANBL0532 in newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma, from the full-text
      methods. Patients were prescribed 21.6 Gy to the primary tumor volume as it
      was before surgery, and those with gross residual tumor after incomplete
      resection received a further 14.4 Gy boost to it, 36 Gy in total.
      Radiotherapy began no sooner than 28 days after transplantation, and the
      full text places the assessment of incomplete resection after the fifth
      induction cycle and before transplantation, so radiotherapy followed
      induction chemotherapy, resection and consolidation with stem cell
      transplant. The trial compared radiation doses, not radiotherapy with no
      radiotherapy, so it is not evidence that radiotherapy itself improves
      outcome. Full-text methods sentences.
  - reference: PMID:32530765
    reference_title: "Prospective Evaluation of Radiation Dose Escalation in Patients With High-Risk Neuroblastoma and Gross Residual Disease After Surgery: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group ANBL0532 Study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Boost radiotherapy to gross residual tumor present at the end of induction did not significantly improve 5-year CILP."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract conclusion of COG ANBL0532. The boost was compared with a
      historical cohort from the preceding trial COG A3973, in which irradiated
      patients received 21.6 Gy without a boost; among patients with residual
      tumor, the difference in 5-year cumulative incidence of local progression
      (CILP) was not significant (P = .4126). Across all irradiated patients,
      5-year CILP was 11.2% in ANBL0532 (323 patients) and 7.1% in A3973 (328
      patients), so primary-site relapse still occurred after radiotherapy in
      both trials. The comparison is historical rather than randomized, and the
      authors conclude that new strategies are needed to lower the risk of
      locoregional failure. Abstract conclusion sentence.

    reference_title: "Pilot induction regimen incorporating pharmacokinetically guided topotecan for treatment of newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma: a Children's Oncology Group study."

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "External beam radiotherapy (21.6 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions) beginning ≥ 28 days following PBSC infusion was administered to the presurgical gross tumor volume and sites of residual disease"
    explanation: >-
      Methods of the Children's Oncology Group pilot ANBL02P1, which enrolled 31
      patients with newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma. Residual primary
      tumor was resected after the fifth of six induction cycles. Patients with
      at least a partial response at the end of induction, an adequate stem cell
      product without detectable tumor contamination, and adequate cardiac and
      renal function then received consolidation with carboplatin, etoposide and
      melphalan, followed by stem cell infusion. The quoted sentence places
      radiotherapy after the transplant, beginning at least 28 days after that
      infusion, and gives the field: the presurgical gross tumor volume, the
      tumor as it was before resection, plus any sites of residual disease. That
      resection came before radiotherapy is not in this sentence; it follows
      from the word 'presurgical' and from the protocol's surgery step, which is
      a separate methods sentence. This is the planned treatment sequence of one
      feasibility pilot whose primary end point was induction feasibility; the
      paper reports no radiotherapy-specific results, so it is not evidence that
      radiotherapy improves outcome. Full-text methods sentence.

    explanation: >-

    reference_title: "Hyperfractionated low-dose radiotherapy for high-risk neuroblastoma after intensive chemotherapy and surgery."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "RT to the primary site followed dose-intensive chemotherapy and tumor resection; the target field encompassed the extent of tumor at diagnosis, plus 3-cm margins and regional lymph nodes."
    explanation: >-

      patients in first remission. Hyperfractionated 21-Gy radiotherapy to the
      primary site was given after dose-intensive chemotherapy and tumor
      resection, to a field covering the tumor's extent at diagnosis plus 3-cm
      margins and regional lymph nodes. It supports this sequence and field

      Oncology Group trials cited on this row, so the extent at diagnosis should

  - reference: PMID:11387353
    reference_title: "Hyperfractionated low-dose radiotherapy for high-risk neuroblastoma after intensive chemotherapy and surgery."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "At 36 months after RT, the probability of primary-site failure was 10.1% +/- 5.3%."
    explanation: >-
      Results sentence from the same series (99 consecutively irradiated
      high-risk patients in first remission, median follow-up 21.1 months from
      radiotherapy): the estimated probability of primary-site failure 36 months
      after radiotherapy was 10.1% +/- 5.3%. The estimate is imprecise: the
      36-month point lies beyond the median follow-up, and the abstract counts
      only 35 patients followed for 36 months or more. There was
      no unirradiated comparison group, so the series reports the failure rate
      among irradiated patients but cannot show that radiotherapy itself lowers
      relapse; the authors conclude only that radiotherapy may help in local
      control. Failure was higher in two subgroups: three of the seven patients
      irradiated with residual primary-site disease relapsed there, and 4 of the
      18 patients with MYCN-amplified disease plus serum LDH above 1,500 U/L had
      local failure (23.4% +/- 10.7% risk at 18 months). No primary-site relapse
      occurred among the 23 patients whose tumors were excised at diagnosis, and
      the authors suggest radiotherapy to the primary site may not be necessary
      for them. Abstract results sentence.
- name: Anti-GD2 Immunotherapy
  description: >-
    An anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody added to post-consolidation therapy is
    standard of care in high-risk neuroblastoma. In the randomized COG trial
    ANBL0032 the comparator arm was isotretinoin, which both arms received, and
    adding the antibody with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2 improved both
    event-free and overall survival; the five-year follow-up kept both
    differences. Dinutuximab is the licensed agent in the United States and
    dinutuximab beta in Europe. The contribution of the two cytokines is not
    settled in the way the antibody's is: in the European HR-NBL1/SIOPEN
    randomization, adding subcutaneous interleukin-2 to dinutuximab beta gave
    no event-free survival benefit and added toxicity, and the trialists
    recommended the regimen without it as the standard of care, while the
    United States label still lists interleukin-2. No trial has ever isolated
    GM-CSF's own contribution.
    The benefit is therefore recorded here as a regimen-level effect of
    anti-GD2-based immunotherapy rather than as an effect of any one component.
    Grade 3 to 5 pain occurred in about half the immunotherapy arm of ANBL0032,
    an on-target toxicity of GD2 on peripheral nerves.
  therapeutic_modality: MONOCLONAL_ANTIBODY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Monoclonal Antibody Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15490
      label: Monoclonal Antibody Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: dinutuximab
      term:
        id: NCIT:C1570
        label: Dinutuximab
    - preferred_term: dinutuximab beta
      term:
        id: CHEBI:759751
        label: dinutuximab beta
    - preferred_term: sargramostim (GM-CSF)
      term:
        id: NCIT:C1492
        label: Sargramostim
  notes: >-
    Both licensed anti-GD2 antibodies are bound, from the vocabulary that
    carries each. NCIT has no dinutuximab beta class: searched 2026-10-22 with
    `l~Dinutuximab Beta` (no results) and `l^Dinutuximab`, which returns only
    NCIT:C1570 Dinutuximab and NCIT:C174559 Dinutuximab/Irinotecan/Temozolomide
    Regimen. CHEBI carries it as CHEBI:759751, so dinutuximab beta is bound
    there while dinutuximab stays on NCIT:C1570, matching the naxitamab record
    below. Interleukin-2 is named in the description but deliberately not bound
    as an agent, because the randomized HR-NBL1 result found no event-free
    survival benefit from adding it.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20879881
    reference_title: "Anti-GD2 antibody with GM-CSF, interleukin-2, and isotretinoin for neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "to receive standard therapy (six cycles of isotretinoin) or immunotherapy (six cycles of isotretinoin and five concomitant cycles of ch14.18 in combination with alternating GM-CSF and interleukin-2)"
    explanation: >-
      The trial design, and the correction it forces on any summary of this
      treatment: isotretinoin was given in both arms, so the randomized
      comparison is the antibody plus cytokines added to isotretinoin, not
      immunotherapy against nothing. Abstract methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:20879881
    reference_title: "Anti-GD2 antibody with GM-CSF, interleukin-2, and isotretinoin for neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Immunotherapy was superior to standard therapy with regard to rates of event-free survival (66+/-5% vs. 46+/-5% at 2 years, P=0.01) and overall survival (86+/-4% vs. 75+/-5% at 2 years, P=0.02 without adjustment for interim analyses)"
    explanation: >-
      The randomized result behind this treatment's place in standard care.
      The overall-survival P value is explicitly unadjusted for the interim
      analyses, which is why the long-term item below is cited for the
      survival claim rather than this one alone. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33504555
    reference_title: "Long-Term Follow-up of a Phase III Study of ch14.18 (Dinutuximab) + Cytokine Immunotherapy in Children with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: COG Study ANBL0032."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "5-year EFS was 56.6 ± 4.7% for patients randomized to immunotherapy (n = 114) versus 46.1 ± 5.1% for those randomized to isotretinoin only (n = 112; P = 0.042)"
    explanation: >-
      The durable result, at five years and with the randomized arms named
      explicitly, which is the figure to cite for the survival benefit rather
      than the early unadjusted one. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:30442501
    reference_title: "Interleukin 2 with anti-GD2 antibody ch14.18/CHO (dinutuximab beta) in patients with high-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NBL1/SIOPEN): a multicentre, randomised, phase 3 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There is no evidence that addition of subcutaneous IL-2 to immunotherapy with dinutuximab beta, given as an 8 h infusion, improved outcomes in patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who had responded to standard induction and consolidation treatment."
    explanation: >-
      The randomized null on interleukin-2 in 406 patients, all of whom
      received isotretinoin. It supports the description's statement that the
      cytokine component is not established, and it is why this record does
      not bind interleukin-2 as a therapeutic agent. Abstract interpretation
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:30442501
    reference_title: "Interleukin 2 with anti-GD2 antibody ch14.18/CHO (dinutuximab beta) in patients with high-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NBL1/SIOPEN): a multicentre, randomised, phase 3 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Dinutuximab beta and isotretinoin without subcutaneous IL-2 should thus be considered the standard of care"
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own recommendation, which is what makes the regimen in the
      description the current European standard. Note the hedge they attach in
      the same sentence, that this holds until ongoing trials of a modified
      interleukin-2 schedule report. Abstract interpretation sentence.
  - reference: PMID:42760926
    reference_title: "Comparative evidence on the independent contribution of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor to anti-GD2 immunotherapy in neuroblastoma: a systematic review and gap analysis."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "No study directly compared otherwise equivalent anti-GD2 regimens that differed only in the inclusion of GM-CSF"
    explanation: >-
      Why GM-CSF's own contribution is described as unisolated rather than
      established or refuted: no trial has made the comparison that would
      settle it. Graded OTHER because the finding is the result of a
      systematic review of the trial literature rather than a study of
      patients. GM-CSF is still bound as a therapeutic agent because it is
      part of the regimen that was tested, not because its separate effect is
      known.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Anti-GD2 Antibody-Mediated Tumor Cell Killing
    treatment_effect: ACTIVATES
    description: >-
      The antibody supplies the opsonizing arm this node needs: bound to
      surface GD2 it recruits Fc-receptor-bearing innate effector cells and
      activates complement, so the treatment creates the killing rather than
      inhibiting an existing disease process. This is why the link is
      ACTIVATES and not INHIBITS.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:34884452
      reference_title: "Mechanisms, Characteristics, and Treatment of Neuropathic Pain and Peripheral Neuropathy Associated with Dinutuximab in Neuroblastoma Patients."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "Anti GD2 antibodies bind to surface GD2 and determine the lysis of neuroblastoma cells induced by immune response via the antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and the complement-dependent cytotoxicity"
      explanation: >-
        States the drug-to-mechanism step this link asserts, naming both
        effector routes. Graded REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER because the citing
        document is a review restating established pharmacology.
- name: Naxitamab with GM-CSF
  description: >-
    A second anti-GD2 antibody, humanized rather than chimeric, with a much
    narrower license than dinutuximab: in the United States it has accelerated
    approval with GM-CSF for relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in
    the bone or bone marrow, on the strength of overall response rate and
    duration of response in single-arm studies rather than a randomized
    survival comparison. Its phase 2 trial reported an overall response rate of
    50%. It is recorded separately from the post-consolidation antibody record
    above because the indication, the line of therapy and the strength of
    evidence all differ.
  therapeutic_modality: MONOCLONAL_ANTIBODY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Monoclonal Antibody Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15490
      label: Monoclonal Antibody Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: naxitamab
      term:
        id: NCIT:C123428
        label: Naxitamab
    - preferred_term: sargramostim (GM-CSF)
      term:
        id: NCIT:C1492
        label: Sargramostim
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33616889
    reference_title: "Naxitamab: First Approval."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma in the bone or bone marrow demonstrating a partial response, minor response, or stable disease to prior therapy"
    explanation: >-
      The licensed indication, which is the narrow scope this record is about
      and the reason it is separate from the post-consolidation record. Graded
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER because the document is a drug-approval
      review reporting a regulatory decision rather than study results.
  - reference: PMID:39952926
    reference_title: "The anti-GD2 monoclonal antibody naxitamab plus GM-CSF for relapsed or refractory high-risk neuroblastoma: a phase 2 clinical trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall response rate (ORR) was 50% (95% CI: 36-64%), and CR and PR were observed in 38% and 12%"
    explanation: >-
      The trial result behind the approval, in 52 evaluable patients. A
      single-arm response rate, so it says nothing about survival relative to
      any alternative, which is what the accelerated-approval basis in the
      item above reflects. Abstract results sentence.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Anti-GD2 Antibody-Mediated Tumor Cell Killing
    treatment_effect: ACTIVATES
    description: >-
      The same antigen and the same effector mechanism as the chimeric
      antibody above; naxitamab is humanized and given with GM-CSF, but it
      acts on this node by the same route.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35435953
      reference_title: "Immunotherapy of Neuroblastoma: Facts and Hopes."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "The identification of strong expression of the disialoganglioside GD2 on the surface of nearly all neuroblastoma cells provided a target for immune recognition by anti-GD2 mAbs that recruit Fc receptor-expressing innate immune cells that mediate cytotoxicity or phagocytosis"
      explanation: >-
        Supports the shared mechanism for anti-GD2 antibodies as a class,
        which is the claim this link makes for naxitamab. Graded
        REVIEW_SYNTHESIS and OTHER as a review statement.
- name: Crizotinib
  description: >-
    First-generation ATP-competitive ALK/MET inhibitor, and the first ALK
    inhibitor tested in neuroblastoma. Its activity in this disease is poor and
    variant-dependent: in the Children's Oncology Group ADVL0912 trial the
    objective response rate in 20 children with relapsed or refractory
    ALK-aberrant neuroblastoma was 15%, all three responders carried the
    R1275Q hotspot mutation, and patients with F1174L or F1174V progressed
    within one to three cycles. The failure has a specific mechanistic reading
    rather than being a general lack of target engagement: the F1174 mutants
    raise ALK's affinity for ATP, which blunts an ATP-competitive inhibitor at
    achievable exposures. This is what motivated the move to
    third-generation inhibitors. The ALK-altered subset this applies to
    includes amplification as well as point mutation, and there the
    preclinical and clinical results diverge: crizotinib inhibited cell lines
    carrying amplified wild-type ALK and produced complete regression of an
    ALK-amplified xenograft, but both amplified patients in ADVL0912 had no
    response and each received a single cycle before progression, and the
    trial concludes it has no objective single-agent activity in amplified
    disease. Two patients is a small denominator, but it is a reported
    negative rather than an absence of data.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Targeted Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: crizotinib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:64310
        label: crizotinib
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The objective response rate for patients with neuroblastoma was 15% [95% confidence interval (CI): 3.3%-34.3%]: two with partial responses and 1 with a complete response."
    explanation: >-
      The response rate quoted in the description, from the disease-specific
      stratum of ADVL0912 at the recommended phase 2 dose. The confidence
      interval runs from 3.3% to 34.3%, so 15% is an imprecise estimate on 20
      patients rather than a settled figure. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Twenty patients with relapsed/refractory ALK-positive neuroblastoma, treated at the RP2D, were enrolled between March 2012 and July 2015; all were eligible and evaluable for response."
    explanation: >-
      The denominator behind the response rate above, and that no patient was
      excluded from the response analysis. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All three patients had a somatic ALK Arg1275Gln mutation, the most common ALK hotspot mutation observed in neuroblastoma and the only mutation predicted to be sensitive to ALK inhibition with crizotinib"
    explanation: >-
      Which patients responded, and the reason this treatment is recorded as
      variant-dependent rather than simply weak: every responder carried
      R1275Q, the one hotspot predicted sensitive to crizotinib. Abstract
      results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Three patients with ALK Phe1174Leu mutations progressed during cycle 1 of therapy, and one patient with an ALK Phe1174Val received three cycles before disease progression."
    explanation: >-
      Contradicts any use of crizotinib against F1174-mutant neuroblastoma:
      all four such patients in ADVL0912 progressed, three of them within the
      first cycle. Recorded as its own REFUTE item because the same trial
      produces both the responses above and this failure, and which applies
      depends on the variant. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The two patients with ALK amplification had no response."
    explanation: >-
      The clinical counterpart of the amplified-xenograft result on the
      mechanism link below, and it cuts the other way: neither amplified
      patient in ADVL0912 responded. Two patients is a small denominator and
      the trial reports elsewhere that each received only one cycle before
      progression, so this is a weak negative rather than a settled one. It
      sits here rather than on the mechanism link because the trial measured
      tumor response, not kinase inhibition, so it bears on whether the drug
      works in amplified disease and not on whether it engages its target.
      Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:33568345
    reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "crizotinib has no objective single agent activity in neuroblastomas harboring other hotspot ALK mutations or amplification"
    explanation: >-
      The trial's own summary of the two negatives this record carries, the
      F1174 progressions above and the amplified pair, in one sentence.
      Quoted because it is the authors' conclusion about those strata rather
      than a reader's inference from two small counts.
  - reference: PMID:23598171
    reference_title: "Safety and activity of crizotinib for paediatric patients with refractory solid tumours or anaplastic large-cell lymphoma: a Children's Oncology Group phase 1 consortium study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the anti-tumour activity was enriched in patients with known activating ALK aberrations (eight of nine with anaplastic large-cell lymphoma, one of 11 with neuroblastoma, three of seven with inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour, and one of two with NSCLC)"
    explanation: >-
      The earlier phase 1 signal that led to the disease-specific stratum, and
      how weak it was for this disease specifically: one of 11 neuroblastoma
      patients responded, against eight of nine with anaplastic large-cell
      lymphoma in the same trial. Indirect for a neuroblastoma treatment
      claim, because the quoted sentence reports a cross-histology comparison
      in a trial of refractory solid tumours and lymphoma rather than a
      neuroblastoma result on its own. Abstract findings sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37561984
    reference_title: Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase Inhibitors for Therapy of Neuroblastoma in Adults.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "No responses were observed with crizotinib (n = 5 patients), ceritinib, alectinib, or brigatinib (n = 1 each)."
    explanation: >-
      An independent null result in a different population: adults and
      adolescents with ALK-mutated adult-onset neuroblastoma treated at a
      single centre, none of the five given crizotinib responding. A small
      series, but it is the only cohort here that compares crizotinib with
      later-generation inhibitors in the same patients. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:34536944
    reference_title: "Second Paediatric Strategy Forum for anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibition in paediatric malignancies: ACCELERATE in collaboration with the European Medicines Agency with the participation of the Food and Drug Administration."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "For neuroblastoma, crizotinib has not shown robust anti-tumour activity."
    explanation: >-
      The regulatory and expert-consensus reading of the trial results above,
      from a strategy forum convened with the European Medicines Agency and
      attended by the Food and Drug Administration. Graded OTHER because a
      forum conclusion is expert consensus rather than a study, and
      REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the forum is synthesising work it did not
      perform.
  effect_modifiers:
  - effect_modifier_type: GENOTYPE
    stratum: patients with ALK F1174L or F1174V
    comparator_stratum: patients with ALK R1275Q
    modified_outcome: objective response
    effect_in_stratum: NO_EFFECT
    modification_analysis: CROSS_STRATUM_COMPARISON
    description: >-
      Within ADVL0912 the response was entirely variant-determined: all three
      responders carried R1275Q, the one hotspot predicted sensitive to
      crizotinib, while all four patients with an F1174 substitution
      progressed, three of them during the first cycle. The trial reports the
      comparison itself, so the direction here is the source's and not a
      reading of two numbers side by side. No treatment-by-genotype
      interaction was tested, so interaction_tested is left off.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33568345
      reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "All three patients had a somatic ALK Arg1275Gln mutation, the most common ALK hotspot mutation observed in neuroblastoma and the only mutation predicted to be sensitive to ALK inhibition with crizotinib"
      explanation: >-
        The comparator stratum: every responder carried R1275Q. Abstract
        results sentence.
    - reference: PMID:33568345
      reference_title: "Activity of Crizotinib in Patients with ALK-Aberrant Relapsed/Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Children's Oncology Group Study (ADVL0912)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Three patients with ALK Phe1174Leu mutations progressed during cycle 1 of therapy, and one patient with an ALK Phe1174Val received three cycles before disease progression."
      explanation: >-
        The stratum with no effect: all four F1174 patients progressed.
        Abstract results sentence.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: ALK Signaling Activation
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      ATP-competitive inhibition of the ALK tyrosine kinase domain removes the
      constitutive receptor autophosphorylation produced by activating ALK
      mutations, and with it the downstream proliferative signal. Target
      engagement is variant-dependent, because the F1174 substitutions raise
      the kinase's ATP affinity and so compete directly with the inhibitor.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:18724359
      reference_title: "Identification of ALK as a major familial neuroblastoma predisposition gene."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Mutations resulted in constitutive phosphorylation, and targeted knockdown of ALK messenger RNA resulted in profound inhibition of growth in all cell lines harbouring mutant or amplified ALK"
      explanation: >-
        Establishes ALK dependence of ALK-mutant and ALK-amplified
        neuroblastoma cells, the mechanistic rationale for ALK-directed
        therapy. Indirect for a drug claim: the experiment knocks the
        transcript down genetically rather than inhibiting the kinase
        pharmacologically, so crizotinib's own effect on this node follows
        only by inference.
    - reference: PMID:22072639
      reference_title: Differential inhibitor sensitivity of anaplastic lymphoma kinase variants found in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "In contrast, cell lines harboring F1174L-mutated ALK were relatively resistant to crizotinib."
      explanation: >-
        The variant dependence of target engagement, across a panel of 18
        human neuroblastoma-derived cell lines spanning ALK genomic states.
        Predicted the clinical F1174L failures above. Abstract sentence.
    - reference: PMID:22072639
      reference_title: Differential inhibitor sensitivity of anaplastic lymphoma kinase variants found in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "These results argue that tumors driven by F1174L-mutated ALK are significantly less sensitive to crizotinib in vivo."
      explanation: >-
        The same variant dependence in vivo, from SH-SY5Y and NBSD (F1174L)
        against NB1643 (R1275Q) human neuroblastoma xenografts in
        immunodeficient mice given crizotinib for four weeks. Full-text
        results sentence closing the xenograft paragraph.
    - reference: PMID:23598171
      reference_title: "Safety and activity of crizotinib for paediatric patients with refractory solid tumours or anaplastic large-cell lymphoma: a Children's Oncology Group phase 1 consortium study."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Crizotinib resistance in neuroblastoma cells expressing an Phe1174 mutation probably arises, at least partly, from increased ATP-binding affinity for this mutant, which might reduce the potency of ATP-competitive inhibitors."
      explanation: >-
        The mechanism given in the description for why an ATP-competitive
        inhibitor fails against F1174 mutants. Graded IN_VITRO with
        quote_role BACKGROUND because the sentence sits in the clinical
        trial's discussion and restates cell-line work the trial did not
        perform; the evidence it describes is the cell-line data, not the
        trial.
    - reference: PMID:25517749
      reference_title: ALK mutations confer differential oncogenic activation and sensitivity to ALK inhibition therapy in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Of the activating mutations, in vitro analyses suggest that only 6 (including R1275Q) will be sensitive to inhibition by crizotinib in vivo."
      explanation: >-
        How narrow the sensitive set is, across 24 patient-derived ALK
        kinase-domain mutations found in 1,596 diagnostic neuroblastoma
        samples and assayed as recombinant kinase domains and in NIH 3T3
        focus assays. Indirect because the sentence is an in vitro prediction
        about in vivo sensitivity, which the authors label as such.
    - reference: PMID:22072639
      reference_title: Differential inhibitor sensitivity of anaplastic lymphoma kinase variants found in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "Crizotinib treatment led to complete tumor regression in NB1 xenografts with amplified, overexpressed wild-type ALK"
      explanation: >-
        Keeps the ALK-amplified subset in view, which the mutation-centred
        items above do not cover: in a xenograft carrying amplified,
        overexpressed wild-type ALK rather than a kinase-domain mutation,
        crizotinib produced complete regression. Preclinical only, and it did
        not carry over: the two amplified patients treated in ADVL0912 both
        failed to respond, which this record's treatment-level evidence
        records. Full-text xenograft result.
- name: Lorlatinib
  description: >-
    Third-generation macrocyclic ALK inhibitor, designed to retain potency
    against the ALK kinase-domain mutations that resist crizotinib and to cross
    the blood-brain barrier. In the NANT phase 1 trial in relapsed or
    refractory ALK-driven neuroblastoma the single-agent response rate was 30%
    in patients under 18 and 67% in those 18 or over, 63% when combined with
    chemotherapy, with activity across all three neuroblastoma hotspot
    mutations and in patients who had already received another ALK inhibitor.
    Reported response rates vary by cohort and by what is counted: 69% in a
    single-centre adult series and 33% in a French compassionate-use registry,
    where no patient with MYCN amplification responded. Lorlatinib has replaced
    crizotinib in the Children's Oncology Group frontline phase 3 trial for
    ALK-altered high-risk disease. Applicable only to the ALK-altered
    molecular subset.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Targeted Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C93352
      label: Targeted Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: lorlatinib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:143117
        label: lorlatinib
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37012551
    reference_title: "Lorlatinib with or without chemotherapy in ALK-driven refractory/relapsed neuroblastoma: phase 1 trial results."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The single-agent response rate (complete/partial/minor) for <18 years was 30%; for >=18 years, 67%; and for chemotherapy combination in <18 years, 63%"
    explanation: >-
      The trial response rates quoted in the description, from 49 patients
      with relapsed or refractory ALK-driven neuroblastoma, 34 of them under
      18. Note the response definition includes minor responses, so these
      figures are not comparable with an objective response rate counting
      complete and partial responses only. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37012551
    reference_title: "Lorlatinib with or without chemotherapy in ALK-driven refractory/relapsed neuroblastoma: phase 1 trial results."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Single-agent lorlatinib demonstrated clinical activity across patients of all ages harboring the three neuroblastoma-specific hotspot ALK mutations, including patients who had previously received other ALK TKIs."
    explanation: >-
      The claim that separates this drug from crizotinib in the record above:
      activity across all three hotspots rather than R1275Q alone, and in the
      20 of 49 patients already exposed to another ALK inhibitor. Full-text
      discussion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37561984
    reference_title: Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase Inhibitors for Therapy of Neuroblastoma in Adults.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of the 13 patients receiving lorlatinib, four, five, and four patients had a complete or partial response (major response rate 69%), and stable disease, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      The adult figure quoted in the description, from the same single-centre
      series that recorded no responses to crizotinib, which is the sharpest
      within-cohort contrast between the two drugs available here. Thirteen
      patients, five of them after another ALK inhibitor. Abstract results
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:38787533
    reference_title: Sequential Analysis of cfDNA Reveals Clonal Evolution in Patients with Neuroblastoma Receiving ALK-Targeted Therapy.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall response rate to lorlatinib was 33% (CI, 13%-59%), with response observed in 6/10 cases without versus 0/8 cases with MYCN amplification"
    explanation: >-
      The lowest response rate reported here, and the stratification that
      matters clinically: in 18 patients given compassionate-use or off-label
      lorlatinib in France, not one of the eight with MYCN amplification
      responded. Supports the description's statement that reported rates
      vary by cohort, and records the MYCN-amplified subset as a limit on this
      treatment. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:39177282
    reference_title: Long-Lasting Response to Lorlatinib in Patients with ALK-Driven Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma Monitored with Circulating Tumor DNA Analysis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All four patients with ALK p.R1275Q experienced major responses and were alive 35 to 61 months after starting lorlatinib."
    explanation: >-
      Duration, which none of the response-rate items above speaks to: four
      R1275Q patients in an unselected Swedish national cohort alive between
      35 and 61 months after starting the drug. Five patients in total, so
      this is a case series rather than a cohort estimate. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37147298
    reference_title: Circulating tumor DNA reveals mechanisms of lorlatinib resistance in patients with relapsed/refractory ALK-driven neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This hypothesis is being addressed formally in the current Children's Oncology Group Phase 3 study for patients with ALK-driven high risk NB (NCT03126916) where lorlatinib has replaced crizotinib during frontline therapy"
    explanation: >-
      Sources the description's frontline statement, and states the
      substitution precisely: one Children's Oncology Group phase 3 study, in
      which lorlatinib replaced crizotinib. Graded BACKGROUND because the
      sentence describes a different trial from the one this paper reports.
      Full-text discussion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:42151367
    reference_title: Lorlatinib monotherapy or combination therapy in anaplastic lymphoma kinase-driven high-risk neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The Children's Oncology Group (COG) Phase III trial (NCT03126916) investigating lorlatinib plus standard therapy in newly diagnosed ALK-altered neuroblastoma is ongoing, with results pending"
    explanation: >-
      Independent confirmation of the frontline statement, and that the trial
      has not reported: results were still pending when this was written, so
      nothing in this record claims a frontline outcome. Graded BACKGROUND
      for the same reason as the item above. Full-text sentence, not in the
      abstract.
  - reference: PMID:37012551
    reference_title: "Lorlatinib with or without chemotherapy in ALK-driven refractory/relapsed neuroblastoma: phase 1 trial results."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Lorlatinib was optimized to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, leading to improved CNS distribution as well as intracranial responses in patients with NCSLC with brain metastases"
    explanation: >-
      The design rationale for central nervous system penetration stated in
      the description. The intracranial responses it reports are in
      non-small-cell lung cancer, not neuroblastoma, which is why it is graded
      BACKGROUND inside a neuroblastoma trial paper. The source's own
      spelling of NSCLC is kept. Full-text discussion sentence.
  - reference: PMID:29074098
    reference_title: "Lorlatinib in non-small-cell lung cancer with ALK or ROS1 rearrangement: an international, multicentre, open-label, single-arm first-in-man phase 1 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Thus, the mean CSF concentrations of lorlatinib correspond to 75% of unbound plasma concentrations"
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the central nervous system exposure behind the design claim,
      from paired lumbar-puncture and plasma sampling in four adults. Indirect
      for this entry: the measurement is a property of the drug rather than of
      neuroblastoma, but it was made in non-small-cell lung cancer patients,
      so its relevance here rests on the exposure carrying over. Full-text
      pharmacokinetics sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37012551
    reference_title: "Lorlatinib with or without chemotherapy in ALK-driven refractory/relapsed neuroblastoma: phase 1 trial results."
    supports: NO_EVIDENCE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Intracranial anti-tumor activity could not be assessed in our study as no patient with CNS metastases enrolled"
    explanation: >-
      The boundary of the two central-nervous-system items above, in the
      authors' own words: the neuroblastoma trial enrolled nobody with
      central nervous system metastases, so it says nothing either way about
      intracranial activity in this disease. Graded NO_EVIDENCE because the
      quoted sentence states the absence of a result rather than supporting or
      contradicting the claim. Full-text discussion sentence.
  effect_modifiers:
  - effect_modifier_type: BIOMARKER
    stratum: MYCN-amplified
    comparator_stratum: without MYCN amplification
    modified_outcome: overall response
    effect_in_stratum: NO_EFFECT
    modification_analysis: CROSS_STRATUM_COMPARISON
    description: >-
      In the French compassionate-use and off-label registry series, response
      was confined to the MYCN-non-amplified patients: six of ten responded
      without amplification against none of eight with it. The source states
      the stratified comparison itself. MYCN amplification is typed BIOMARKER
      rather than GENOTYPE because it is a somatic tumour feature used to
      stratify, not a germline or variant genotype of the patient. No
      interaction test is reported, so interaction_tested is left off.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:38787533
      reference_title: Sequential Analysis of cfDNA Reveals Clonal Evolution in Patients with Neuroblastoma Receiving ALK-Targeted Therapy.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Overall response rate to lorlatinib was 33% (CI, 13%-59%), with response observed in 6/10 cases without versus 0/8 cases with MYCN amplification"
      explanation: >-
        The stratified comparison, reported by the source in that form, in 18
        patients given compassionate-use or off-label lorlatinib in France.
        Abstract results sentence.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: ALK Signaling Activation
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Inhibition of the ALK tyrosine kinase domain by a macrocyclic inhibitor
      whose binding is less sensitive to the ATP-affinity increase that the
      F1174 and F1245 substitutions produce, so the constitutive signal is
      removed in the variants that resist crizotinib as well as in R1275Q.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26554404
      reference_title: The ALK/ROS1 Inhibitor PF-06463922 Overcomes Primary Resistance to Crizotinib in ALK-Driven Neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "We find that PF-06463922 has high potency across ALK variants and inhibits ALK more effectively than crizotinib in vitro."
      explanation: >-
        Direct biochemical and cell-line comparison of the two inhibitors on
        this node, against purified ALK kinase domains carrying R1275Q, F1174L
        and F1245C plus neuroblastoma cell lines. PF-06463922 is lorlatinib's
        development code, which is how both preclinical papers cited here name
        it. Abstract sentence.
    - reference: PMID:26554404
      reference_title: The ALK/ROS1 Inhibitor PF-06463922 Overcomes Primary Resistance to Crizotinib in ALK-Driven Neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "Most importantly, PF-06463922 induces complete tumor regression in both crizotinib-resistant and crizotinib-sensitive xenograft mouse models of neuroblastoma, as well as in patient-derived xenografts harboring the crizotinib-resistant F1174L or F1245C mutations."
      explanation: >-
        The in vivo result that made the clinical trial worth running, in
        cell-line xenografts and in patient-derived xenografts carrying the
        two variants that failed on crizotinib. Mouse models only; no human
        subjects. Abstract sentence.
    - reference: PMID:27483357
      reference_title: The ALK inhibitor PF-06463922 is effective as a single agent in neuroblastoma driven by expression of ALK and MYCN.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "In contrast to crizotinib, single agent administration of PF-06463922 caused dramatic tumor inhibition in both subcutaneous and orthotopic xenografts as well as a mouse model of high-risk neuroblastoma driven by Th-ALK(F1174L)/MYCN"
      explanation: >-
        Independent replication by a second group, and the only preclinical
        item here in a model that carries MYCN as well as mutant ALK, which is
