        the genotype the French registry found unresponsive in patients.
        Orthotopic adrenal and subcutaneous xenografts in nude mice plus
        Th-ALK(F1174L)/MYCN double-transgenic mice. Abstract sentence.
- name: Adavosertib (WEE1 Inhibition)
  description: >-
    An oral WEE1 inhibitor, tested in children with relapsed neuroblastoma in
    two combinations. In the Children's Oncology Group ADVL1312 phase 2
    expansion it was given with irinotecan to 20 patients and produced three
    objective responses, meeting that trial's pre-set efficacy bar, in a
    population with a median of three prior regimens of whom 95% had already
    had irinotecan. In AcSe-ESMART Arm C it was given with carboplatin across
    paediatric malignancies, where the overall response rate was 11% with two
    partial responses in neuroblastoma, and the combination was limited by
    haematologic toxicity. Both are small, early-phase and uncontrolled, and
    neither establishes that the benefit comes from relieving the checkpoint
    dependence the drug targets.
  context: Relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma, in combination
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: adavosertib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:91414
        label: adavosertib
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Replication-Stress Checkpoint Dependence
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Adavosertib inhibits WEE1, one of the two checkpoint kinases the node is
      built on, which is intended to let stressed cells enter mitosis
      unrepaired.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37081608
    reference_title: "Pediatric phase 2 trial of a WEE1 inhibitor, adavosertib (AZD1775), and irinotecan for relapsed neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There were three objective responses (9, 11, and 18 cycles) meeting the protocol defined efficacy end point."
    explanation: >-
      The trial's own efficacy result in the neuroblastoma cohort, against a
      bar it set in advance of at least three responses in twenty.
  - reference: PMID:37081608
    reference_title: "Pediatric phase 2 trial of a WEE1 inhibitor, adavosertib (AZD1775), and irinotecan for relapsed neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 20 patients with neuroblastoma (part B) had a median of three prior regimens and 95% had a history of prior irinotecan."
    explanation: >-
      What that bar was cleared against, and the reason the description does
      not present three responses as a modest result without saying so: nearly
      all of these children had already progressed on the partner drug.
      Indirect, because prior exposure is context for the result rather than a
      measure of the drug's effect.
  - reference: PMID:38051741
    reference_title: "Phase I/II Study of the WEE1 Inhibitor Adavosertib (AZD1775) in Combination with Carboplatin in Children with Advanced Malignancies: Arm C of the AcSé-ESMART Trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall response rate was 11% (95% confidence interval, 0.0-25.6) with partial responses in 2 patients with neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The second combination's result, across a mixed paediatric population
      with the two responses falling in neuroblastoma. Note the confidence
      interval includes zero.
  - reference: PMID:38051741
    reference_title: "Phase I/II Study of the WEE1 Inhibitor Adavosertib (AZD1775) in Combination with Carboplatin in Children with Advanced Malignancies: Arm C of the AcSé-ESMART Trial."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Adavosertib-carboplatin combination exhibited significant hematologic toxicity."
    explanation: >-
      Bears against this particular combination as a usable regimen: the trial
      de-escalated twice and set no recommended phase 2 dose. It does not bear
      against WEE1 inhibition as such, which the irinotecan combination
      delivered without dose-limiting toxicity.
- name: Isotretinoin (Retinoic Acid)
  description: >-
    13-cis-retinoic acid (isotretinoin) given during maintenance therapy, on
    the rationale that it drives differentiation of residual neuroblastoma
    cells. Its place rests on the second randomization of CCG-3891, which
    reported significantly better three-year event-free survival for six
    months of the drug than for no further therapy, 46% against 29%. The
    long-term report of that same randomization is weaker: at five years
    event-free survival was still higher with the drug, 42% against 31%, but
    not significantly so, and after a published correction the paper concludes
    that neither myeloablative therapy with autologous rescue nor
    13-cis-retinoic acid significantly improved overall survival. CCG-3891
    enrolled between January 1991 and April 1996, whereas current standard of
    care adds anti-disialoganglioside antibody immunotherapy in the same
    maintenance phase, so the trial that established this drug tested it
    without the treatment it now sits beside.
  notes: >-
    The 2009 long-term report carries an erratum, J Clin Oncol 2014;32:1862-3,
    which reversed its overall-survival conclusion. The cached record holds
    both versions: the corrected conclusion in the abstract, quoted below, and
    the uncorrected sentence in the full text, which asserts an independent
    overall-survival benefit for 13-cis-retinoic acid. Cite the corrected one.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: isotretinoin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:6067
        label: isotretinoin
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:10519894
    reference_title: "Treatment of high-risk neuroblastoma with intensive chemotherapy, radiotherapy, autologous bone marrow transplantation, and 13-cis-retinoic acid. Children's Cancer Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The event-free survival rate three years after the second randomization was significantly better among the 130 patients who were assigned to receive 13-cis-retinoic acid than among the 128 patients assigned to receive no further therapy (46+/-6 percent vs. 29+/-5 percent, P=0.027)."
    explanation: >-
      The result this treatment record rests on, from the second randomization
      of CCG-3891: six months of 13-cis-retinoic acid against no further
      therapy, in patients who had completed cytotoxic therapy without
      progression. Note the size, 130 against 128 patients, and that the
      endpoint is event-free survival at three years.
  - reference: PMID:19171716
    reference_title: "Long-term results for children with high-risk neuroblastoma treated on a randomized trial of myeloablative therapy followed by 13-cis-retinoic acid: a children's oncology group study."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 5-year EFS (42% +/- 5% v 31% +/- 5%) from the time of second random assignment was higher for cis-RA than for no further therapy, though it was not significant."
    explanation: >-
      The same randomization followed for five years: the event-free survival
      advantage is still in the same direction but no longer significant. This
      bears against reading the three-year result above as a durable
      event-free survival benefit. It does not say the drug is ineffective,
      and the trial was not powered for a five-year comparison in this second
      randomization.
  - reference: PMID:19171716
    reference_title: "Long-term results for children with high-risk neuroblastoma treated on a randomized trial of myeloablative therapy followed by 13-cis-retinoic acid: a children's oncology group study."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "neither myeloablative therapy with ... autologous hematopoietic cell rescue nor cis-RA given after consolidation therapy significantly improved OS"
    explanation: >-
      The paper's conclusion on overall survival as it now stands, after the
      2014 erratum recorded in this record's notes. Quoted from the corrected
      abstract; the uncorrected full text in the same cached file says the
      opposite, that 13-cis-retinoic acid independently improved overall
      survival, and must not be cited. The corrected sentence carries an
      editorial bracket mid-clause, which the quote bridges rather than
      reproduces, since the claim does not turn on it.
  - reference: PMID:19171716
    reference_title: "Long-term results for children with high-risk neuroblastoma treated on a randomized trial of myeloablative therapy followed by 13-cis-retinoic acid: a children's oncology group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Enrollment occurred between January 1991 and April 1996."
    explanation: >-
      Dates the trial, which is what makes the description's point about
      sequence checkable rather than rhetorical: the randomization that
      established this drug ran years before anti-GD2 immunotherapy entered
      the same maintenance phase. Indirect, because a date is not a result
      about the drug.
  - reference: PMID:31454045
    reference_title: "Effect of Tandem Autologous Stem Cell Transplant vs Single Transplant on Event-Free Survival in Patients With High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Induction chemotherapy followed by high-dose therapy with autologous stem cell transplant and subsequent antidisialoganglioside antibody immunotherapy is standard of care for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma, but survival rate among these patients remains low."
    explanation: >-
      The other half of that comparison: what maintenance now contains.
      Graded BACKGROUND because the sentence opens a trial report by stating
      the standard of care rather than reporting that trial's result, and
      INDIRECT because it describes the setting this drug is given in rather
      than its effect.
- name: Eflornithine (DFMO) Maintenance Therapy
  description: >-
    An oral ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor given as maintenance after
    front-line therapy, to reduce the risk of relapse rather than to treat
    active disease. The United States approved indication, granted on 13
    December 2023, is for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have
    demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality
    therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy; dosing in the pivotal study was
    oral, twice daily and continued for up to two years. The evidence base is
    unusual and the record is written around that: approval rested on an
    externally controlled trial, a single-arm study compared with an external
    control drawn from a separate cooperative-group trial, and the review
    describes it as the first oncology approval to rely on that design as its
    primary clinical data. Against the external control, event-free and overall
    survival both favoured eflornithine. No randomized trial has tested it in
    this setting.
  context: High-risk neuroblastoma, post-immunotherapy maintenance in remission
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  dosing_interval: twice a day
  dosing_interval_days: 0.5
  notes: >-
    Three caveats bear on how much this record should be taken to settle, and
    none of them is visible from the approval alone. First, the reviewers
    themselves called the missing randomized trial a significant limitation,
    given reliance on a time-to-event endpoint, and the cited approval summary
    is quoted for that below rather than only for the indication. Second, the
    mechanism at the approved dose is open: a 2025 study found that low-dose
    eflornithine did not extend survival in mouse models and that sensitivity
    did not track MYCN or ODC1 copy number, which is why the linked
    pathophysiology node is marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED. Third,
    two facts relevant to reading the approval are not carried by any
    publication cached here and are therefore stated without an evidence item:
    the European Medicines Agency application was withdrawn in July 2025, with
    a provisional view that effectiveness had not been demonstrated, per the
    agency's own public medicine page; and the one randomized test of
    eflornithine in neuroblastoma, an add-on in relapsed or refractory disease
    (NCT03794349), posted response rates showing no advantage for the
    eflornithine arm. The registry record's cached body holds only its brief
    summary, so those figures cannot be quoted as a snippet. Both are recorded
    here because omitting them would leave "FDA-approved" reading as settled
    and global.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: eflornithine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:41948
        label: eflornithine
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38917371
    reference_title: "US Food and Drug Administration Approval Summary: Eflornithine for High-Risk Neuroblastoma After Prior Multiagent, Multimodality Therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "On December 13, 2023, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved eflornithine (IWILFIN, US WorldMeds) to reduce the risk of relapse in adult and pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have demonstrated at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy."
    explanation: >-
      The approved indication, in full, which is narrower than "approved for
      high-risk neuroblastoma": it is maintenance to reduce relapse risk, in
      patients who already responded to prior therapy that included anti-GD2
      immunotherapy. Graded OTHER because the quoted sentence states a
      regulatory decision rather than a study result.
  - reference: PMID:38917371
    reference_title: "US Food and Drug Administration Approval Summary: Eflornithine for High-Risk Neuroblastoma After Prior Multiagent, Multimodality Therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The approval was based on an externally controlled trial (ECT) consisting of a single-arm trial, study 3(b), compared with an external control (EC) derived from a National Cancer Institute/Children's Oncology Group-sponsored clinical trial (Study ANBL0032) and supported by confirmatory evidence."
    explanation: >-
      What the approval rested on, and the reason this record describes its
      own evidence base rather than presenting the indication alone: the
      comparison is against patients from a different trial, not a randomized
      control arm. Graded OTHER as a regulatory fact.
  - reference: PMID:38917371
    reference_title: "US Food and Drug Administration Approval Summary: Eflornithine for High-Risk Neuroblastoma After Prior Multiagent, Multimodality Therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Notably, this is the first oncology drug approval which relies on an ECT as the primary clinical data to support substantial evidence of effectiveness."
    explanation: >-
      How unusual the design is, in the reviewers' own words. Recorded because
      it is the fact a reader most needs in order to weigh this treatment
      against one approved on a randomized trial. Graded OTHER as a
      regulatory fact.
  - reference: PMID:38917371
    reference_title: "US Food and Drug Administration Approval Summary: Eflornithine for High-Risk Neuroblastoma After Prior Multiagent, Multimodality Therapy."
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Even so, the lack of an RCT was a significant limitation to this application given the reliance on a time to event endpoint with no expected objective response rate data."
    explanation: >-
      The reviewers' own statement of the weakness, recorded as a REFUTE item
      against reading this treatment's benefit as established rather than
      hidden in prose. It cuts against the strength of the evidence, not
      against the approval, which was granted. Graded OTHER as a regulatory
      fact.
  - reference: PMID:37883734
    reference_title: "Eflornithine as Postimmunotherapy Maintenance in High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Externally Controlled, Propensity Score-Matched Survival Outcome Comparisons."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "DFMO after completion of immunotherapy was associated with improved EFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.50 [95% CI, 0.29 to 0.84]; P = .008) and OS (HR, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.76]; P = .007)."
    explanation: >-
      The effect estimates behind the approval, from the externally controlled
      comparison of 141 patients against propensity-score-matched external
      controls. Read with the design in mind: these are not randomized
      estimates, and the item above records what the reviewers made of that.
      Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37883734
    reference_title: "Eflornithine as Postimmunotherapy Maintenance in High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Externally Controlled, Propensity Score-Matched Survival Outcome Comparisons."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "who received up to 2 years of continuous treatment with oral DFMO (750 ± 250 mg/m2 twice a day)"
    explanation: >-
      The route, schedule and duration stated in the description, and the
      source of the twice-daily dosing interval recorded on this record.
      Abstract methods clause.
  - reference: PMID:30262852
    reference_title: Maintenance DFMO Increases Survival in High Risk Neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "101 subjects enrolled on Stratum 1 and 100 were eligible for ITT analysis; two-year EFS was 84% (±4%) and OS 97% (±2%)."
    explanation: >-
      The single-arm survival figures from the pivotal study's first-remission
      stratum. Quoted with its denominator because the number that matters for
      an uncontrolled result is how many patients it rests on; no comparison
      arm is implied by this item.
  - reference: PMID:40774224
    reference_title: High-dose DFMO alters protein translation in neuroblastoma.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "We show that low-dose DFMO does not extend survival in mouse models in vivo nor alter translation biomarkers in vitro."
    explanation: >-
      Cuts against polyamine depletion being the operative mechanism at the
      dose that was approved: in mouse models the low dose neither extended
      survival nor moved the molecular readouts, while the high dose did. It
      does not contradict the clinical result, which stands on its own data;
      it contradicts the inference from that result to this mechanism, which
      is why the linked pathophysiology node is PROVISIONAL. Abstract
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:40774224
    reference_title: High-dose DFMO alters protein translation in neuroblastoma.
    supports: REFUTE
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "No correlation was seen among MYCN and/or ODC1 copy number and sensitivity to DFMO."
    explanation: >-
      A second tested null against the mechanistic reading, and the one that
      bears on patient selection: if the drug worked by blocking a
      MYCN-driven ODC1 dependence, sensitivity should track those copy
      numbers, and it did not. Graded IN_VITRO because the sensitivity
      comparison was made across cell lines. Supports leaving the approved
      indication unrestricted by MYCN status.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Polyamine Biosynthesis Dependence
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Eflornithine is an irreversible inhibitor of ornithine decarboxylase, the
      rate-limiting enzyme of the pathway this node describes, so the drug acts
      on the node directly. What is not established is that this inhibition is
      what produces the clinical effect at the approved dose; the treatment's
      own evidence records the two results that cut against that inference.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:19047152
      reference_title: ODC1 is a critical determinant of MYCN oncogenesis and a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "DFMO treatment of neuroblastoma-prone genetically engineered mice (TH-MYCN) extended tumor latency and survival in homozygous mice and prevented oncogenesis in hemizygous mice."
      explanation: >-
        The preclinical result that made this pathway a therapeutic target:
        inhibiting it delayed and in hemizygous animals prevented tumors in a
        MYCN-driven mouse model. Mouse models only, and at preclinical doses,
        which is the gap the 2025 low-dose result on this record's evidence
        opens up. Abstract sentence.
- name: 131I-MIBG Therapy
  description: >-
    A radiopharmaceutical given for MIBG-avid relapsed or refractory disease,
    in which the norepinephrine analogue carries iodine-131 into the tumor cell
    through the norepinephrine transporter. Eligibility turns on avidity: the
    randomized NANT phase II required at least one MIBG-avid site, and absence
    of avidity on a properly performed diagnostic scan is in principle a
    contraindication. Response figures from different designs are not
    comparable and are given separately. In that randomized trial the response
    rate after one course was 14% for MIBG alone, 14% with vincristine and
    irinotecan, and 32% with vorinostat; the trial used a pick-the-winner
    design, so the vorinostat arm is the one its design selected rather than
    one shown superior. Outside randomized comparison, a 164-patient phase II
    reported a 36% complete plus partial response rate, and a systematic review
    that identified no randomized controlled trials found objective response
    across 25 studies ranging from 0% to 75%, mean 32%. The frontline role is
    unproven: a Cochrane review found no randomized or controlled clinical
    trial comparing newly diagnosed high-risk regimens with and without the
    therapy, and could not make recommendations for its frontline use. One
    cohort of 106 relapsed or refractory patients found that markers of lower
    NET and VMAT2 protein expression were associated with a higher likelihood
    of response, while the NET H-score itself was not significantly associated
    with it.
  context: High-risk neuroblastoma, MIBG-avid relapsed or refractory disease
  therapeutic_modality: RADIOTHERAPY
  notes: >-
    The therapeutic agent is bound to CHEBI:135997 "iobenguane (131I)", a
    specific small molecule, which is what the repository's therapeutic-agent
    rule prefers; NCIT:C970 "Iobenguane I-131" is the alternative and is the
    form the Pheochromocytoma_Paraganglioma MIBG Therapy row uses. The
    high-specific-activity formulation has its own NCIT class, NCIT:C82344
    "Cold Contaminant-free Iobenguane I-131", which is deliberately not bound
    because this row does not distinguish formulations. No treatment_effect is
    set on the mechanism link below: the drug uses the transporter as its route
    into the cell and does not inhibit, activate, modulate, bypass or restore
    it, and no TreatmentEffectEnum value states that. The nearest precedent
    reads the same way, the CD123-directed row in
    Blastic_Plasmacytoid_Dendritic_Cell_Neoplasm, where the agent likewise uses
    the node's own surface protein as its address; note that
    Thymic_Neuroendocrine_Carcinoma's 177Lu-DOTATATE row chose INHIBITS for the
    same shape by reading the cell-killing consequence instead of the route.
    Administered activity, dose levels and product availability are
    deliberately absent: they are clinical and commercial specifics that go out
    of date with no signal that they have, and nothing here can check them.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: radiopharmaceutical therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C192439
      label: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: iobenguane I-131 (131I-MIBG)
      term:
        id: CHEBI:135997
        label: iobenguane (131I)
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34270348
    reference_title: "Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "After one course, the response rates (partial response or better) on arms A, B, and C were 14% (95% CI, 5 to 30), 14% (5 to 31), and 32% (18 to 51)."
    explanation: >-
      The only randomized response figures for this therapy, and the reason
      the description separates them from the uncontrolled ones. Arms A, B and
      C are MIBG alone, MIBG with vincristine and irinotecan, and MIBG with
      vorinostat. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:34270348
    reference_title: "Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The trial was designed with 105 patients to ensure an 80% chance that the arm with highest response rate was selected."
    explanation: >-
      Why the description says the vorinostat arm was the one the design
      selected rather than a superior regimen. A pick-the-winner design is
      powered to choose an arm for further study, not to establish superiority
      between arms, so reading the 32% as a demonstrated advantage would
      overstate the trial. Abstract methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:17369569
    reference_title: "Phase II study on the effect of disease sites, age, and prior therapy on response to iodine-131-metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in refractory neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "One hundred sixty-four patients with progressive, refractory or relapsed high-risk neuroblastoma, age 2 to 30 years, were treated in a limited institution phase II study."
    explanation: >-
      The denominator for the 36% figure below, and the design it came from: a
      single-arm phase II with no comparison group, which is why the
      description does not set that number beside the randomized rates.
      Abstract methods sentence.
  - reference: PMID:17369569
    reference_title: "Phase II study on the effect of disease sites, age, and prior therapy on response to iodine-131-metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in refractory neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The overall complete plus partial response rate was 36%."
    explanation: >-
      The uncontrolled response rate quoted in the description, from the
      164-patient cohort named in the item above. Abstract results sentence.
  - reference: PMID:24333097
    reference_title: A systematic review of 131I-meta iodobenzylguanidine molecular radiotherapy for neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The objective tumour response rate reported in 25 studies ranged from 0% to 75%, mean 32%. We conclude that (131)I-mIBG is an active treatment for neuroblastoma, but its place in the management of neuroblastoma remains unclear."
    explanation: >-
      The spread across the published literature, and the reviewers' own
      conclusion that the therapy is active while its place in management is
      unsettled. The range from 0% to 75% is the point: a single mean response
      figure for this therapy would misrepresent how much the studies differ.
      Abstract sentences.
  - reference: PMID:24333097
    reference_title: A systematic review of 131I-meta iodobenzylguanidine molecular radiotherapy for neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "No randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were identified."
    explanation: >-
      Why the 25-study range is a synthesis of uncontrolled series rather than
      pooled trial evidence. Abstract sentence.
  - reference: PMID:28429876
    reference_title: Iodine-131-meta-iodobenzylguanidine therapy for patients with newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We identified no RCTs or CCTs comparing the effectiveness of treatment including 131I-MIBG therapy versus treatment not including 131I-MIBG therapy in patients with newly diagnosed HR NBL."
    explanation: >-
      Supports the description's claim that the frontline role is unproven: a
      Cochrane search found no randomized or controlled clinical trial
      comparing newly diagnosed high-risk regimens with and without the
      therapy. The absence of trials is what the claim asserts, so the
      sentence bears on it directly rather than failing to bear on it, which
      is what NO_EVIDENCE would mean. The review's searches run to 2016.
      Abstract conclusions sentence.
  - reference: PMID:28429876
    reference_title: Iodine-131-meta-iodobenzylguanidine therapy for patients with newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Based on the currently available evidence, we cannot make recommendations for the use of 131I-MIBG therapy in patients with newly diagnosed HR NBL in clinical practice."
    explanation: >-
      The reviewers' own conclusion drawn from that absence, which is the
      claim the description makes about frontline use. Abstract conclusions
      sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37885116
    reference_title: Norepinephrine transporter and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 tumor expression as a predictor of response to (131) I-MIBG in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Markers of lower NET and VMAT2 protein expression are associated with higher likelihood of response to 131 I-MIBG therapy in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      Quoted in the direction the study found it, which is the opposite of the
      intuitive one: lower rather than higher transporter expression went with
      a higher likelihood of response, in 106 relapsed or refractory patients.
      Nothing in this record claims that more NET predicts better response.
      The cache preserves the source's own "131 I-MIBG" spacing. Abstract
      conclusions sentence.
  - reference: PMID:37885116
    reference_title: Norepinephrine transporter and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 tumor expression as a predictor of response to (131) I-MIBG in patients with relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "NET H-score was not significantly associated with response (≥PR), though the percentage of tumor cells expressing NET was lower among responders (median 80% for ≥PR vs. 90% for <PR; p = .0014)."
    explanation: >-
      The qualifier the headline conclusion needs: the composite NET H-score
      itself was not significantly associated with response, and what did
      differ was the percentage of tumor cells staining. Recorded so the
      previous item is not read as a validated predictor. Abstract results
      sentence.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Norepinephrine Transporter (NET/SLC6A2) Expression
    description: >-
      MIBG is a norepinephrine analogue actively transported into the tumor
      cell by NET and retained in neurosecretory granules through VMAT; iodine
      131 then decays locally, inside the cell the transporter admitted it to.
      The transporter is the drug's route in rather than a target it acts on,
      which is why no treatment_effect is set. Avidity on a diagnostic scan is
      the clinical readout of that route being open, and is the eligibility
      criterion.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41528635
      reference_title: "Clinical applications and future directions of Iodine-131-Metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in neuroblastoma: from salvage treatment to frontline integration."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "As a structural analog of norepinephrine, MIBG is actively transported into tumor cells via the norepinephrine transporter (NET) and stored in neurosecretory granules through vesicular monoamine transporters (VMAT)"
      explanation: >-
        Both halves of the uptake route this link asserts: NET carries MIBG in,
        VMAT holds it in neurosecretory granules. Graded IN_VITRO because the
        sentence describes cell-level transport and storage biology, with
        quote_role REVIEW_SYNTHESIS because the review restates it from a cited
        source rather than measuring it. Full-text background sentence, quoted
        up to its trailing citation.
    - reference: PMID:34270348
      reference_title: "Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "131I-metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) is a radiopharmaceutical selectively taken up via NET."
      explanation: >-
        Names NET as the route for the therapeutic isotope specifically, not
        only for the MIBG molecule in general. Graded BACKGROUND because the
        sentence is introduction material citing earlier work rather than a
        result of this trial, and IN_VITRO because the uptake biology it
        describes is cellular.
    - reference: PMID:34270348
      reference_title: "Randomized Phase II Trial of MIBG Versus MIBG, Vincristine, and Irinotecan Versus MIBG and Vorinostat for Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma: A Report From NANT Consortium."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Patients 1-30 years were eligible if they had relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma, at least one MIBG-avid site, and adequate autologous stem cells."
      explanation: >-
        How the uptake route is used clinically: the trial required a
        demonstrated MIBG-avid site, so avidity is the operational test that
        this node's transporter is present and working in a given patient's
        tumor. Abstract methods sentence.
    - reference: PMID:41528635
      reference_title: "Clinical applications and future directions of Iodine-131-Metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy in neuroblastoma: from salvage treatment to frontline integration."
      supports: SUPPORT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: "In principle, absence of MIBG avidity on a properly performed diagnostic scan is considered a contraindication to 131I-MIBG therapy."
      explanation: >-
        The converse of the item above, and the sharpest statement that this
        node gates the therapy: no avidity, no treatment. Graded OTHER because
        the sentence states a clinical-practice convention rather than a study
        result. Full-text contraindications list.
- name: Alisertib (Aurora A Inhibition)
  description: >-
    An oral Aurora A kinase inhibitor, studied in relapsed or refractory
    neuroblastoma with irinotecan and temozolomide. The rationale is the
    Aurora A-Mediated N-Myc Protein Stabilization node: removing Aurora A's
    hold on N-Myc should lower the protein. The clinical result does not match
    that rationale. A phase 2 trial of alisertib with irinotecan and
    temozolomide found antitumor activity, but the activity was concentrated
    in patients whose tumours were not MYCN-amplified, and MYCN amplification
    was associated with inferior progression-free survival, which is the
    opposite of what the mechanism predicts.
  context: Relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma, with irinotecan and temozolomide
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  notes: >-
    Alisertib is a catalytic-site inhibitor. The work that defines the N-Myc
    mechanism distinguishes that class from compounds that distort Aurora A's
    conformation, and reports that catalytic inhibitors lower N-Myc only
    modestly, so a weak clinical effect on MYCN-amplified disease is not by
    itself evidence against the stabilisation mechanism. The entry records the
    mismatch as an open human-model question rather than resolving it in
    either direction.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: alisertib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:125628
        label: alisertib
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Aurora A-Mediated N-Myc Protein Stabilization
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      The drug inhibits Aurora A's catalytic activity, which is the node's
      target protein but not the activity the node turns on.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30093449
    reference_title: "Phase II Trial of Alisertib in Combination with Irinotecan and Temozolomide for Patients with Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "This combination shows antitumor activity, particularly in patients with MYCN nonamplified tumors."
    explanation: >-
      The trial's own conclusion. It supports the combination having activity,
      and it locates that activity in the subgroup the mechanism predicts
      should benefit least.
  - reference: PMID:30093449
    reference_title: "Phase II Trial of Alisertib in Combination with Irinotecan and Temozolomide for Patients with Relapsed or Refractory Neuroblastoma."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Higher alisertib trough concentration was associated with first cycle DLT, whereas MYCN amplification was associated with inferior PFS."
    explanation: >-
      This bears against the therapeutic corollary of the stabilisation
      mechanism: if the drug worked by freeing N-Myc for degradation, the
      amplified tumours should do better, and they did worse. Indirect,
      because it is an exploratory association in a pooled analysis across
      phase 1, phase 2 and oral-solution cohorts rather than a randomized
      comparison, and because inferior survival in amplified disease is also
      the untreated natural history. The first clause concerns toxicity and is
      not used here.
  - reference: PMID:25175806
    reference_title: "Drugging MYCN through an allosteric transition in Aurora kinase A."
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Consistent with this modest effect on MYCN, early phase clinical testing of MLN8237 in patients with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma has shown little efficacy, underscoring the need for inhibitors of Aurora A that more potently block MYCN"
    explanation: >-
      The same disappointment stated earlier and from outside the trial,
      together with its proposed reading: that catalytic inhibitors move N-Myc
      too little. Graded HUMAN_CLINICAL because the sentence describes clinical
      testing, and BACKGROUND because it restates other work in this paper's
      introduction. Indirect: it summarises an early-phase result it does not
      report.
clinical_trials:
- name: NCT00567567
  phase: PHASE_III
  status: COMPLETED
  description: >-
    ANBL0532, the Children's Oncology Group trial that compared tandem
    myeloablative consolidation with a single transplant. It is the source of
    the tandem-versus-single result on the Autologous Stem Cell Transplant
    record, and one of the two trials the consolidation knowledge gap is about.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT00567567
    reference_title: "Phase III Randomized Trial of Single vs. Tandem Myeloablative Consolidation Therapy for High-Risk Neuroblastoma"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This randomized phase III trial compares two different high-dose chemotherapy regimens followed by a stem cell transplant in treating younger patients with high-risk neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the trial's identity and design: a
      randomized phase III comparison of two high-dose regimens before stem
      cell transplant. Graded OTHER because a registry summary is a
      registration document rather than study evidence; the trial's results
      are cited on the treatment record from its publication.
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT00567567
    reference_title: "Phase III Randomized Trial of Single vs. Tandem Myeloablative Consolidation Therapy for High-Risk Neuroblastoma"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "It is not yet known which regimen of high-dose chemotherapy is more effective for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma undergoing a peripheral blood stem cell transplant."
    explanation: >-
      The registry's own statement of the question at the time of
      registration, which is what makes this trial the right citation for the
      comparison rather than for a conclusion. The uncertainty it records was
      resolved for the arms this trial ran, and not for the comparison the
      knowledge gap describes.
- name: NCT01704716
  phase: PHASE_III
  status: UNKNOWN
  description: >-
    SIOPEN's High Risk Neuroblastoma Study 1, the European trial whose R1
    randomization set its high-dose consolidation regimen, and which adopted
    busulfan-melphalan on that result. The registry record quoted below does
    not name what busulfan-melphalan was compared against; that comparison is
    a finding of the trial's publication and is cited where the comparison is
    made, not here. It is the second of the two trials the consolidation
    knowledge gap is about. Its registry status is recorded as unknown, which is the
    registry's own value where a sponsor has not confirmed a status within the
    expected interval, not a statement that the trial stopped.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT01704716
    reference_title: "High Risk Neuroblastoma Study 1 of SIOP-Europe (SIOPEN)"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Consolidation consists of BuMel MAT based on the results of the R1 randomization followed by peripheral blood stem cell rescue (PBSCR) and radiotherapy to the site of the primary tumour."
    explanation: >-
      The registry record showing that this trial both ran the high-dose
      comparison and then built its own consolidation on the winning arm,
      which is why the Autologous Stem Cell Transplant record treats
      busulfan-melphalan as the European standard. Graded OTHER as a
      registration document.
- name: NCT00026312
  phase: PHASE_III
  status: COMPLETED
  description: >-
    ANBL0032, the trial that established anti-GD2 immunotherapy in
    post-transplant maintenance. Both arms received isotretinoin and the
    randomization was of dinutuximab, aldesleukin and sargramostim added to
    it, so the trial establishes what anti-GD2 adds to isotretinoin and not
    what isotretinoin adds in the anti-GD2 era. That asymmetry is the reason
    the Isotretinoin record describes its own evidence base as predating the
    treatment it now sits beside.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT00026312
    reference_title: "Phase III Randomized Study of Chimeric Antibody 14.18 (Ch14.18) in High Risk Neuroblastoma Following Myeloablative Therapy and Autologous Stem Cell Rescue"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This partially randomized phase III trial studies isotretinoin with dinutuximab, aldesleukin, and sargramostim to see how well it works compared to isotretinoin alone following stem cell transplant in treating patients with neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record, and the basis for the point above: the
      comparison is isotretinoin plus immunotherapy against isotretinoin
      alone, so isotretinoin is in both arms. Note also "partially
      randomized", which the registry states and which bears on how the
      trial's result should be read. Graded OTHER as a registration document.
- name: NCT02395666
  phase: PHASE_II
  status: COMPLETED
  description: >-
    The single-agent eflornithine maintenance trial in high-risk neuroblastoma
    in remission, registered as a preventative study with up to 27 cycles of
    oral eflornithine. It is the clinical setting the Eflornithine (DFMO)
    Maintenance Therapy record describes, and a single-arm design, which is
    why that record is written around an externally controlled comparison.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT02395666
    reference_title: "A Phase II Preventative Trial of DFMO (Eflornithine HCl) as a Single Agent in Patients With High Risk Neuroblastoma in Remission"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The purpose of this research study is to evaluate a new investigational drug to prevent reoccurrence of neuroblastoma that is in remission. This study drug is called DFMO."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the trial's purpose and population:
      prevention of recurrence in patients already in remission, which is the
      maintenance indication rather than treatment of active disease. Graded
      OTHER as a registration document.
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT02395666
    reference_title: "A Phase II Preventative Trial of DFMO (Eflornithine HCl) as a Single Agent in Patients With High Risk Neuroblastoma in Remission"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The proposed dosing regimen is an oral dose of DFMO tablets two times a day for each day while on study. There will be 27 cycles. Each cycle will be 28 days in length."
    explanation: >-
      The registered schedule, which is the source of the twice-daily dosing
      interval on the Eflornithine treatment record and of the roughly
      two-year duration described there. Graded OTHER as a registration
      document.
- name: NCT03794349
  phase: PHASE_II
  status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING
  description: >-
    The randomized add-on test of eflornithine in relapsed, refractory or
    progressive neuroblastoma, on an irinotecan, temozolomide and dinutuximab
    backbone. It is the one randomized test of eflornithine in neuroblastoma,
    in a different setting from the approved maintenance indication, and it is
    named in the Eflornithine record's notes.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT03794349
    reference_title: "A Phase 2 Randomized Study of Irinotecan/Temozolomide/Dinutuximab With or Without Eflornithine (DFMO) in Children With Relapsed, Refractory or Progressive Neuroblastoma"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This phase II trial studies how well irinotecan hydrochloride, temozolomide, and dinutuximab work with or without eflornithine in treating patients with neuroblastoma that has come back (relapsed) or that isn't responding to treatment (refractory)."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the design and population: a
      with-or-without eflornithine randomization in relapsed or refractory
      disease. The cached body holds only this brief summary, so the posted
      outcome figures cannot be quoted from it, which is what the Eflornithine
      record's notes say. Graded OTHER as a registration document.
- name: NCT00033293
  phase: PHASE_III
  status: COMPLETED
  description: >-
    The randomized trial of intravenous immunoglobulin added to
    cyclophosphamide and prednisone for neuroblastoma-associated
    opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome. The mechanism and the immunotherapy
    evidence for that syndrome are curated in the Paraneoplastic Neurological
    Syndromes entry; this record places the trial on the tumour whose presence
    defines the paraneoplastic setting.
  target_phenotypes:
  - preferred_term: Opsoclonus
    term:
      id: HP:0010543
      label: Opsoclonus
  - preferred_term: Myoclonus
    term:
      id: HP:0001336
      label: Myoclonus
  - preferred_term: Ataxia
    term:
      id: HP:0001251
      label: Ataxia
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT00033293
    reference_title: "A Phase III Randomized Trial of Intravenous Gammaglobulin Therapy for Patients With Neuroblastoma Associated Opsoclonus-Myoclonus-Ataxia Syndrome Treated With Chemotherapy and Prednisone"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This randomized phase III trial is studying cyclophosphamide, prednisone, and immunoglobulin to see how well they work compared to cyclophosphamide and prednisone alone in treating patients with abnormal trunk muscle movements associated with neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the design: immunoglobulin added to
      cyclophosphamide and prednisone, against those two alone, in children
      whose movement disorder is associated with neuroblastoma. The three
      target phenotypes are bound from the registered title, which names
      opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome. Graded OTHER as a registration
      document.
- name: NCT03126916
  phase: PHASE_III
  status: RECRUITING
  description: >-
    The frontline Children's Oncology Group phase 3 trial that adds either
    131I-MIBG or ALK-inhibitor therapy to intensive therapy in newly diagnosed
    high-risk neuroblastoma. It anchors two records at once: the 131I-MIBG
    Therapy record and the Lorlatinib record, whose frontline claim is
    currently sourced to two publications that name this trial rather than to
    the trial itself. Recruiting at the time of curation, so it carries no
    result and none is claimed for it.
  notes: >-
    The two arms are not two halves of one randomization, and the difference
    decides what this trial can support. Its registered primary objectives put
    the iobenguane I-131 question "in the context of a randomized trial", while
    the lorlatinib question is whether adding lorlatinib for patients whose
    tumours carry an activating ALK point mutation gives superior event-free
    survival "compared to a contemporaneously treated cohort of patients with
    tumors without documented ALK activating mutations", with a further
    objective comparing that arm against a historical control of ALK-aberrant
    patients treated on ANBL0532, which is NCT00567567 in this same section. So
    the lorlatinib arm has no randomized comparator, and the frontline
    lorlatinib claim should not be read as resting on one. These objectives are
    in the registry's detailed description, which the cached brief summary does
    not carry, so they are recorded here rather than quoted as a snippet.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT03126916
    reference_title: "A Phase 3 Study of 131I-Metaiodobenzylguanidine (131I-MIBG) or ALK Inhibitor Therapy Added to Intensive Therapy for Children With Newly Diagnosed High-Risk Neuroblastoma (NBL)"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This phase III trial studies iobenguane I-131 or lorlatinib and standard therapy in treating younger patients with newly-diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the design and population, and why
      this one trial bears on two treatment records: it adds either iobenguane
      I-131 or lorlatinib to standard therapy in newly diagnosed disease. The
      cached summary does not say how patients reach each agent, and this
      explanation does not either; the record's notes carry that, because it
      decides what the trial can support. Graded OTHER because a registry
      summary is a registration document rather than study evidence, and the
      trial is still recruiting, so there is no result to grade.
- name: NCT02095132
  phase: PHASE_I
  status: COMPLETED
  description: >-
    ADVL1312, the Children's Oncology Group study of adavosertib with oral
    irinotecan in relapsed or refractory paediatric solid tumours. It is the
    trial behind the Adavosertib treatment record, and the reason the
    replication-stress checkpoint has any clinical test at all in this disease.
    The registry lists it as phase 1/2 and the published report is of the phase
    2 expansion, which ran disease-specific cohorts; neuroblastoma was part B
    and its response figures are curated on the treatment record rather than
    repeated here. Recorded as PHASE_I because ClinicalTrialPhaseEnum is
    single-valued and that is the earliest of the two phases the registry
    carries; the registry's own phase list is named in this description instead.
  evidence:
  - reference: clinicaltrials:NCT02095132
    reference_title: "A Phase 1/2 Study of AZD1775 (MK-1775) in Combination With Oral Irinotecan in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With Relapsed or Refractory Solid Tumors"
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "This phase I/II trial studies the side effects and best dose of adavosertib and irinotecan hydrochloride in treating younger patients with solid tumors that have come back (relapsed) or that have not responded to standard therapy (refractory)."
    explanation: >-
      The registration record establishing the trial's design, combination and
      population. Note what it does not establish: the summary says solid
      tumours and does not name neuroblastoma, so the disease-specific cohort
      and its results come from the published report cited on the Adavosertib
      treatment record, not from this row. Graded OTHER because a registry
      summary is a registration document rather than study evidence.
animal_models:
- name: Xenopus anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cell differentiation model
  species: Xenopus laevis
  genotype: >-
    Embryos expressing wild-type Ascl1, a phospho-mutant Ascl1 that cannot be
    phosphorylated at serine-proline motifs, CDKs, or MYCN, with Ascl1
    morpholino knockdown
  category: Developmental model of the presumed cell of origin
  publication: PMID:25786414
  description: >-
    Rather than growing a tumour, this model reconstructs the normal
    differentiation of the neural-crest-derived sympathoadrenal cell that
    neuroblastoma is thought to arise from, and asks what stops it. Frog AVNA
    cells differentiate under transient Ascl1 expression; in neuroblastoma cells
    Ascl1 is instead persistently expressed and multiply phosphorylated.
    Introducing that phospho-state into the frog cells blocks their
    differentiation, and CDK or MYCN overexpression blocks it too — but not when
    Ascl1 cannot be phosphorylated, which places phosphorylation downstream of
    both. The model tests the differentiation-arrest hypothesis in a normal
    developmental context; it does not produce tumours and so says nothing about
    transformation, growth, or metastasis.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ASCL1
    term:
      id: hgnc:738
      label: ASCL1
  - preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Neural Crest Developmental Arrest
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: MODERATE
    description: >-
      Supplies a molecular switch for the arrest this node asserts: multi-site
      phosphorylation of Ascl1 converts it from a driver of sympathoadrenal
      differentiation into an inert factor, matching the phospho-state Ascl1 is
      held in within neuroblastoma cells.
    limitations: >-
      Frog AVNA cells are a developmental counterpart of the presumed cell of
      origin, not tumour cells, and the model contains no transformed tissue —
      arrest is scored as failure to differentiate on schedule rather than as
      tumour formation. The link to human disease rests on the observed
      phospho-state of ASCL1 in neuroblastoma lines, so the model shows the
      state is sufficient to block differentiation, not that it is what maintains
      any patient's tumour.
    readouts:
    - name: AVNA cell differentiation driven by wild-type versus phospho-mutant Ascl1
      target: Neural Crest Developmental Arrest
      direction: DECREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Differentiation fails when Ascl1 can be multiply phosphorylated and
        proceeds when it cannot, isolating phospho-status as the controlling
        variable.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:25786414
        reference_title: "Ascl1 phospho-status regulates neuronal differentiation in a Xenopus developmental model of neuroblastoma."
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        snippet: "ability to induce differentiation of AVNA cells is inhibited by its multi-site phosphorylation at serine-proline motifs"
        explanation: States the measured effect of Ascl1 phospho-status on differentiation in this model.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:25786414
      reference_title: "Ascl1 phospho-status regulates neuronal differentiation in a Xenopus developmental model of neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "Here, we use Xenopus frog embryos to characterise the differentiation of anteroventral noradrenergic (AVNA) cells, cells derived from the neural crest."
      explanation: Establishes what the model is and that its cells are neural crest derived.
    - reference: PMID:25786414
      reference_title: "Ascl1 phospho-status regulates neuronal differentiation in a Xenopus developmental model of neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "We find that the transcriptional regulator Ascl1 is expressed transiently in normal AVNA cell differentiation but its expression is aberrantly maintained in NB cells, where it is largely phosphorylated on multiple sites."
      explanation: >-
        The neuroblastoma-cell half of this comparison is cell-based, and it is
        what connects the frog readout to the human disease state.
  - target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
    relationship: PERTURBS
    fidelity: MODERATE
    description: >-
      Positions MYCN upstream of the differentiation block: MYCN overexpression
      prevents Ascl1-driven differentiation, and loses that ability when Ascl1
      cannot be phosphorylated.
    limitations: >-
      This is the differentiation-blocking arm of MYCN only. The node is about
      proliferation, and no proliferative or tumour-growth readout was taken
      here; MYCN is introduced by overexpression in a normal embryo, not by the
      genomic amplification that defines high-risk neuroblastoma.
    readouts:
    - name: Ascl1-driven AVNA differentiation under CDK or MYCN overexpression
      target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
      direction: DECREASED
      interpretation: >-
        The epistasis result: MYCN and CDKs block differentiation only when Ascl1
        is phosphorylatable, so their effect on this cell fate runs through Ascl1
        phospho-status.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:25786414
        reference_title: "Ascl1 phospho-status regulates neuronal differentiation in a Xenopus developmental model of neuroblastoma."
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        snippet: "overexpression of cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) and MYCN inhibit wild-type Ascl1-driven AVNA differentiation, but not differentiation driven by a phospho-mutant form of Ascl1"
        explanation: Reports the measured differentiation block and the phospho-mutant control that makes it interpretable.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:25786414
      reference_title: "Ascl1 phospho-status regulates neuronal differentiation in a Xenopus developmental model of neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "This suggests that the maintenance of ASCL1 in its multiply phosphorylated state might prevent terminal differentiation in NB, which could offer new approaches for differentiation therapy in NB."
      explanation: >-
        The authors put the therapeutic and disease-level reading as a
        suggestion, which is the level of support this link carries.
- name: Lin28B sympathetic-adrenergic lineage transgenic mouse
  species: Mouse
  genotype: LIN28B transgene expressed in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage
  category: Transgenic tumour-initiation model
  publication: PMID:23042116
  description: >-
    Forced LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage induces
    neuroblastomas in mice, and the tumours carry low let-7 and high MYCN
    protein, which is the chain this entry models run forwards in an animal. It
    shows that LIN28B overexpression is sufficient for tumour formation in that
    lineage; it says nothing about how often that route operates in human
    disease.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LIN28B
    term:
      id: hgnc:32207
      label: LIN28B
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: let-7 Depletion
    relationship: PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: MODERATE
    model_scale: ORGANISM
    description: >-
      The model runs the LIN28B-to-let-7 arm forwards: driving LIN28B in the
      sympathetic adrenergic lineage produces tumours whose let-7 is low and
      whose MYCN protein is high.
    limitations: >-
      In a Lin28B mouse reported separately, sympathetic ganglion and adrenal
      medulla volume and Let-7a were unchanged despite a 12- to 17-fold rise in
      Lin28B, while Let-7a was strongly reduced in that line's tumour tissue.
      The let-7 arm of this model is therefore established in the tumours and
      not in normal developing sympathoadrenal tissue; do not read the mouse as
      evidence that let-7 depletion initiates the disease.
    readouts:
    - name: Mature let-7 abundance in tumour tissue
      target: let-7 Depletion
      direction: DECREASED
      interpretation: The tumours arising in this model carry low let-7, which is
        the node state the link claims.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:23042116
        reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
          suppression.
        supports: SUPPORT
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        snippet: "These findings were fully recapitulated in a mouse model in which LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage induced development of neuroblastomas marked by low let-7 miRNA levels and high MYCN protein expression"
        explanation: >-
          The measurement behind this readout: the tumours arising in the mouse
          are reported as marked by low let-7 miRNA levels. Repeated from the
          link's own evidence so the readout is self-describing, which is the
          reason its target is required to restate the link's target. The
          abstract reports the direction without a quantity or a comparator
          tissue.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:23042116
      reference_title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7
        suppression.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "These findings were fully recapitulated in a mouse model in which LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage induced development of neuroblastomas marked by low let-7 miRNA levels and high MYCN protein expression"
      explanation: >-
        The paper's own in vivo experiment states every element of the link in
        one sentence: LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage
        induced development of neuroblastomas, and those tumours carried low
        let-7 and high MYCN protein. The cached record is abstract-only and the
        abstract names no mouse line or promoter, so the construct behind this
        model is not established from this reference.
    - reference: PMID:26674877
      reference_title: Lin28B and Let-7 in the Control of Sympathetic Neurogenesis
        and Neuroblastoma Development.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: "Sympathetic ganglion and adrenal medulla volume and the expression level of Let-7a were not altered, although Lin28B expression increased by 12- to 17-fold ... Let-7a expression was strongly reduced in LSL-Lin28B(DbhiCre) NB tumor tissue"
      explanation: >-
        The same conditional Lin28B allele, driven in the sympathoadrenal
        lineage and examined by an independent group before tumours arise: a
        12- to 17-fold rise in Lin28B left Let-7a and the volume of the normal
        sympathetic ganglia and adrenal medulla unaltered, while Let-7a was
        strongly reduced in the tumours the line went on to form. Both
        fragments must travel together, because the first bounds the let-7 link
        away from normal developing sympathoadrenal tissue and the second
        places it in established tumour. Graded INDIRECT because reading the
        two measurements as placing the let-7 arm after initiation rather than
        at it is an inference step the quoted text does not take.
